They have turned away from the Book and the Sunnah, mocking their adherents and belittling them, and they have refused to submit to the judgement of the two revelations, exulting in the knowledge they possess, which does not benefit those who accumulate much of it, out of pride and arrogance. You will always find them mocking those who hold fast to clear revelation. ﴿God mocks them, and He leaves them to wander blindly in their transgression﴾ [al-Baqarah: 15].

They set out in search of a ruinous trade across the seas of darkness, and they boarded ships of doubts and suspicions that sail with them on the waves of imagination. A violent wind toyed with their vessels and cast them among the ships of the lost. ﴿Those are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance, so their trade has not profited them, nor were they guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16].

The fire of faith lit up for them, and by its light they saw the places of guidance and error. Then that light was extinguished, and there remained a fire blazing with flame and burning. They are tormented by that fire and wander in those darknesses. ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire; when it lit up all around him, God took away their light and left them in darkness, unable to see﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17].

The ears of their hearts are weighed down with deafness, so they do not hear the call of faith. The eyes of their insight are covered with the veil of blindness, so they do not see the realities of the Qur'an. Their tongues are mute with respect to the truth, so they do not speak it. ﴿Deaf, dumb, and blind; so they will not return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18].

The rain-cloud of revelation poured down upon them, and in it is the life of hearts and spirits. But they heard from it only the thunder of threat and warning and the obligations imposed upon them morning and evening. So they put their fingers in their ears, wrapped themselves in their garments, hastened to flee, and raised their outcry in pursuit of those who followed the Prophetic way. They were called out before the assembled witnesses, their condition was exposed to those who have insight, and two parables were struck for them corresponding to the condition of the two groups among them: the disputants and the blind followers. It is said: ﴿Or like a rain-cloud from the sky, in which are darknesses, thunder and lightning; they put their fingers in their ears against the thunderbolts, fearing death; and God encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 19].

The eyes of their insight are too weak to bear what is in the rain-cloud of its flashes of light and the brilliance of its meanings. Their ears are unable to receive the thunder of its promises, its commands and its prohibitions. So at that point they stand bewildered in valleys of wandering, neither the hearer benefiting from what he hears nor the seer being guided by what he sees. ﴿Whenever it lights up for them, they walk in it, and when darkness falls on them, they stand still. Had God willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight; surely God has power over all things﴾ [al-Baqarah: 20].

They have signs by which they are recognised, clearly stated in the Sunnah and the Qur'an, manifest to whoever reflects upon them among the people of insight into faith. Ostentation (al-riya') has taken hold of them, and by God it is the most shameful station a human being can occupy. Laziness has kept them from what they were commanded by the commands of the Merciful, so sincerity (al-ikhlas) has become burdensome for them. ﴿When they stand up to pray, they stand lazily, showing off to people and remembering God only a little﴾ [al-Nisa': 142].

One of them is like a lone sheep between two flocks, bleating toward this one at one time and toward that one at another, never settling with either group. They stand between the two parties, watching which is stronger and mightier in number. ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those; and whomever God leaves astray, you will not find a way for him﴾ [al-Nisa': 143].

They wait for misfortunes to befall the people of the Sunnah and the Qur'an. If God grants victory to them, they say: "Were we not with you?" and they swear by God with their most solemn oaths. And if the enemies of the Book and the Sunnah obtain a share of victory, they say: "Do you not know that the bond of brotherhood between us is firm, and that our kinship is close?" So, O you who seek to know them, take their description from the words of the Lord of the worlds, and you will need no other proof after it. ﴿Those who wait for you: if you have a victory from God, they say, "Were we not with you?"; and if the disbelievers have a share, they say, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?" God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [al-Nisa': 141].

The listener is pleased by the speech of one of them because of its sweetness and softness, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart of lying and falsehood. You see him asleep when it comes to the truth, but on his feet when it comes to falsehood. So take their description from the words of the Holy, the Peaceful. ﴿Among people is one whose speech pleases you in the life of this world, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾ [al-Baqarah: 204].

The commands they give to their followers involve the corruption of lands and of people, and their prohibitions against what is good for their livelihood and their hereafter. Yet one of them, when you meet him among the company of the people of faith, appears in prayer, remembrance, asceticism, and diligence. ﴿When he turns away, he hastens about the earth to cause corruption in it, destroying crops and offspring; and God does not love corruption﴾ [al-Baqarah: 205].

They are a kind whose members resemble one another. They command the wrong after they have done it, and forbid the right after they have abandoned it. They are stingy with wealth in the cause of God and seeking His pleasure, refusing to spend it. How often has God reminded them of His blessings, and they turned away from remembering Him and forgot Him! How often has He exposed their condition to His believing servants so that they would avoid it! So listen, O believers: ﴿The hypocrite men and hypocrite women are of one another; they enjoin the wrong, forbid the right, and withhold their hands. They forgot God, so He forgot them. Surely the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67].

If you bring them to judgement by clear revelation, you will find them recoiling from it, and if you call them to the judgement of the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger (ﷺ), you will see them turning away from it. Had you witnessed their realities, you would have seen a vast distance between them and guidance, and you would have seen them turning away from revelation with a severe aversion. ﴿When it is said to them, "Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with utter aversion﴾ [al-Nisa': 61].

How, then, can they attain success and guidance, after they have been afflicted in their minds and their religion? And how can they be freed from error and ruin, when they have bought disbelief with their faith? How losing is their barren trade! They have exchanged the sealed wine for the blazing fire. ﴿So how will it be when a calamity strikes them because of what their hands have sent ahead, and then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good and reconciliation"?﴾ [an-Nisa': 62].

The thorny tree of doubts and suspicions has lodged in their hearts, and they find no way to swallow it. ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah knows. So turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them a far-reaching word concerning themselves﴾ [an-Nisa': 63].

Ruin to them! How far they are from the reality of faith! How false is their claim to verification and knowledge! The people are in one affair, and the followers of the Messenger are in another. Allah, exalted is His majesty, swore in His Book by His own sacred Self, a mighty oath whose meaning is known to those of insight, so their hearts are wary of it out of reverence and magnification of Him. Allah, exalted, said, as a warning to His allies and a notice and explanation concerning the state of these people: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is disputed between them, and then find within themselves no discomfort at what you decide, and submit fully﴾ [an-Nisa': 65].

Their oath precedes their speech, without anyone having challenged it, because they know that the hearts of the people of faith do not feel at ease with them. So they disclaim suspicion of themselves with their oaths, and reveal what is in them. Likewise, the people of doubt lie and swear, so that the listener will think they are truthful. ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and have averted [people] from the way of Allah. Evil is what they have been doing﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 2].

Ruin to them! They set out into the desert with the caravan of faith, but when they saw the length of the road and the distance of the journey, they turned back on their heels and retreated, thinking they would enjoy the good life and the pleasure of sleep in their homes. Yet they were not given enjoyment of it, nor did they benefit from that rest. Then, as soon as the one who calls out called to them, they rose from the tables of their food while the people were hungry and had not been satisfied. How, then, will their state be at the encounter? They recognized [the truth] then denied it, and they became blind after they had seen the truth and perceived it. ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts, and they do not understand﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 3].

They are the best of people in bodies, the most eloquent in tongue, the most fluent in expression, the most wicked in hearts, and the weakest in courage. They are like propped-up timbers that bear no fruit, uprooted from their planting places and leaning against a wall that holds them up, lest travelers tread upon them. ﴿When you see them, their bodies impress you, and if they speak you listen to their words. They are as if they were propped-up timbers. They consider every cry to be against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May Allah destroy them! How are they deluded?﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4].

They delay the prayer from its first time until the graves are split open, so that the dawn prayer is performed when the sun rises, and the afternoon prayer at sunset. They peck at it like the crow pecks, for it is the prayer of the bodies, not the prayer of the hearts. They look about during it with the glance of the fox, for it is certain it is pursued and sought. They do not attend congregational prayer; rather, if one of them prays, it is in the house or the shop. When he disputes, he deviates; when he makes a covenant, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays. This is their dealing with the creation, and that is their dealing with the Creator. So take their description from the beginning of [surat] al-Mutaffifin to the end of [surat] at-Tariq, for none informs you of their attributes like the One who is All-Aware. ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and what a wretched destination﴾ [at-Tahrim: 9]. How numerous they are! Yet they are the fewest. How weak they are! Yet they are the most abased. How ignorant they are! Yet they claim to be the knowers. How deceived they are concerning Allah, for they are ignorant of His greatness! ﴿And they swear by Allah that they are surely of you, but they are not of you; rather, they are a people who are fearful﴾ [at-Tawbah: 56].

If the People of the Book and the Sunnah are granted well-being, victory, and dominance, that displeases them and grieves them. But if they are struck by a trial from Allah and a test through which He purifies their sins and expiates their misdeeds, that delights them and gladdens them. This confirms their inheritance and the inheritance of those other than them, and one whose inheritance is the hypocrites is not equal [to the other]. ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them; and if a misfortune strikes you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution before," and they turn away rejoicing. Say, "Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us. He is our Protector, and upon Allah let the believers rely"﴾ [at-Tawbah: 50-51]. And Allah, exalted, said concerning the two conflicting groups, while the truth is not repelled by the arrogance of the people of deviation and confusion: ﴿If good touches you, it distresses them; and if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. But if you are patient and fear Allah, their plot will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 120].

Allah disliked their acts of obedience, because of the corruption of their hearts and the corruption of their intentions. So He held them back from them and kept them inactive, and He hated their nearness to Him and their proximity to Him, because of their inclination toward His enemies. So He drove them away from Him and distanced them. They turned away from His revelation, so He turned away from them. He made them wretched, and how far they are from felicity! He passed upon them a just judgment, with no hope for them of success after it, except that they repent. So Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Had they wanted to go out, they would have prepared for it some equipment. But Allah disliked their setting out, so He held them back, and it was said, "Sit with those who sit"﴾ [at-Tawbah: 46]. Then He mentioned His wisdom in holding them back and keeping them inactive, and in driving them from His door and distancing them, and that this is from His gentleness toward His allies and their happiness. He said, and He is the most Wise of judges: ﴿Had they gone out with you, they would have added to you nothing but corruption, and they would have hurried about among you seeking to cause discord, and among you there are those who would listen to them. And Allah is All-Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾ [at-Tawbah: 47].

The texts have become heavy for them, so they disliked them. Carrying them wearied them, so they threw them off their shoulders and set them down. The Sunan slipped from them, so they did not preserve them, and they neglected them. The texts of the Book and the Sunnah attacked them, so they devised rules by which they pushed them back and repelled them. Allah has torn away their veils and uncovered their secrets, and He has struck examples for His servants of them. He informed that whenever groups of them pass away, their likes succeed them. So He described their attributes to His allies, that they might be wary of them, and He made them clear to them. He said: ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 9].

This is the condition of one for whom the texts have become heavy. He sees them as barriers between himself and his innovation and his desires. They stand before him like a firmly built structure. So he sold them for a paltry gain of false speech, and exchanged them for trivial matters. That led to his corrupting their public and private affairs for them. ﴿That is because they said to those who hated what Allah had sent down, "We will obey you in some of the matter." Allah knows their secrets. So how will it be when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs? That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 26-28].

They concealed the secrets of hypocrisy, but Allah made them manifest on the surfaces of their faces and in the slips of their tongues. He marked them, because of these, with a sign by which they cannot be hidden from the people of insight and faith. They thought that when they hid their disbelief and displayed their faith, they would pass as genuine before the money-changers and assayers. How could that be, when the discerning Critic has exposed it for you? ﴿Or do those in whose hearts is a disease think that Allah will not bring forth their malice? Had We willed, We would have shown them to you, and you would have known them by their marks. And you will surely know them by the tone of their speech. And Allah knows your deeds﴾ [Muhammad: 29-30].

So how will it be when they are gathered for the Day of Meeting, when Allah, exalted is His majesty, manifests Himself to the servants and the Shin is uncovered? They will be called to prostrate, but they will not be able to. ﴿Their eyes will be humbled, humiliation will cover them, and they used to be called to prostration while they were sound﴾ [al-Qalam: 43].

Or how will it be with them when they are gathered to the bridge of Hell? It is finer than a hair and sharper than a sword, slippery and treacherous, dark, and no one can cross it except with a light by which he sees the places of his feet. The lights are distributed among the people, and they are in proportion to their varying degrees in passing and going. Those with the people of Islam are given an apparent light, just as they were among them in this abode, coming with prayer, zakah, hajj, and fasting. But when they reached the middle of the bridge, winds of hypocrisy blew upon their lights and extinguished the lamps in their hands. So they stood bewildered, unable to pass. Then a wall with a gate was set up between them and the people of faith. But the people were prevented from reaching the keys. Its inner side, facing the believers, contains mercy, and what is on their side facing them contains punishment and vengeance. They call out to those who went ahead of them from the company of faith, whose torches gleam from afar like stars, appearing to the sight of man: ﴿Wait for us that we may borrow from your light﴾ [al-Hadid: 13], so that they may be able to cross this narrow passage, for our lights have been extinguished, and there is no passage today except with a lamp of light. ﴿It will be said, "Go back behind you and seek light"﴾, for the lights have been divided. How far is standing still for anyone in such an arena! How can we seek to stand in this narrow passage? Will anyone today turn back for anyone on this road? Will a companion today look toward a companion?

Then they remind them of their gathering with them and their companionship with them in this abode, just as a stranger reminds the homeland's companion of their companionship during journeys. ﴿Were we not with you?﴾ We used to fast as you fast, pray as you pray, recite as you recite, give charity as you give charity, and perform hajj as you perform hajj. So what has separated us today, so that you have gone on alone past us?

﴿They will say, "Yes"﴾, but your outward appearances were with us while your inner selves were with every atheist and every ungrateful wrongdoer. ﴿But you led yourselves into temptation, waited, doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came, and the Deceiver deceived you concerning Allah. So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved. Your refuge is the Fire; it is your protector, and what a wretched destination﴾ [al-Hadid: 14-15].

Do not prolong the description of these people, for what is left unsaid is, by Allah, more than what is mentioned. The Qur'an almost entirely concerns them, because of their multitude upon the face of the earth and in the depths of the graves. The regions of the earth would never be empty of them, lest the believers feel lonely on the roads, the means of livelihood be disrupted through them, and the wild beasts and predators snatch them in the wilderness. Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, heard a man say, "O Allah, destroy the hypocrites." He said: "O my nephew, if the hypocrites were destroyed, you would feel lonely on your roads due to the scarcity of travelers."

By Allah, the fear of hypocrisy has cut the hearts of the foremost early [Companions], because they knew its fine and coarse details, its particulars and its totalities. Their opinions of themselves were so poor that they feared they might be among the hypocrites. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said to Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with both of them: "O Hudhayfah, I adjure you by Allah, has the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named me among them to you?" He said, "No, and I will not vouch for anyone after you." Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: "I met thirty of the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), all of whom feared hypocrisy for themselves, and none of them said that his faith was like the faith of Jibril and Mika'il." Al-Bukhari recorded it. It is also reported from al-Hasan al-Basri: "None feels secure from it except a hypocrite, and none fears it except a believer." It is also reported of one of the Companions that he used to say in his supplication: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the humility of hypocrisy." It was said: "And what is the humility of hypocrisy?" He said: "That the body appears humble while the heart is not humble."

By Allah, the hearts of these people are filled with faith and certainty. Their fear of hypocrisy is intense, and their concern about it is heavy. But many others among them, their faith does not go beyond their throats, and they claim that their faith is like the faith of Jibril and Mika'il.

The seed of hypocrisy grows on two channels: the channel of lying and the channel of showing off. Its outflow comes from two springs: the spring of weakened insight and the spring of weakened resolve. When these four pillars are complete, the plant of hypocrisy (nifaq) and its structure become firmly established. Yet it stands on the edge of a crumbling precipice, carved by the paths of torrents. When they witness the flood of realities on the Day when secrets are tested, what is hidden is exposed, what is in the graves is overturned, and what is in the breasts is brought out, then it becomes clear to the one whose merchandise was hypocrisy that what he had gathered was like a mirage: ﴿The thirsty one thinks it is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and he finds Allah with him, and He pays him his account in full. And Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

Their hearts are heedless of good deeds, and their bodies are eager for them. Immorality is widespread in their ways. When they hear the truth, their hearts are hard to hearing it. When they attend falsehood and witness false testimony, the eyes of their hearts are opened, and their ears are attentive. These, by Allah, are the signs of hypocrisy, so beware of them, O man, before the decisive calamity befalls you. When they make a covenant, they do not keep it. If they promise, they break it. If they speak, they are not just. If they are called to obedience, they hold back. When it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," they turn away. When their desires call them to their aims, they hurry to them and go off. So leave them to what they have chosen for themselves of humiliation, disgrace and loss. Do not trust their covenants, and do not be reassured by their promises, for they are liars in them, and they are violators of anything other than them. ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity and we will surely be among the righteous." But when He gave them of His bounty, they became stingy with it and turned away while refusing. So He caused hypocrisy to follow in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke to Allah what they had promised Him and because they used to lie﴾ [al-Tawbah: 75–77].

[Chapter: Sins Weaken the Heart]

Among the punishments of sins is that they weaken the heart's journey to Allah and the Hereafter. Or they hinder it, or they halt it and cut it off from the journey, so that it does not take a single step toward Allah. This is the case if they do not turn it back from its direction to what lies behind it. Sin blocks the one who would arrive, cuts off the traveler, and reverses the seeker. The heart travels to Allah only by its strength. When it is sickened by sins, that strength which moves it weakens. If it disappears altogether, the heart is cut off from Allah with a severance that is hard to remedy. And Allah is the One sought for help.

Sin either kills the heart, or makes it sick with a dangerous sickness, or weakens its strength, and inevitably so, until its weakness reaches the eight things from which the Prophet (ﷺ) sought refuge: "Anxiety (hamm), grief (huzn), incapacity ('ajz), laziness (kasal), cowardice (jubn), miserliness (bukhl), the burden of debt (dal' al-dayn), and being overpowered by men (ghalabat al-rijal)." Each two of them are companions.

Anxiety and grief are companions: when a disliked matter enters the heart and it concerns a future event that one fears, it produces anxiety (hamm). If it concerns a past matter that has already happened, it produces grief (huzn).

Incapacity and laziness are companions: if a servant falls short of the means of goodness and success, then if it is because he lacks ability, it is incapacity ('ajz), and if it is because he lacks will, it is laziness (kasal).

Cowardice and miserliness are companions: if the benefit he gives is withheld by his body, it is cowardice (jubn), and if it is withheld by his wealth, it is miserliness (bukhl).

The burden of debt and the subjugation of men are companions: if another's domination over him is by right, it is from the burden of debt (dal' al-dayn), and if it is by falsehood, it is from the subjugation of men (qahr al-rijal).

The point is that sins are among the strongest causes that bring about these eight, just as they are among the strongest causes that bring about the severity of trials, the depth of misery, the evil of decree, and the gloating of enemies. They are also among the strongest causes that bring about the removal of Allah's blessings and the turning of His well-being into His vengeance, and they draw down all of His wrath.

Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them﴾ [an-Nisa: 142].

And He says concerning the people of the covenant: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 62].

So He, glorified and exalted, informs that these deceivers are themselves deceived, and they do not perceive that Allah deceives whoever deceives Him, and that He suffices the one who is deceived against the evil of the one who deceived him.

Al-mukhada'ah (deception) is trickery and evasion by displaying good while concealing its opposite, in order to achieve the deceiver's aim. This agrees with the derivation of the word in the language. They say: "a khayda' path," when it deviates from the intended direction, so that one does not notice it or become aware of it. Mirage is called al-sarab al-khaydaʿ, because it deceives whoever sees it. A dabb khadaʿ (a lizard that is evasive) means one who dodges. As they said: "more cunning than the dabb." From this comes: "War is deception" (khud'ah), and a khadi'ah market, meaning one that fluctuates. Its root meaning is concealment and covering. From it the storeroom is called makhda' (a closet).

Since the one who says "I believe" displays this word without intending its true, binding reality which is required by the Sharia, but intends only its ruling and its fruit, he is a deceiver. Likewise, one who uses the words "I sold," "I bought," "I divorced," "I married," "I khula'd (divorced by compensation)," "I rented out," "I gave to drink," and "I made a bequest," without intending their legal realities which the Sharia requires, but intends other matters than what they were prescribed for, or the opposite of what they were prescribed for, is a deceiver. The former is a deceiver regarding the foundation of faith, and this one is a deceiver regarding his actions and his legal obligations.

Our shaykh said: "This is a kind of hypocrisy regarding the signs and limits of Allah, Exalted is He, just as the former is hypocrisy regarding the foundation of religion."

This is supported by what Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man came to him and said: "My uncle divorced his wife three times. Can a man make her lawful to him?" He said: "Whoever deceives Allah, He deceives him."

And from Anas ibn Malik: he was asked about al-'ina, meaning the sale of hariri (a particular trick sale). He said: "Indeed Allah does not deceive. This is what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden."

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Hafiz, known as Mutayn, narrated it in his book on sales.

And from Ibn Abbas: he was asked about al-'ina, meaning the sale of hariri, and he said: "Indeed Allah is not deceived. This is among what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden." Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad al-Nakhshabi narrated it.

So the Companions named those who displayed a contract of sale while intending by it riba (usury) as deceiving Allah. They are the ones referred to in this matter and relied upon in understanding the Qur'an. It has already been mentioned from Uthman and Abdullah ibn Umar, and others, that they said concerning a woman divorced three times: "Only a marriage of desire makes her lawful, not a marriage of deceit (dilsah)."

The lexicographers said: al-mudalasah means al-mukhada'ah (deception).

Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said concerning those who employ stratagems (hiyal, legal tricks): "They deceive Allah as they deceive children. If they had performed the matter openly, it would have been easier for me."

Shurayk ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi said in his book on stratagems: "It is the book of deception (al-mukhada'ah)."

Likewise, the covenant-holders, when they showed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, that they wanted peace, while they intended by that to scheme against him without his perceiving it. They displayed safety to him while concealing its opposite. Just as the muhallil (one who makes a divorced woman lawful to her former husband) and the murabi (one who engages in riba) display the marriage and sale they intend, while the aim of the former is divorce after he has had intercourse with the woman, and the aim of the latter is what the two agreed upon before displaying the contract, namely selling a thousand (due at once) for twelve hundred payable at a term. Thus, contradicting what the contract indicates, whether by the Sharia or by custom, is deception.

He said: The summary of this is that deceiving Allah, Exalted is He, is forbidden, and stratagems are deception of Allah.

Explanation of the first: Allah, Exalted is He, censured the hypocrites for deception, and informed that He deceives them. His deceiving the servant is a punishment that entails his committing what is forbidden.

Explanation of the second: Ibn Abbas, Anas, and others among the Companions and the Successors issued legal rulings that tahlil (the intermediary marriage) and similar stratagems are deception of Allah, Exalted is He, and they are the most knowledgeable of the Book of Allah, Exalted is He.

Third: deception is displaying some good while concealing its opposite, as has preceded.

Fourth: when the hypocrite displayed Islam while his intention was other than it, he was called a deceiver of Allah, Exalted is He. Likewise the one who engages in riba. Indeed hypocrisy and riba are of one category. So if this one displayed a statement which he does not believe in nor intend what it implies, and this one displayed an action which he does not believe in nor intend what it was prescribed for, both are deceivers. The one who employs a stratagem does not go outside one of the two categories: either displaying an action for other than its intended purpose for which it was legislated, or displaying a statement for other than its intended purpose for which it was legislated. If he shares with them the meaning for which they were named deceivers, it is necessary that he share with them the name of deception. It is known that deception is a name for all stratagems, not only for this particular hypocrisy.

(Benefit)

The word khida' (deception) is divided into praiseworthy and blameworthy. If it is with right, it is praiseworthy; if it is with falsehood, it is blameworthy.

From the praiseworthy type is his, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, saying: "War is deception." And his saying in the hadith narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others: "Every lie is recorded against the son of Adam, except three matters: a man who lies to his wife to please her, a man who lies between two people to reconcile them, and a man who lies in the deception of war."

From the blameworthy type is his saying in the hadith of Iyad ibn Jammar, narrated by Muslim in his Sahih: "The people of the Fire are five, and he mentioned a man who does not rise in the morning or evening except that he deceives you regarding your family and your wealth."

And the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿They try to deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves, and they do not perceive﴾ [al-Baqarah: 9].

And the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 62].

From the praiseworthy type: the deception of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Abu Rafi', the enemies of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, until they were killed, and the killing of Khalid ibn Sufyan al-Hudhali.

Among the best of these: the deception of Mu'bid ibn Abi Ma'bad al-Khuza'i against Abu Sufyan and the army of the polytheists when they resolved to return in order to wipe out the Muslims, and he turned them back immediately.

Among that: the deception of Na'im ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i against the Jews of Banu Qurayzah and against the Quraysh disbelievers and the confederates, until he sowed discord among them, and it was the cause of their dispersal and their return. Similar examples are many.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 10:

And he said: ﴿So do not be soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾, and he said: ﴿And that those who were given the Scripture may not doubt, and that the believers may increase in faith, and that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾.

The sickness of the heart is its departure from its health and balance. Its health is that it should know the truth and love it, preferring it over other things. Its sickness is either by doubt about it, or by preferring other things over it.

So the sickness of the hypocrites is a sickness of doubt and suspicion, and the sickness of the sinners is misguidance (ghayy) and desire.

Allah, glorified is He, has called each of them a sickness.

Ibn al-Anbari said: The origin of "marad" (sickness) in the language is corruption. "Marida fulan": his body became corrupted and his condition changed. And "maridat bi-l-marad": it changed and became corrupted. Layla al-Akhiliyya said:

*When al-Hajjaj descends upon a sickly land,*
*It follows the furthest of its ailments and cures it.*

Another said:

*Do you not see that the earth has become sick*
*Due to the loss of al-Husayn, and the lands have shuddered?*

The root meaning of marad revolves around four things: corruption, weakness, deficiency, and darkness. From it comes "marida al-rajul fi al-amr" when a man became weak in a matter. And "ayn mariḍat al-nazar" means an eye whose gaze is languid and weak. And "rih mariḍa" when its blowing is gentle, as he said:

*The winds have gone to your traces, gentle*

That is, soft and weak, so that its trace is not erased.

Ibn al-A'rabi said: The origin of marad is deficiency. From it: "badan marid," meaning one whose strength is deficient; "qalb marid," meaning one whose religion is deficient; and "marada fi hajati," when its movement is diminished.

Al-Azhari, from al-Mundhiri, from some of his companions, said: Marad is the darkening of nature and its disturbance after its clarity.

He said: Marad is darkness, and he recited:

*A night became sick from every side,*
*No sun or moon shines in it.*

This is its origin in the language.

Then doubt, ignorance, bewilderment, misguidance, the desire for error, and the craving for immorality in the heart all return to these four matters. The servant then engages in the causes of sickness until he becomes ill, so Allah punishes him with an increase in sickness, because he preferred its causes and pursued them.

(Section)

Sickness is of two kinds: sickness of the hearts and sickness of the bodies, and both are mentioned in the Qur'an.

Sickness of the hearts is of two kinds: sickness of doubt and suspicion, and sickness of desire and error, and both are in the Qur'an. Allah, exalted is He, said regarding the sickness of doubt: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾. And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers may say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?"﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 31]. And Allah, exalted is He, said concerning those who were called to judgment by the Qur'an and the Sunnah and refused and turned away: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, behold, a party of them turn away. But if the right were theirs, they would come to him in compliance. Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Nur: 48-49]. This is the sickness of doubts and suspicions.

As for the sickness of desires, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32]

﴿If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease should covet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 32]. This is the sickness of the desire for fornication, and Allah knows best.

[Section: Sins make the hearts sick]

Among its punishments is that they divert the heart from its health and uprightness to its sickness and deviation, so it remains sick and ailing, not benefiting from the nourishments by which its life and well-being are sustained. The effect of sins on hearts is like the effect of diseases on bodies; indeed, sins are the diseases of the hearts and their illness, and there is no cure for them except abandoning them.

The travellers toward Allah have agreed that hearts are not given their desire until they reach their Lord, and they do not reach their Lord until they are sound and healthy, and they are not sound and healthy until their illness is reversed, becoming the very cure for it, and this is achieved only by opposing their desire. Its desire is its sickness, and its cure is opposing it. If the sickness becomes firmly established, it kills or nearly does.

Just as whoever restrains his soul from desire, Paradise will be his abode, so likewise his heart in this world will be in an immediate paradise, whose bliss does not resemble the bliss of its people at all. Rather, the difference between the two blisses is like the difference between the bliss of this world and the Hereafter, and this is a matter that no one believes except one whose heart has experienced both.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verses 11–13:

When you reflect upon the Qur'an, ponder over it, and give it full attention, you will discover in it the secrets of debate, the establishment of sound proofs, the refutation of corrupt doubts, and the mention of counter-argument (naqd), distinction (farq), opposition (mu'aradah), and denial (man'), in a manner that satisfies and suffices for whoever Allah has granted insight and blessed with understanding of His Book. Among these is His saying, Exalted is He:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Do not cause corruption on the earth," they say, "We are only reformers." Unquestionably, it is they who are the corrupters, but they do not perceive.﴾

This is a debate that took place between the believers and the hypocrites. The believers said to them, ﴿Do not cause corruption on the earth,﴾ and the hypocrites replied with their words, ﴿We are only reformers.﴾ It is as if the debate ended between the two groups, and the hypocrites rejected what the people of faith had claimed against them, namely that they were corrupters, and that what they were accused of was only reform, not corruption. Then the Mighty, the Wise, judged between the two parties by recording four rulings against the hypocrites:

First: their denial (of the claim).

Second: the report that they are corrupters.

Third: restricting corruption to them, by His saying, ﴿It is they who are the corrupters.﴾

Fourth: describing them with the utmost ignorance, namely that they have absolutely no awareness of being corrupters.

Observe how He negated awareness from them in this place, then negated knowledge in His saying, ﴿Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ Then He said, ﴿Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know.﴾ Thus He negated their knowledge of their own foolishness and their awareness of their corruption. This is the most emphatic form of blame and of attributing ignorance: that a person is a corrupter while having no awareness at all of his corruption, even though the effect of his corruption is well known outside and visible to the servants of Allah, yet he does not perceive it. This indicates that corruption has become firmly established in his faculties and his means of knowing. Likewise, being foolish: foolishness is the utmost ignorance, and it is composed of the lack of knowledge of what sustains one's livelihood and one's afterlife, together with a will that works against it. When a person is in this condition and does not know his own state, he is among the most wretched of mankind. So the negation of knowledge from him, given the foolishness he is in, includes the affirmation of his ignorance, and the negation of awareness from him, given the corruption that proceeds from him, includes the corruption of the instruments of his perception. Thus the two verses contain a double ruling against them: ignorance, and corruption of the faculties of perception, to the extent that they regard corruption as reform and evil as good.

The second debate with them was similar. The believers said to them, ﴿Believe as the people have believed,﴾ and the hypocrites answered with their words, ﴿Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ The structure of the debate from both sides is this: the believers called them to the faith held by the wise, who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and that the sensible person is obliged to join what the wise and sincere advisers of their own souls have joined, especially when its proofs are established and its evidences are sound. The hypocrites answered with something whose meaning is that we are only obliged to agree with the wise, and that we are not obliged to agree with the foolish, who lack the intellect by which they distinguish between what benefits and what harms. Allah, Exalted is He, rejected their claim and ruled in favor of the believers, and He recorded against the hypocrites four kinds of ruling:

First: calling them foolish.

Second: restricting foolishness to them.

Third: negating knowledge from them.

Fourth: denying their claim, contained in their answer, that they are free from foolishness.

First: their denial (of the claim).

Second: the report that they are corrupters.

Third: restricting corruption to them, by His saying, ﴿It is they who are the corrupters.﴾

Fourth: describing them with the utmost ignorance, namely that they have absolutely no awareness of being corrupters.

Observe how He negated awareness from them in this place, then negated knowledge in His saying, ﴿Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ Then He said, ﴿Unquestionably, it is they who are the foolish, but they do not know.﴾ Thus He negated their knowledge of their own foolishness and their awareness of their corruption. This is the most emphatic form of blame and of attributing ignorance: that a person is a corrupter while having no awareness at all of his corruption, even though the effect of his corruption is well known outside and visible to the servants of Allah, yet he does not perceive it. This indicates that corruption has become firmly established in his faculties and his means of knowing. Likewise, being foolish: foolishness is the utmost ignorance, and it is composed of the lack of knowledge of what sustains one's livelihood and one's afterlife, together with a will that works against it. When a person is in this condition and does not know his own state, he is among the most wretched of mankind. So the negation of knowledge from him, given the foolishness he is in, includes the affirmation of his ignorance, and the negation of awareness from him, given the corruption that proceeds from him, includes the corruption of the instruments of his perception. Thus the two verses contain a double ruling against them: ignorance, and corruption of the faculties of perception, to the extent that they regard corruption as reform and evil as good.

The second debate with them was similar. The believers said to them, ﴿Believe as the people have believed,﴾ and the hypocrites answered with their words, ﴿Shall we believe as the foolish have believed?﴾ The structure of the debate from both sides is this: the believers called them to the faith held by the wise, who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and that the sensible person is obliged to join what the wise and sincere advisers of their own souls have joined, especially when its proofs are established and its evidences are sound. The hypocrites answered with something whose meaning is that we are only obliged to agree with the wise, and that we are not obliged to agree with the foolish, who lack the intellect by which they distinguish between what benefits and what harms. Allah, Exalted is He, rejected their claim and ruled in favor of the believers, and He recorded against the hypocrites four kinds of ruling:

First: calling them foolish.

Second: restricting foolishness to them.

Third: negating knowledge from them.

Fourth: denying their claim, contained in their answer, that they are free from foolishness.

He, glorified and exalted is He, likened His enemies, the hypocrites, to people who kindled a fire so that it would light up for them and they could benefit from it. When the fire illuminated for them, and in its light they saw what would benefit them and what would harm them, and they saw the path after having been bewildered and lost, they were like a group of travelers who had strayed from the road and so kindled a fire to light the way for them. When it illuminated for them and they saw and understood, that fire went out, and they remained in darkness, unable to see. The three doors of guidance were closed to them. Guidance enters the servant through three doors: what he hears with his ear, what he sees with his eye, and what he comprehends with his heart. These people had the doors of guidance closed to them, so their hearts hear nothing, do not see it, and do not comprehend what would benefit them.

It has been said: When they did not benefit from their hearing, their sight, and their hearts, they were placed in the station of one who has no hearing, no sight, and no intellect. The two explanations are mutually connected. He said concerning their description: ﴿So they will not return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18], because they had seen in the light of the fire and had perceived guidance, and when it went out from them, they did not return to what they had seen and perceived. He, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah has taken away their light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17], and He did not say: "Their light went away." In this there is a wondrous secret, namely the cutting off of that special companionship (ma'iyyah) which belongs to the believers from Allah, the Exalted. Indeed, Allah the Exalted is with the believers, and indeed Allah is with the patient, and ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾ [al-Nahl: 128]. So Allah's taking away of that light is the severing of His special companionship, which belongs to the believers, which He reserved for His friends. He cut it off between Himself and the hypocrites, so after the going away of their light, He is not with them, nor are they with Him. Therefore they have no share in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us﴾ [al-Tawbah: 40], nor in: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 62].

Reflect on His saying: ﴿it illuminated what was around him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17]: how He made its light external to him, separate from him. Had its light connected with him and mixed with him, it would not have gone away. But it was a light of proximity, not of union and intermingling. The light was accidental and the darkness was原 essential, so the light returned to its source, and the darkness remained in its source. Each of them returned to its fitting origin. This is a clear proof from Allah and a profound wisdom by which He made Himself known to the people of understanding among His servants.

Reflect also on His saying: ﴿Allah has taken away their light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17], and He did not say "their fire," so that it would correspond to the beginning of the verse. Fire contains both brightness and burning. He took away what it contained of brightness, which is light, and left them what it contained of burning, which is the fiery nature.

Reflect on how He said ﴿their light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17] and did not say "their illumination," despite His saying: ﴿when it illuminated what was around him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17]. This is because illumination (daw') is an increase in light (nur). Had it been said, "Allah took away their illumination," it would have implied the taking away of the increase only, not the origin. Since light is the origin of illumination, taking it away is taking away the thing together with its increase. Moreover, it is more emphatic in negating them and in showing that they are of the people of darkness who have no light. Also, Allah the Exalted named His Book "light," and His Messenger (ﷺ) "light," and His religion "light," and His guidance "light," and among His names is "the Light," and prayer is "light." So His taking away their light, glorified is He, is a taking away of all of this.

Reflect on the correspondence of this parable with what preceded it, His saying: ﴿These are the ones who have bought error in exchange for guidance, so their trade has not profited, nor were they guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16]. How it corresponds to this losing trade, which included obtaining error and being pleased with it, giving up guidance in exchange for it, and obtaining the darknesses, which are error and being pleased with it, in place of the light, which is guidance. So they gave up guidance and light and took in exchange darkness and error. How wretched is such a trade, how ruinous, and how severe is the loss in such a bargain!

Reflect on how Allah said: ﴿Allah has taken away their light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17], using the singular, then said: ﴿and left them in darkness, unable to see﴾, using the plural. This is because the truth is one: it is the straight path of Allah, and no path leads to Him other than it, which is worshipping Him alone, without partner, by what He has legislated through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), not by desires and innovations (bid'ah) and the ways of those who deviate from what Allah sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth. Contrary to this are the ways of falsehood, which are many and branching. For this reason He, glorified is He, mentions the truth in the singular and gathers falsehood in the plural, as in His saying: ﴿Allah is the ally of those who believe; He brings them out from the darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve, their allies are the taghut; they take them out from the light into the darknesses. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257].

He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And that this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This He has instructed you that you may fear Him﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

Thus He gathered the ways of falsehood and made His way, the truth, singular. This is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿By it Allah guides those who pursue His pleasure to the ways of peace﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 16]. Those are the ways of His good pleasure, which are gathered into His one way and His straight path, for all the ways of His pleasure return to one path and one way, which is His way, and there is no access to Him except through it. It is authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he drew a straight line and said: "This is the path of Allah." Then he drew lines to its right and to its left and said: "These are paths, upon each path is a shaytan calling to it." Then he recited His saying: ﴿And that this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way. This He has instructed you that you may fear Him﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

It has been said that this is a parable for the hypocrites and the fire of strife (fitnah) that they kindle among the people of Islam. It would be in the same position as His saying: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64]. His saying ﴿Allah has taken away their light﴾ would correspond to His saying ﴿Allah extinguishes it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64]. Their frustration and the nullification of what they sought would be His leaving them in the darknesses of bewilderment, not guided to escape what they have fallen into, and not seeing a way. Rather, they are deaf, dumb, and blind.

This interpretation, although it is true, is questionable as to whether it is intended by the verse, for the context was directed toward something else. His saying ﴿when it illuminated what was around him﴾ rejects it, since the hearth of the fire of war never illuminates what is around it at all. His saying ﴿Allah has taken away their light﴾ also rejects it, since the hearth of the fire of war has no light. His saying ﴿and left them in darkness, unable to see﴾ rejects it too.

This indicates that they moved from the light of knowledge and insight into the darkness of doubt and disbelief. Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "It is the hypocrite who saw, then became blind; who knew, then denied." For this reason He said: ﴿So they will not return﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18], meaning: they will not return to the light which they left.

Concerning the disbelievers He said: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they will not return﴾. Thus He negated understanding from the disbelievers, since they were not of the people of insight and faith, and He negated return from the hypocrites, because they believed and then disbelieved, so they did not return to faith.
