He means by these two: His saying: ﴿As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a light account, and will return to his family joyful (masrur)﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 7–9], and the second place: His saying: ﴿And He will give them radiance and joy (surur)﴾ [al-Insan: 11].

It is said: Surur also occurs regarding the affairs of this world in one place, in a blameworthy sense, such as His saying: ﴿But as for he who is given his record behind his back, he will call for destruction, and will enter the Blaze. Indeed, he was among his people joyful (masrur)﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 10–13].

So you have seen that each of farah and surur occurs in the Qur'an in relation to the conditions of this world and the conditions of the Hereafter. Therefore the preference he mentioned does not appear.

Indeed, it may be said that farah is preferred, because the Lord, blessed and exalted, is described by it, and His name is applied to Him, but surur is not. This shows that its meaning is more complete than the meaning of surur. And Allah commanded it in His saying: ﴿Let them rejoice in that﴾ [Yunus: 58], and praised the blessed for it in His saying: ﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ [Al 'Imran: 170].

As for His saying: ﴿And He will give them radiance and joy﴾ [al-Insan: 11] and His saying: ﴿And he will return to his family joyful﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 9], He turned to the word surur because of the agreement of the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayy). Had he titled the chapter "the chapter of farah," it would have matched the verse he cited more precisely. But the matter here is minor; the intended point lies beyond that.

(Section)

"Al-azwaj" (the spouses) is the plural of zawj. A wife is a zawj (spouse) of a man, and he is her zawj. This is the most eloquent usage, and it is the dialect of Quraysh, and the Qur'an was revealed in it, as in His saying: ﴿Dwell, you and your spouse (zawjuka), in the Garden﴾ [2:35]. Some Arabs say "zawjah" (wife), but this is rare, and they hardly ever say it.

As for "al-mutahharah" (purified): if it is used as an adjective for a singular noun, it is applied as an adjective to a plural of multitude, treating it as a group, as in His saying: ﴿And goodly dwellings (masakin tayyibah)﴾, and their saying: "quwan zahirah" (manifest powers), and similar examples.

And "al-Mutahharah" (the purified ones) are those purified from menstruation, urine, postnatal bleeding, excrement, mucus, spittle, and every filth, and from every harm that comes from the women of this world. Her inner self is also purified from bad character and blameworthy qualities, her tongue is purified from obscenity and foul speech, her gaze is purified from aspiring to anyone other than her husband, and her garments are purified from any dirt or grime.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Shu'bah narrated to us from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding ﴿wa lahum fiha azwajun mutahharah﴾ ("and for them therein are purified spouses"), that they are purified "from the filth" and said: "from menstruation, excrement, phlegm, and spittle."

Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn Abbas said: "Mutahharah: they do not menstruate, do not defecate, and are not soiled."

Ibn Abbas also said: "Purified from filth and harm: they do not urinate, do not defecate, do not emit madhy, do not emit semen, do not menstruate, do not spit, do not expectorate phlegm, and do not give birth."

Qatadah said: "Purified from sin and harm; God, glorified is He, has purified them from every urine, excrement, filth, and sin."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "Al-Mutahharah: the one who does not menstruate. The women of this world are not purified. Do you not see that they bleed and abandon prayer and fasting?"

He said: "Hawwa' was created in this way too, until she disobeyed. When she disobeyed, God said to her: 'I created you, and I will make you bleed as this tree was made to bleed.'"

(A wondrous benefit)

The word of God, exalted is He: ﴿Whenever they are provided with fruit therefrom as provision, they say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in resemblance; and for them therein are purified spouses, and they therein will abide eternally﴾ [2:25].

The noun from (hadha) is the letter dhal alone, without the alif, according to the more correct of the two opinions. The evidence is that the alif drops in the dual and in the feminine forms. The dhal was specially assigned to this noun because it is articulated from the tip of the tongue. The thing indicated is indefinite, so the speaker points toward it with his utterance or his hand, and at the same time with his tongue, since the limbs serve the heart. When the heart turns to something with a perceived attention, the limbs turn toward it with a sensed motion. The main means of pointing in situations of address is the tongue, and it is not possible to indicate with a letter except one whose point of articulation is the uvula-tip of the tongue (*'udhbat al-lisan*), which is the instrument of pointing, rather than any other part of it. As for the dhal or the ta', the ta' is voiceless and soft (*mahmusah rakhwah*). Of the letters, the voiced or hard ones are more suitable than it for clarity. The dhal is voiced, so it was assigned to the indication of the masculine, and the ta' was assigned to the indication of the feminine, to make a distinction. The ta' was more appropriate for it because of its voicelessness and the weakness of the feminine, and because the feminine marker has already been established in other contexts.

Then they clarified the vowel of the dhal with an alif, as they did with the nun in *ana* ("I"). Sometimes they made the feminine share the masculine form with the dhal and were content with a kasrah (vowel) to distinguish them. Sometimes they were content with the bare letter ta' to distinguish them. Sometimes they combined the letter ta' with the kasrah, out of eagerness for clarity. As for the feminine absent (third person) form, the letter ta' with the kasrah is necessary, because it needs more clarification, since visual perception indicates the referent to the mind. So you say *tilka* ("that, fem."). Sometimes they added the lam for emphasis, as they added it to the masculine absent form (*dhalika*), except that in the feminine they made it sukun (unvowelled), so that kasrahs would not follow one another with the ta', which is heavy for them. The lam was more appropriate for this position when they wanted to point to what is distant. The letters increased as the distance of this pointing increased, and they reduced them when the distance decreased. This is because the lam is found in their speech as emphasis, and this position is a position of emphasis. It is also found with the meaning of attribution (*al-idafah*) to a thing, and this position resembles that, because when you gesture toward an absent thing with the indefinite noun, you are indicating to someone addressed, who attends to you so that he may look at what you point to, either with the eye or with the heart. Likewise you bring the kaf of address, as if you were saying to him: "To you I speak, and to you I signal with this noun." So in the lam there is a share of this meaning, as there is in the kaf. Just as the kaf is not here a pronoun noun, the lam is not a prepositional particle (*harf jarr*). Each of them carries only a part of the meaning, not all of it. For this reason they removed from the place the sense of nouniness and kept in it the sense of address. The lam is likewise brought in for a part of the meaning for which it was devised in the matter of attribution.

As for the entry of the particle of alerting (*ha' al-tanbih*), it is because the addressee needs to be alerted to the noun by which the speaker points to him, since pointing has contextual indicators that one must look at. The speaker is as if commanding him to turn attention to the thing pointed at, or alerting him. For this reason this position is specially marked by alerting. They rarely use it with the indefinite absent noun, because the kaf of address suffices in its place, while the addressee is commanded to turn his glance to the present indefinite thing. So alerting at the beginning of the utterance is more appropriate for this position, because it stands in the place of the command that heads the speech.

In my view, the particle of alerting stands in the place of the particle of vocative (*harf al-nida'*). The other particles of meaning (*harf al-ma'ani*) may not have their meanings operate upon circumstantial accusatives (*al-hal*) or adverbs of time and place (*al-zarf*), just as the meaning of interrogation and negation does not operate in *hal* and *ma* in that respect. We know of no particle whose meaning operates upon a circumstantial accusative or an adverb except *kana* and its sisters, which are verbs. So leave aside what they have fumbled over in questions of the circumstantial accusative in this matter, such as their saying *hadha qa'iman Zayd* and *qa'iman hadha Zayd*. Of these, only placing the circumstantial accusative after the noun *dha* is valid, because the operator in it is the meaning of pointing, not the meaning of alerting, and both are meanings of a conceptual kind.

If it is said: Why is it permissible for the meaning of pointing to operate in it and not the meaning of alerting, when both are conceptual?

It is answered: The meaning of pointing is indicated by contextual evidences: gesturing with the glance, the utterance coming from the tip of the tongue, and the speaker's bearing. That indication takes the place of an explicit statement of the pointing word, because what indicates a meaning is either a word, or a gesture, or a glance. So pointing has taken the course of the word, and so it may operate in what the word operates upon, even if its strength does not equal the word's in all rules of operation.

More correct than this is to say that the meaning of pointing is not itself the operator, since the noun *hadha* is not derived from *ashara yushiru* (to point). If the demonstrative nouns could operate in this way, then the pronominal markers would also operate, since they too are a gesture and a pointing toward something mentioned. Rather, the operator is an implied verb whose estimate is *unẓur* (look) and *abşir* (behold), because the context indicates it through the orientation and the utterance. They have said: *min al-dari maftuhan babuha* ("from the house, its door being open"), and so they made the meaning of "look" and "behold" operate upon the circumstantial accusative, and the orientation of the speaker toward it with his face indicated it. Likewise is ﴿wa hadha ba'li shaykhan﴾ ("and this is my husband, an old man") [11:72], and it is strong in indication because the utterance coincides with the orientation. Once this is established, there is no way to place the circumstantial accusative before the operator, because the conceptual operator is hidden, and what indicates it is the verbal evidence, or the orientation, or what resembles them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verses 26–27:

﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ [The verse continues.]

This is the answer to an objection that the disbelievers raised against the Qur'an. They said: "The Lord is greater than to mention flies, spiders and similar lowly creatures. If what Muhammad brought were the speech of Allah, it would not mention such lowly creatures." So Allah the Exalted answered them by saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ For the coining of examples using a mosquito or what is above it, when it serves to establish the truth and clarify it, and to nullify falsehood and refute it, is among the finest of things, and what is fine is not something to be ashamed of. This is the answer to the objection. Then it is as if an objector objected to this answer, or asked for its wisdom, so Allah the Exalted informed of the wisdom He has in coining those examples, which is to lead astray whom He wills and to guide whom He wills. Then it is as if a questioner asked about the wisdom of misguidance for those whom He misguides by it, so Allah the Exalted informed of His wisdom and justice, and that He misguides by it only the defiantly disobedient: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on earth.﴾ So these ugly deeds that they committed were the cause of His misguiding them and blinding them from guidance.

Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then give you life again, then to Him you will be returned.﴾ This is a decisive argument that belief in Allah the Exalted is a matter established in natural disposition (fitrah) and in reason, and that there is no excuse for anyone in disbelieving in Him whatsoever.

He mentioned four matters, three of which are witnessed in this world, and the fourth is awaited, promised by the promise of truth:

The first: that they were dead, with no spirits in them, but rather drops of semen, clots and lumps of flesh, dead with no life in them.

The second: that He gave them life after this death.

The third: that He will cause them to die after this life.

The fourth: that He will give them life after this death, and they will return to Him. So what is the matter with the intelligent person who witnesses the three earlier stages and denies the fourth? Is the fourth anything other than a stage of the stages of creation? The One who gave you life after you were dead, then caused you to die after He had given you life, what is there that would make Him unable to give you life after He causes you to die? And is your denial of that anything but pure disbelief in Allah the Exalted? How can it occur from you after you have witnessed [these things]? Thus within this verse is the proof of the existence of the Creator, His attributes and His acts, and of the Return (ma'ad).

(Section)

As for the second principle, namely that wickedness, arrogance and lying necessitate misguidance, it is also abundant in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿He misleads by it many and guides by it many, and He misleads by it only the defiantly disobedient, who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on earth. Those are the losers.﴾

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah misleads the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you are divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites, when Allah has overturned them for what they earned?﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight, as they did not believe in it the first time.﴾

So He informed that He punished them for their failure to believe when it came to them and they recognized it, and turned away from it, by turning their hearts and sights and placing a barrier between them and faith. As He said: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart.﴾ So He commanded them to respond to Him and to His Messenger when he calls them to what contains their life, then warned them against lagging behind and delaying in responding, which would be the cause of Allah intervening between them and their hearts. He said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ And He said: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts.﴾ So He informed, glorified is He, that their earning covered their hearts and placed a barrier between them and faith in His signs, so they said, "These are the legends of the ancients." And He, exalted is He, said about the hypocrites: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves.﴾ So He requited their forgetting of Him by making them forget them, so He did not remember them with guidance and mercy. He informed that He caused them to forget their own selves, so they did not seek their perfection through beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds, and these two are guidance and the religion of truth. So He caused them to forget the seeking of that, its love, its knowledge and eagerness for it, as a punishment for their forgetting of Him. And He, exalted is He, said concerning them: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed, and who followed their desires; and those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ So He combined for them following desire and the misguidance which is its fruit and consequence, just as He combined for the guided ones piety and guidance.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verses 26–27:

﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ [The verse continues.]

This is the answer to an objection that the disbelievers raised against the Qur'an. They said: "The Lord is greater than to mention flies, spiders and similar lowly creatures. If what Muhammad brought were the speech of Allah, it would not mention such lowly creatures." So Allah the Exalted answered them by saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it.﴾ For the coining of examples using a mosquito or what is above it, when it serves to establish the truth and clarify it, and to nullify falsehood and refute it, is among the finest of things, and what is fine is not something to be ashamed of. This is the answer to the objection. Then it is as if an objector objected to this answer, or asked for its wisdom, so Allah the Exalted informed of the wisdom He has in coining those examples, which is to lead astray whom He wills and to guide whom He wills. Then it is as if a questioner asked about the wisdom of misguidance for those whom He misguides by it, so Allah the Exalted informed of His wisdom and justice, and that He misguides by it only the defiantly disobedient: ﴿Those who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on earth.﴾ So these ugly deeds that they committed were the cause of His misguiding them and blinding them from guidance.

Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then give you life again, then to Him you will be returned.﴾ This is a decisive argument that belief in Allah the Exalted is a matter established in natural disposition (fitrah) and in reason, and that there is no excuse for anyone in disbelieving in Him whatsoever.

He mentioned four matters, three of which are witnessed in this world, and the fourth is awaited, promised by the promise of truth:

The first: that they were dead, with no spirits in them, but rather drops of semen, clots and lumps of flesh, dead with no life in them.

The second: that He gave them life after this death.

The third: that He will cause them to die after this life.

The fourth: that He will give them life after this death, and they will return to Him. So what is the matter with the intelligent person who witnesses the three earlier stages and denies the fourth? Is the fourth anything other than a stage of the stages of creation? The One who gave you life after you were dead, then caused you to die after He had given you life, what is there that would make Him unable to give you life after He causes you to die? And is your denial of that anything but pure disbelief in Allah the Exalted? How can it occur from you after you have witnessed [these things]? Thus within this verse is the proof of the existence of the Creator, His attributes and His acts, and of the Return (ma'ad).

(Section)

As for the second principle, namely that wickedness, arrogance and lying necessitate misguidance, it is also abundant in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿He misleads by it many and guides by it many, and He misleads by it only the defiantly disobedient, who break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, and sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on earth. Those are the losers.﴾

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah misleads the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills.﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you are divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites, when Allah has overturned them for what they earned?﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are wrapped." Rather, Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so little is it that they believe.﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight, as they did not believe in it the first time.﴾

So He informed that He punished them for their failure to believe when it came to them and they recognized it, and turned away from it, by turning their hearts and sights and placing a barrier between them and faith. As He said: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart.﴾ So He commanded them to respond to Him and to His Messenger when he calls them to what contains their life, then warned them against lagging behind and delaying in responding, which would be the cause of Allah intervening between them and their hearts. He said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾ And He said: ﴿No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts.﴾ So He informed, glorified is He, that their earning covered their hearts and placed a barrier between them and faith in His signs, so they said, "These are the legends of the ancients." And He, exalted is He, said about the hypocrites: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves.﴾ So He requited their forgetting of Him by making them forget them, so He did not remember them with guidance and mercy. He informed that He caused them to forget their own selves, so they did not seek their perfection through beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds, and these two are guidance and the religion of truth. So He caused them to forget the seeking of that, its love, its knowledge and eagerness for it, as a punishment for their forgetting of Him. And He, exalted is He, said concerning them: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed, and who followed their desires; and those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ So He combined for them following desire and the misguidance which is its fruit and consequence, just as He combined for the guided ones piety and guidance.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 28:

They were dead, and they were sperm-drops in the loins of their fathers and in the wombs of their mothers; then He gave them life after that, then He causes them to die, then He will bring them back to life on the Day of Resurrection (al-nushur). This does not include the taking of their souls before the Day of Resurrection, for otherwise there would be three deaths. The swooning (sa'q) of the souls at the blast of the Trumpet (al-sur) does not necessarily entail their death. In the authentic hadith, it is related that "people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness, and behold, Musa is holding onto a pillar of the Throne, and I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was recompensed with a swoon for the swoon at Mount Sinai (al-Tur)."

This is a swooning at the station of the Resurrection, when Allah, exalted is He, comes to judge between the creatures, and the earth shines with His light. Then all creatures swoon, as He, the Exalted, says: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless﴾. And had this swooning been a death, there would have been another death.

(Fa'ida)

People have differed over whether the heaven is nobler than the earth or the earth is nobler than the heaven. The majority hold the former view.

Those who prefer the earth argue as follows. God Most High created His prophets, messengers and believing servants from it. It is their dwelling place and the place where they live and die. When God, glorified and exalted is He, willed to display Adam to the angels, He said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a vicegerent﴾, and so He showed His favour over them through his knowledge and his being made a successor on the earth. Also, God, glorified and exalted is He, endowed the earth by making it the place of His blessings, both general and specific, when He said: ﴿And He placed firmly on it mountains from above it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance﴾.

The Levant (al-Sham) is described as blessed in six verses, and some of them describe it as sacred: in it is the "blessed land" and the "holy land," and the "sacred valley," and in it is His Sacred House, the rites of the Hajj, the mosques which are His houses, and the mountain (al-Tur) upon which He spoke to His interlocutor (Kalim) and confidant (Najiy). He also swears by the earth, in general and specific terms, more than He swears by the heaven: He swore by the mount (al-Tur), the secure city (al-Balad al-Amin), the fig and the olive. And when He swore by the heaven, He swore by the earth along with it. Also, He, glorified is He, created it before creating the heaven, as indicated by the surah of (Ha Mim al-Sajda). Also, it is the descent place of His revelation, the repository of His books and messengers, and the place of the deeds most beloved to Him, which are jihad, charity, enjoining good and forbidding evil, enraging His enemies and supporting His allies; none of this exists in the heaven. Also, its inhabitants among the messengers, prophets and the pious are better than the inhabitants of the heaven, the angels, as is the position of the People of the Sunna; so their dwelling is nobler than the dwelling of the angels. Also, what He placed in it of benefits, rivers, fruits, knowledge, sustenance, animals and plants is from their blessings, and He placed nothing like it in the heaven. Also, God, glorified is He, said: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who have certainty﴾, then He said: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised﴾. So He made the earth the place of His signs and the heaven the place of His provision. Even if He had given the earth nothing but His House and the House of the Seal of His prophets and messengers, alive and dead, that would suffice. Also, God made the earth a resting place, a spread, a cradle, a bed, a receptacle (kifat), and a material for its dwellers for their clothing, food, drink, mounts and all their implements, especially when it brings forth its blessing, is adorned and grows every lovely pair.

Those who prefer the heaven over the earth say: it suffices for its excellence that the Lord of the worlds, glorified is He, is in it; that His Throne and His Footstool are in it; that the Supreme Companion (al-Rafiq al-A'la), upon whom God bestowed favour, is in it; that the abode of His honour is in it; that it is the resting place of His prophets, messengers and believing servants on the Day of Assembly; and that it is purified and cleared of every evil, wickedness and filth that occurs on the earth. For this reason its gates are not opened to evil spirits, and they cannot enter its kingdom. And because it is the dwelling of those who do not disobey God for the blink of an eye: there is not a space of four fingers in it except that an angel is prostrating or standing. Also, it is the nobler substance and is vaster, brighter, purer, of better creation, and greater in signs. And the earth needs it for its perfection, while it does not need the earth.

For this reason, in most places in the Book of God the heaven is mentioned before the earth, and the heaven is mentioned in the plural while the earth is mentioned in the singular. Because of its nobility and excellence, it is mentioned in plural form.

As for the earth, it is only ever mentioned in the singular; and where its enumeration is intended, He says: ﴿and of the earth﴾.

This view is the correct one, and God, glorified and exalted is He, knows best.

The Lord, exalted is He, knew what was in Iblis's heart of disbelief, arrogance and envy, which the angels did not know. When He commanded them to prostrate, what was in the angels' hearts of obedience, love, awe and submission became apparent, so they hastened to comply. What was in the heart of their enemy of arrogance, deceit and envy also became apparent. So he refused, grew arrogant, and was among the disbelievers.

(A subtle point)

God, glorified is He, prepared the earth for Adam and his offspring before creating him, so He said: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾. He decreed that Adam would know the gravity of disobedience, and He established his excuse by saying: ﴿So Satan caused them to slip from it﴾. Then He reached him with His mercy by saying: ﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾.

O Adam, do not grieve over a cup of error that was the cause of your intelligence. It has brought out from you the disease of self-admiration and clothed you in the garment of servitude.

"Had you not sinned..."

Do not grieve over My saying to you ﴿Go down from it﴾. I created it for you, but go out to the farm of striving, work diligently in sowing, and water the tree of regret with the channel of tears. When the branch returns green, return to what you were.

(Section)

His answer, glorified is He, to one who asks about the specification and distinction that occur in His acts is that it is for a wisdom which He knows, even if the questioner does not know it. This is as He answered the angels when He said to them: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾, and they said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ So He answered them with His saying: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾.

Had His act been stripped of wisdom, purposes and interests, the angels would have been more knowledgeable of it, and their question would not have been answered by His singular knowledge of what they do not know of the wisdom and benefit in the creation of this successor. For this reason their question was about the aspect of wisdom and was not an objection against the Lord, exalted is He. Even if it were assumed to be an objection, it is evidence that they knew He does nothing except for a wisdom. When they saw that the creation of this successor appeared to contradict wisdom, they asked Him about it. From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah is most knowing of where He places His message﴾. He answered them that His wisdom and knowledge refuse to place His messages in other than their place and with other than their people. If the matter were referred merely to pure will, this would not be an answer. Rather the answer would be that His acts are not subject to causes, and that He favours one like another without a preponderant reason, and the matter returns to mere power, as the deniers say. Likewise His saying: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ When they asked about the specification by the will of Allah and denied it, they were answered that Allah knows best who is fit for His will and who deserves it, and they are the grateful who recognise the measure of the blessing and thank the Benefactor for it. These are fit for His will. Had the matter been referred to pure will, this answer would not have been fitting. For this reason, He mentions the attribute of knowledge where He mentions specification and distinction, indicating that it arises from His knowledge of what the specification and detailed distinction contain that calls for their specification and distinction, and it is He who made them fit for that. As He said: ﴿And for Solomon, the wind, blowing strongly, moving by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever Knowing of all things﴾. He mentioned His knowledge after specifying Solomon with the subjection of the wind to him and specifying the said land with blessing. From this is His saying: ﴿Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a means of stability for the people, and the sacred month, and the offerings and the garlands. That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. He mentioned the attribute of knowledge which required the specification of this place and this time with a matter that distinguished them over all other places and times. Among this is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Allah sent down His tranquillity upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and imposed upon them the word of righteousness, and they were most deserving of it and worthy of it. And Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾. He informed that He placed this word with its people, those who are most deserving of it, and that He is most knowing of who among others deserves it. Is this the description of one who specifies by pure will without cause and purpose?

(Benefit)

He said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority. They said, "Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know"﴾.

Then, glorified is He, manifested from His knowledge and wisdom, which was hidden from the angels regarding this successor, what they had not known: that from his offspring He would make friends, beloved ones, messengers and prophets who draw near to Him with all kinds of nearness, who spend themselves in His love and pleasure, who glorify Him with His praise in the hours of the night and the ends of the day, remember Him standing, sitting and on their sides, worship Him, remember Him and thank Him in ease and hardship, in health and trial, in adversity and comfort. Hardship does not turn them from His remembrance, thanks and worship; neither hardship, nor trial, nor poverty, nor sickness. They worship Him despite the opposition of desire, the dominance of passion, the mutual support of natures for their rulings, and the enmity of their own kind and others towards them. That does not prevent them from His worship, thanks, remembrance and drawing near to Him. If your worship of Me is without opposition or hindrance, then their worship of Me amid these oppositions, obstacles and preoccupations is greater. Also, He, glorified is He, willed to show them what was hidden from them concerning the matter of what they used to revere and exalt, and did not know what was in His own self of arrogance, envy and evil. That is the good, and this evil is latent in souls they do not know, so it must be brought out and made manifest, so that the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges is known, by rendering to each of them what befits it.

Also, He, glorified is He, when He created His creatures in stages and kinds, and His judgement and wisdom had preceded the preference of Adam and his children over many of those He created with a preference, made their servitude more perfect than the servitude of others, and servitude was the best of their conditions and highest of their ranks; I mean voluntary servitude, which they perform willingly and by choice, not under compulsion and necessity. For this reason, Allah sent Gabriel to the master of this human kind, giving him the choice between being a servant and messenger, or a king and prophet. By the success granted to him by his Lord, he chose to be a servant and messenger. He mentioned him, glorified is He, with perfect servitude in his most noble stations and best conditions, such as the station of the call, the challenge, the night journey and the sending down of the Qur'an: ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him﴾; ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾; ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾; ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾. He praised him and exalted him for his complete servitude to Him. For this reason the people of the gathering, when seeking intercession, say: "Go to Muhammad, a servant whom Allah has forgiven his past and future sins." Since servitude is the most noble state of the children of Adam and the most beloved to Allah, and it has requirements and conditioned causes which are attained only through it, it was among the greatest wisdom that they be brought out to a dwelling in which the rulings of servitude, its causes, its conditions and its necessities apply to them. So their removal from Paradise was both a punishment for them and a completion of His favour upon them, along with what that contains of the beloved things of the Lord, exalted is He. He loves the answering of supplications, the relief of distresses, the aid of those who cry for help, the forgiveness of slips, the expiation of misdeeds, the averting of afflictions, the honouring of those who deserve honour, the humiliating of those who deserve humiliation, the support of the oppressed, the mending of the broken, and the elevation of some of His creatures over others, making them in ranks so that the measure of His favour and specification is known. His complete dominion and perfect praise required that He bring them out to a dwelling in which His beloved things would be realised, even though many of them have paths and causes that He dislikes. Standing upon a thing is not possible without that thing, and the bringing into existence of the requirements of wisdom is itself wisdom, just as the bringing into existence of the requirements of justice is itself justice, as you will come to understand in the section on the suffering of children, God willing.

It was said: He answered them, glorified is He, that in His creation there are wisdoms and interests which the angels do not know, while the Creator, glorified is He, knows them. If the angels do not know what is in the creation of this human who causes corruption on earth and sheds blood of the wisdoms and interests, then others are even less able to comprehend them in knowledge. The creation of this human is part of perfect wisdom, mercy and interest, and even if its existence entails an evil, it is an evil submerged in the good of bringing it into being, like the sending down of rain and snow, the blowing of winds, the rising of the sun, the creation of animals, plants, mountains and seas. Just as this is so in His creation, so it is in His law, religion and command. For what He commands of righteous deeds, their good and benefit outweigh, and even if there is evil in them, it is utterly submerged in relation to their good. What He forbids of ugly deeds and words, their evil and corruption outweigh, and the good in them is utterly submerged in relation to their evil. So His custom, glorified is He, in His creation and command is to do pure and preponderant good, and to command pure and preponderant good. When the causes of good and evil contradict, and combining two contradictories is impossible, He gives precedence to the preponderant causes of good over the subordinate ones, and the loss of the subordinate is not an evil. He repels the preponderant causes of evil by the subordinate causes, and the occurrence of the subordinate is not an evil in comparison with the preponderant evil that is averted by it. Likewise is His custom in His law and command: He puts forward the preponderant good even if there is a subordinate evil within it, and He suspends the preponderant evil even if a subordinate good is lost by suspending it. This is His custom in what He brings into being and originates in His heavens and earth, and in what He commands and forbids. Likewise is His custom in the Hereafter. He, glorified is He, has perfected everything He created and made excellent all that He did. This is a matter that those who know Allah know in general, and they differ in knowledge of its details.

When this is known, pains and hardships are either a kindness and mercy, or justice and wisdom, or a reform and preparation for a good that follows them, or to avert a pain that is harder than them, or because they arise from pleasures and blessings which are generated by a necessary matter attached to those pleasures, or they are among the requirements of justice or the requirements of grace and kindness, so that they are among the requirements of good whose necessitating causes, if suspended, would lose by that suspension a good greater than the harm of those pains.

Both the law and the decree bear witness to this. How much pain there is for the traveller and the resident in the rising of the sun, and how much harm there is in the falling of rain and snow, as Allah named it in His saying: ﴿If there is upon you harm from rain﴾.

And how much harm there is in this heat, cold and wind, which necessitates various kinds of pain for kinds of animals. And the greatest of the pleasures of this world are the pleasure of eating, drinking, marriage, clothing and leadership, and most or all of the pains of the people of the earth arise from them and are generated from them. Indeed, human perfections are not attained except through pains and hardships, such as knowledge, courage, asceticism, chastity, forbearance, manliness, patience and kindness, as the poet said:

"Were it not for hardship, all people would be masters: generosity makes one poor, and feet are fighting."

When pains are causes of pleasures greater than them and more lasting than them, reason decides that they should be borne. Often pains are causes of health which, were it not for those pains, would be lost. This is the case with the greatest illnesses of the bodies. This fever contains benefits for the bodies that only Allah knows, and it contains the dissolving of excess matter, the ripening of crude substances and their expulsion, which no other medicine reaches. Many illnesses, when fever comes upon their owner, the physician rejoices at it. As for the benefit of the heart and the spirit from pains and illnesses, it is a matter which only one who has life feels. The health of hearts and spirits depends upon the pains and hardships of bodies. The benefits of illnesses have been counted and exceed a hundred benefits. Allah, glorified is He, has veiled the greatest pleasures with various disliked things and made them a bridge leading to them, just as He veiled the greatest pains with desires and pleasures and made them a bridge leading to them. For this reason all the wise have agreed that bliss is not attained through bliss, that rest is not gained through rest, and that whoever prefers pleasures loses pleasures. Therefore these pains, illnesses and hardships are among the greatest blessings, for they are causes of blessings. As for what non-accountable animals bear of them, it is utterly submerged in relation to their interests and benefits, as they bear the heat of summer, the cold of winter, the withholding of rain and snow, the pain of pregnancy and birth, and the striving to seek their sustenance and other things. But their pleasures are many times greater than their pains, and what they gain of benefits and goods is many times greater than what they gain of evils and pains. So the custom of Allah in His creation and command is the one which His perfect knowledge, wisdom and might have necessitated. Even if all the minds of all the wise gathered to propose something better than it, they would be unable to do so. And it is said to each of them: Return the gaze of reason; do you see any flaw? ﴿Then return the gaze twice; your gaze will return to you humbled and weary﴾.

Blessed is He who, from the perfection of His wisdom and power, brought opposites out of their opposites and things out of their contraries. He brought the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living, the moist out of the dry and the dry out of the moist. Likewise, He produced pleasures from pains and pains from pleasures. So the greatest pleasures are the fruits and results of pains, and the greatest pains are the fruits and results of pleasures. Moreover, pleasure, joy, good, blessings, health, benefit and mercy in this abode, which is filled with trials and afflictions, are more than their opposites by multiplied amounts. Where is the animal's pain in comparison with its pleasure, where is its sickness in comparison with its health, where is its hunger and thirst in comparison with its satiety and quenching, and its fatigue in comparison with its rest? Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So indeed, with hardship is ease. Indeed, with hardship is ease﴾. And one hardship will never overcome two eases. This is because mercy has overcome wrath, pardon has preceded punishment, and blessing has preceded trial. Goodness is in His attributes and acts, and evil is in what is created, not in His acts. His attributes are all perfection and His acts are all goods. The pain of an animal, by its pain, does not deprive it of health from a pain harder than that pain, or of preparation for strength, health and perfection, or of a compensation to which that pain bears no relation in any way. So all the pains of this world, compared to the pleasures and goods of the Hereafter, are less than the relation of a grain of dust to the mountains of this world by a great deal. Likewise, all the pleasures of this world, compared to the pains of the Hereafter. Allah, glorified is He, did not create pains and pleasures in vain, nor did He decree them as mere play. From the perfection of His power and wisdom is that He made each of them produce the other. Moreover, the necessities of creation cannot be removed, just as poverty, need and deficiency cannot be removed from the created. The created is only poor, needy, and deficient in knowledge and power. If the human and other animals did not hunger, thirst or suffer in the world of generation and corruption, they would not be animals, and this abode would be an abode of permanence and absolute, perfect pleasure. But Allah did not make it so; He made it an abode in which its pain is mixed with its pleasure, its joy with its sorrows and griefs, and its health with its sickness, as a wisdom from Him that is complete.

Moreover, when Allah said to the angels, ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾ they said, ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ He answered them, ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know.﴾ Then Allah made manifest to His servants and to His angels that which He had placed upon the earth of the special ones of His creation: His messengers, His prophets, His friends (awliya'), and those who draw near to Him and expend their souls in love of Him and seeking His pleasure, while striving against their desires and their caprice. They abandon what they love seeking nearness to Me, abandon their appetites seeking My pleasure, and spend their blood and souls in My love. I single them out with a knowledge you do not know. They glorify My praise in the hours of the night and the ends of the day, and they worship Me despite the opposition of caprice, desire, the self and the enemy. As for you, you worship Me without any opponent opposing you, without any appetite afflicting you, and without any enemy I have set over you. Rather, your worship of Me is like the soul of one of them.

Moreover, I want to manifest what was hidden from you concerning the affair of My enemy, his fighting against Me, his arrogance toward My command, and his striving to oppose My pleasure. Both of these were latent and concealed in the father of mankind and the father of the jinn. So I sent them down to a dwelling in which I manifest what Allah, glorified is He, had alone in His knowledge, which no one else knows; His wisdom becomes apparent, His command is fulfilled, and there becomes manifest to the angels from His knowledge what they did not know.

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, since He loves the patient, loves the doers of good, loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, loves the repentant, loves those who purify themselves, and loves the grateful, and since His love is the highest type of honour, His wisdom required that He settle Adam and his offspring in a dwelling where they would come with these attributes by which they attain the highest honours of His love. Therefore their descent to the earth was among the greatest blessings upon them. ﴿And Allah singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, willed to take from Adam offspring whom He would befriend, love and be loved by. Their love for Him is the goal of their perfection and the end of their nobility. This lofty rank could not be realized except by conforming to His pleasure, following His command, and abandoning the soul's desires and appetites that their Beloved dislikes. So He sent them down to a dwelling in which He gave them commands and prohibitions. They stood by His command and prohibition, and so attained the degree of loving Him, and He granted them the degree of His love for them. This is part of the completeness of His wisdom and the perfection of His mercy, for He is the Righteous, the Merciful.

Moreover, when Allah, glorified is He, created His creation in varied stages and kinds, and His judgment preceded the preferment of Adam and his offspring over many of His creatures, He made their servanthood the best of their ranks, namely voluntary servanthood, which they perform willingly and by choice, not by compulsion and necessity. It is established that Allah, glorified is He, sent Gabriel to the Prophet (ﷺ) to let him choose between being a king-prophet or a servant-prophet. He looked at Gabriel as one seeking counsel, and Gabriel gestured to him to be humble. He said, "Rather, I would be a servant-prophet." So Allah mentioned him by the name of his servanthood in his most noble stations: in the station of the Night Journey, the station of the call, and the station of challenge. He said in the station of the Night Journey, ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾, and did not say "His messenger" or "His prophet," indicating that he attained this supreme station through the perfection of his servanthood to his Lord. He said in the station of the call, ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up calling Him, they almost became around him a compact mass.﴾

He said in the station of challenge, ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a surah like it.﴾ In the two Sahihs, in the hadith of intercession and the prophets' turning back from it, and the Messiah's saying, "Go to Muhammad, a servant whom Allah forgave his earlier and later sins," this indicates that he attained that supreme station through the perfection of his servanthood to Allah and the perfection of Allah's forgiveness toward him. If servanthood with Allah has this status, His wisdom required that He settle Adam and his descendants in a dwelling where they could attain this rank through the perfection of their obedience to Allah, their nearness to Him through what He loves, and their abandonment of what is familiar to them for His sake. This was part of the completeness of His blessing upon them and His kindness toward them.

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, willed to make His servants who received the complete blessing know it and its measure, so that they would have greater love, more thankfulness, and greater delight in the bliss He gave them. So He showed them what He did to His enemies and what He prepared for them of punishment and varieties of pain, and He let them witness their deliverance from that and their being singled out with the highest kinds of bliss, so that their joy would increase, their happiness would be complete, their gladness would grow, and their pleasure would be perfected. This was part of the completion of His favours upon them and their love. There was no escape from sending them down to the earth, testing and trying them, granting success to whomever of them He willed by His mercy and grace, and forsaking whomever of them He willed by His wisdom and justice. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. There is no doubt that when the believer sees his enemy and his beloved, the thing most dear to him, in various kinds of punishment and pain while he himself is living in various kinds of bliss and pleasure, his joy increases, his delight is magnified, and his blessing is perfected.

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, created creation only for His worship, and that is their ultimate purpose. He, exalted is He, said, ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me.﴾ It is known that the perfection of servanthood required from creation is not attained in the abode of bliss and permanence; it is attained only in the abode of trial and testing. The abode of permanence is an abode of pleasure and bliss, not an abode of trial, examination and obligation.

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, His wisdom required the creation of Adam and his offspring from a composition that necessitates the call of desire and temptation and the call of intellect and knowledge. Allah, glorified is He, created in him intellect and appetite and appointed them as two callers according to their requirements, so that His purpose would be fulfilled and His might in His wisdom, His majesty, His mercy, His righteousness and His kindness in His dominion and kingdom would be manifest to His servants. His wisdom and mercy required that He let their father taste the bitterness of his disobedience and made him know the consequences of answering appetite and caprice, so that he would be more cautious in it and more intent on fleeing it. This is like the situation of a man travelling on a road where enemies lie in ambush on its sides, behind him and in front of him, while he is unaware. When he is struck by a calamity from them once, he prepares himself on his journey, takes the precautions of his enemy, and prepares for himself what will repel them. Had he not tasted the pain of his enemy's raid upon him and his ambush against him, his soul would not have consented to readiness, caution, and taking provision. So it is part of Allah's completion of blessing upon Adam and his offspring that He showed them what the enemy did to them, so they prepared against him and took his precautions.

If it is said: it was possible that the enemy not be allowed over them. It is answered: it has already been established that He, glorified is He, created Adam and his offspring with a constitution and composition that necessitates their mixing with their enemy and being tested by him. Had He willed, He would have created them like the angels, who are intellects without appetites; then the enemy would have had no way to them. But had they been created thus, they would have been a different creation from the children of Adam, for the children of Adam were constituted with intellect and appetite.

Moreover, since the love of Allah alone is the goal of the servant's perfection and happiness, without which there is no perfection or happiness at all, and since true love is realized only by preferring the Beloved over other beloved things of the souls, and by enduring the greatest hardships in His obedience and seeking His pleasure, through this love is realized and its firmness in the heart is known, His wisdom, glorified is He, required that He bring them out into this abode surrounded by appetites and the beloved things of the souls, by preferring the Truth over them and turning away from them, whereby their love for Him and their preference of Him over others is realized. For this reason they bear severe hardships, undertake dangers, endure blame, and are patient against the calls of error and misguidance. Through striving against them the authority of love grows strong, its tree takes root in the heart, and its fruit is fed to the limbs. The love that remains firm despite many obstacles, hindrances and distractions is the true, beneficial love. As for love conditioned on well-being, bliss and pleasure, and on the beloved's attaining what the lover wants, it is not true love and has no permanence when faced with opposition and obstacles. Whatever is conditioned on a condition ceases when the condition ceases, and whoever loves for a reason, his love ends when the reason ends. There is a difference between one who worships Allah in ease, prosperity and well-being only, and one who worships Him in ease and hardship, prosperity and adversity, well-being and trial.

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, has absolute and perfect praise that has no end after it. The appearance of the causes for which He is praised is part of His being praised, and they are among the necessities of His praise, exalted is He. They are of two kinds: grace and justice. He, glorified is He, is praised for this and for that. Therefore there must be the manifestation of the causes of justice and what they require of their objects, so that perfect praise, which He deserves, may be realized through them. Just as He, glorified is He, is praised for His kindness, righteousness, grace and reward, He is also praised for His justice, His vengeance and His punishment, since all of that proceeds from His might and wisdom. For this reason He, glorified is He, has drawn attention to this often, as in Surat ash-Shu'ara', where at the end of every story of the messengers and their peoples He says, ﴿Indeed in that is a sign, yet most of them were not believers. And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.﴾

He, glorified is He, informed that this proceeds from His might, which includes the perfection of His power, and from His wisdom, which includes the perfection of His knowledge and His placing of things in their fitting places. He placed His blessing and salvation for His messengers and their followers, and His vengeance and destruction of their enemies, only in their appropriate place, owing to the perfection of His might and wisdom. For this reason, after informing of His judgment between the people of happiness and the people of misery, and their return each to their abode, which is not fitting for them other than it, and which His wisdom does not require otherwise, He said, ﴿And it is judged between them with truth, and it is said, "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, His wisdom and His praise required that He vary among His servants with the greatest and most evident variation, so that the one upon whom His blessing and favour appear would thank Him, and would know that he has been favoured with bounty and specially honoured over others. Had they all been equal in blessing and well-being, the possessor of blessing would not know its worth and would not expend its thanks, for he would see no one except in his own situation. Among the strongest causes of gratitude, and the greatest in drawing it forth from the servant, is that he sees others in the opposite of his own state, in which he is perfect and successful.

In the well-known report: "When Allah showed Adam his descendants and the differences of their ranks, he said, 'O Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?' He said, 'I love to be thanked.'" So His love, glorified is He, to be thanked required that He create the causes by which the thanks of the grateful would be greater and more perfect. This is the very wisdom proceeding from the attribute of praise.

Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, has nothing more beloved to Him in His servant than his humbling himself before Him, his submission, his poverty, his brokenness, and his supplication to Him. It is known that this, which is required of the servant, is completed only through its causes, and the presence of these causes in the abode of absolute bliss and complete well-being is impossible, for that necessitates combining two opposites. Moreover, Allah, glorified is He, possesses creation and command. Command is His law, His order and His religion, which He sent with His messengers and sent down with His books. Paradise is not an abode of obligation upon which the rulings of obligation and their requirements apply; it is an abode of bliss and pleasure. Allah, glorified is He, His wisdom required bringing Adam and his offspring out to an abode in which the rulings of His religion and His command apply to them, so that the requirement of the command and its implications would become manifest in them. Just as His actions, His creation, are requirements of the perfection of His beautiful names and sublime attributes, so too are His command, His law, and what follows from it of reward and punishment. He, glorified is He, has guided to this meaning in more than one place in His Book, saying, exalted is He, ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾ That is, left idle and unoccupied, neither commanded nor forbidden, neither rewarded nor punished.

This indicates that this contradicts the perfection of His wisdom, and that His lordship, might and wisdom reject it. For this reason the statement was delivered in the form of denial against one who claims it. It also indicates that its goodness is established in natures and intellects, and that the ugliness of leaving it neglected and idle is likewise established in natures. How, then, is attributed to the Lord what its ugliness is established in your natures and intellects?

And He, exalted is He, said, ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us? Exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾

(Section)

The first of the creations was the Pen, to write the decrees before their existence, and Adam was made the last of the creations.

In this are several wisdoms. The first: preparing the house before its occupant. The second: that he is the end for which everything else was created, such as the heavens, the earth, the sun, the moon, the land and the sea. The third: that the most skilful craftsman concludes his work with its finest part, just as he begins it with its foundation and beginnings. The fourth: that souls are always inclined toward ends and last things; for this reason Moses said to the sorcerers, ﴿Throw what you are going to throw.﴾ When the people saw their deed, they looked forward to what would come after it. The fifth: that Allah, glorified is He, delayed the best of the books, the prophets and the nations until the end of time, and made the Hereafter better than the first life, and endings more perfect than beginnings. How great is the difference between the angel's saying to the Messenger, "Read," and his saying, "I am not a reader," and between His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you.﴾ The sixth: that He, glorified is He, gathered in Adam what He had scattered in the world, so he is the small world, and what is in the great world is in him. The seventh: that the essence of existence and its fruit is man, so it was fitting that his creation come after the existing things. The eighth: that among his honour with his Creator is that He prepared for him his needs, the instruments of his livelihood and the causes of his life, so that whenever he raised his head, all of that was present and ready. The ninth: that He, glorified is He, wished to manifest his nobility and superiority over the rest of creation, so He placed them before him in creation. For this reason the angels said, "Let our Lord create what He wills; He will not create a creature more honourable to Him than us." When He created Adam and commanded them to prostrate to him, his superiority and nobility over them in knowledge and recognition became manifest. When he fell into sin, the angels thought that this superiority had been abrogated, and they did not perceive the servanthood of repentance that was latent. When he turned to his Lord and performed that servanthood, the angels knew that Allah has a secret in His creation that no one else knows. The tenth: that when He, glorified is He, began the creation of this world with the Pen, it was of the best fitting that He conclude it with the creation of man, for the Pen is the instrument of knowledge and man is the one who knows. For this reason He manifested Adam's superiority over the angels through the knowledge specific to him to the exclusion of them. Consider how He wrote Adam's excuse before his descent to the earth, drew the angels' attention to his excellence and nobility, and announced his name before his existence with His saying, ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority.﴾

The passage is translated below.

And reflect on how He named him "khalifah" (vicegerent), and that was a guardianship for him before his existence. He established his excuse before the descent with His words, ﴿on the earth﴾, and the one who loves establishes the excuse of the beloved before his offence. When He had fashioned him, He cast him at the gate of Paradise for forty years, because it is the custom of the lover to stand at the door of the beloved. He threw him onto a path of humiliation, ﴿nothing worth mentioning﴾, lest he be vain on the day of ﴿Prostrate yourselves﴾. Iblis used to pass by his body, marvel at it, and say, "This is a thing that has been created for a purpose." Then he would enter through its mouth and exit through its back, saying, "If I am given power over you, I shall destroy you, and if you are given power over me, I shall disobey you." He did not know that his own destruction would be at his hands. He saw a heap of clay and despised it. When the clay was fashioned into a form, the disease of envy infected it, and when the spirit was breathed into it, the envier died. When the carpet of honour was spread for him, the creatures were presented to him, and he summoned the claimant of ﴿while we glorify You﴾ before a judge, ﴿Tell me﴾. The Advocate had concealed from him the proof, and He taught him. So they overturned the heads of claims upon the chests of acknowledgement. Then the herald of preference stood in the assemblies of the angels, calling, "Prostrate yourselves." So they purified themselves from the talk of claim, while we are with the water of excuse in vessels, ﴿we have no knowledge﴾. So they prostrated in the purity of submission, and Iblis stood aside and did not prostrate, because he was impure, and he had become tainted with the filth of objection. His filth could not be remedied by purification, because it was inherent. When the perfection of Adam was complete, He said, "There must be a beauty mark on the face of the prostration, 'Prostrate yourselves.'" So the decree came to pass with the sin, so that the trace of servitude would become manifest in humiliation. "O Adam, if that morsel had been pardoned for you, the envious would have said, 'How is one of great greed preferred, who did not endure patiently before a tree?' Had it not been for your descent, the sighs of breaths would not have ascended, nor would the messages 'Is there any petitioner?' have been sent down, nor would fragrances have spread, nor the change in the mouth of the fasting person." Then it became clear that that eating was not out of greed. "O Adam, your laughter in Paradise is for you, and your weeping in the abode of obligation is for us. What harm does it do to the one whose honour is broken, when My honour mends him? My favour is only befitting: the robe of honour belongs to the body of brokenness. I am with those whose hearts are broken for My sake." That morsel continued to harm him until its disease took hold of his offspring. Then the Subtle, the All-Aware, sent to them the cure through the hands of the physicians of existence: ﴿And if guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be unhappy﴾. So the Physician protected them with prohibitions, preserved their strength with commands, and purged their harmful humours through repentance, and so well-being came from every direction.

O you who have wasted your strength and not preserved it, who mixed up your illness and did not protect yourself, and did not endure the bitterness of purgation: do not deny the nearness of destruction, for the disease has advanced toward corruption. If destiny assists you, you will help the physician against yourself through abstention from base desire. You have attained various pleasures and kinds of desirable things, and the vapour of desire has covered the eye of insight, so you thought that prudence was selling a promise for cash. What blind insight! You were distressed by an hour's patience, yet you endured the humiliation of eternity. You travelled in pursuit of this world, which is passing away from you, and you sat back from journeying toward the Hereafter, which is travelling toward you. When you see a man buying the base for the precious, and selling the great for the small, know that he is foolish.

(Section)

This is like a debate between the angels and the answer to their question. It is as if they had said, "If You appoint a khalifah on the earth, there will be corruption in it and bloodshed, and Your wisdom requires that You not do that. And if You do appoint one, then appoint in it those who glorify You and sanctify You, for we do that." So He, exalted is He, answered this question by saying that He has a wisdom in appointing this khalifah on earth that the angels do not know. Behind what you suppose of corruption are benefits and wisdoms that you do not know. We have mentioned about forty of them in the book al-Tuhfah al-Makkiyyah. So, exalted is He, brought forth from this khalifah and his offspring the prophets, messengers, friends of God, and believers, and populated Paradise through them, and He distinguished the wicked among his offspring from the good, and populated Hell through them.

Within that were wisdoms and benefits that the angels could not know. Then He, glory be to Him, manifested the excellence of the khalifah over them through the knowledge with which He singled him out, which the angels did not know, and He commanded them to prostrate to him, as an honouring and exalting of him and a manifestation of his excellence.

Within that are wisdoms that none knows except God. Among them is testing them with prostration to one whom they claimed would corrupt the earth and shed blood. He made them prostrate to him and manifested his excellence over them, because they praised themselves and disparaged the khalifah, just as He, exalted is He, did with Moses when he reported about himself that he was the most knowledgeable person on earth, so He tested him with Khidr and his inability with him in those three incidents. This is His, exalted is He, way with His creation, and He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing.

Among them is His informing this khalifah and beginning with him with honour and bounty, knowing what would befall him of brokenness, calamity, and trial. So He began with restoration and favour, then trial, affliction, and humiliation came, and its outcome was a return to goodness, favour, and beneficence. The calamity that struck him was enveloped by two favours, one before it and one after it. The believing offspring share in what belonged to their father, for God, exalted is He, bestowed on them faith at the outset and made the final outcome theirs. Whatever sins and calamities befall them in between are enveloped by a favour before them and a favour after them. Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds.

Among them is His bringing out what was hidden in the soul of His enemy Iblis of arrogance and disobedience, which became manifest when he was commanded to prostrate. He thus deserved the curse, expulsion, and distance, for what was hidden in his soul became apparent. God knew it, but He would not have punished and cursed him for His knowledge of it, but for its actual occurrence. So His command to prostrate to Adam, along with the angels, made manifest the wickedness and disbelief that were hidden within him, which the angels did not know. So He, glory be to Him, displayed to them what He knew and what was concealed from them regarding him. In the command to prostrate to Adam there was an honouring of His khalifah, whom He had informed them would be placed on the earth, a consolation for him, a discipline for the angels, and a manifestation of what was hidden in the soul of Iblis. That was a cause for distinguishing the wicked from the good. This is among the wisdoms of His, exalted is He, in having them prostrate to Adam. Then, when He, glory be to Him, taught Adam what He taught him, He tested the angels with that knowledge, and they did not know it, so Adam informed them of it. Within that was an answer to them concerning the claim that this khalifah had no benefit in being placed on earth, for he would corrupt it and shed blood. So He showed them from His excellence and knowledge what was contrary to their assumption.

(Fasl: The Fifth Stage, which is one of the stages of the people of steadfastness (istiqamah, uprightness): the stage of wisdom (hikmah))

This is the stage of the wisdom of God in His decreeing for His servant what He, glory be to Him, hates and abhors, and blames and punishes for, and that had He willed, He would have preserved him from it and prevented it between him and it. He, glory be to Him, is not disobeyed by compulsion, and nothing in the world occurs except by His will: ﴿Surely to Him belong creation and command. Blessed is God, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-A'raf: 54].

These people witness that God, glory be to Him, did not create anything in vain or purposelessly, and that to Him belongs perfect wisdom in everything He decreed and ordained, of good and evil, of obedience and disobedience, and a dazzling wisdom that intellects cannot grasp in its essence, and tongues fail to express.

The source of His decree and destiny for what He hates and is angered by is His name, the All-Wise, whose wisdom has dazzled minds. He, exalted is He, said to His angels when they said, ﴿Will You place in it one who will cause corruption in it and shed blood, while we glorify You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. He answered them, glory be to Him, with His words: ﴿Indeed I know what you do not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30]. So for God, glory be to Him, in the manifestation of disobedience, sins, and crimes, and the consequences that follow from them, there are signs and wisdoms, and various kinds of ways of making Himself known to His creation, and diversity of His signs, and indications of His lordship, oneness, divinity, wisdom, might, complete dominion, perfect power, and encompassing knowledge, which those of insight witness directly with the insight of their hearts. So they say, ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You﴾ [Al 'Imran: 191]. These are nothing but Your dazzling wisdom and Your manifest signs.

*And for God, in every movement and every stillness, there is always a witness.*
*And in everything there is a sign for Him, indicating that He is One.*

How many a manifest sign on earth points to God, and to the truthfulness of His messengers, and to the truth of meeting Him, whose cause was the disobedience and sins of the children of Adam! Such as His sign in the drowning of the people of Noah, when the water rose above the mountaintops until it drowned all the people of the earth and saved His friends and the people of His knowledge and monotheism. How many signs, lessons, and lasting indications there are in that across the ages! So too the destruction of the people of Aad and Thamud.

How many signs He has in Pharaoh and his people, from the time Moses, peace be upon him, was sent to them, and even before his mission, until their drowning. Had it not been for their disobedience and disbelief, those signs and wonders would not have appeared. In the Torah it is said that God, exalted is He, said to Moses: "Go to Pharaoh, for I will harden his heart and prevent him from faith, so that I may display My signs and wonders in Egypt." And so He, glory be to Him, did, and He displayed His signs and wonders because of the sins of Pharaoh and his people, to the extent that He displayed them.

Likewise is His, glory be to Him, manifestation of making the fire cool and safe for Abraham, because of the sins and disobedience of his people, and their throwing him into the fire, until that became a sign, and through it Abraham attained the perfection of intimate friendship.

Likewise is what befell the messengers of honour, rank, nearness, and standing with God, because of their patience with the harm of their people, and their fighting against them and their enmity.

Likewise is God's taking of martyrs, friends, and chosen ones from the children of Adam, because of their patience with the harm of the children of Adam from the people of disobedience and oppression, and their striving for God, and their enduring for His sake what they endured from His enemies, which is exactly in His knowledge and sight, and their deserving of elevation in ranks through that.

And besides that are benefits and wisdoms that came about because of the manifestation of sins and crimes, and among their causes was the decree of what God hates and is angered by. That was pure wisdom, because of what follows from it that is more beloved to Him and more preferred by Him than its absence would have been, had there been no disobedience.

So the attainment of this great beloved thing is more beloved to Him than the absence of that hated, angering thing. Its absence, though beloved to Him, yet the attainment of this beloved thing could not be achieved without the existence of that disliked, angering thing. The perfection of His wisdom requires the attainment of the more beloved of the two matters through the loss of the lesser of the two beloved things, and that this greater beloved not be nullified by the nullification of that disliked thing. Supposing in the mind the existence of this without that is like supposing the existence of effects without their causes, and of necessary implications without their necessary consequences, which the wisdom of God and the perfection of His power and lordship forbid.
