Enough of this is one example: had it not been for the disobedience of the father of mankind in eating from the tree, there would not have followed from it the existence of these great beloved things for the Lord, exalted is He: the testing and obligating of His creation, the sending of His messengers, the revelation of His books, the manifestation of His signs and wonders, their diversity and variety, the honouring of His friends, the humiliation of His enemies, the manifestation of His justice and bounty, His might and vengeance, His pardon, forgiveness, forbearance, and clemency, and the appearance of those who worship Him, love Him, and act in accordance with His pleasure, among His enemies, in the abode of trial and testing.

So if it were supposed that Adam had not eaten from the tree, and he and his offspring had not been removed from Paradise, none of those things would have existed, and that which was latent in the heart of Iblis, which God knows and the angels do not know, would not have come from potential into actual. The wicked of creation would not have been distinguished from its good, the kingdom would not have been completed, since there would have been no honour and reward, punishment and humiliation, abode of happiness and bounty, and abode of wretchedness and justice.

And how much wisdom is perfect, and how much blessing is abundant, in His empowering of His friends over His enemies, and His empowering of His enemies over His friends, and the gathering of both in one abode, and the testing of some of them with others!

And how many beloved things for the Lord are attained therein, and praise of Him from the people of His heavens and earth, and humility and submission before Him, and worship, fear, and need of Him, and brokenness before His presence, that He not make them among His enemies. For they witness them, and they witness God's abandonment of them, His turning away from them, His hatred of them, and what He has prepared for them of punishment. All of this is by His will and volition, and His disposal of His kingdom. So His friends, out of fear of being forsaken by Him, are humble, fearful, in the utmost dread, greatest awe, and complete brokenness.

When the angels see Iblis and what befell him, and Harut and Marut, they lower their heads before the Lord in humility to His greatness, in submissiveness to His might, in fear of being removed and expelled from Him, in humbling themselves before His majesty, and in need of His protection and mercy. They know through that His favour upon them, His beneficence toward them, and His singling them out with His grace and honour.

Likewise, His righteous friends, when they witness the conditions of His enemies, His hatred of them, His anger against them, and His abandonment of them, increase in submission and humility, need and brokenness, seeking His help, turning to Him in repentance, relying upon Him, longing for Him, and fearing Him. They know that they have no refuge from Him except in Him, that none can protect them from His wrath except Him, and that nothing saves them from His displeasure except His good pleasure. So bounty is in His hand, first and last.

This is a drop from the ocean of His wisdom that encompasses His creation, and the one of insight contemplates with his insight what lies beyond it, so it reveals to him wonders of His wisdom that expression cannot reach and description cannot attain.

And as for the share of the servant in himself, and what pertains to him of witnessing this wisdom, it is according to his readiness (istidad), the strength of his insight, the completeness of his knowledge and his recognition of Allah and His names and attributes, and his knowledge of the rights of servanthood (ubudiyyah) and lordship (rububiyyah). Every believer has from that a known portion (shirb ma'lum) and a station which he does not exceed or transgress. And Allah is the One who grants success and help.

(Lata'if – A Subtle Point)

Al-Sha'bi was asked about a matter and said: "I do not know." It was said to him: "Are you not ashamed to say 'I do not know' while you are the jurist of the people of Iraq?"

He replied: "But the angels were not ashamed when they said: ﴿We have no knowledge except what You have taught us﴾."

Some of the scholars said: "Learn to say 'I do not know', for if you say 'I do not know', they will teach you until you know, and if you say 'I know', they will question you until you do not know."

'Utbah ibn Muslim said: "I accompanied Ibn 'Umar for thirty-four months, and he would often be asked and say: 'I do not know'."

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib would scarcely issue a fatwa or say anything without saying: "O Allah, keep me safe and keep others safe from me."

Al-Shafi'i was asked about a matter and remained silent. It was said: "Will you not answer?" He said: "Until I know whether the virtue lies in my silence or in the answer."

Ibn Abi Layla said: "I met one hundred and twenty men from the Ansar, companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One of them would be asked a question and would refer it to this one, and this one to that one, until it returned to the first. None of them would narrate a hadith or be asked about something without wishing that his brother would suffice him."

Abu al-Husayn al-Azdi said: "Indeed one of them would issue a fatwa on a matter which, if it had come to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, he would have gathered the people of Badr for it."

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad was asked about something and said: "I do not do well at it." The questioner said to him: "I came to you because I know no one other than you." Al-Qasim said to him: "Do not look at the length of my beard or the crowd of people around me; by Allah, I do not do well at it." An elderly man of Quraysh sitting beside him said: "O nephew, stick to it, for by Allah, we have not seen you in a gathering more noble than you are today." Al-Qasim said: "By Allah, for my tongue to be cut off is dearer to me than that I should speak about what I have no knowledge of."

Salman wrote to Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with both of them, and there was a bond of brotherhood between them: "It has reached me that you have sat down as a physician. Beware lest you become a quack, or kill a Muslim." So it was that when two litigants came to him, he would judge between them and then say: "Return them to me. A quack, by Allah! Repeat your case to me."

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 33:

God (subhanahu) differentiated among the human species with the greatest difference that exists among created beings. Of any single kind, no two can be known to differ as much as the best of mankind differs from the worst of them. God created the angels as intellects without appetites, and He created the animals as beings with appetites without intellects. He created the human being composed of intellect and appetite. Whoever's intellect overcomes his appetite is better than the angels, and whoever's appetite overcomes his intellect is worse than the animals. God also differentiated among them in knowledge, so He made their learned one the teacher of the angels, as He said, Exalted is He: ﴿O Adam, inform them of their names﴾. That is a rank above which there is no rank. And He made their ignorant one such that Satan is not pleased with him and he is not fit for him, as Satan said to their ignorant one who obeyed him in disbelief: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you﴾, and said to their foolish ones who disobeyed His Messenger: ﴿Indeed, I am free of you all﴾. How severe, then, is this difference between two persons, one of whom the angels prostrate to and who is taught by God what He has taught him, and the other of whom Satan is not pleased to take as an ally.

This great difference arises only through knowledge and its fruit. Even if knowledge offered nothing but nearness to the Lord of the worlds, joining the world of the angels, and companionship with the exalted assembly, it would be sufficient as a virtue and honour. How much more so, when the might of this world and the Hereafter is bound to it and conditioned upon its attainment.

(Fa'ida)

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when We said﴾, ﴿And when We delivered you﴾, ﴿And when We parted﴾. This occurs very often, with the conjunctive waw and without mention of a governing verb for idh (إذ), because the discourse is enumerating blessings and repeating accounts. By the conjunctive waw it points to them, as though they were stated explicitly, since the addressee knows what is meant. Because this was hidden from some of the literalist grammarians (ظاهرية النحاة, Ẓāhiriyya), they said that the particle *aw* (أو) is extra here, and this is not so. Of this same category is the waw that carries the meaning of *rubba* (رب, "many a"). You often find it at the beginning of speech, indicating that what follows it is an enumeration of something, whether boasting, praise, or otherwise. All of these are meanings concealed in the soul, and these particles are conjunctive to them. Sometimes they state that concealed matter explicitly, as in the saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Leave what is in your soul, even if they give you a fatwa about it and they give you a fatwa." Of this category is the omission of many responses (jawab) in the Qur'an, because the waw indicates them, since the addressee knows that the waw is conjunctive and is used only to conjoin to something. Such is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when they took him away and agreed to put him into the depths of the well﴾, and His saying: ﴿Until, when they came to it and its gates were opened﴾. This category is broad in the language. This is what there is on this question. This very matter occurred to me before, at the station in Mecca, and it was circulating in my mind, but I turned away from it, because I had not seen it in the investigations of the scholars.

Then I saw it afterwards in two distinguished grammarians. One of them circled around it and mentioned what was reported, and I do not know his name. The second was Abu al-Qasim al-Suhayli, may Allah have mercy on him, for he uncovered it and stated it explicitly. When realities appear, be the happiest of people with them, even if the ignorant spurn them. And Allah is the Granter of success in what is correct.

(Section)

The pillars of disbelief are four: pride, envy, anger, and desire.

Pride prevents him from submission. Envy prevents him from accepting advice and giving it. Anger prevents him from justice. Desire prevents him from devoting himself to worship. When the pillar of pride collapses, submission becomes easy for him. When the pillar of envy collapses, accepting advice and giving it becomes easy for him. When the pillar of anger collapses, justice and humility become easy for him. When the pillar of desire collapses, patience, chastity, and worship become easy for him. The removal of mountains from their places is easier than the removal of these four from the one afflicted with them, especially when they become firmly established dispositions, settled habits, and fixed qualities. For then no action can ever be sound for him with them, and his soul does not grow purified while they remain in him. Whenever he strives in action, these four spoil it for him, and all calamities are born from them. When they become entrenched in the heart, they show him falsehood in the form of truth and truth in the form of falsehood, the good in the form of the evil and the evil in the form of the good. The world draws near to him and the Hereafter recedes from him. If you reflect upon the disbelief of nations, you will see that it arises from these four, and upon them punishment falls. Its lightness and severity are according to their lightness and severity. Whoever opens them upon his soul, Allah opens upon him the doors of all evils, in this life and the next. Whoever closes them upon his soul, Allah closes from him the doors of evils. For they prevent submission, sincerity, repentance, turning back to Allah, accepting the truth, giving counsel to the Muslims, and humility before Allah and His creation.

The origin of these four is his ignorance of his Lord and his ignorance of himself. For if he knew his Lord through the attributes of perfection and the descriptions of majesty, and knew himself through its deficiencies and defects, he would not be proud, would not become angry for his own sake, and would not envy anyone for what Allah has given him. For envy, in reality, is a kind of enmity toward Allah, since he dislikes the blessing of Allah upon His servant, while Allah has loved it and loves its continuation for him, and Allah dislikes its removal. So he opposes Allah in His decree, His destiny, His love, and His dislike. For this reason Iblis was truly Allah's enemy, because his sin was from pride and envy. So he uprooted these two qualities through knowledge of Allah, His tawhid, contentment with Him, being pleased with Him, and turning to Him. He uprooted anger through knowledge of the self and that it does not deserve to be angered for or avenged for, for that is preferring it with contentment and anger over its Creator and Originator. The greatest remedy for this disease is that he train himself to become angry for the sake of Allah, Glorified is He, and to be pleased for His sake. Whenever some anger or contentment for the sake of Allah enters him, there goes out from him its counterpart, the anger and contentment for the sake of himself. And likewise the reverse.

As for desire, its remedy is sound knowledge and recognition that giving it what it desires is the greatest cause of its deprivation, and that denying it is the greatest cause of its reaching them. So whenever you open to it the door of desires, you are striving to deprive it of them, and whenever you close that door to it, you are striving to bring it to them in the most perfect manner.

Anger is like a beast of prey: if its owner lets it loose, it begins by devouring him. Desire is like fire: if its owner kindles it, it begins by burning him. Pride is like contending with a king for his kingdom: if he does not destroy you, he expels you from it. Envy is like opposing one who is more powerful than you. He who overcomes his desire and anger, Satan flees from his shadow, and he whom his desire and anger overcome, Satan flees from his phantom.

(Section: Beware of sins, for they removed the honor of "Prostrate", and expelled from the iqta' of "Dwell" — O what a moment that produced the heat of anguish for a thousand years. It keeps writing with the blood of regret the lines of sorrow in the narratives, and sends them with the breaths of regret, until there came the response ﴿So He accepted his repentance﴾. Iblis rejoiced at Adam's descent from Paradise, and he did not know that the descent of the diver into the depths in pursuit of a pearl is an ascent. How great is the distance between His saying to Adam ﴿Indeed I am placing upon the earth a vicegerent﴾ and His saying to you ﴿Go, and whoever follows you among them…﴾. What befell Adam is the very purpose of his existence (Had you not sinned...)

O Adam, do not grieve over My saying to you ﴿Go down from it﴾. It is for you and for the benefit of your offspring that I created it.

O Adam, you used to enter upon Me as kings enter upon kings, and today you enter upon Me as servants enter upon kings.

O Adam, do not grieve over a cup of error which was the cause of your gain. It has drawn out from you the disease of self-admiration, and you were clothed in the robe of servanthood. ﴿And it may be that you dislike a thing…﴾

O Adam, I did not take your iqta' to give to another. I only removed you from it in order to perfect its cultivation for you and to send to its workers provisions. ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾.

By Allah, his obedience did not benefit him in honor ﴿Prostrate﴾, nor in nobility ﴿And He taught Adam﴾, nor in distinction ﴿What I created with My own hands﴾, nor in pride ﴿And I breathed into him of My spirit﴾. He benefited only from the humble saying ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾.

When he put on the armor of tawhid over the body of gratitude, the arrow of the enemy fell upon it in a place that was not fatal.

So it wounded him, and the mighty one of brokenness was placed upon it, and it returned as it was, and the wounded one stood up as though there had never been a wound upon him.)

(Section: The debate of Iblis concerning Adam)

In mention of the argument of Iblis, the enemy of Allah, concerning Adam, and his refusal to prostrate to him, and clarification of its corruption: Allah, the Exalted, has repeated its mention in His Book, and He informed that Iblis's refusal to prostrate was out of pride and disbelief, and mere refusal. He mentioned the doubt only as obstinacy. Otherwise, the cause of his disobedience was arrogance, refusal, and disbelief. Otherwise, there is nothing in His command to prostrate to Adam that contradicts wisdom in any way. As for his baseless doubt, which is that his origin and substance is fire, while the origin and substance of Adam is clay, and he inferred from this that he is better than Adam, and then, on the basis of these two premises, he concluded that it is not fitting for him to humble himself before one who is above him and better than him, it is false in many respects. Among them: his claim that he is better than Adam is a false and baseless claim, and his argument for it, that he was created from fire and Adam from clay, is an invalid argument. Fire is not better than clay and dust; rather, dust is better than fire and more excellent in substance, in several respects:

First: fire by its nature is corruption and destroys whatever it touches, unlike dust.

Second: its nature is lightness, sharpness, and recklessness, while dust's nature is gravity, tranquility, and steadiness.

Third: from dust come the provisions of animals, their sustenance, the clothing and adornment of servants, the tools of their livelihoods, and their dwellings. Nothing of this comes from fire.

Fourth: dust is necessary for animals, which cannot do without it at all, nor without what grows in it and from it. Brute animals can do without fire altogether, and man can even do without it for days and months, so necessity does not compel him to it. How can the benefit of all animals from dust compare to man's benefit from fire at certain times?

Fifth: when food is placed in dust, it brings forth many times over what was placed in it. By its blessing it returns to you what you entrust to it, multiplied. If you entrusted fire with it, it would betray you, consume it, and leave nothing, and you would not even have a trace left.

Sixth: fire does not stand by itself, but needs a substance in which it subsists, so that substance bears it. Dust does not need a bearer. Therefore dust is more perfect than it.

Seventh: fire needs dust, and dust does not need it. For the vessel in which fire subsists can only be made of dust or contained in it. So fire is the one in need of dust, and dust is the one independent of it.

Eighth: the Iblisian substance is the smokeless fire (al-māriǧ), which is weak, toyed with by desire, inclining wherever desire inclines. For this reason desire overcame the one created from it, and captured and subdued him. But the Adamic substance is dust, which is strong, does not go wherever desire goes, subdues its desire, and captures it, and returns to its Lord, so He chose him and selected him. Thus the desire that accompanied the Adamic substance was accidental and quickly passed away, so it departed. Steadiness and gravity were original to him, so he returned to them. Iblis was the opposite. Thus each of the two parents returned to its origin: Adam's substance returned to its good and noble origin, and the accursed one to his base origin.

Ninth: fire, though some benefit and enjoyment come from it, its evil is restrained only by force and confinement. Were it not for the restrainer and confiner, it would ruin crops and offspring. As for dust, goodness, righteousness, and blessing are hidden in it, and whenever it is stirred and turned over, its blessing, goodness, and fruit appear. How can one of them be compared to the other?

Tenth: Allah has mentioned the earth often in His Book, informed of its benefits and its creation, that He made it a cradle, a bed, a carpet, a dwelling place, and a receptacle for the living and the dead, and He called His servants to reflect upon it, to look at its signs and the wonders He has placed in it. He has not mentioned fire except in the context of punishment, warning, and torment, except in one or two places where He mentioned it as a reminder and a provision for the wayfarers: "a reminder of the fire of the Hereafter and a provision for those who are in need," the ones who dwell in the empty land, when the traveler lands there, enjoys the fire at a station. How does this compare with the descriptions of the earth in the Qur'an?

Eleventh: Allah described the earth with blessing in many places of His Book, especially, and informed that He blessed it, generally. He said: ﴿Do you indeed disbelieve in Him who created the earth in two days, and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed in it firm mountains above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask﴾. This is a general blessing.

As for the blessing specific to some of it, such as His saying: ﴿And We delivered him and Lot to the land which We blessed for all the worlds﴾, and His saying: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed visible towns﴾, and His saying: ﴿And to Solomon the wind, blowing violently, running by his command to the land which We had blessed﴾. As for fire, He did not inform that He placed any blessing in it at all. Rather, it is well known that it removes blessing and annihilates it. How different is that which is blessed in itself and blesses what it is placed in, from that which removes blessing and annihilates it!

Twelfth: Allah made the earth the place of His houses, in which His name is mentioned and He is glorified morning and evening, generally, and His Sacred House, which He made a place of standing for the people, blessed and a guidance for the worlds, specifically. If there were nothing in the earth but His Sacred House, that alone would suffice it for honor and superiority over fire.

Thirteenth: Allah has deposited in the earth benefits, minerals, rivers, springs, fruits, grains, provisions, varieties of animals and their enjoyments, mountains, gardens, meadows, beautiful vehicles, and delightful forms, of which He has deposited nothing in fire. What meadow or garden is there in fire, or what minerals, forms, gushing spring, flowing river, delicious fruit, beautiful wife, or clothing and covering?

Fourteenth: the ultimate state of fire is that it was placed to serve what is in the earth. So fire's place is that of a servant to these things, completing them. It follows them and serves them only. When they are not in need of it, they drive it away and keep it far from them. When they need it, they summon it as the served summons his servant and one who fulfills his needs.

Fifteenth: the accursed one, because of the shortness of his sight and the weakness of his insight, saw the form of clay as dust mixed with water, so he despised it. He did not know that clay is composed of two elements: water, from which Allah made every living thing, and dust, which He made a storehouse of benefits and blessings. How much benefit and kinds of enjoyment come from clay! If his sight had gone beyond the form of clay to its substance and its end, he would have seen that it is better than fire and more excellent. When you examine the aspects that show you that dust is better than fire and superior to it, you will find them very many. We have only pointed to them briefly. Then, even if we grant by false supposition that fire is better than clay, it does not follow that what is created from fire is better than what is created from clay. The One Who is capable of all things creates from the lesser substance one who is better than one created from the superior substance, and judging by the perfection of the final outcome does not diminish the substance. The accursed one did not go beyond the place of the substance, nor cross from it to the perfection of the form and the final stage of creation. Where is the despised water, which is a drop and a clot, and the disgust of souls toward it, compared to the complete human form, perfect in beauty of form and character? Allah created the angels from light and Adam from dust, and from Adam's offspring has come one better than the angels, even though light is more excellent than dust. This and similar things show you the weakness of the accursed one's argument, the corruption of his view and understanding, and that wisdom required him to humble himself before Adam. Instead he opposed Allah's judgment and command with his own false opinion and corrupt view. Thus his analogy is invalid, both by text and by reason. Whoever opposes the texts of the Prophets with his analogy and opinion is among his successors and followers. We seek refuge with Allah from abandonment, and we ask Him for success and protection from this trial, which no servant has been struck with a worse one than it. Meeting Allah with the sins of all creatures, except associating partners with Him, is safer for him than meeting Allah having opposed the texts of His Prophets with his own opinion and the opinion of his kind. Did Allah expel Iblis, curse him, and bring down upon him His wrath and anger, except when he opposed the text with opinion and analogy, then preferred himself over it? Allah knows that the doubt of the enemy of Allah, despite being baseless and false, is stronger than many of the doubts of those who oppose the texts of the Prophets with their opinions and intellects. So the scholar should reflect on the secret of Allah's repeating this story time and again, and beware lest he have a share of this opinion and analogy while he is unaware. The enemy of Allah swore that he would mislead all the children of Adam except the sincere among them, and Allah confirmed his assumption about them, and informed that the sincere have no path for him over them. The sincere are those who sincerely devoted worship, love, glorification, and obedience to Allah, and followed and submitted to the texts of the Prophets. They single out the worship of Allah apart from the worship of anything else, and single out the following of His Messenger and abandon what contradicts it, following no one else's word. Let the intelligent person weigh himself by this scale before he is weighed on the Day of meeting Allah. And Allah is the One sought for help, upon Whom one relies, and there is no power nor strength except by Allah, the Exalted.

(Section)
As for "al-azwaj" (the spouses), it is the plural of zawj, and it is also said zawjah; the former is more eloquent, and it is the form in which the Qur'an came.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O Adam, dwell, you and your spouse, in the Garden﴾ [al-Baqarah: 35].
And He the Exalted said concerning Zakariyya, upon him be peace: ﴿And We made his spouse fit for him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 90].
And from the second usage is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: "Indeed she is your Prophet's spouse in this world and in the Hereafter."
And al-Farazdaq said:
"Indeed, whoever seeks to corrupt my spouse
is like one who runs to a lion's den to steal its prey."
It may also be pluralized as zawjat, but that is the plural of zawjah; the plural of zawj is azwaj.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They and their spouses are in shade, reclining upon couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56].
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You and your spouses will be made joyful﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 70].
The Qur'an has already reported about the people of faith using the word zawj in both singular and plural, as mentioned before.
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers﴾ [al-Ahzab: 6].
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 59].
As for reporting about the people of polytheism, the word used is "the woman." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab... and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾, up to His words.
And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾ [al-Tahrim: 10]. Since both were polytheists, the name "woman" was applied to them. And He said concerning Pharaoh: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾ [al-Tahrim: 11]. Since he was the polytheist and she was a believer, He did not call her his spouse.
And He said concerning Adam: ﴿Dwell, you and your spouse, in the Garden﴾.
And He said to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Indeed We have made lawful to you your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50].
And He said concerning the believers: ﴿And for them therein are pure spouses﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25].
Some scholars, among them al-Suhayli and others, said: the reason the word "spouses" was not used for these disbelieving women is that they are not spouses to their men in the Hereafter, and because marriage is a legislated adornment and a matter of religion, so the disbeliever is stripped of it, just as the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot were stripped of it.
Then al-Suhayli raised an objection against himself with the words of Zakariyya, upon him be peace: ﴿And my wife is barren﴾ [Maryam: 5], and His words about Abraham: ﴿Then his wife came forward in a loud cry﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 29].
He answered that mentioning "the woman" is more fitting in these places, because it is in the context of pregnancy and childbirth; so mentioning "the woman" is more appropriate, because the attribute that requires conception and delivery is femaleness, not being a spouse.
I say: even if it were said that the secret in mentioning the believers and their women with the word "spouses" is that this word implies similarity, homogeneity and pairing, as is understood from its form, for the two spouses (zawjan) are two things that are alike, matching, or equal. From this is His saying: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their spouses﴾ [al-Saffat: 22].
'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Their spouses are their likes and their peers."
Imam Ahmad also said the same.
From this also is His saying: ﴿And when the souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7], meaning each like is joined with its like in bliss and punishment.
'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said concerning this verse: the righteous with the righteous in Paradise, and the wicked with the wicked in the Fire.
This was also said by al-Hasan, Qatadah, and most scholars.
It was also said: the souls of the believers are paired with the wide-eyed houris, and the souls of the disbelievers with the devils; and this returns to the first view.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Eight pairs (azwaj)﴾ [al-An'am: 143], then explained them: ﴿two from the sheep and two from the goats﴾, ﴿and two from the camels and two from the cattle﴾ [al-An'am: 143-144]. So He made the pair to be the two single members of one kind.
From this is the common saying: "a pair of shoes" (zawja khuff) and "a pair of pigeons" (zawja hamam), and the like.
There is no doubt that Allah, glorified and exalted, cut off resemblance and similarity between the disbeliever and the believer.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of the Garden are not equal﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. And He the Exalted said concerning the believers and disbelievers among the People of the Book: ﴿They are not all alike, among the People of the Book﴾ [Al 'Imran: 113]. He also cut off their association in worldly rulings, so they do not inherit from each other, do not marry each other, and neither one takes the other as a protector. Just as the bond between them was severed in meaning, it was severed in name. So He attributed the woman to them with the bare word for femaleness, without the word implying similarity and resemblance.
Reflect on this meaning and you will find it to correspond more closely with the words and meanings of the Qur'an. For this reason, the term "woman" rather than "spouse" was applied to the Muslim woman married to a disbeliever and to the disbelieving woman married to a believer, in order to realize this meaning. And Allah knows best.
This is more correct than the view of those who said that He called the wife of Abu Lahab "his woman" and did not call her "his spouse" because the marriages of disbelievers do not have the ruling of validity, unlike the marriages of the people of Islam. This is invalid, because of His applying the name "woman" to the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot, even though that marriage was valid.
Reflect also on this meaning in the verses of inheritance, and how Allah made inheritance conditional on the word "spouse" rather than "woman," as in His saying: ﴿And for you is half of what your spouses leave﴾ [al-Nisa': 12], announcing that this inheritance occurs only through the spousal relationship, which requires similarity and proportion. The believer and the disbeliever have no similarity or proportion between them, so no inheritance occurs between them.
The secrets of the individual words and compound structures of the Qur'an are beyond the intellects of all beings.

(Admonition)
Do not belittle a sin, for how many a spark has set fire to much! Do you not know the secret of: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾?
If Adam had been content, he would have been sufficient; but the trial was in the nearness. Seclusion is a snare for the hunt of intimacy. The hunters hid a person, and the least movement is the greatest catch of prey. Whoever hunts does not make a sound.
Ever do the souls of lovers yearn toward your abodes,
and likewise hearts, by remembering you, after fear, find rest.
Another said:
"My ruins, when a love-sick man complains to them,
he complains to one without speech, to one without understanding."
Another said:
"The life of a youth is only a caravan's march,
from which he departs either a winner or a loser."
Another said:
"Be wary when the funerals pass by us,
and we play when they vanish,
like a flock startled by the appearance of a wolf,
and when it has gone, they return grazing."
Train yourself with the firm resolutions and do not seek concessions. The inner wall is in ruins, so what use is plastering it?
Knowledge and action are twins, whose mother is high aspiration.
Ignorance and idleness are twins, whose mother is preferring laziness.
O teacher, be steadfast with the beginner, and be patient in private, for the scholar has firmness and the learner has restlessness. And O student, be humble in seeking, for the dust between us is beneath the sole of the foot, which becomes a purifier for the face. The bride of knowledge has unveiled herself to you, but she is not compatible with me. Looking is only permissible once the contract is valid. So lower your gaze, for you are from the spring of Numayr. The scholar is not one person; the scholar is the one of writings. The scholar's immortal children are his works, apart from his children. Whoever is created for knowledge reveals its essence from youth. Prolonged nights lead to a sound sleep, and humiliation lies hidden in the shade of ease. The grandeur of dangers lies in riding dangers. The waters of meanings are stored in the heart of the scholar, from which he draws for irrigation, channel after channel, and he saves the purest for the people of purity; when they multiply upon him, he calls out for the path, and his knowledge remains flowing, and therefore it is multiplied; upon him is the zakat of gratitude. Every hour, the merchandise of his thought travels from the city of his heart to the hearts of seekers, and the auctioneer of his tongue proclaims it, presenting it in seasons of advice to the merchants of seeking and will, who buy his wisdom and knowledge at the price of choice.
So, O you who sees the height of that rank, do not forget the steps. How many have plunged into a salty sea until they reached sweet water, and how many have wandered in a barren wilderness until they were called a guide. How many have worn out the vehicles of the body, broken the desires of the senses, traveled by night and day, and kindled the fire of patience in the darkness of passion. If you trust his honesty, then this is the report of the journey. The world projects its arrows toward its children and says: take your precaution, for the blood of its slain is wasted. The hoopoe was absent from Solomon for an hour, and he threatened it. So O you who prolonged absence from his Lord, have you felt safe from his anger? The three who stayed behind from the Messenger in one battle had what you have heard happen to them; how then of one whose whole life is staying behind from Him? When the crow gets drunk on the wine of greed, it moves about among carrion; when it sobers from its intoxication, it regrets the ruins. Moses opposed al-Khidr three times on the road of companionship, and so the knot of union was undone by the words: "This is the parting between me and you." Do you not fear, O you who never once kept faith with his Lord, that he will say at some of your slips: "This is the parting between me and you"?

(Chapter Two: On the disagreement of people about the Garden in which Adam, upon him be peace, was made to dwell and from which he was sent down, whether it is the Garden of Eternity or another garden, in an elevated place on earth.)

Mundhir ibn Sa'id said in his commentary on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Dwell, you and your spouse, in the Garden﴾: One group said Allah made Adam dwell in the Garden of Eternity, which the believers enter on the Day of Resurrection.
Others said it is a different garden, which Allah made for him and settled him in; it is not the Garden of Eternity.
He said: this is a view supported by many proofs that point to it and necessitate holding it.
Abu al-Hasan al-Mawardi said in his commentary: "People differed about the Garden in which We settled him into two views:
One: that it is the Garden of Eternity.
Second: that it is a garden Allah the Exalted prepared for them both and made a trial, and it is not the Garden of Eternity which He made the house of recompense."
Those who held this view differed in two views:
One: that it is in the heaven, because He sent them down from it; this is the view of al-Hasan.
Second: that it is on earth, because He tested them there by prohibiting the tree they were forbidden, rather than other fruits; this is the view of Ibn Bahr. And that was after Iblis was commanded to prostrate to Adam, upon him be peace. And Allah knows best the correct view." This was his statement.
Ibn al-Khatib said in his well-known commentary: "They differed about the Garden mentioned in this verse: was it on earth or in heaven? And if it was in heaven, was it the Garden which is the abode of reward, the Garden of Eternity, or another garden?" Abu al-Qasim al-Balkhi and Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: "This Garden is on earth," and they interpreted the descent as moving from one place to another, as in His saying: ﴿Go down to a city﴾, and they argued for it with several points.
The second view, that of al-Jubba'i, is that the garden which was in heaven was the seventh heaven.
The third view, which is that of the majority of our companions, is that this Garden is the abode of reward. Abu al-Qasim al-Raghib said in his commentary: "They differed about the Garden in which Adam was settled. Some of the theologians said it was an orchard which Allah made for him as a trial, and it was not the Garden of Refuge." He mentioned some of the reasoning for both views.
Among those who also mentioned the disagreement was Abu 'Isa al-Rummani in his commentary; he chose that it is the Garden of Eternity, then said: "The position we have chosen is the view of al-Hasan, 'Amr, Wasil, and most of our companions; it is the view of Abu 'Ali and our teacher Abu Bakr, and it is the view of the people of tafsir." Ibn al-Khatib chose to suspend judgment on the matter and made it a fourth view, saying:
"The fourth view: that each is possible, and the proofs conflict, so suspension is required and definitive judgment is to be avoided." Mundhir ibn Sa'id said: the view that it is a garden on earth and not the Garden of Eternity is the view of Abu Hanifah and his companions. He said: "I have seen groups rise to oppose us regarding the garden of Adam, upon him be peace, by asserting their position without proof, relying only on claims and wishes. They did not bring any proof from the Book, the Sunnah, a narration from a Companion, a Follower, a follower of the Follower, whether connected or isolated, or well-known and anomalous.
We have shown them that the jurist of Iraq and those who follow his view said that Adam's garden is not the Garden of Eternity, and these registers are full of their knowledge, not known only to some anomalous scholars, but among the leaders of the opponents. I only say this so that it is known that I do not defend the school of Abu Hanifah; I defend only what evidence from the Qur'an and Sunnah has established for me."
"This is Ibn Zayd the Maliki, who says in his commentary: I asked Ibn Nafi' whether the Garden is created, and he said: silence about speaking on this is better." "This is Ibn 'Uyaynah, who says concerning the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed for you is that you will not hunger therein, nor be unclothed﴾" [Ta-Ha: 118-119]. He said: meaning on earth. Ibn Nafi' and Imam and Ibn 'Uyaynah are an imam; they do not bring us anyone like them, nor anyone who opposes their statement with their view.
"This is Ibn Qutaybah, who in the book al-Ma'arif, after mentioning God's creation of Adam and his wife, said: then He left them and said: 'Multiply and fill the earth, and dominate the fish of the seas, the birds of the sky, the cattle, and the plants and trees and fruits of the earth.' So He informed that His creation was in the earth and His command was in it. Then he said: 'He planted the Paradise, which divided into four rivers: Sayhun, Jayhun, the Tigris, and the Euphrates.' Then he mentioned the serpent and said: it was among the greatest of the land animals, and it said to the woman: 'Indeed you both will die if you eat from this tree.'
Then, after some discussion, he said: 'He removed him from the east of the Garden of Eden to the land from which he was taken.' Then he said: 'Wahb said: his descent, when he was sent down from the Garden of Eden, was in the east of the land of India. He said: Qabil carried his brother until he brought him to a valley of the valleys of Yemen, east of Aden, and he hid him there.' Another said, reported by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the saying 'Go down': it is as one says 'so-and-so descended to such-and-such a land.'"
Mundhir ibn Sa'id said: "This is Wahb ibn Munabbih relating that Adam, upon him be peace, was created on earth, lived on earth, and the Paradise was planted for him there; that it was in Aden, and that the four rivers divided from that river which was called the Paradise of Adam; and those rivers remain on earth, without disagreement among the Muslims about that. So take heed, O people of insight. He informed that the serpent that spoke to Adam was among the greatest land animals, and did not say among the greatest animals of the sky. They say the Garden was not on earth but above the seventh heaven."
Then he said: "And He removed him from the east of the Garden of Eden, and the Garden of Refuge has no east or west, for there is no sun in it."
Then he said: "And He removed him to the land from which he was taken, meaning He removed him from the Paradise planted for him in Eden, in the east of the land of India." These reports which Ibn Qutaybah related only point to the land of Yemen and to Aden, which is part of the land of Yemen, and he informed that God planted Paradise for Adam, upon him be peace, in Aden, then confirmed this by saying: 'the four rivers mentioned are divided from the river which was called the Paradise of Adam.'"
Mundhir said: "Ibn Qutaybah related, from Ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'Adam, at his death, longed for a cluster from the Garden in which he had been, according to their claim, on the back of the seventh heaven, while he was on earth. So his children went out seeking it for him, until the angels reached them with news of his death.' Then, if what Ibn Qutaybah related is true, Adam's children were, in your view, madmen, seeking for their father fruit of the Garden of Eternity on earth."
He said: "We have said nothing other than what these people said. Had the Garden been the Garden of Eternity, the eternal would be in it, and we have deduced from the Qur'an, while others have asserted without any proof."
This is a mention of some of the views of those who narrated the disagreement on this question. We will set out the arguments of both sides, God willing, and make clear to them what is for them and what is against them.

Chapter Three: On presenting the arguments of those who chose that it is the Garden of Eternity which people enter on the Day of Resurrection.
They said: "Our view is the one on which God created people, young and old; nothing else occurred to their hearts, and most of them know of no dispute about it."
They said: "Muslim related in his Sahih, from the narration of Abu Malik, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah; and Abu Malik from Rib'i, from Hudhayfah, both said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Allah the Exalted gathers the people, and the believers stand until the Garden is brought near to them, and they come to Adam and say: O our father, ask for the opening of the Garden for us. He says: Did not your father's sin remove you from the Garden?'" and he mentioned the hadith.
They said: "This shows that the Garden from which he was removed is the very same Garden from which he is asked to open the gate."

I need to translate this passage, but first a note on its coverage: it is a long Arabic text, and I will translate all of it faithfully below.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary, part 2 of 4, on surah 2, verse 35

It is in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) the hadith of the argument between Adam and Musa, and Musa's words: "You expelled us and yourself from the Garden." Even if it were on earth, they had come out of gardens, not out of the Garden. Likewise is the saying of Adam to the believers on the Day of Resurrection: "Did your father's sin expel you from the Garden?" His sin did not expel them from the gardens of this world.

They say: Allah the Exalted has said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden and eat therefrom in abundance wherever you will; but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers." Then Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and for you on earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time."﴾ This indicates that their descent was from the Garden to the earth, in two respects. The first is from the word "Go down," for it is a descent from a height to a lower place. The second is "and for you on earth is a dwelling place," following His saying "Go down," which shows that they had not been on earth before that. He confirmed this with His saying in Surat al-A'raf: ﴿He said, "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾ Had the Garden been on earth, their living in it would have been both before the expulsion and after it.

They say: Allah the Exalted has described the Garden of Adam with attributes that apply only to the Garden of Eternity, saying: ﴿Indeed, it is [granted] that you will not be hungry therein, nor naked, and that you will not be thirsty therein, nor be exposed to the sun.﴾ This does not occur in this world at all, for a man, even if he lives in its finest dwelling, must inevitably encounter something of these things. He contrasted hunger with thirst, and nakedness with exposure to the sun. Hunger is the humiliation of the inner self, nakedness is the humiliation of the outer self, thirst is the heat of the inner self, and exposure to the sun is the heat of the outer self. So He negated from its inhabitants the humiliation of the outer and inner self and the heat of the outer and inner self. This is better than contrasting hunger with thirst and nakedness with exposure to the sun, and this is the condition of the inhabitant of the Garden of Eternity.

They say: Also, if that Garden were in this world, Adam would have known that Iblis lied in his saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ For Adam knew that this world is finite and perishable, and that its kingdom decays.

They say: Also, this story in Surat al-Baqarah is very clear that the Garden from which they were expelled is above the heavens, for He the Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers. And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat therefrom in abundance wherever you will; but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers." Then Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, [all of you], as enemies to one another, and for you on earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time." Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ This is the descent of Adam, Eve and Iblis from the Garden, and therefore the plural pronoun is used in it. It has been said that the address is to the two of them and to the serpent, but this is very weak, since there is no mention of the serpent in any part of the story of Adam, and nothing in the context indicates it. It has been said that the address is to Adam and Eve, and the plural pronoun is used as in His saying: ﴿And We were witnesses to their judgment﴾, where the two are David and Solomon. It has also been said that it is to Adam, Eve and their offspring.

These views are weak, other than the first, because each is a claim without evidence, and the wording itself indicates otherwise. Thus it is established that Iblis is included in this address and that he is among those who were made to descend. Given this, He mentioned the descent a second time with His saying: ﴿We said, "Go down from it, all of you. And if there comes to you from Me guidance, then whoever follows My guidance – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve."﴾

The apparent meaning is that this second descent is different from the first: the second is a descent from the heaven to the earth, and the first is a descent from the Garden. In that case, the Garden from which they first descended, which is above the heaven, is the Garden of Eternity. Al-Zamakhshari thought that His saying "Go down from it, all of you" is addressed to Adam and Eve alone, and that the plural was used to include their offspring. He said: "The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿He said, 'Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others.'﴾" He said: "This is also indicated by His saying: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance – no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve. But those who disbelieve and deny Our signs – those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾" And this is nothing but a ruling that applies to all of mankind.

The meaning of His saying "some of you enemies to others" is what people have of enmity and transgression and misleading one another. This, which he chose, is the weakest of the views on the verse, for the enmity Allah mentioned is only between Adam and Iblis and their offspring, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾

He, the Exalted, has emphasized the matter of enmity between Satan and man, and repeated and reiterated its mention in the Qur'an because of the great need to guard against this enemy.

As for Adam and his wife, He has only informed in His Book that He created her so that he might find rest in her, and placed between them affection and mercy. So affection and mercy are between a man and his wife, and enmity is between a human being and Satan.

Adam, his wife and Iblis have been mentioned before, and they are three. Why then does the pronoun return to some of what was mentioned, despite its departure from the course of the discourse, rather than to all of it, while both the wording and the meaning require it? Thus al-Zamakhshari did nothing.

As for His saying in Surat Ta-Ha: ﴿He said, "Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others."﴾ This is an address to Adam and Eve, and He has made some of them enemies to others. The pronoun in "Go down from it" either refers to Adam and his wife, or to Adam and Iblis, and the wife is not mentioned because she follows him. On this basis, the enmity mentioned is between those addressed by the descent, namely Adam and Iblis, and the matter is clear. But according to the first view, the verse includes two matters:
The first: His command to Adam and his wife to descend.
The second: His informing of enmity between Adam and his wife on one side and Iblis on the other. This is why the plural pronoun is used in the second and not in the first. It is certain that Iblis must be included in the ruling of this enmity, as He said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife﴾, and He said to the offspring: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾

Consider how the passages in which enmity is mentioned all agree on the plural pronoun rather than the dual.

As for the descent, He sometimes mentions it with the plural, sometimes with the dual, and sometimes with the singular, as in His saying in Surat al-A'raf: ﴿He said, "Descend from it."﴾
Likewise in Surat Sad, and this is to Iblis alone.

Wherever it comes in the plural, it refers to Adam, his wife and Iblis, since the story revolves around them. Wherever it comes in the dual, it refers either to Adam and his wife, since they are the two who engaged in eating from the tree and committed the sin, or to Adam and Iblis, since they are the two fathers of the two species (humans and jinn) and the origin of the offspring. So their condition and the outcome of their affair are mentioned as an admonition and lesson for their children. Both views have been related on this.

What clarifies that the pronoun in His saying "Descend from it, all of you" refers to Adam and Iblis is that when Allah the Exalted mentioned the disobedience, He singled out Adam with it without his wife, saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him. He said, "Descend from it, all of you."﴾

This indicates that the one addressed by the descent is Adam and whoever embellished disobedience to him, and the wife is included as a follower. For the purpose is Allah the Exalted's informing the two species of what befell their two parents of the ill effects of disobedience and opposing the command. Mentioning their two parents is more effective in conveying this meaning than mentioning only the two parents of mankind.

Allah has informed of the wife that she ate with Adam, and He informed that He brought him down and expelled him from the Garden because of that eating. So it is known that the wife's ruling is the same, and that she came to the same state as Adam. And directing attention to the condition of the two parents of both species is more fitting than directing it to the father and mother of mankind alone. So reflect on this.

They say: Also, the Garden is mentioned with the definite article in all instances, as in His saying: ﴿Dwell, you and your wife﴾ and its like. No Garden that the addressees know and recognize is meant except the Garden of Eternity, which the Merciful promised His servants in the unseen. This name has thus become a proper name for it by dominance, like "the City," "the Star," "the House," "the Book," and similar. Wherever its word comes definite, it refers to the known Garden, familiar in the hearts of believers. If another garden is meant, it comes indefinite, or restricted by an annexation, or restricted by the context in a way that indicates it is a garden on earth:
The first, like His saying: "two gardens of grapes."
The second, like His saying: "Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say..."
The third, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the companions of the Garden.﴾

They say: Among what indicates that the Garden of Adam is the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa) is what Hawdhah ibn Khalifah related from 'Awf, from Qasamah ibn Zuhayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: "When Allah the Exalted expelled Adam from the Garden, He provided him with fruits of the Garden and taught him the craft of everything. So these fruits of yours are from the fruits of the Garden, except that these change and those do not change."

They say: Allah the Exalted has guaranteed him, if he repents to Him and turns back to Him, that He will return him to it, as related by al-Minhal from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance.﴾ He said: "O Lord, did You not create me with Your hand?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Lord, did You not breathe into me of Your spirit?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Lord, did You not settle me in Your Garden?" He said: "Yes." He said: "O Lord, did Your mercy not precede Your wrath?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do You see that if I repent and reform, You will return me to the Garden?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is His saying: 'Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance.'" It has several chains from Ibn 'Abbas, and in some of them: Adam said to his Lord when he disobeyed Him, "My Lord, if I repent and reform," and his Lord said to him, "I will return you to the Garden."

This is some of what those who say it is the Garden of Eternity have argued. We now set forth the arguments of the others.

Chapter Four: On presenting the arguments of the group who said it is not the Garden of Eternity but a garden on earth.

They say: This is a view for which the indications supporting it are numerous, so we mention some of them. They said: Allah the Exalted has informed through all His messengers that entry into the Garden of Eternity will only be on the Day of Resurrection, and that time of entry has not yet come. Allah the Exalted has described it for us in His Book with its attributes, and it is impossible that Allah the Exalted describes something with an attribute and that thing is other than the attribute by which He described it.

They said: We find that Allah the Exalted described the Garden prepared for the righteous as "the abode of permanence," so whoever enters it remains in it. Adam did not remain in the Garden he entered, yet He described it as the Garden of Eternity, and Adam was not made eternal in it. He described it as a place of reward and recompense, not a place of obligation, command and prohibition. He described it as an abode of absolute safety, not a place of trial and testing, yet Adam was tested in it with the greatest trial. He described it as an abode in which no one disobeys Allah ever, yet Adam disobeyed his Lord in the Garden he entered. He described it as not a place of fear or grief, yet the two parents experienced in it as much fear and grief as they did. He named it the abode of peace, yet the two parents were not safe in it from temptation; and the abode of settlement, yet they did not settle in it. He said of its residents: ﴿They will not be removed from it﴾, yet the two parents were expelled from it. He said: ﴿No fatigue will touch them therein﴾, yet Adam fled in haste and fear and began to tie leaves of the Garden upon himself, and this is exactly fatigue. He informed that there is no idle talk therein nor sin, yet Adam heard in it the idle talk and sin of Iblis. He informed that they will not hear therein idle talk or lying, yet Adam heard in it the lie of Iblis. He named it "a seat of truth," yet Iblis lied in it and swore to his lie.

Allah the Exalted said to the angels: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will make upon the earth a successive authority"﴾, and did not say "I will place in the Garden of Refuge." Then the angels said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood?﴾ And it is impossible that this was in the Garden of Refuge.

Allah the Exalted informed that Iblis said to Adam: "Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" If Allah the Exalted had settled Adam in the Garden of Eternity and the kingdom that does not decay, how could he not reply to him, saying, "How can you direct me to something I am already in, and I have been given it?" And Allah the Exalted had not informed Adam, when He settled him in the Garden, that he would be there among the eternal. Had he known it was the abode of eternity, he would not have inclined to Iblis's words or leaned toward his advice; rather, since he was in a place that was not an abode of eternity, he was deceived by what Iblis offered him of immortality.

They said: If Adam had been settled in the Garden of Eternity, the abode of holiness which only a pure and sanctified being inhabits, how did the accursed, filthy, blameworthy, expelled Iblis gain access to it, so that he tempted Adam and whispered to him? That whispering was either in his heart or in his ear, and under either assumption, how did the accursed one reach the entry of the abode of the righteous? Also, after it was said to him, "Descend from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein," would he be permitted to ascend to the Garden of Refuge above the seventh heaven, after being cursed, distanced, rebuked and expelled for his transgression and arrogance? Does this fit His saying: ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾? If his address to Adam with what he addressed him and his oath to him was not arrogance, what then is arrogance?

If you say: perhaps his whispering reached the two parents while he was on earth and they were above the heaven in 'Illiyyin, this is not sound linguistically, sensorially, or customarily. And if you claim that he entered the belly of the serpent until he conveyed the whispering to them, that is also refuted, for how would he ascend after the descent to enter the Garden, even if in the belly of a serpent?

And if you say that he entered their hearts and whispered to them, the objection still stands. Also, Allah the Exalted related His address to them as speech they heard face to face: "What has your Lord forbidden you from this tree?" This indicates that He was witnessing them and the tree. And since Adam was outside the Garden and no longer resident in it, Allah said to him: ﴿Did I not forbid you from that tree?﴾ and did not say "this tree." So when He said to them, "What has your Lord forbidden you from this tree," as He fed them in His dominion and in the eternity of its abode, He used the demonstrative with the proximal form, bringing it near and present to them. But when Allah, their Lord, said to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree," and when He intended to expel them from it, He used the demonstrative with the distal and absent form, as though nothing of the Garden remained to them, not even seeing the tree they had been forbidden. Also, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾, and the accursed one's whispering is among the most wicked words, so it does not ascend to the place of holiness.

Mundhir said: It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ that Adam, peace be upon him, slept in his Garden. But the Garden of Eternity has no sleep, by the text and the consensus of the Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ was asked, "Do the people of Paradise sleep?" He said: "No. Sleep is the brother of death, and sleep is a death." The Qur'an has also expressed this, and death is a change of state, while the abode of peace is free from changes of state, and the sleeper is dead or like the dead.

I say: The hadith he alluded to is well known to be a mawquf report, from the narration of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid, who said: "Hawwa' was created from Adam's rib while he was sleeping."

Asbat related from al-Suddi: Adam, peace be upon him, was settled in the Garden, and he used to walk in it, lonely, with no wife to find rest with. He slept a sleep, then woke, and beside his head was a woman sitting, whom Allah had created from his rib. He asked her, "What are you?" She said, "A woman." He said, "Why were you created?" She said, "So that you may find rest in me."

Ibn Ishaq related from Ibn 'Abbas: Allah cast drowsiness upon Adam, peace be upon him, then took one of his ribs from his left side and filled its place with flesh. Adam was asleep and did not awaken from his sleep until Allah had created from his rib that wife, Hawwa', and made her a woman with whom he would find rest. When the drowsiness was lifted from him and he awoke from his sleep, he saw her beside him, and said: "Flesh of my flesh, and blood of my blood, and spirit of my spirit," and he found rest in her.

They say: There is no dispute that Allah the Exalted created Adam on earth, and He never mentions in any place at all that He later transported him to the heaven. If He had transported him to the heaven, this would have been more worthy of mention, for it is among the greatest signs and among the greatest blessings upon him, since it was an ascension of his body and soul from the earth to above the heavens.

They said: "How could He, glory be to Him, move him [Adam] and settle him above the heavens, when He had told His angels that He was placing a successor (khalifah) on the earth? And how could He settle him in the Abode of Eternity (dar al-khuld), whoever enters which lives forever and does not leave it?" The Exalted said: ﴿And they will not be removed from it﴾.

They said: "There was no matter in dispute between us except that God, glory be to Him, cast Iblis down from the heaven when he refused to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him. This was a decree of creation (amr takwin) that cannot be contradicted. Then God caused Adam, peace be upon him, to enter the Garden after this, for the command to prostrate came immediately after his creation without any interval. So if the Garden were above the heavens, Iblis would have had no way to ascend to it, since he had been cast down from it."

As for those estimates you have made, they are manifest artifices: such as the statement of one who says it is possible that he ascended to it briefly, not to settle there; the statement of one who says the serpent carried him in; the statement of one who says he entered into its bellies; and the statement of one who says his whispering could reach them while he was on earth and they were above the heavens. The extreme strain and far-fetched artifice in this is not hidden. Our view is different: when He cast him down from the dominion of the heavens because he did not prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him, He caused enmity to be instilled in him. So when He settled Adam in His Garden, his enemy envied him, and he strove with his scheming and deception to get him expelled from it. And God knows best.

They said: "Among what indicates that the Garden of Adam was not the Garden of Eternity promised to the righteous is that when God created him, He informed him that his life had a term at which it would end, and that He had not created him for permanence. This is as al-Tirmidhi related in his Jami', from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'When God created Adam, peace be upon him, and breathed the spirit into him, he sneezed and said, "Praise be to God," so he praised God with His permission. His Lord said to him, "May God have mercy on you, O Adam. Go to those angels, to a group of them sitting, and say, 'Peace be upon you.'" They replied, "And upon you peace..." etc.' Then he returned to his Lord and said, 'This is your greeting and the greeting of your children among themselves.' God said to him, while His hands were closed: 'Choose whichever of them you wish.' He said: 'I choose the right hand of my Lord, and both hands of my Lord are right hands, blessed.' Then He opened it, and there were Adam and his offspring in it. He said: 'O Lord, who are these?' He said: 'These are your descendants.' Then every person's lifespan was written between his eyes. Among them was a man who was the brightest of them. He said: 'O Lord, who is this?' He said: 'This is your son David, whose lifespan I have written as forty years.' He said: 'O Lord, increase his lifespan.' He said: 'That is what I have written for him.' He said: 'O my Lord, then I give him sixty years from my lifespan.' He said: 'You and that.' Then He let him dwell in the Garden as long as He willed, then he was cast down from it. Adam, peace be upon him, used to count his own years. Then the Angel of Death came to him, and Adam said: 'You have hastened; a thousand years have been written for me.' He said: 'Yes, but you gave your son David sixty years.' So he denied it, and his descendants denied it; he forgot, and his descendants forgot. From that day on, writing and witnesses were ordained.'" He said: this is a hasan gharib hadith from this route, and it has been related from Abu Hurayrah by other routes.

They said: "This is explicit that Adam, peace be upon him, was not created in the abode of permanence, which no one who enters it dies, but was created in the abode of perishing, for which God appointed a known term for it and its inhabitants, and in it He settled him."

If it is said: "If Adam, peace be upon him, knew that he had an appointed lifespan and an end to which it would come, and that he was not among the immortals, how did he not know that Iblis was lying when he said, ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld)?﴾ and ﴿or you become of the immortals﴾?"

The answer is in two respects. First, khuld does not imply perpetuity and permanence, but rather a long stay, as will come. Second, when Iblis swore to him, deceived him, and made him covet immortality, he forgot what had been decreed for his lifespan.

They said: "Furthermore, it is known, which no Muslim disputes, that God, glory be to Him, created Adam, peace be upon him, from the dust of this earth, and informed that He created him from an extract of clay (sulalah min tin), and that He created him from clay like pottery (salsal) from black decayed mud (hama masnun). It has been said that salsal is that which has a dry clattering sound, and it has been said that it is that whose smell has changed, from their saying sall al-lahm when meat changed. Hama is black mud that has changed, and masnun is poured. All these are stages of the dust which is his first origin, just as He informed of the stages of the creation of offspring: from a drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh. He, glory be to Him and exalted, did not inform that He raised him from the earth above the heavens, neither before shaping nor after. So where is the proof that indicates the elevation of his matter, or his elevation after his creation? This is something for which you have no evidence, nor is it a necessary consequence of what God has informed?"

They said: "It is known that what is above the heavens is not a place for earthly clay whose smell has changed, which has become foul from its change. The place of this earth is the place of changing and corrupting things. As for what is above the spheres, change, stench, corruption, and transformation do not reach it. This is a matter about which intelligent people have no doubt."

They said: "God, the Exalted, has said: ﴿As for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift never cut off﴾. So He informed that the gift of the Garden of eternity is not cut off."

They said: "So when what God has informed is combined, namely that He created him from the earth, and made him a successor on the earth, and that Iblis whispered to him in the place where He had settled him after casting him down from the heaven because of his refusal to prostrate to him, and that He informed His angels that He was placing a successor on the earth, and that the Garden of eternity is an abode of recompense and reward for the trial and obligations, and that there is no idle talk in it, nor sin, nor lying, and that whoever enters it does not leave it, nor despairs, nor grieves, nor fears, nor sleeps, and that God has forbidden it to the disbelievers, and Iblis is the head of disbelief: when all this is combined, part with part, and the fair-minded person ponders it, whom the banner of evidence has been raised for, and who aspires to it with himself out of the lowland of imitation, the truth becomes clear to him. And God is the Granter of success."

They said: "Even if the matter contained nothing but that the Garden is not an abode of obligation, while God, glory be to Him, obligated the two parents, prohibiting them from eating from the tree, this indicates that it is an abode of obligation, not of recompense and eternity. This too is among the arguments this group has used for their view. And God knows best."

Chapter Five: On the response of the proponents of this view to the proponents of the first view.

They said: "As for your statement that our view is that upon which God created His servants, such that they know nothing else, the matter is one known only through revelation (sam'iyyah), known only through the reports of the messengers. We and you have taken this only from the Qur'an, not from reason or innate nature (fitrah). So what is relied upon in it is what the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger indicate. We demand from you a single companion, follower, or sound or good report that it is the Garden of eternity itself which God prepared for the believers. You will not find a way to that. We have brought you from the words of the early generations what indicates the opposite. But since the Garden was mentioned in absolute terms in this narrative and agreed with the name of the Garden that God prepared for His servants in its general application and some of its attributes, many illusions went to the view that it is the same. If you mean by innate nature only this much, it has benefited you nothing. If you mean that God created people upon this, as He created them upon the goodness of justice and the ugliness of injustice and other innate matters, then it is a false claim. When we return to our innate nature, we do not find our knowledge of it like our knowledge of the necessity of obligations and the impossibility of impossibilities."

As for your proof from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, and Adam's saying, ﴿Did He expel you from it except for the sin of your father?﴾, it only indicates that Adam, peace be upon him, was later in finding the sin repugnant, a sin he had committed earlier in the worldly abode, and that because of that sin he was expelled from the Garden, as in the other wording: "I was forbidden from eating from the tree, and I ate from it." Where in this is anything indicating that it was the Garden of refuge (jannat al-ma'wa), by correspondence, implication, or necessary consequence? Likewise Musa's saying to him, ﴿You expelled us and yourself from the Garden﴾: he did not say, "from the Garden of eternity."

As for your statement that they went out to orchards of the same kind as the Garden on earth, the name "Garden" applies to those orchards, but between them and the Garden of Adam is what only God knows. They are like a prison compared to it. Their sharing in being on earth does not negate their difference, which is of the greatest degree in all things.

As for your proof from His saying, ﴿And We said: Go down﴾, following their expulsion from the Garden, the word "descend" (al-hubut) does not necessitate descent from heaven to earth. At most it indicates descent from a high place to a lower one, and this is not objectionable, for it was a garden on high ground on the earth, so they went down from it to the earth. We have shown that the command was addressed to Adam, peace be upon him, his wife, and their enemy. If the Garden were in heaven, their enemy could not have been present in it after his first casting down, since he had refused to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him. So this verse is also among the clearest proofs against you, and the various strained and artificial ways you have estimated do not avail you, as has already been mentioned.

As for His saying, ﴿And for you on the earth is a dwelling place and enjoyment for a time﴾, this does not indicate that they were not on the earth before that, for "earth" is a generic noun. They were in its highest, best, and most excellent part, in a place where hunger, nakedness, thirst, and the heat of the sun did not reach them. Then they were sent down to an earth where all these occur, and where their life and death and their emergence from graves take place. The Garden in which We settled them was not a place of toil, fatigue, or harm. The earth to which they were sent down is the place of toil, fatigue, harm, and all kinds of hardships.

As for your statement that He described it with attributes that do not exist in this world, the answer is that those attributes do not exist in the earth to which they were sent down. From where do you know that they do not exist in the earth from which they were sent down?

As for your statement that Adam, peace be upon him, knew that the world is finite and perishing, so if the Garden were in it he would have known that Iblis was lying in his saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity?﴾

The answer is in two respects. First: the word only indicates khuld, which is more general than the permanence that has no end, for in the language it means a long stay, and the stay of each thing is according to its nature. From it comes the saying, "a man is mukhalladd" when he has aged and grown old. From it also comes the saying that the stones of hearths are khawalid (lasting) because of the length of their remaining after the traces of the encampments have faded. The poet said:

"Nothing but ashes, still and cold, which the winds have swept away, sooty and lasting."

A parallel to this is their use of "ancient" (qadim) for what has long been known, even though it has a beginning, as God says: ﴿Like the old withered palm stalk﴾, ﴿Indeed you are in your ancient error﴾, and ﴿an ancient lie﴾. God has also applied "eternal" (khulud) to the punishment of the Fire for some sinners, such as the one who kills himself, and the Prophet ﷺ applied it to the one who kills himself.

Second: knowledge of the cessation of the world and the coming of the Hereafter is known only through revelation, and no prophethood had preceded Adam, peace be upon him, through which he could know this.
