Although God did raise him up, inspire him, and send down scrolls to him, as in the hadith of Abu Dhar, this was after his casting down to the earth, by the explicit text of the Qur'an. God said: ﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others. Then, if guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray nor be wretched﴾. Likewise in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿We said: Go down from it, all of you. Then, if guidance comes to you from Me...﴾

As for your statement that the Garden is mentioned in definite form with the article, not meaning the Garden of eternity with certainty, as in His saying: ﴿We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore they would surely harvest it in the morning﴾, and your statement that the context here indicates that it was a garden on earth:

We say: the proofs we have mentioned indicate that the Garden of Adam, peace be upon him, was on earth, and therefore we have come to its implication, since it is not permissible to suspend the indication of a sound proof.

As for your proof from the report of Abu Musa, that God brought Adam, peace be upon him, out of the Garden and provided him with some of its fruits, it contains nothing beyond what the Qur'an indicates, except his taking provision from it, and this does not necessitate that it was the Garden of eternity.

As for your statement that these fruits change and those do not: from where do you know that the Garden in which Adam was settled was one where change befell its fruits as it befalls these fruits? It is established in the authentic hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Were it not for the Children of Israel, meat would not spoil," meaning it would not change or become foul. And God, the Exalted, has preserved in this world the food and drink of the Mighty (al-Aziz) for a hundred years without change.

As for your statement that God, glory be to Him, guaranteed Adam, peace be upon him, that if he repented He would return him to the Garden: there is no doubt that the matter is so. But it is not known that the guarantee refers to his return to that very Garden. Rather, if He returned him to the Garden of eternity, He has fulfilled His guarantee in full. The word "return" does not necessitate going back to the exact former state, its time, or its place, nor even to its likeness, as Shu'ayb said to his people: ﴿We would have invented a lie against God if we returned to your religion after God has rescued us from it. It is not for us to return to it, except that God our Lord wills. Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾. And God has made the one who declares his wife unlawful (zihar) to return by his intention to have intercourse a second time, or by the intercourse itself, or by refraining, and each of these is other than the first, not the same as it. This is what this group answered to those who disputed with them.

Chapter Six: On the response of those who claimed it was the Garden of eternity to what their opponents argued.

They said: "As for your statement that God, glory be to Him, informed that the Garden of eternity is entered only on the Day of Resurrection, and that the time of entering it has not yet come: this is true regarding absolute entry, which is entry of settlement and permanence. But temporary entry occurs before the Day of Resurrection. The Prophet ﷺ entered the Garden on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey), and the spirits of the believers and martyrs are in the Garden in the barzakh (intermediate state between death and resurrection). This is other than the entry that God informed of on the Day of Resurrection. So entry into eternity happens only on the Day of Resurrection. From where do you know that absolute entry does not occur in this world? With this the answer to your argument from its being the abode of permanence and the abode of eternity is clear."

They said: "As for your argument from all the other attributes you mentioned of the Garden, that they did not exist in Adam's Garden, such as nakedness, toil, grief, idle talk, lying, and others: all this is true, and neither we nor anyone among the people of Islam deny it.

But this applies when the believers enter it on the Day of Resurrection, as the context of all the verses indicates, for the negation of that is linked to the believers' entering it. This does not negate that there was in it, between the two parents of the two weighty ones (thaqalayn: humans and jinn), what God, glory be to Him and exalted, related of that. Then the matter will, upon the believers' entry, become what God has informed about it. So there is no contradiction between the two matters."

As for your statement that it is an abode of recompense and reward, not an abode of obligation, and that God obligated Adam by forbidding him to eat from that tree, indicating that that Garden was an abode of obligation, not an abode of eternity: the answer is in two respects.

First: it is impossible for it to be an abode of obligation only when the believers enter it on the Day of Resurrection, for then obligation ends. As for obligation occurring in it in the worldly abode, there is no proof at all that this is impossible. How could it be, when it has been established from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Last night I entered the Garden and saw a woman performing ablution beside a palace, so I said, 'To whom do you belong?'" The hadith continues.

It is not impossible that there are in it those who act by God's command and worship God before the Day of Resurrection. Indeed this is the reality, for those who are in it now are obeying commands from their Lord and do not transgress them, whether that is called obligation or not.

Second: obligation in it was not with the deeds that people are obligated to in this world, such as fasting, prayer, jihad, and the like. It was only a prohibition regarding one tree among its many trees, either that one in particular or its kind. This degree is not impossible to occur in the abode of eternity, just as each one is forbidden to approach the family of another in it. If you mean by its not being an abode of obligation that such a thing cannot occur in it at any time, there is no proof for that. If you mean that the obligations of this world are absent from it, that is true, but it does not support your claim.

As for your argument from Adam's sleeping in it, while the people of the Garden do not sleep: if the report of Adam's sleeping is established, it negates sleep from its people only on the day of entering eternity, when they will not die. Before that, it does not.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 35 (part 4 of 4):

As for your argument from the story of Iblis's whispering to him (Adam) after his descent and expulsion from heaven, by God, it is among the strongest and clearest evidences for the soundness of your view. Those far-fetched explanations of his entering Paradise and ascending to heaven after God had sent him down from it are not accepted by any fair-minded person. Yet it is not impossible that he ascended there as a temporary ascent, to fulfil the trial and test that God had decreed and whose causes He had ordained, even though that place was not his permanent, settled abode as it had been. God, glorified is He, has informed us that the devils used to take up positions in heaven before the mission of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to eavesdrop, and they would overhear something of the revelation. This is an ascent to that place, but it is a temporary ascent, and they did not settle in the place to which they ascended. This is consistent with His words, ﴿Go down, some of you being enemies to others﴾. There is no contradiction between this ascent and the command to descend. This is a possibility, and God knows best.

As for your argument that God informed Adam (peace be upon him) of the length of his lifespan, and what you mentioned of the hadith and the way you derived the proof from it, the answer is that his being informed of that does not contradict his being admitted into the Garden of Eternity and made to dwell in it for a period. As for God's informing us that whoever enters it does not die and does not leave it, that refers to the Day of Resurrection.

As for your argument that he was created from earth, there is no doubt about that. But from where do you know that his creation was completed there? It has been reported in some narrations that God cast him at the gate of Paradise for forty mornings, and Iblis would go around him saying, "For what purpose were you created?" When he saw that he was hollow, he knew that this was a creature he could not control. He said, "If I am given power over him, I will destroy him; and if he is given power over me, I will disobey him." Moreover, God's words, ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them; then He presented them to the angels and said, "Tell Me the names of these, if you are truthful." They said, "Glory be to You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise." He said, "O Adam, inform them of their names." And when he had informed them of their names, He said, "Did I not tell you that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal?"﴾ indicates that he was with them in heaven when he informed them of those names. Otherwise, they had not all descended to earth to hear it from him. Had his creation been completed on earth, it would not be impossible for God to raise him up to heaven for a matter He had planned and decreed, and then return him to earth. Indeed, He raised up the Messiah to heaven and will send him down to earth before the Day of Resurrection. And the Prophet (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey with his body and spirit up above the heavens. This is the answer of those who say it is the Garden of Eternity, to their opponents. And God knows best.

Chapter Seven: On mentioning the arguments of those who claimed that Paradise has not yet been created.

They said: If Paradise were created now, it would necessarily follow that it would perish on the Day of Resurrection, and everything in it would be destroyed and die, based on God's words, ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾, and ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾. Thus the Houris (ḥūr ʿīn, the wide-eyed maidens of Paradise) in it would die, as would the wildan (immortal young boys of Paradise). Yet God has informed us that it is the abode of eternity, and those in it are immortal and will not die there. And God's report cannot be contradicted or abrogated.

They said: Al-Tirmidhi has narrated in his Jami' (collection of hadith) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God said: "I met Abraham on the night I was taken on the Night Journey, and he said, 'O Muhammad, convey my greetings of peace to your community, and inform them that Paradise has pure soil and sweet water, that it is a plain (qiʿān), and that its plants are: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar.'" He said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Also in the same work, from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever says, 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi' (Glory be to God and praise be to Him), a palm tree will be planted for him in Paradise." He said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

They said: If Paradise were created and completed, it would not be a plain, and this planting would have no meaning. They also said: God has said, quoting the wife of Pharaoh, ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾. It is impossible for anyone to say to one who has woven cloth for him or built him a house, "Weave for me a cloth and build me a house." Even more explicit than this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever builds a mosque for God, God will build him a house in Paradise." (Agreed upon.)

This is a compound sentence of condition and consequence, which by the consensus of the grammarians of Arabic requires that the consequence occurs after the condition. This is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) through the transmission of ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, Anas ibn Malik, and ʿAmr ibn ʿAnbasa.

They said: There have also been reports that the angels plant in it and build for the servant as long as he is working, and when he slackens, the angel also ceases working.

They said: Ibn Hibban has narrated in his Sahih, and Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, who said: The Messenger of God said: "When God takes the child of a servant, He says, 'O Angel of Death, you have taken the child of My servant, you have taken the coolness of his eye and the fruit of his heart.' He says, 'Yes.' He says, 'What did he say?' He says, 'He praised You and said, "Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un."' He says, 'Build for him a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.'"

And in the Musnad, from his hadith also, he said: The Messenger of God said: "Whoever prays twelve rak'ahs in a day and night other than the obligatory prayers, God will build for him a house in Paradise."

They said: This is not the saying of the people of innovation and Mu'tazilism as you claim. Ibn Muzin has mentioned in his tafsir (Qur'anic commentary), from Ibn Nafi', who is one of the imams of the Sunnah, that he was asked whether Paradise is created, and he said, "Silence about this is better." And God knows best.

Ibn al-Qayyim, *al-Tafsir al-Qayyim*, on Surah al-Baqarah (2), verse 36:

Al-Zamakhshari thought that His saying ﴿Go down from it, all of you﴾ is addressed to Adam and Eve specifically, and that He used the plural for them because it includes their offspring.

He said: The evidence for this is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾. He said: What confirms this is His saying: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance, no fear will there be upon them, nor will they grieve. And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

This is nothing but a ruling that applies to all people. And the meaning of His saying ﴿some of you enemies to others﴾ is the mutual hostility and oppression that people practise, and the misguiding of one another.

This view that he chose is the weakest of the opinions on the verse.

The enmity that God mentions is between Adam and Iblis and their offspring, as He said: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ He, glorified is He, has emphasised the matter of enmity between Satan and man, and repeated and reiterated its mention in the Qur'an because of the great need to guard against this enemy. As for Adam and his wife, He only informed us in His Book that He created her for him so that he might find rest in her, and placed between them affection and mercy.

So affection and mercy are between a man and his wife, and enmity is between Satan and man. Adam, his wife and Iblis have already been mentioned, and they are three. So why would the pronoun refer to some of what was mentioned, despite this being contrary to the course of the discourse, rather than to all of it? Yet the wording and the meaning both require it. Thus al-Zamakhshari has achieved nothing.

As for His saying in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾, this is addressed to Adam and Eve. Some of them became enemies to others, so the pronoun in His saying *ihbiṭā minhā* (اهْبِطا مِنها, "go down from it," dual) either refers to Adam and his wife, or refers to Adam and Iblis, and the wife is not mentioned because she is a follower of him.

On this basis, the enmity mentioned is for those addressed with the descent, namely Adam and Iblis, and the matter is clear.

As for the first reading, namely that it refers to Adam and his wife, the verse then contains two matters:

One: His command to Adam and his wife to descend.

Two: His informing of the enmity between Adam and his wife on one side and Iblis on the other. That is why He used the plural pronoun in the second matter, but not in the first. And it is certain that Iblis must be included in the ruling of this enmity, as He said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife﴾, and He said to their offspring: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾

Consider how the passages in which enmity is mentioned all agree on the plural pronoun rather than the dual.

As for the descent, He sometimes mentions it with the plural form, sometimes with the dual form, and sometimes with the singular form, as in His saying in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿He said: Go down from it﴾ (singular).

Likewise in Surah Sad, and this is for Iblis alone.

Wherever it occurs in the plural form, it refers to Adam, his wife and Iblis, since the story revolves around them. Wherever it occurs in the dual form, it either refers to Adam and his wife, since they are the two who directly ate from the tree and undertook the disobedience,

or it refers to Adam and Iblis, since they are the two fathers of the two species (humans and jinn) and the origins of the offspring. So their condition and the outcome of their affair are mentioned as an admonition and lesson for their descendants. Both views have been related regarding this.

What clarifies that the pronoun in His saying ﴿Go down from it, both of you, all of you﴾ refers to Adam and Iblis is that when God mentioned the disobedience, He singled out Adam without his wife, saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance and guided him. He said: Go down from it, all of you﴾. This indicates that the one addressed with the descent is Adam and whoever beautified disobedience for him, and the wife entered as a follower. The purpose is God's informing the two species (jinn and humans) of what befell their two parents from the ill omen of disobedience and opposing the command. Mentioning their two parents is more effective in conveying this meaning than mentioning only the two parents of mankind.

He, glorified is He, has informed us that the wife ate together with Adam, and that He sent him down and expelled him from Paradise because of that same eating. So it is known that the wife's ruling is the same, and that she went to what Adam went to. And directing the attention to the condition of the two parents of the two species is more fitting than directing it only to the father and mother of mankind. So reflect upon it.

In summary: His saying ﴿Go down, some of you enemies to others﴾ is clearly plural, so it is not permissible to apply it to the dual in His saying ﴿Go down (dual)﴾ without a valid reason.

(A grand benefit)

Sahl ibn Abd Allah said: Abandoning a command before God is greater than committing a prohibited act, because Adam was forbidden to eat from the tree, so he ate from it, and God accepted his repentance; and Iblis was commanded to prostrate to Adam, so he did not prostrate, and God did not accept his repentance.

I say: This is a great matter with significant standing, namely that abandoning commands is greater before God than committing prohibitions, and that is for several reasons:

The first is what Sahl mentioned concerning the case of Adam and the enemy of God, Iblis.

The second: the sin of committing a prohibition generally arises from desire and need, whereas the sin of abandoning a command generally arises from arrogance and pride. No one whose heart contains an atom's weight of arrogance will enter Paradise, and whoever dies upon *tawhid* (monotheism) will enter it even if he committed adultery and theft.

The third: doing what is commanded is more beloved to God than abstaining from what is forbidden, as the texts indicate. Such as His saying (ﷺ): "The most beloved of deeds to God is prayer at its proper time," and his saying (ﷺ): "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your Sovereign, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than meeting your enemy and striking their necks and them striking yours?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of God." He said: "The remembrance of God." And his saying (ﷺ): "Know that the best of your deeds is the prayer," and other texts. Abstaining from prohibitions is indeed a deed, for it is the restraining of the self from action. This is why God, glorified is He, linked love to the performance of commands, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in a row, as if they were a solid structure﴾; ﴿And God loves the doers of good﴾; His saying ﴿And act justly; indeed, God loves those who act justly﴾; ﴿And God loves the patient﴾. As for the side of prohibitions, the negation of love mostly occurs, as in His saying ﴿And God does not love corruption﴾; His saying ﴿God does not love every arrogant boaster﴾; His saying ﴿And do not transgress; indeed, God does not love transgressors﴾; His saying ﴿God does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾; His saying ﴿Indeed, God does not love one who is self-conceited and boastful﴾, and the like.

In another place He informed that He dislikes and is displeased by them, as in His saying ﴿All of that, its evil is hateful in the sight of your Lord﴾, and His saying ﴿That is because they followed what displeased God﴾.

Having understood this, doing what He loves is intended for its own sake. This is why He decrees what He dislikes and is displeased by, because it leads to what He loves. Just as He decreed sins, disbelief and wickedness, because of what results from their decree that He loves: jihad, the taking of martyrs, the repentance of the servant, his humbling himself and submission before Him, the manifestation of His justice, His pardon, His retribution, His might, the realisation of loyalty and enmity for His sake, and other effects which come about because of His decreeing what He dislikes. He loves these more than their removal by the removal of their causes. He, glorified is He, does not decree what He loves because it leads to the occurrence of what He dislikes and is displeased by, as He decrees what He dislikes because it leads to what He loves. Thus it is known that doing what He loves is more beloved to Him than what He dislikes.

(Section)

If it is said: What is the wisdom and benefit in the expulsion of Adam from Paradise to the abode of trial and testing?

The answer is to say: God, glorified is He, has in this many wisdoms, and in it is every kind of blessing and benefit, which minds are unable to know in detail even if they exhausted all their powers in knowing it. The descent of Adam and his expulsion from Paradise was difficult to accept, so that he might return to it in the best of his conditions. He, glorified is He, created him only to make him and his descendants inhabit the earth, and to make them successors, each succeeding the other. So He made them successors that He might command them, forbid them and test them. Paradise is not an abode of trial and obligation. So He brought out the two parents to the abode from which they were created and in which they were, so that they might provision themselves from it for the abode for which they were created. When they fulfil the obligation of the abode of duty, and endure its toil, they will know the value of that abode, its nobility and its excellence. Had they grown up in that abode, they would not have known the measure of His blessing upon them in it. So He settled them in the abode of testing, and exposed them there to His command and prohibition, so that they might attain by obedience the best of His reward and His honour. It was possible for them to have obtained lasting bliss there, but what is obtained after trial and testing, the suffering of death and what follows it, the terrors of the Resurrection, and crossing the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), is another kind of bliss, whose value cannot be perceived, and which is more perfect than the bliss of those created in Paradise among the young boys and the wide-eyed maidens, in no way comparable to it.

Among the wisdoms in this is that He, glorified is He, willed to take from the descendants of Adam messengers, prophets and martyrs, whom He loves and who love Him, to whom He sends down His books, with whom He makes His covenant, and whom He makes servants to Him in ease and hardship, preferring His love and His good pleasure over their desires and what they love and crave. So His wisdom required that He send them down to an abode in which He tests them with what He tests them, so that through that trial they might perfect the ranks of their servitude, and worship Him with what their souls dislike. That is pure servitude. For whoever worships God only with what he loves and desires is in reality worshipping himself. He, glorified is He, loves that His friends should show loyalty for His sake, show enmity for His sake, and spend their souls in seeking His good pleasure and His love. All of this cannot be attained in the abode of absolute bliss.

Among the wisdoms in His expulsion of him from Paradise is what was previously pointed out, namely that the divine names require their objects and what is related to them, such as the Forgiving, the Merciful, the Accepter of repentance, the Pardoner, the Avenger, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Honourer, the Humiliator, the Giver of life, the Bringer of death, and the Inheritor. The effect of these names must become manifest and their related objects must exist. So His wisdom required that the descent of the two parents from Paradise should take place, so that the requirement of His names and attributes might become manifest in them and in their descendants. Had the descendants been raised in Paradise, the effects of these names and their objects would have been lost, and the divine perfection refuses that, for He is the True King, the Manifest. A king is one who commands, forbids, honours, humiliates, rewards, punishes, gives, withholds, exalts and abases. So He sent down the two parents and their descendants to an abode in which these rulings apply to them. Also, they were sent down to an abode in which their faith would be complete, for faith is speech and action, striving, patience and endurance.

All of this occurs only in the abode of testing, not in the Garden of bliss. Several scholars, among them Abu al-Wafa ibn Aqil and others, have said that the deeds of the messengers, prophets and believers in this world are superior to the bliss of Paradise. They said: because the bliss of Paradise is their portion and enjoyment, so how can it be compared with faith, its deeds, the prayers, the recitation of the Qur'an, jihad in the cause of God, spending their souls in seeking His good pleasure, and preferring it over their own desires and appetites? Faith is connected to Him, glorified is He, and it is His right over them, whereas the bliss of Paradise is connected to them and is their portion. They were created only for worship, and Paradise is an abode of bliss, not an abode of obligation and worship.

Also, His wisdom and decree preceded that He would place a successor on the earth, and He informed His angels of that. He, glorified is He, willed that this successor and his descendants should be on the earth before He created him, because of the wisdom and praiseworthy ends in that. So there was no alternative to his descent from Paradise to an abode in which they had already been settled before He created him. That decree was made through causes and wisdoms. Among its causes was the prohibition concerning that tree, and His leaving him between himself and his enemy until he whispered to him to eat, and His leaving him between himself and his soul until he fell into disobedience. Those causes led to praiseworthy and desired ends, which were the consequences of his descent from Paradise. Then other causes followed from his descent, made into ends for other wisdoms. Among those ends is his return to it in the most complete way. That decree, those causes and their ends proceed from the pure, far-reaching wisdom for which the people of the heavens and the earth, and the people of this world and the next, praise Him. The Most Wise of the wise did not decree that in vain, nor arrange it for nothing, nor did He leave it devoid of His far-reaching wisdom and His complete praise.

Also, He, glorified is He, said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾. They said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ He said: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know.﴾

Then He, glorified is He, manifested from His knowledge and wisdom, which had been hidden from the angels, concerning this successor, what they did not know. He made from his offspring those who are His friends, beloved ones, messengers and prophets, who draw near to Him by every kind of drawing near, and who spend their souls in seeking His love and good pleasure, glorifying Him with His praise in the hours of night and the ends of day, remembering Him standing, sitting and on their sides, worshipping Him, remembering Him and thanking Him in ease and hardship, health and affliction, adversity and prosperity. Neither hardship nor affliction, neither poverty nor sickness, turns them away from His remembrance, thanks and worship. They worship Him despite the opposition of desire, the dominance of passion, the conjoined pull of natures toward their rulings, and the enmity of their own kind and others toward them. Yet none of this prevents them from worshipping, thanking, remembering and drawing near to Him. So if your worship of Me is without opposition or obstruction, the worship of these people for Me is in the midst of these oppositions, obstructions and distractions.

Also, He, glorified is He, willed to show them what had been hidden from them concerning that which they used to magnify and honour, and they did not know what was in his soul of pride, envy and evil. That good and this evil were hidden within souls that they did not know. So it was necessary to bring them out and reveal them, so that the Most Wise of the wise might know the wisdom of placing each of them against what suits it.

Also, when He, glorified is He, created His creatures in stages and kinds, and His wisdom and decree had already determined that Adam and his offspring should be preferred over many of those He created, He made their servitude more perfect than the servitude of others. Servitude was the best of their conditions and the highest of their ranks, namely the voluntary servitude which they perform willingly and by choice, not by compulsion and necessity. For this reason God sent Gabriel to the master of this human species, giving him the choice between being a servant and messenger, or a king and prophet. By the success granted him by his Lord, he chose to be a servant and messenger. He, glorified is He, mentioned his complete servitude in his noblest stations and best conditions, such as the station of calling to God, the challenge, the Night Journey and the sending down of the Qur'an: ﴿And when the servant of God stood up calling Him﴾; ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾; ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾; ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant﴾.

So He praised him and raised his rank because of his perfect servitude to Him. This is why the people of the Gathering, when they seek intercession, say: "Go to Muhammad, a servant whom God has forgiven his past and future sins."

Since servitude is the most noble of the conditions of the children of Adam and the most beloved to God, and since it has necessary requirements and conditioned causes which cannot be attained except through them, it was among the greatest wisdoms that they should be sent out to an abode in which the rulings of servitude, its causes, conditions and necessary consequences apply to them. Their expulsion from Paradise was thus a means of trial for them and a completion of His blessing upon them, along with what that contains of the things the Lord, exalted is He, loves: He loves the answering of supplications, the relief of distress, the aid of the helpless, the forgiveness of slips, the expiation of sins, the repelling of calamities, the honouring of those who deserve honour, the humbling of those who deserve humiliation, the victory of the oppressed, the mending of the broken, and the raising of some of His creatures above others and making them in ranks, so that the measure of His favour and His choosing may be known. His complete dominion and perfect praise required that He bring them out to an abode in which His beloved things would be realised, even though many of them have paths and causes that He dislikes. Establishing a thing is not possible without its prerequisites, and bringing about the necessary consequences of wisdom is itself wisdom, just as bringing about the necessary consequences of justice is itself justice, as you will understand in the section on the suffering of children, God willing.

**(Section: When the foundation of servitude ('ubudiyyah) was secured for Adam, sin did not harm it)**

O son of Adam, if you were to meet Me with sins as great as the earth's expanse, and then met Me without associating anything with Me, I would meet you with forgiveness equal to it.

When the Master knows that his servant's sin was not intended as opposition to him, nor as a flaw in his wisdom, He knows how to accept his excuse. ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He turned to him in forgiveness.﴾ The servant does not intend, by his disobedience, to oppose his master, nor to be bold against his sacred prohibitions. Rather, it is the overpowering of natural inclination, the adorning of the self, Satan, the subjugation of desire, reliance on pardon, and hope for forgiveness. This is from the servant's side.

From the side of Lordship, it is the execution of decree, the manifestation of the might of Lordship and the humility of servitude, the perfection of need, and the appearance of the effects of the Most Beautiful Names: such as the Pardoner (al-'Afuww), the Forgiving (al-Ghafur), the Ever-Relenting (al-Tawwab), and the Forbearing (al-Halim) toward whoever comes repentant and remorseful; and the Avenger (al-Muntaqim), the Just (al-'Adl), and the Possessor of Severe Assault (dhu al-batsh al-shadid) toward whoever persists and clings to sin.

He, glorified is He, wills that His servant see His singularity in perfection, and the servant's deficiency and need for Him. He lets him witness His perfect power and might, His perfect forgiveness, pardon, mercy, perfect kindness, concealment, forbearance, overlooking, and pardoning. And that His mercy toward him is a benefit to him, not an opposition. And that if He does not envelop him with His mercy and bounty, he is certainly doomed.

How much wisdom there is in the decree of sin! And how much benefit and mercy there is for the servant in it, together with the realization of repentance.

Repentance from sin is like taking medicine for the sick. Many an illness has been the cause of health.

*Perhaps your rebuke has praiseworthy outcomes,*
*and bodies are often made well through ailments.*

Were it not for the decree of sin, the son of Adam would perish from self-admiration. A sin that humbles him is more beloved to Him than an act of obedience that makes him feel pride. The lamp of victory only descends into the candlestick of brokenness. A servant does not honor his self with anything like humiliating it, nor make it mighty with anything like abasing it, nor give it rest with anything like wearying it, as it has been said:

*I will weary my self, or I will find rest;*
*for the humiliation of the self is in the nobility of the self.*

He does not satisfy it with anything like hungering it, nor secure it with anything like frightening it, nor make it intimate with anything like its loneliness from all that is other than its Originator and Creator, nor give it life with anything like its death, as it has been said:

*The death of souls is their life;*
*whoever wishes to live, let him die.*

The drink of desire is sweet, but it bequeaths choking. Whoever remembers the snare's strangling, the abandonment of the grain becomes easy for him.

O you who are entangled in the snares of desire, a leap of resolve! The net has been torn. There is no escape from the passage of decree, so incline to peace.

To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth. He asked you for a single grain, and you withheld it. He created seven seas, and asked you for a single tear, and your eye dried up from it. Releasing the gaze engraves on the heart the image of what is looked at. The heart is a Ka'bah, and the Worshipped One does not accept being crowded by idols. The pleasures of this world are like a black slave-woman who has overpowered you, while the dark-eyed maidens (al-hur al-'in) marvel at your bad choice over them. But when the whirlwind of desire rises, it blows dust into the eye of insight, so the path is hidden.

Glory be to God! The Garden has adorned itself for the suitors, so they strove to obtain the dowry. The Lord of Might made Himself known to the lovers through His names and attributes, so they worked toward meeting Him, while you are busy with carrion.

*May he who has his heart on other than You never be;*
*and may you have the tongue with the false affection.*

Gnosis (ma'rifah) is a carpet only the near ones tread upon. Love (mahabbah) is a song only the lovers, smitten with love, are moved by. It is like a pool in a desert with no path to it; therefore few come to it. The lover flees to seclusion and solitude with his Beloved and to intimacy through His remembrance, like the fish's flight to water, or the child's to its mother.

*And I shall go out from among the houses, perhaps I shall,*
*alone in secret, speak to my heart about You.*

The worshipper has no resting place except beneath the Tree of Tuba, and the lover has no abode except the Day of Increase (yawm al-mazid). Busy yourself with it in this life, and what comes after death will suffice you. O you who spend the capital of your life in opposing the Beloved and distancing yourself from Him: among your enemies, none is more harmful to you than yourself.

*Enemies cannot reach from an ignorant man*
*what the ignorant man reaches from himself.*

The lofty aspiration belongs to one whose owner has prepared himself for meeting the Beloved, and sent forward his provisions before the meeting, so he rejoices upon arrival. ﴿And send ahead for yourselves, and fear God, and know that you will meet Him, and give good tidings to the believers.﴾

By God, the enemy has only attacked you after the Protector turned away from you. So do not think that Satan has won, but rather the Guardian turned away. Beware of your self, for no affliction has ever befallen you except from it. Do not make peace with it. By God, whoever does not humiliate it does not honor it; whoever does not abase it does not make it mighty; whoever does not break it does not mend it; whoever does not oppose it does not give it rest; whoever does not frighten it does not secure it; whoever does not sadden it does not gladden it.

Glory be to God! Your outside is adorned with the garment of piety, but your inside is a flask of the wine of desire. Whenever you perfume the garment, the scent of the intoxicant rises from beneath it. So the truthful distance themselves from you, and the wicked gravitate toward you. The thief of desire enters upon you while you are in the corner of worship, and you see no repelling of him from you, so he does not cease working on you until he takes you out of the mosque.

Be more sincere in seeking, for help has come to you. A man said to Ma'ruf: "Teach me love." He said: "Love does not come through teaching."

*It is longing, indicating the fatal death of passion,*
*when one does not return, yearning, to meet the Beloved.*

The wonder is not in His saying "He loves them," but the wonder is in His saying "He loves them." The wonder is not in a poor, humble man loving a benefactor toward him; the wonder is in a benefactor loving a poor, humble man.

**(Section)**

Among these is that one should strip from one's heart the force of obedience, and remove from oneself the cloak of pride and greatness that is not rightfully one's own, and dress in the garment of humility, brokenness, poverty, and need. For if that force and pride remained in the heart, one would be in danger of what is among the greatest afflictions, as in the hadith: "If you did not sin, I would fear for you what is worse than that: self-admiration," or as he said. How great is the difference between the effects of self-admiration and pride and the force of obedience, and between the effects of humility and brokenness!

As it has been said:

*O Adam, do not grieve over the cup of slip,*
*which was the cause of your intelligence.*
*It brought out from you the disease of self-admiration,*
*and you put on the garment of servitude.*

O Adam, do not grieve over My words to you, "Get out of it." For I created it for you, but descend to the abode of striving, and sow the seed of servitude. When the crop is complete and ripe, then come and collect it. Let that rebuke not frighten you, for it has a gentleness that will show you contentment in the state of anger.

While he was wearing the garment of humiliation, which does not befit one like him, his Lord overtook him with His mercy, took it off him, and clothed him in the garment of abasement. Abasement does not befit the servant other than this. The servant has never worn a garment more perfect, more beautiful, or more radiant than the garment of servitude, which is the garment of lowliness, in which there is no might apart from it.

Know that when God, glorified is He, sent down Adam, father of mankind, from the Garden, He did so for wisdoms that minds cannot grasp and tongues cannot describe. His sending down from it was in fact part of His perfection, so that Adam would return to it in the best of states. God, glorified is He, willed to make him and his offspring taste the hardship, sorrows, and anxieties of this world, and its troubles, so that they would come to appreciate the greatness of their entry into the Abode of the Hereafter, for opposites reveal each other's beauty. Had they been raised in the abode of bliss, they would not have known its true worth.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, willed to command them, forbid them, test them, and examine them. The Garden is not a place of obligation, so He sent them down to the earth and exposed them through this to the greatest reward, which could not be attained without command and prohibition.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, willed to take from among them prophets, messengers, friends, and martyrs, whom He loves and who love Him. So He left them between Himself and His enemies and tested them through them. When they preferred Him and gave their souls and wealth in pursuit of His pleasure and His love, they attained from His love, His good pleasure, and nearness to Him what could not have been attained at all without this. Thus the rank of messengership, prophethood, martyrdom, love for His sake, hatred for His sake, allegiance to His friends, and enmity toward His enemies are, in His sight, among the highest ranks, and this could not be attained except in the manner He decreed and ordained, through His sending Adam down to the earth and making their livelihood and the livelihood of their offspring therein.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, has the Most Beautiful Names. Among His names are the Forgiving, the Merciful, the Pardoner, the Forbearing, the Abaser, the Exalter, the Bestower of honour, the Humiliator, the Giver of life, the Causer of death, the Inheritor, and the Patient. The effects of these Names must become manifest, so His wisdom required that He cause Adam and his offspring to descend to a dwelling in which the effect of His Names would become manifest upon them: He forgives whom He wills, has mercy on whom He wills, abases whom He wills, raises whom He wills, honours whom He wills, humiliates whom He wills, takes vengeance on whom He wills, gives and withholds, and extends provision, and so on, of the manifestation of the effects of His Names and Attributes.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, is the True, Manifest King. Sovereignty is that which commands and forbids, rewards and punishes, humiliates and honours, exalts and abases. So His sovereignty required that He send Adam and his offspring down to a dwelling in which the rules of sovereignty would apply to them, and then transfer them to a dwelling in which that would be fulfilled for them.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, sent them down to a dwelling in which their faith would be in the Unseen, and faith in the Unseen is beneficial faith.

As for faith in what is witnessed, everyone will believe on the Day of Resurrection, a day on which no soul will benefit from faith except the faith it had in this world. Had they been created in the abode of bliss, they would not have attained the rank of faith in the Unseen, and the delight and honour that result from it would not have been attained without it. Rather, what they would have obtained in the abode of bliss would be a different delight and honour.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, created Adam from a handful He took from all the earth, and the earth contains the good and the wicked, the easy and the rough, the noble and the base. God, glorified is He, knew that within his loins were those who were not fit to dwell with Him in His abode. So He sent him down to a dwelling in which the good and the wicked would be brought out from his loins. Then God, glorified is He, distinguished them by two abodes: He made the good the people of His neighbourhood and of dwelling with Him in His abode, and He made the wicked the people of the abode of misery, the abode of the wicked. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿So that God may distinguish the wicked from the good and place the wicked, some of them upon others, heap them all together, and put them in Hell. Those are the losers﴾ [8:37].

When He knew that among His offspring were those not fit for His nearness, He sent them to a dwelling from which He would extract those people and join them to the abode to which they belong. This is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing, with perfect wisdom and effective will.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, when He said to the angels: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successive authority﴾ [2:30]. They said: ﴿Will You place upon it one who causes corruption therein and sheds blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?﴾ He answered them: ﴿Indeed, I know that which you do not know﴾ [2:30]. Then God, glorified is He, manifested His knowledge to His servants and to His angels through what He placed on the earth of His chosen creation, His messengers, His prophets, and His friends, and those who draw near to Him and give their souls in His love and for His pleasure while struggling against their desire and their whims. They abandon what they love to draw near to Me, abandon their desires seeking My good pleasure, and expend their blood and souls in My love. I have singled them out with a knowledge you do not know. They glorify My praise in the hours of the night and the edges of the day, and they worship Me in spite of the opposition of passion, desire, the self, and the enemy. When you worship Me, you do so without any opponent confronting you, without any desire overtaking you, and without any enemy whom I have set upon you. Rather, your worship of Me is like the soul of one of them.

Furthermore, I want to make manifest what was hidden from you concerning the affair of My enemy: his hostility toward Me, his arrogance toward My command, and his striving against My good pleasure. These two things were latent and concealed in the father of mankind and the father of the jinn. So I sent them down to a dwelling in which I made manifest what God, glorified is He, alone possessed knowledge of, which no one else knows. His wisdom became apparent, His command was fulfilled, and there appeared to the angels from His knowledge what they had not known.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, since He loves the patient, loves the doers of good, loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, loves the repentant, loves those who purify themselves, and loves the grateful, and since His love is the highest kind of honour, His wisdom required that He settle Adam and his offspring in a dwelling in which they would perform these qualities, by which they would attain the highest honours of His love. Thus their sending down to the earth was among the greatest blessings upon them. ﴿God specifies for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [2:105].

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, willed to take from Adam offspring whom He would befriend, love, and who would love Him. Their love for Him is the goal of their perfection and the culmination of their happiness. This lofty station could not be realized except by agreeing with His good pleasure, following His command, and abandoning the soul's own desires and appetites, which their Beloved dislikes. So He sent them down to a dwelling in which He commanded and forbade them, and they upheld His command and prohibition. Thus they attained the rank of His love, and He bestowed upon them the rank of His love for them.

This is part of the completeness of His wisdom and the perfection of His mercy, for He is the Good, the Merciful.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, when He created His creation in stages and categories, and His judgment had already determined the preference of Adam and his offspring over many of His creatures, made their servitude their highest rank, namely voluntary servitude, which they perform willingly and by choice, not under compulsion or constraint. It is established that God, glorified is He, sent Gabriel to the Prophet (ﷺ), giving him the choice between being a king-prophet or a servant-prophet. He looked at Gabriel as one seeking counsel, and Gabriel gestured to him to be humble. He said: "Rather, I will be a servant-prophet." God, glorified is He, mentioned him by the name of his servitude in his most noble stations: in the station of the Night Journey, the station of the call, and the station of challenge. He said in the station of the Night Journey: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night﴾ [17:1]. He did not say "His messenger" or "His prophet," indicating that he stood in this greatest station through the perfection of his servitude to his Lord. He said in the station of the call: ﴿And when the servant of God stood calling upon Him, they nearly became on top of him in a crowd﴾ [72:19]. He said in the station of challenge: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then produce a sura like it﴾ [2:23].

In the two Sahihs, in the hadith of intercession, the prophets turning back from it, and the saying of Jesus: "Go to Muhammad, a servant whom God has forgiven his past and future sins," this indicates that he attained that greatest station through the perfection of his servitude to God and the perfection of God's forgiveness toward him. When servitude is with God at this rank, His wisdom required that He settle Adam and his offspring in a dwelling in which they would attain this rank through the perfection of their obedience to God, their nearness to Him through His beloved things, and their abandonment of what they were accustomed to for His sake. This was part of the completion of His blessing upon them and His kindness toward them.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, willed that His servants whom He blessed would know the completeness of His blessing upon them and its worth, so that they would have greater love, more gratitude, and greater delight in the bliss He had given them. So He showed them His action toward His enemies, the punishment and various pains prepared for them, and made them witness their deliverance from that and their being singled out with the highest kinds of bliss, so that their joy would increase, their felicity would be complete, their gladness would grow, and their pleasure would be perfected. This was part of completing the blessings upon them and their love. It was necessary for this that He send them down to the earth, test and examine them, and grant success to whom He willed among them as mercy and bounty, and abandonment to whom He willed among them as wisdom and justice. He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. There is no doubt that when the believer sees his enemy and his beloved, who is the dearest thing to him, in various kinds of punishment and pain, while he himself is turning in various kinds of bliss and pleasure, his joy increases, his delight grows, and his blessing is complete.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, created creation only for His worship, and that is the purpose of them. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [51:56]. It is well known that the perfection of worship required of creation cannot be realized in the abode of bliss and permanence; it is realized only in the abode of trial and tribulation.

As for the abode of permanence, it is an abode of delight and bliss, not an abode of testing, examination, and obligation.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, by His wisdom, created Adam and his offspring from a composition that necessitates the call of desire and temptation and the call of intellect and knowledge. He, glorified is He, created in him intellect and desire, and appointed them as two callers, each with its requirements, so that His purpose would be fulfilled and His servants would see the manifestation of His might in His wisdom, His majesty, His mercy, His kindness, His gentleness, and His sovereignty and dominion. His wisdom and mercy required that He let their father taste the bitterness of His disobedience and make him know the consequences of yielding to desire and whim, so that he would be more cautious and more eager to flee from them. This is like the condition of a man travelling along a road where enemies are lying in ambush on its sides, in front of him and behind him, while he is unaware. When he is struck by a calamity from them once, he prepares for his journey, takes precautions against his enemy, and readies what will repel them. Had he not tasted the pain of his enemy's raid upon him and his ambush against him, his soul would not have consented to preparation, caution, and taking provisions. So among the completion of God's blessing upon Adam and his offspring was that He showed them what the enemy had done to them, so that they would prepare against him and take their precautions.

If it is said: Was it possible that the enemy not be given power over them?

It is said: It has already been mentioned that He, glorified is He, created Adam and his offspring with a structure and composition that necessitates their mixing with their enemy and being tested by him. Had He willed, He would have created them like the angels, who are intellects without desires, so the enemy would have had no path to them. But had they been created in that way, they would have been a different creation from the children of Adam, for the children of Adam were built upon intellect and desire.

Furthermore, since the love of God alone is the goal of the servant's perfection and felicity, without which he has no perfection or felicity at all, and since true love is realized only by preferring the Beloved over other beloved things of the souls, and by bearing the greatest hardships in His obedience and seeking His good pleasure, through this love is realized and its firmness in the heart is known, God, glorified is He, by His wisdom, required that He bring them out to this abode surrounded by desires and the beloved things of the souls, by preferring the Truth over them and turning away from them, their love for Him and their preference for Him over others would be realized. For this reason, they bear severe hardships, undertake dangers, endure blame, and are patient in the face of the callers to error and misguidance. By struggling against these, the authority of love grows strong, its tree takes firm root in the heart, and its fruit appears in the limbs. Firm love that persists despite many obstacles, distractions, and diversions is true, beneficial love.

As for love conditioned on well-being, bliss, pleasure, and the beloved's attaining what he desires from the beloved, that is not true love, nor is it firm when faced with opposition and obstacles. For what is attached to a condition ceases when the condition is absent, and whoever is devoted to something for a reason ceases when the reason ends. There is a difference between one who worships God only in ease, comfort, and well-being, and one who worships Him in ease and hardship, in hardship and comfort, in well-being and affliction.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, has absolute, complete praise after which there is no end. The manifestation of the causes for which He is praised is a consequence of His being praised, and these are part of the requirements of His praise, the Exalted. They are of two kinds: grace and justice. He, glorified is He, is praised for this and for that. So there must be a manifestation of the causes of justice and what they require of their objects, so that complete praise, which He deserves, may follow from them. Just as He, glorified is He, is praised for His kindness, goodness, grace, and reward, He is praised for His justice, vengeance, and punishment, for all of that proceeds from His might and wisdom. For this reason He, glorified is He, drew attention to this often, as in the sura of the Poets, where at the end of each story of the messengers and their peoples He says: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign, but most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Almighty, the Merciful﴾ [26:8-9]. He informed that this proceeds from His might, which includes the completeness of His power, and from His wisdom, which includes the completeness of His knowledge and His placing of things in their fitting places. He placed His blessing and salvation for His messengers and their followers, and His vengeance and destruction of their enemies, only in their appropriate place, owing to the completeness of His might and wisdom. For this reason, after informing of His decree between the people of felicity and the people of misery, and the return of each of them to their abodes that suit none other and which His wisdom requires no other, and after judging between them with truth, He said: "And it is said: Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds."

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, by His wisdom and praiseworthiness, made His servants differ with the greatest difference and manifest it, so that He would be thanked by those upon whom His blessing and bounty became manifest, and so they would know that He has bestowed favours and singled out with honour, beyond others. Had they all been equal in blessing and well-being, the one blessed would not know its worth and would not give thanks for it, since he would see no one except in a state like his own. Among the strongest causes of thankfulness, and the greatest in drawing it forth from the servant, is that he sees another in the opposite of his own state, one of lack and failure. There is a well-known report that when God, glorified is He, showed Adam his offspring and the differences in their ranks, he said: "O Lord, why did You not make Your servants equal?" He said: "I love to be thanked." So His love, glorified is He, that He be thanked required that He create the causes by which the thanks of the thankful would be greater and more perfect. This is the very wisdom proceeding from the attribute of praise.

Furthermore, God, glorified is He, has nothing more beloved to Him than the servant's humbling himself before Him, submitting, being needy, broken, and imploring Him. It is well known that this which is required of the servant is completed only through its causes, on which it depends, and the existence of these causes in the abode of absolute bliss and complete well-being is impossible, for that would entail the combination of two opposites.

Also, He, glorified is He, possesses creation and command. The command is His law, His order, and His religion, with which He sent His messengers and revealed His scriptures. Paradise is not a house of obligation (taklif) in which the rules of obligation and their consequences apply to its people. It is a house of bliss and pleasure. His wisdom, glorified is He, required that Adam and his offspring be brought out to a house in which the provisions of His religion and command apply to them, so that the requirement of the command and its consequences might become manifest in them. Just as His actions and creation are among the necessary requirements of the perfection of His Most Beautiful Names and His lofty Attributes, so too are His command and law, and the reward and punishment that follow from them. He, glorified is He, has directed attention to this meaning in more than one place in His Book. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾ That is, left without purpose, idle, not commanded, not forbidden, neither rewarded nor punished. This indicates that such a thing contradicts the perfection of His wisdom, and that His lordship, His might, and His wisdom reject it. For this reason, the statement was expressed as a rebuke against whoever claims it. It also indicates that the goodness of this is established in natural disposition (fitrah) and in intellects, and that the ugliness of leaving someone neglected and idle is likewise established in natural disposition. So how can that be attributed to the Lord which its ugliness is established in your natural disposition and your intellects? He, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain, and that you would not be returned to Us? So exalted is Allah, the True King; there is no god except Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne.﴾ He declared Himself free of this false assumption, which contradicts the requirement of His names and attributes, and that it is not fitting for His majesty to be ascribed to it. There are many similar examples in the Qur'an.

Also, He, glorified is He, loves from His servants things whose attainment depends upon the causes that necessitate them, and which cannot be attained except in the house of trial and testing. He, glorified is He, loves those who are patient, loves those who are grateful, loves those who fight in His cause in ranks, loves those who repent, and loves those who purify themselves. There is no doubt that the attainment of these beloved things without their causes is impossible, just as the attainment of the necessitated thing without its necessary cause is impossible. Glorified is He, He is more delighted at the repentance of His servant when he turns to Him than a man who has lost his mount, upon which were his food and drink, in a desert wasteland of destruction, and then finds it, as is established in the Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah is more delighted at the repentance of His believing servant than a man who was in a desert wasteland of destruction with his mount, upon which was his food and drink. He slept, then awoke, and it had gone. He searched for it until thirst overtook him. Then he said: 'I will return to the place where I was and sleep until I die.' So he placed his head on his forearm to die. Then he awoke and found his mount beside him, with his provisions, food, and drink on it. Allah is more delighted at the repentance of the believing servant than this man with his mount." The discussion of this hadith and the explanation of the secret of this delight at the servant's repentance will come, God willing.

The point here is that this mentioned delight occurs only after repentance from sin. Repentance and sin are the condition for this delight, and the necessitated thing does not exist without its necessary cause. Since this mentioned delight is attained only through repentance, which necessarily presupposes sin, its occurrence in the house of bliss, where there is no sin and no disobedience, is impossible. And since this delight is more beloved to the Lord, glorified is He, than its absence, His love for it required the creation of the causes that lead to it, so that the effect that is beloved to Him might follow from them.

Also, Allah, glorified is He, made Paradise a house of recompense and reward, and He distributed its dwellings among its people according to their deeds. He created it upon this basis, because of the wisdom which His names and attributes require. Paradise has degrees, some above others, and the distance between two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, as is established in the Sahih from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, Paradise has one hundred degrees, and the distance between each two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth." The wisdom of the Lord, glorified is He, requires that all these degrees be populated, and they are populated, and the differences among them arise, according to deeds. As many of the salaf (the early generations of Muslims) said, they are saved from the Fire by Allah's pardon and forgiveness, they enter Paradise by His grace, His blessing, and His forgiveness, and they divide the dwellings according to their deeds. On this basis, more than one scholar interpreted what has come affirming entry into Paradise through deeds, such as His saying: ﴿And that is the Garden which you have been given as an inheritance for what you used to do﴾ and His saying: ﴿Enter Paradise for what you used to do.﴾ They said:

As for the negation of entry into it through deeds, as in his saying: "No one will enter Paradise by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I."

The intended meaning of this is the negation of the very basis of entry. A better explanation is to say that the bi' that indicates entry is different from the bi' with which entry is negated. The one that indicates entry is the bi' of causation, which indicates that deeds are a cause of entry and necessitate it, just as all other causes necessitate their effects. The bi' with which entry is negated is the bi' of exchange and compensation, as in their saying: "I bought this for that." So the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that entry into Paradise is not in exchange for anyone's deed, and that were it not for Allah, glorified is He, covering His servant with His mercy, He would not have admitted him to Paradise. The servant's deed, however great it may be, does not by itself necessitate entry into Paradise, nor is it a payment for it. For his deeds, even if they were performed in the manner that Allah loves and approves, cannot match or equal the blessing of Allah which He bestowed upon him in the life of this world. Indeed, if He were to call him to account, all his deeds would be counted against only a small part of His blessings, and the remaining blessings would still require gratitude. So if He punished him in this state, He would be punishing him without being unjust to him. And if He showed him mercy, His mercy would be better for him than his deed, as in the Sunan, from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit and Hudhayfah and others, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ) who said:

"If Allah were to punish the people of His heavens and the people of His earth, He would punish them while not being unjust to them. And if He were to show them mercy, His mercy would be better for them than their deeds."

The point is that His wisdom, glorified is He, required the creation of Paradise in degrees, some above others, its settlement with Adam and his offspring, and their placement in it according to their deeds. The necessary consequence of this is their descent to the house of work and striving.

Also, Glorified is He, created Adam and his offspring so that He might appoint them as successors on the earth, as He informed in His Book: ﴿Indeed, I am going to place upon the earth a successor﴾ and His saying: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ and He said: ﴿And He will make you successors upon the earth.﴾ He, glorified is He, willed to transfer him and his offspring from this succession to the inheritance of the Garden of Eternity (Jannat al-Khuld). Glorified is He, knowing by His eternal knowledge that because of his weakness and the limitation of his vision, he might choose the hastening, base thing over the lasting, precious thing, for the soul is inclined to love the immediate and prefer it over the Hereafter. This is among the necessary requirements of his having been created from haste, and of his having been created hasty. So He, glorified is He, knew what was in his nature of weakness and frailty. Thus His wisdom required that He admit him to Paradise so that he might know, by direct witness, the bliss prepared for him, and so he would become more longing for it, more eager for it, and more intensely seeking it. For the love of a thing, seeking it, and longing for it are among the necessary requirements of imagining it. Whoever tastes the goodness and pleasure of something and experiences it will hardly be patient without it. This is because the soul is a taster and a longer: when it tastes, it longs. For this reason, when a servant tastes the sweetness of faith and its delight mixes with his heart, his love for it becomes firmly rooted, and he never prefers anything over it. In the Sahih, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), Allah, Mighty and Majestic, asks the angels, saying: "What do My servants ask Me?" They say: "They ask You for Paradise." He says: "Have they seen it?" They say: "No, O Lord." He says: "How would it be if they saw it?" They say: "If they saw it, they would be even more eager for it." So His wisdom required that He show it to their father and settle him in it. Then he related its story to his sons, so they became as though they were witnessing it, present with their father. So he who was created for it responded, and it was created for him, and he hastened toward it. The immediate world did not hold him back from it, but he regarded himself as being in it. Then the enemy took him captive, and he saw his first homeland, so he remains constantly yearning for his homeland and has no rest until he sees himself in it, as it has been said:

"Move your heart wherever you wish in love;
Love is only for the first Beloved."

"How many dwellings on the earth does a youth become attached to,
Yet his yearning is always for the first dwelling."

And I have some verses that touch on this meaning:

"Come to the Gardens of Eden, for they
Are your first dwellings, and in them is your resting place.
But we are captives of the enemy, so will we see
Our way back to our homelands, safe?"

So the secret of these aspects is that He, glorified and exalted is He, decreed in His judgment and wisdom that the desired ends cannot be attained except through their causes, which Allah made causes leading to them. Among those ends are the highest kinds of bliss, the best and most majestic of them. So they cannot be attained except through causes He established as leading to them. If the ends that are lower than that cannot be attained without their causes, despite their weakness and transience, such as obtaining food, drink, clothing, children, wealth, and status in this world, then how could one imagine the attainment of the highest ends and the most noble stations without a cause that leads to it? The acquisition of those causes could only occur in the house of striving and sowing. So the settlement of Adam and his offspring in this house, where they attain the causes that lead to the highest stations, was part of the completion of His favor upon them. Its secret also includes that He, glorified is He, made the messengership, prophethood, friendship (khullah), speaking with Him, guardianship (wilayah), and servitude among the noblest stations of His creation and the ultimate perfections. So He placed them in a house from which He brought forth the prophets, in which He sent the messengers, from which He took one as a friend (Khalil), spoke to Musa directly, and took from among them guardians, martyrs, servants, and a chosen elite whom He loves and who love Him. And their descent to the earth was part of the completion of favor and kindness.

Also, He made manifest to His creation the effects of His names and the operation of their rulings upon them, which His wisdom, mercy, and knowledge required. Its secret also is that He made Himself known to His creation through His actions, names, and attributes, and through what He brought about in His friends and His enemies: the honor and bounty He gave to the friends, the humiliation and misery He inflicted upon the enemies, His answering of their supplications, His fulfilling of their needs, His relieving of their distress, His removing of their trials, His directing of them under His decree as He wills, and His turning them through various kinds of good and evil. In this there is the greatest proof for them that He is their Lord and their King, that He is Allah, there is no god but Him, that He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, that He is the true God, and that everything other than Him is false. The proofs of His lordship and oneness were thus manifest on earth, diverse, and present from every direction. The blessed among His servants recognized Him and acknowledged His oneness in faith and submission. And the forsaken among His creatures denied Him and associated others with Him in wrongdoing and ingratitude. So whoever perished, perished upon clear evidence, and whoever lived, lived upon clear evidence. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Whoever reflects upon His signs that are seen and heard on the earth, and observes their effects, will know the completeness of His wisdom in settling Adam and his offspring in this house until a known term. Glorified is He, He created Paradise only for Adam and his offspring, and made the angels its servants for them. But His wisdom required that He create for them a house from which they might gather provisions for the house that was created for them, and that they would not attain it except with provisions. As He said, Exalted is He, regarding this world: ﴿And He carries your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.﴾ This is the matter of travel in this world from one land to another. So how much more so is the transfer from this world to the abode of permanence? He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And take provisions, for the best provision is piety.﴾

So the defrauded sold their dwellings in it for the lowest share and the least price. And the successful sold their souls and their wealth to Allah, making them the price for Paradise. Their trade was profitable, and they attained the great victory. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise.﴾ So He, glorified is He, did not remove Adam from it except that He wished to return him to it in the most complete return, as has been said in the words of destiny: "O Adam, do not be distressed by My saying to you, 'Go down from it.' It was for you that I created it. For I am the Self-Sufficient, free of it and of everything. I am the Generous, the Bountiful. I do not take pleasure in it, for I feed and am not fed. I am the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. But descend to the house of sowing. When you sow, and the crop stands upon its stalk and becomes harvest, then come and take what you most need. A grain yields ten like it, up to seven hundred times, up to many multiples. For I know your interest better than you do, and I am the Most High, the All-Wise."

If it is said: what you have mentioned of these aspects and their like is complete only if it is said that the Garden in which Adam was settled and from which he was sent down is the Garden of Eternity (Jannat al-Khuld), which is prepared for the God-fearing and the believers on the Day of Resurrection, and then the secret of his descent and removal from it becomes manifest. But a group among them, including Abu Muslim and Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Baluti and others, said that it was a garden on earth, at a high place in it, and not the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Ma'wa) which Allah prepared for His believing servants on the Day of Resurrection. Mundhir ibn Sa'id mentioned this opinion in his tafsir, citing a group of scholars, and said:

As for His saying to Adam: "Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden," a group said: Allah, the Exalted, settled Adam in the Garden of Eternity (Jannat al-Khuld) which the believers will enter on the Day of Resurrection.

Some others said: it is a garden other than that one, which God made for him and settled him in. It is not the Garden of Eternity (Jannat al-Khuld). He said: this is an opinion for which many proofs bear witness and which necessitates adopting it, because the Garden that people enter after the Resurrection belongs to the realm of the Hereafter, and it is entered on the Last Day, which has not yet come. God, exalted is He, has described it to us in His Book with its attributes. It is impossible that God should describe a thing with an attribute and then that thing be without the attribute He described for it. Holding this view also rebuts what God has informed us of.

They said: We find that God, blessed and exalted, described the Garden prepared for the God-fearing as the abode of permanence after the Resurrection has taken place, and Adam did not dwell in it. He described it as the Garden of Eternity, and Adam did not remain eternal in it. He described it as a place of recompense, and did not say that it is a place of trial, though Adam was tested in it with disobedience and temptation. He described it as a place in which there is no sorrow, and that those who enter it say: "Praise be to God who has removed sorrow from us," yet Adam grieved in it. We find that He named it the Abode of Peace, yet Adam was not safe in it from the afflictions that occur in this world. He named it the Abode of Settlement, yet Adam did not settle in it. He said of those who enter it: "They shall not be removed from it," yet Adam was removed from it because of his disobedience. He said: "No weariness shall touch them therein," yet Adam fled in fear when he committed the sin and began to stick leaves of the Garden upon himself. That very weariness which God negated from it is what Adam experienced. He informed us that in it no vain talk or sinful speech is heard, yet Adam sinned in it and heard in it something greater than vain talk, namely that he was commanded therein to disobey his Lord. He informed us that in it no vain talk or lying is heard, yet Iblis made him hear lies in it, deceived him, and swore to him, after making him hear it.
