Adam drank from its drink, which He named in His Book "a pure drink" (sharaban tahuran), meaning purifying from all blameworthy afflictions, yet Adam was not purified from those afflictions. God named it "a seat of truthfulness" (maq'ad sidq), yet Iblis lied to Adam in it, while a seat of truthfulness contains no lie. The 'Illiyyun (the highest place) never had any change or alteration, and by the consensus of those who pray, the Garden is in the highest 'Illiyyun. God said: "Indeed I am placing a successor on the earth," and did not say "I am placing him in the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa)." The angels said: "Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?" The angels are too God-fearing to say what they do not know, and they are the ones who said: "We have no knowledge except what You have taught us." This indicates that God had informed them that the children of Adam would cause corruption on the earth; otherwise how could they have been saying what they did not know? God, exalted is He, says: "His word is the truth" and "They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command." The angels say and do nothing except what they are commanded, and God said: "They do what they are commanded." God informed us that Iblis said to Adam: "Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" If God had settled him in the Garden of Eternity and a kingdom that does not decay, how could he not reject this counsel and refute it by saying: "How can you direct me to something that I already have and have chosen?" Indeed, how did he not throw dust in Iblis's face and revile him? For if Iblis, by these words, was seeking to mislead him, he would only be belittling him, since he promised him something in exchange for disobedience to his Lord, of something he already had, not something beyond it. Such words are addressed only to madmen who do not reason, because the reward he promised him for disobeying his Lord had already been secured by him: eternity and a kingdom that does not decay. God did not inform Adam, when He settled him in the Garden, that he was among those who would abide forever. Had he been among those who would abide forever, he would not have inclined to Iblis's words or accepted his counsel. Rather, since he was in a place other than the abode of eternity, Iblis deceived him by what he made him covet of eternity, so he accepted from him. Had God informed Adam that he was in the Abode of Eternity and then he doubted his Lord's report, He would have called him a disbeliever, and would not have called him a disobedient one. God named Adam a disobedient one and did not name him a disbeliever, because whoever doubts God's report is a disbeliever, while whoever does other than what God commanded him, while still believing in the truth of his Lord's report, is a disobedient one.

They said: If Adam was settled in the Garden of Eternity, which is the abode of holiness that none enters except the pure and sanctified, then how did Iblis, the defiled, impure, cursed, blamed, and rejected one, reach it, so that Adam was tempted therein? Iblis is a sinner who has transgressed his Lord's command, and the Garden of Eternity is not the abode of sinners; none at all enters it except the God-fearing, and Iblis is not God-fearing. After it was said to him: "Get down from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein" (7:13), it became possible for him to ascend to the Garden of Refuge above the seventh heaven after the wrath and distancing that came upon him for his rebellion and arrogance. This contradicts the verse "Get down from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein." If his addressing Adam with what he addressed him with, and swearing to him, was not arrogance, then the Arabs in whose tongue the Qur'an was revealed would not understand what arrogance is. Perhaps one whose vision has weakened and whose investigation is shallow may say that Iblis did not reach it, but his whisper reached it. This is a statement that resembles its speaker and matches his belief. But God's saying is the judge between us and him. God's saying: "and he swore to them both" (7:21) refutes what he said, because swearing is not whispering; it is address and direct speech, and it cannot occur except between two present parties, not absent, nor with one of them absent. Among what shows that his whispering was direct address is God's saying: "Then Satan whispered to him, saying: 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?'" (20:120). He informed that he said this to him, which indicates that he whispered to him by direct address and not that it merely arose in his soul without speech. Whoever claims a figurative interpretation of the apparent sense without providing evidence for it, his statement is not worthy of acceptance. Also, whispering may be audible speech or a sound. Ru'ba said:

"Whispering, calling upon the Lord of the daybreak, sincere..."

And al-A'sha said:

"You hear the whispering of the jewelry when she turns, like a wind that brings a sound of a bell."

They said: In Iblis's words to them both, "What has your Lord forbidden you from this tree?" (7:20), there is evidence that he saw them and the tree. When Adam was outside the Garden and not dwelling in it, God said: "Did I not forbid you from that tree?" (7:22), and did not say "this tree" as Iblis had said to him, because at that time Adam was not in the Garden and was not seeing the tree. This accords with God's, exalted is He, saying: "To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous deed raises it" (35:10). He, glorified is He, has informed us with a firm, unambiguous report that only a good word ascends to Him and a righteous deed. This is among what we have already mentioned: that none enters the holy, purified place except one who is holy, purified, and good. Far be it from God that Iblis's whispering should be holy, pure, or good; rather it is all evil, darkness, corruption, and defilement. Exalted is God far above that, to a great degree.

Just as the deeds of disbelievers cannot enter the pure holy place nor reach it, because they are wicked and not good, so too the whispering of Iblis does not reach it and never reached it, nor did it enter the holy place. God, exalted is He, said: "No indeed! The record of the wicked is in Sijjin" (83:7). It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that Adam slept in his Garden. The Garden of Eternity has no sleep, by the consensus of the Muslims, because sleep is a kind of death, and the Qur'an has stated this, and death is a change of state, while the Abode of Peace is free from changes of state. The sleeping person is dead or like one who is dead.

They said: It has been narrated from him (ﷺ) that he said to the mother of Harithah, when she said to him: "O Messenger of God, Harithah was killed alongside you. If he has gone to the Garden, I will be patient and seek reward; but if he has gone elsewhere, you will see what I do." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "Is it one garden? Rather, there are many gardens." Thus he informed that God has many gardens. Perhaps God settled Adam in one of His gardens, which is not the Garden of Eternity.

They said: Some reports have come that Adam's Garden was in the land of India.

They said: Even if the narrators of reports and transmitters of traditions do not authenticate this, what the intellects accept and what the apparent text of the Book supports is that Adam's Garden is not the Garden of Eternity nor the Abode of Permanence. How could it be permissible that God settled Adam in the Garden of Eternity so that he would be among those who abide forever, while He said to the angels: "Indeed I am placing a successor on the earth"? How could He inform the angels that He wants to place a successor on the earth and then settle him in the Abode of Eternity, which none enters except those who will abide forever therein, as it is called the Abode of Eternity? God has named it by the names mentioned earlier with an absolute naming, not restricted. So when the Garden is called the Abode of Eternity, the meaning of this name cannot be diminished in any way. This is some of what those who hold this doctrine have argued.

On this basis, settling Adam and his progeny in this Garden does not contradict their being in the abode of trial and testing, and then those aspects and benefits you have mentioned are possible to achieve in the Garden.

The answer: It is said that there are two opinions among people on this matter. We will mention both opinions and the arguments of both sides, and show the establishment of the aspects we mentioned and similar ones under both opinions. First, we mention the opinion of those who say it is the Garden of Eternity promised to the God-fearing, and what they argued, and what they refuted of the arguments of those who say it is other than that. Then we follow with the view of the others and what they argued, and how they answered the arguments of their opponents, without taking sides for either opinion or refuting the other, since that is not our aim. Our aim is only to mention some of the wisdoms and interests that necessitated Adam's removal from the Garden and his settlement on earth in the abode of trial and testing. The purpose of that was to refute those who claim that God's wisdom refuses to admit Adam into the Garden and expose him to the sin for which he was removed from it, and asks what benefit there is in that; and to refute those who deny that there is any wisdom in it, claiming it proceeds only from pure will with no wisdom behind it.

Since the aim is achieved under either assumption, whether it was the Garden of Eternity or another, we have discussed both assumptions. We saw that refuting these people with a blunt club would neither achieve an aim nor cure a sickness, so we took this course, so that their claim would be refuted by every opinion of the Community. And with God is help, and upon Him is reliance, and there is no power nor strength except with God.

So we say: As for what you have mentioned, that the Garden from which Adam was sent down is not the Garden of Eternity but another garden, this is a matter on which people have differed. The most well-known opinion among the elite and the common people, which no other thought comes to their hearts, is that it is the Garden of Eternity prepared for the God-fearing. More than one of the early scholars explicitly stated this. Whoever supports this has used what Muslim transmitted in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, and Abu Malik from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah, who both said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"God, the Mighty and Majestic, will gather the people until the Garden is brought near to them. They will come to Adam, peace be upon him, and say: 'O our father, ask that the Garden be opened for us.' He will say: 'Did your father's sin not expel you from the Garden?'" and he mentioned the hadith...

They said: This indicates that the Garden from which Adam was expelled is the very one from which they ask him to open it for them. They said: It also indicates this: God, exalted is He, said: "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden..." up to His saying: "Get down, some of you being enemies to others, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time" (2:35-36), immediately after His saying "Get down." This shows that they were not on the earth at first.

Also: He, glorified is He, described the Garden in which He settled Adam with attributes that do not exist in the worldly garden. He said: "Indeed, for you there is that you will not hunger therein, nor be naked, and that you will not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun" (20:118-119). This does not occur in this world at all; even if a man were in the finest of its dwellings, hunger, thirst, nakedness, and exposure to the sun would necessarily befall him.

Also: If the Garden were in this world, Adam would have known that Iblis lied in his words: "Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?" For Adam knew that this world is finite and perishing, and that its kingdom decays.

Also: The story of Adam in the Surah of the Cow is very clear that the Garden from which he was expelled is above the heaven. He, glorified is He, said: "And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant, and was among the disbelievers. And We said: 'O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden, and eat therefrom freely wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers.' So Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from what they were in. And We said: 'Get down, some of you being enemies to others, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time.' Then Adam received words from his Lord, and He accepted his repentance; indeed He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful" (2:34-37).

This is the descent of Adam, Eve, and Iblis from the Garden, and for this reason the plural pronoun is used in it.

It has been said that it is addressed to them and to the serpent, but this requires a firmly established report, since there is no mention of the serpent in any part of the story of Adam and Iblis.

It has been said that it is addressed to Adam and Eve, and the plural is used for them, as in His saying: "And We were witnesses to their judgment" (21:78). It has also been said that it is addressed to Adam, Eve, and their progeny. These sayings are weak, and different from the first, because they are between a saying without evidence and what the apparent address indicates otherwise. Thus it is established that Iblis is included in this address and that he is among those sent down from the Garden. Then God, exalted is He, said: "We said: Get down from it, all of you. Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve" (2:38). This second descent must be different from the first, which is his descent from the heaven to the earth. In that case, the Garden from which they were first sent down is above the heaven, and it is the Garden of Eternity.

Some scholars, including al-Zamakhshari, held that His saying "Get down from it, all of you" is addressed to Adam and Eve alone, and the plural was used for them because it includes their progeny. He said: The evidence for this is His saying: "He said: Get down from it, all of you, some being enemies to others; then, when guidance comes to you from Me..." He said: This is indicated also by His saying: "Whoever follows My guidance, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve. But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Fire, wherein they will abide forever" (2:38-39). This is only a ruling that applies to all people. And His saying "some being enemies to others" means what people have of hostility and hatred, and misguiding one another.

This opinion which he chose is the weakest of the opinions regarding the verse, because the enmity God mentioned is only between Adam and Iblis and their progeny, as God said: "Indeed Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy" (35:6).

Ibn al-Qayyim's Commentary (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 38 (part 4 of 8):

As for Adam and his wife, God, glory be to Him, informed in His Book that He created her from him so that he might find rest in her. He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾. Thus He made affection between a man and his wife, and He made enmity between Adam and Iblis and their descendants. This is also indicated by the return of the pronoun to them in the plural form, and Adam, his wife and Iblis have already been mentioned in His words: ﴿Then Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they were﴾. These are three: Adam, Eve and Iblis. Why, then, does the pronoun return to only some of what was mentioned, despite this being contrary to the flow of the speech, and not return to all that was mentioned, although that is the direction of the speech?

If it is said: What do you make of His words in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you being enemies to others﴾? This is addressed to Adam and Eve, and yet it reports the enmity of some of them toward one another.

It is answered: Either the pronoun in His words ﴿Go down﴾ refers to Adam and his wife, or it refers to Adam and Iblis, and the wife is not mentioned because she follows him.

On the second view, the enmity mentioned is directed at those addressed by the descent, namely Adam and Iblis. On the first view, the verse includes two matters: one, His command to Adam and his wife to descend; and two, His making enmity between Adam, his wife and Iblis. Iblis must definitely be included in the ruling of this enmity, as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife﴾, and He said to his descendants: ﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy﴾. Consider how the places in which enmity is mentioned all agree on the plural pronoun rather than the dual.

As for the mention of the descent, it sometimes comes with the plural pronoun, sometimes with the dual, and sometimes in the singular for Iblis alone, as in His words in Surah al-A'raf: ﴿He said: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? He said: I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay (12). He said: Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾. This descent is for Iblis alone, and the pronoun in His words ﴿from it﴾ is said to refer to Paradise. It is also said to refer to the heaven. Where the plural form is used, it is for Adam, his wife and Iblis, since the story revolves around them. Where the dual is used, it refers either to Adam and his wife, since they are the two who actually ate from the tree and committed the disobedience, or to Adam and Iblis, since they are the two fathers of the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), so their condition and what their affair came to are mentioned as an admonition and lesson for their offspring. Both views are reported on this. Where the singular is used, it is for Iblis alone.

Furthermore, what clarifies that the pronoun in His words ﴿Go down from it, all of you﴾ refers to Adam and Iblis is that when God, glory be to Him, mentioned the disobedience, He singled out Adam alone for it, not his wife, saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him. He said: Go down from it, all of you﴾.

This indicates that the one addressed by the descent is Adam and the one who made disobedience appealing to him, while the wife is included by following. This is because the purpose is for God, exalted is He, to inform His servants, the responsible among jinn and humans, of what befell their two parents because of the evil consequence of disobedience and opposing the command, so that they would not follow them in that. Mentioning the father of the two weighty ones is more effective in achieving this meaning than mentioning only the parents of mankind. God, glory be to Him, also informed about the wife that she ate with Adam, and informed that He sent him down and expelled him from the Garden because of that eating, so it is known that this was required by the ruling of marriage, and that she came to what Adam came to. Thus, directing attention to the mention of the two parents who are the origin of the descendants is more appropriate than directing it to the mention of the father and mother of mankind alone. And God knows best.

In sum, His words ﴿Go down, some of you being enemies to others﴾ are clearly in the plural, so it is not permissible to interpret them as referring to the two in His words ﴿Go down﴾.

They said: As for your question of how Iblis could whisper to him after his descent from it, when it is impossible for him to ascend to it after God's words ﴿Go down﴾, the answer to this is from several aspects:

First: He was expelled from it and prevented from entering it in the manner of dwelling, honor, and taking it as a home. From where do you know that he was prevented from entering it in the manner of trial and testing for Adam and his wife? This would be an incidental entry, just as the condition of a house is entered by those who were commanded to be tested and afflicted in it, even if they were not fit to dwell in that house.

Second: He would approach the heaven and speak to them, without entering their dwelling.

Third: Perhaps he stood at the door, called out to them and swore to them, without entering Paradise.

Fourth: It has been narrated that he wanted to enter upon them, but the guardians prevented him, so he entered into the mouth of the serpent until it brought him in upon them, and the guardians did not perceive that.

They said: Among what indicates that it is the Garden of Eternity itself is that it came definite with the article in all places, as in His words ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾. There is no garden known to the addressees and recognized by them except the Garden of Eternity, which the Most Merciful promised His servants in the unseen. This name has become a proper name for it by predominance, even though its original meaning is a garden of fruit trees and fruits. This is like al-Madinah al-Tayyibah and al-Najm for the Pleiades and their likes. So wherever the word occurs with the definite article, it refers to the known Garden that is familiar in the hearts of the believers.

As for if it is intended to be another garden, it comes indefinite, as in His words ﴿two gardens of grapevines﴾, or restricted by an annexation, as in His words ﴿and why, when you entered your garden﴾, or restricted by the context in a way that indicates it is a garden on earth, as in His words ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore to pick its fruit in the morning﴾, the verses. This context and restriction indicate that it is a garden on earth.

They said: Furthermore, the People of the Sunnah and the Community agree that Paradise and Hellfire are created, and the hadiths from the Prophet about this are widely transmitted, as in the two Sahihs from Abdullah ibn Umar, from the Prophet, that he said: "When any one of you dies, his place is shown to him morning and evening; if he is among the people of Paradise, then he is of the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of the Fire, then he is of the people of the Fire. It is said: This is your place, until God resurrects you on the Day of Resurrection." And in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, he said: "Paradise and the Fire disputed. Paradise said: What is wrong with me that only the weak among people and their rabble enter me? And the Fire said: What is wrong with me that only the tyrants and the arrogant enter me? So He said to Paradise: You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will. And He said to the Fire: You are My punishment; I punish through you whom I will."
The hadith...

In the Sunan, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God said: "When God created Paradise and the Fire, He sent Gabriel to Paradise and said: Go and look at it and at what I have prepared for its people. He went, looked at it and at what God had prepared for its people." The hadith...

In the two Sahihs, in the hadith of the Night Journey: "Then the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for me, and its leaves were like the ears of elephants, and its fruits like the jars of Hajar, and four rivers: two apparent and two hidden. I said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: As for the two apparent rivers, they are the Nile and the Euphrates. As for the two hidden, they are two rivers in Paradise."
And in it also: "Then I was made to enter Paradise, and there were domes of pearls, and its dust was musk."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "While I was walking in Paradise, I came upon a river whose banks were domes of hollow pearls. I said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has given you. Its clay, or its fragrance, was pure musk."

In Sahih Muslim, in the hadith on the prayer of the eclipse, that the Prophet moved forward and backward during the prayer, then turned to his companions and said: "Paradise and the Fire were presented to me; Paradise came so close to me that if I had reached out for a cluster from it I would have taken it, and if I had taken it you would have eaten from it as long as the world endures."

In Sahih Muslim, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding God's words ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾: their spirits are in the crops of green birds that have lamps hanging from the Throne; they roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then return to those lamps. Your Lord looked upon them with a look and said: Do you desire anything? They said: What could we desire, while we roam freely in Paradise wherever we wish? The hadith...

In the Sahih, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "When your brothers were struck at Uhud, God placed their spirits in the crops of green birds that come to the rivers of Paradise, eat of its fruits, and return to lamps of gold hanging in the shade of the Throne. When they found the goodness of their food, drink and resting place, they said: Who will convey to our brothers on our behalf that we are alive in Paradise, provided for, so that they will not be lax in jihad or shrink back in war? God, Mighty and Majestic, said: I will convey it to them on your behalf." So God revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead; rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for, rejoicing in what God has given them﴾ [Al-Imran: 170], the verse.

In the Muwatta, from the hadith of Ka'b ibn Malik, the Messenger of God said: "The soul of the believer is only a bird that hangs in Paradise until God returns it to its body on the day He resurrects him."

In al-Bukhari, when Ibrahim, the son of the Messenger of God, died, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, he has a wet nurse in Paradise."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Imran ibn Husain, the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I looked into Paradise and saw that most of its people were the poor; and I looked into the Fire and saw that most of its people were women."

The reports on this subject are too numerous to mention.

As for the claim that Paradise and the Fire have not yet been created, it is the view of the innovators from the misguided Mu'tazilah and those who speak with their view, who say that the Garden from which Adam was sent down was a garden in the east of the earth.

These hadiths and their like refute their view.

They said: As for your argument by all the aspects you mentioned concerning Paradise, that it is free of idle talk, lying, toil, nakedness and other things, in the Garden where Adam was made to dwell, all of that is true and we do not deny it, nor does any Muslim. But this applies when the believers enter it on the Day of Resurrection, as the context of the speech indicates. This does not negate that there was, in it, between Adam and Iblis, what God, Mighty and Majestic, related of the test and trial; then the matter becomes, when the believers enter it, what God, Mighty and Majestic, has informed of. So there is no contradiction between the two matters.

They said: As for your claim that Paradise is an abode of reward and recompense and not an abode of obligation, and God, glory be to Him, obligated Adam in it by prohibiting the tree, the answer to this is from two aspects. The first: it is impossible for it to be an abode of obligation only when the believers enter it on the Day of Resurrection, for then obligation ends.
As for the impossibility of obligation occurring in it in the abode of this world, there is no proof for it.

The second: obligation in it was not by the deeds for which people are obligated in this world, such as fasting, prayer, jihad and the like; rather, it was a restriction upon him regarding a tree among its trees. This is not impossible in the Garden of Eternity, just as everyone is restricted from approaching the wives of others in it. If you mean that Paradise is not an abode, how is the occurrence of such a thing in it at any time impossible? You have no proof for it. If you mean that most of the obligations which exist in this world are absent in it, that is true, but it does not support your claim.

They said: This is as it is indicated by the texts and the saying of the early Community, so no scholar among the imams of knowledge is known to hold your view, nor is it given any attention or consideration.

The first party said: The response to what you mentioned is from two aspects: a general and a detailed.

As for the general: you have not brought, for your view, any evidence that necessitates adopting it, neither from the Qur'an, nor the Sunnah, nor any established report from any of the Companions of the Messenger of God or the Successors, whether with a chain or without. And we can show you someone who held our view, one of the imams of Islam: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, who said regarding God's words, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿Indeed, for you there is that you will not hunger therein, nor be bare﴾, that he said: "meaning, on earth."
And this is Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Qutaybah, who said in his Ma'arif, after mentioning God's creation of Adam and his wife, that God, glory be to Him, brought him out from the east of the Garden of Eden to the earth from which he was taken.
And this is Ubayy, of whom al-Hasan related that when Adam was dying, he desired a bunch of grapes from the grapes of Paradise. His sons set out to seek it for him, and the angels met them and said: Where are you going, O children of Adam? They said: Our father desires a bunch from the bunches of Paradise. They said to them: Turn back, for you have been spared it. They reached him, took his soul, washed him, applied perfume to him, shrouded him, and Gabriel prayed over him, with his sons behind the angels, and they buried him, and they said: This is your custom for your dead.
And this is Abu Salih, who related from Ibn Abbas, regarding God's words ﴿Go down from it﴾, that he said: it is like saying "so-and-so descended into such-and-such a land."
And this is Wahb ibn Munabbih, who mentions that Adam was created on earth, and on earth he dwelt, and on earth the Paradise of Eden was set up for him, and that he was in Eden, and that the Seihon, Jeihon and Euphrates were separated from the river that was in the middle of Paradise, which was what watered it.
And this is Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Balluti, who chose it in his Tafsir and supported it with what we have related from him, and related it outside the Tafsir from Abu Hanifah in what he disagreed with him on; so why did he speak according to his view in this matter?
And this is Abu Muslim al-Isfahani, author of the Tafsir and others, one of the well-known virtuous scholars, who held this view, defended it, and argued for it with what is well known in his book.
And this is Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq ibn Atiyyah, who mentioned both views in his Tafsir in the story of Adam in al-Baqarah.

Ibn Hazm (Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm) mentioned the two opinions in his book al-Milal wa'l-Nihal, saying: "Al-Mundhir ibn Sa'id al-Qadi used to hold that Paradise and the Fire are both created, except that he would say that they are not the same one in which Adam and his wife were." Among those who also related the two opinions is Abu 'Isa al-Rummani in his tafsir, and he chose that it is the Paradise of eternity (jannat al-khuld). He then said: "The position we have adopted is the view of al-Hasan and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd (or Wasil), and most of our companions hold it. It is also the view of Abu 'Ali and our shaykh Abu Bakr, and it is the position of the people of tafsir."

Among those who mentioned the two opinions is Abu'l-Qasim al-Raghib in his tafsir. He said: "There is disagreement about the Garden in which Adam was made to dwell. Some of the theologians (mutakallimun) said it was an orchard that God made as a test for him, and it was not the Garden of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa). Whoever says it was not the Garden of Refuge reasons that there is no obligation (taklif) in the Garden, and Adam was under obligation." He said: "It has been answered that the Garden cannot be the abode of obligation in the Hereafter, but there is nothing to prevent it from being an abode of obligation at one time and not at another, just as a person is under obligation at one time and not at another."

Among those who mentioned the disagreement on this question is Abu 'Abd Allah ibn al-Khatib al-Razi in his tafsir. He mentioned these two opinions and a third, which is suspension of judgment (tawaqquf), saying that all of them are possible and that certainty cannot be reached, as will come with the quotation of his words.

Among the exegetes there are those who mentioned only this one opinion: that it was not the Garden of eternity, but rather a garden wherever God willed on earth. They said the sun and moon rose over it, Iblis was in it, and then he was expelled from it. They said: "If it had been the Garden of eternity, he would not have been expelled from it."

Among those who also mentioned the two opinions is Abu'l-Hasan al-Mawardi, who said in his tafsir: "There is disagreement about the Garden in which they were made to dwell, on two opinions. One is that it is the Garden of eternity. The second is that it is a garden which God prepared for them and made an abode of trial, and it is not the Garden of eternity which God made an abode of recompense." Those who hold this view differ on it in two opinions: one is that it is in heaven, because He caused them to descend from it; this is the view of al-Hasan. The second is that it is on earth, because He tested them there by forbidding them the tree they were forbidden, rather than other fruits; this is the view of Ibn Yahya. This was after Iblis had been commanded to prostrate to Adam. And God knows best the correct position. This is his speech.

Ibn al-Khatib said in his tafsir: "They differed over whether the Garden mentioned in this verse was on earth or in heaven, and if it was in heaven, whether it is the Garden which is the abode of reward and the Garden of eternity, or another garden."

Abu'l-Qasim al-Balkhi and Abu Muslim al-Isfahani said: this garden was on earth, and they understood the descent (ihbat) as movement from one place to another, as in the words of God Most High: ﴿Go down to a city﴾.

The second opinion, which is the view of al-Jubba'i, is that it was in the seventh heaven. He said the evidence for this is His words "go down," and that the first descent was from the seventh heaven to the lowest heaven, and the second descent was from heaven to earth.

The third opinion, which is the view of the majority of our companions, is that this garden is the abode of reward. The evidence for this is that the definite article in the word "Garden" does not indicate generality, because it is impossible for Adam to have dwelt in all the gardens; therefore it must be restricted to the known, previously mentioned garden. The Garden known among the Muslims is the abode of reward, so the word must be taken to refer to it.

He said: The fourth opinion is that all of these are possible, the textual evidences are weak and contradictory, and so suspension of judgment is required and certainty should be avoided.

They said: We do not follow these people, nor do we rely on what has been related from them, and the sound proof is the judge between disputants.

They said: We have already mentioned, in this view, what is sufficient.

As for the detailed answer, we will discuss the arguments you have cited, so that the correct position may become clear. We say, and with God is success:

As for your using the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Hudhayfah, where people say to Adam: "Open for us the Garden," and he says: "Did your father's sin not expel you from it?"

This hadith does not indicate that the Garden they asked him to open for them is the very same one from which he was expelled. The word "Garden" is a generic noun (ism jins), so every orchard is called a garden, as God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore to pick its fruit in the morning﴾, and He said: ﴿They said, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth from the earth for us, or you have a garden of palms and grapes"﴾, and He said: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth seeking God's pleasure and for the strengthening of their souls is like a garden on a height﴾, and He said: ﴿Set forth for them the example of two men: for one of them We had made two gardens of grapes, and We surrounded them with palm trees﴾, up to His words ﴿Why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, "What God willed; there is no power except in God"?﴾. Since the word "Garden" is generic, when they asked Adam to open for them the Garden of eternity, he informed them that it was not fitting for him to do so, since he had himself been removed, along with his offspring, from the Garden in which God had placed him, because of his sin and error. This is what the hadith indicates.

As for whether the Garden from which he was expelled is the very one they asked him to open, the hadith does not indicate this by any of the three types of indication (manṭūq, mafhūm, and iqtiḍā'), and if it did, it would be obligatory to act upon the meaning of the hadith and forbidden to contradict it. Is not our whole basis only the understanding of what the Truthful and Believed one (ṣādiq al-maṣdūq), may God's blessings and peace be upon him, intended?

They said: As for your using the descent, and that it is a coming down from a height to a lower place, its answer is in two respects:

The first is that "descent" (hubut) has been used in the sense of moving from one land to another, as one says "so-and-so descended to such-and-such a land," and God Most High said: ﴿Go down to a city, for you will have what you ask﴾. This is common in Arabic verse and prose. He said:

"That you descend into the lands of a people / who graze on the thorny plants."

Abu Salih related from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: it is as one says, "so-and-so descended to such-and-such a land."

The second is that we do not dispute with you that descent in its literal sense is what you have described, but from where does it follow that the Garden from which the descent took place must be above the heavens? If it was on the highest part of the earth, could one not say "he descended from it," just as a stone descends from the top of a mountain to its base and the like?

As for His words: ﴿And for you on earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾, this indicates that the earth to which they were sent down is a place where they have a dwelling and provision for a time. It does not indicate that they were not in a high garden above the earth to which they were sent down, one that differs from the earth in its qualities, trees, bliss and goodness. God, glory be to Him, made the regions of the earth differ with the greatest difference, and this is witnessed by the senses. So from where do you know that that was not a garden distinguished from the rest of the regions of the earth by what could be found only in it, and then they were sent down from it to the earth, which is the place of toil, fatigue, trial and testing?

This very answer also responds to your citing His words: ﴿Indeed, for you there is that you will not hunger therein, nor be naked﴾, and the rest of what you mentioned. Moreover, this is a ruling conditioned on a stipulation, and the stipulation was not fulfilled. For He, glory be to Him, said it immediately after His words: ﴿And do not approach this tree﴾, and His words ﴿Indeed, for you there is that you will not hunger therein, nor be naked﴾ are a promise connected to what precedes it. The meaning is: if you avoid the tree I forbade you and do not approach it, you will have this promise. A conditional ruling is nullified when the condition is absent, so when he ate from the tree, his entitlement to this promise ceased.

He said: As for your claim that if the Garden had been in this world, Adam would have known that Iblis was lying in his words ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ up to the end, this is an assertion without proof. For you have no evidence that God, glory be to Him, had informed Adam at his creation that the world is perishable and transient and that its dominion decays and passes away. And even if we assume that Adam had been informed of this, Iblis's words ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ do not indicate that by "eternity" he meant that which has no end, for in the language of the Arabs "khuld" means a long stay, as they say "a long-lasting bond" and "a lasting imprisonment." God Most High said to Thamud: ﴿Do you build on every high place a sign, sporting? And do you take fortresses that perhaps you will abide forever?﴾ Likewise His words ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾ mean a long-lasting, enduring dominion.

Furthermore, there is no justification for excusing Iblis's words, given the certainty of his lie and his swearing to Adam and Eve on falsehood, while God, glory be to Him, has informed us that he swore to them and deceived them with delusion. This indicates that they were deceived by his words, for he deluded them by making them covet eternal abiding and a kingdom that does not decay.

In sum, the argument from this to the claim that the Garden in which Adam dwelt is the Garden of eternity promised to the righteous is not clear. Then we say: if the Garden were the Garden of eternity whose dominion does not cease, all of its trees would be trees of eternity, and that tree would have no particular distinction among all the trees by being the tree of eternity, and Adam would have mocked Iblis, since he knew that the Garden is the abode of eternity.

If you say: perhaps Adam did not know that at that time, and the wicked one deceived and tricked him into thinking this tree alone was the tree of eternity?

We say: then be content with us giving this very same answer to your claim that if the Garden had been in this world, Adam would have known that Iblis was lying in that, because his words were purely deception and delusion in every case. Thus your argument turns into a proof against you. And with God is success.

They said: As for your claim that the story of Adam in the Cow chapter is very clear that Adam's garden was above the heaven, we demand this clarity from you, and you have no way to establish it.

Your claim that He repeated mention of the descent twice, and the second must convey something other than the first, so the first descent is from the Garden and the second from the heaven:

There is disagreement among the exegetes about this. One group said this is the view you mentioned. Another group, including al-Naqqash and others, said the second descent is from the Garden to the heaven and the first descent is to the earth, and it is the last of the two descents in occurrence, though the first in mention.

And another group said it was mentioned in the manner of emphasis and reinforcement, as one says to a man, "Get out, get out!"

These views are weak. As for the first, its weakness appears in several respects:

The first is that it is merely an assertion with no evidence for it from the wording or from a report that must be followed, and what is of this nature cannot be imposed upon the Qur'an.

The second is that God, glory be to Him, sent Iblis down when he refused to prostrate to Adam, with a cosmic, decreed descent from which he had no way to escape. He said: ﴿Go down from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein; so get out, for you are of the debased﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿Get out of it, for you are accursed, and upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense﴾, and in another place: ﴿Get out of it, reproached and expelled. Whoever follows you among them, I will surely fill Hell with you all﴾. Whether the pronoun in His words "from it" refers to heaven or to the Garden, this is explicit about his being sent down, cast out, cursed and expelled, and "madhur" means banished. Based on this, if the Garden were above the heavens, he would have ascended to it after God had sent him down, and though this is possible, it is far from the wisdom of God and is not implied by the report, so one should not turn to it.

As for the four aspects you mentioned concerning his ascent for the whispering, they, together with God's absolute command to descend and His casting out, cursing and banishing him, have no evidence for them, neither from the wording nor from a report that must be followed. They are nothing but bare possibilities and suppositions without proof.

The third is that the context of God's sending Iblis down clearly indicates that it was a descent to the earth, in several respects. The first is that He, glory be to Him, drew attention to the wisdom of his descent by his arrogance, which warranted his utter humiliation, his expulsion, and his being treated with the opposite of his aim, namely his descent from above the heavens to the bottom of the earth. Wisdom does not require that he be above the heaven, given his greatness and the incompatibility of his state with the state of the noble angels.

The second is that He said: ﴿So get out of it, for you are accursed, and My curse is upon you until the Day of Recompense﴾, and his being accursed and rejected negates that he is in heaven among the near and purified ones.

The third is that He said: ﴿Get out of it, reproached and banished﴾, and the kingdom of the heavens is never entered by one who is reproached and banished.

As for the second opinion, it is the first opinion itself, with the addition of what the context does not indicate in any way, namely placing before what is actually after and placing after what is actually before. It is therefore refuted by the same refutation as the opinion before it.

As for the third opinion, that it is for emphasis: if by this is meant bare verbal emphasis, this does not occur in the Qur'an. If what is meant is that it entails strong admonition and emphasis together with the benefit it contains, this is correct.

The correct view is therefore that the descent is repeated a second time, because a different ruling is attached to it than the one attached to the first descent. For to the first he attached the enmity of some of them toward others, saying: ﴿Get down, some of you enemies to others﴾, and this is a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya), and it is a nominal clause with the pronoun alone according to most, and the meaning is: get down as enemies. To the second descent he attached two other rulings:

The first is their all descending together. The second is His words: ﴿Then, when there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, no fear shall be upon them, nor shall they grieve﴾. It is as if it were said: descend under this condition, with this covenant taken from you: that whenever guidance comes to you from Me, whoever of you follows it, no fear shall be upon him and no grief shall reach him. In the first descent there is a notice of punishment and retribution for the transgression, and in the second descent there is the spirit of consolation and good tidings of the good outcome of this descent for whoever follows My guidance, and his destiny is security and joy, the opposite of fear and grief. Thus He broke them with the first descent, and comforted those who follow His guidance with the second descent, in keeping with His custom, glory be to Him, and His kindness toward His servants and the people of His obedience, just as Adam was broken by being expelled from the Garden and was comforted by the words he received from his Lord, so He accepted his repentance and guided him.

And whoever reflects on His wisdom, glory be to Him, His kindness, and His benevolence toward His servants, and toward those who obey Him, in breaking them and then mending them after they have been broken, just as a servant is broken by sin and humbled by it, and then He mends him through his repentance and His forgiveness of him, and just as He breaks him with various kinds of calamities and trials and then mends him with well-being and blessing, a great door of knowing Him and loving Him will open for him. He will know that He is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child, and that this breaking is in fact His mercy toward him, His kindness, and His gentleness, and that He knows his servant's welfare better than the servant himself does. But the servant, because of the weakness of his insight and his lack of knowledge of his Lord's names and attributes, can hardly perceive this, and does not attain the pleasure of the Beloved, His nearness, the joy and delight of drawing close to Him, or favor in His sight, except by crossing the bridge of humility and lowliness. On this the matter of love is founded, and there is no way to reach the Beloved except by this, as it has been said:

Humble yourself to the one you desire, so that you may gain his nearness,
For how many a honor has a servant attained through humility!

If the one you desire is mighty, and you are not humbled before him,
Then bid farewell to union.

Another said:

Submit and be humbled before the one you love, for in the law of passion
There is no pride that lifts its head and sits.

Another said:

No noble soul has rejoiced in union,
And honor is nothing but its humiliation and its brokenness.

They said: When it is known that Iblis was cast down from the abode of honor immediately after his refusal and arrogance in not prostrating to Adam, it is established that his whispering to him and to his wife took place in other than the place from which he was cast down. And Allah knows best.

They said: As for your statement that Paradise was mentioned with the definite article, and that it refers to the Paradise that the children of Adam know of, there is no doubt that it came in that way. But the reference was established in the address of Allah, exalted is He, to Adam for dwelling in it, when He said: ﴿Dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾. So it was known to Adam. Then He informed us of it, defining it with the definite article, so the customary sense of it turned to that Garden which was known in the mind, the one in which Adam dwelt and from which he was then expelled. So how does this indicate its location or place, by negation or affirmation?

As for the coming of Jannat al-Khuld (the Garden of Eternity) with the definite article, it is because it is the Garden which the Messengers informed their peoples of, and which the All-Merciful promised His servants in the unseen. Therefore, whenever it is mentioned, the mind turns to it and not to any other, because it has become known in hearts and settled in them, and the mind does not turn to anything else, nor is the address directed to anything else. The Garden has indeed come in the Qur'an with the definite article, and what is meant by it is an orchard in a certain tract of land, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed We have tested them as We tested the people of the garden, when they swore that they would surely harvest its fruit in the morning﴾. In this case, the mind does not turn to the Garden of Eternity, nor to the Garden of Adam in any way.

They said: As for your statement that Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah (the People of the Sunnah and the Community) agreed that the Garden and the Fire are created, and that none disputed this except some people of innovation and misguidance, and your use of evidence for the present existence of the Garden, this is true, and we do not dispute with you on it. We have evidence for its existence many times over what you have mentioned. But what is the necessary connection between the Garden of Eternity being created and it being the very Garden of Adam? It is as if you claim that whoever says the Garden of Adam is a garden on earth must say that the Garden and the Fire have not yet been created. This is an error on your part, arising from your imagining that whoever says the Garden has not yet been created must say that the Garden of Adam is on earth, and conversely, that whoever says the Garden of Adam is on earth must say that the Garden has not been created. As for the first, there is no doubt about it.

As for the second, it is an illusion; there is no necessary connection between them, neither in doctrine nor in evidence. You have set up your argument against a group with which we and you agree in rejecting, refuting, and nullifying their view. But it does not follow from this that the falsity of this third view is established, and this is clear.

They said: As for your statement that all that Allah, glory be to Him, negated from the Garden, such as idle talk, punishment, and the other afflictions, some of which were experienced by Iblis, the enemy of Allah, this only occurs after the Resurrection, when the believers enter it, as the context indicates. The answer to this is in two respects:

The first is that the apparent meaning of the report requires its negation absolutely, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no idle talk in it, nor sin﴾, and His saying: ﴿You will not hear in it any idle talk﴾. This is a general negation which may not be restricted except by a clear specifier. Allah, exalted is He, has judged that it is the abode of eternity, a absolute judgment, so none enters it except to abide in it forever. Therefore, your restriction of this description to what comes after the Resurrection contradicts the apparent meaning.

The second is that what you mention is only resorted to when there is evidence, free from a stronger counter-evidence, that it is precisely the Garden of Eternity. Then, and only then, it becomes necessary to adopt what you have mentioned. But when no sound evidence for that exists, and the Ummah has not agreed upon it, it is not permissible to oppose what the clear texts indicate without a valid reason. And Allah knows best.

They said: Among what indicates that it is not the Garden of Eternity which Allah promised to the God-fearing is that when Allah, exalted is He, created Adam, He informed him that his life had an appointed term at whose end it would cease, and that He had not created him for permanence. This is indicated by what al-Tirmidhi related in his Jami', saying: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Safwan ibn Isa told us, saying: al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b told us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah created Adam and breathed the spirit into him, he sneezed and said, 'Praise be to Allah.' His Lord said to him, 'May Allah have mercy on you, O Adam. Go to those angels, to a group of them sitting, and say, Peace be upon you.' They said, 'And upon you be peace.' Then he returned to his Lord, and He said, 'This is your greeting and the greeting of your descendants among themselves.' Then Allah said to him, while His two hands were closed, 'Choose whichever of the two you wish.' He said, 'I have chosen the right hand of my Lord,' and both hands of my Lord are right hands, blessed. Then He opened it, and in it were Adam and his descendants. He said, 'O Lord, who are these?' He said, 'These are your descendants.' Then each person's lifespan was written between his eyes. Among them was a man whose light was the brightest, or one of the brightest. He said, 'O Lord, who is this?' He said, 'This is your son David, and I have decreed for him a lifespan of forty years.' He said, 'O Lord, increase his lifespan.' He said, 'That is what I have decreed for him.' He said, 'O Lord, I have given him from my lifespan sixty years.' He said, 'You and that.'"

He said: "Then He made him dwell in the Garden for as long as Allah willed, then he was sent down from it. Adam used to count the days for himself. Then the Angel of Death came to him, and Adam said to him, 'You have come early! Did you not decree for me a thousand years?' He said, 'Yes, but you gave your son David sixty years.' He denied it, so his descendants denied it, and he forgot, so his descendants forgot. From that day, the writing and the witnesses were commanded."

This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route.

It has also been related through other routes from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet.

They said: This is explicit that Adam was not created in the abode of eternity, in which whoever enters does not die, but he was created in the abode of perishing, for which Allah has appointed a known term for it and its people, and in which He made him dwell. If it is said: If Adam knew that he had a lifespan at whose end he would arrive, and that he was not among the eternal, then how did he not disbelieve Iblis and know the falsity of his words when he said to him: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ Rather, he allowed that and ate from the tree, hoping for eternity?

The answer is what has preceded in the two aspects: either the intended meaning of "eternity" is a long stay until the eternity of eternities, or his enemy Iblis, when he swore to him and to his wife and others, and when they hoped for their remaining in the Garden, forgot what had been decreed for him of his lifespan.

They said: What is relied upon in this is His saying, exalted is He, to the angels: ﴿Indeed I am placing a khalifah (successor/vicegerent) on the earth﴾. This khalifah is Adam, by the agreement of people. When the angels wondered at this and said: ﴿Will You place in it one who will cause corruption in it and shed blood, while we exalt You with Your praise and sanctify You?﴾, He, glory be to Him, made them know that this khalifah whom He was placing on the earth was not in the state they imagined, of corruption. Rather, "I will teach him from My knowledge what you do not know." He then showed his excellence and nobility by teaching him all the names, then presented them to the angels, but they did not know them, and they said: ﴿Glory be to You, we have no knowledge except what You have taught us. Indeed, You are the All-Knowing, the All-Wise﴾. This indicates that this khalifah whose announcement by the Lord, exalted is He, preceded to His angels, and Allah, exalted is He, showed his excellence and nobility, and taught him what the angels did not know, and he is a khalifah placed on the earth, not above the heaven.

If it is said: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed I am placing on the earth a khalifah﴾ means "I will place him on the earth," so the earth is his destination and final place, and this does not contradict his being in the Garden of Eternity above the heaven first, and then going down to the earth for the khilafah which Allah appointed for him. And is the active participle here in the sense of the future, which is why an object is attached to it? The answer is that Allah, glory be to Him, informed His angels that He would create him for the khilafah of the earth, not for dwelling in the Garden of Eternity. His report is true, and His word is the truth. The angels knew that he was Adam. Had He made him dwell in the Garden of Eternity above the heaven, the occurrence of what was announced would not have appeared to the angels, and they would not have needed Him to explain to them his excellence, nobility, and knowledge, which contains the refutation of their words: ﴿Will You place in it one who will cause corruption in it and shed blood?﴾ For they only asked this question about the khalifah placed on the earth. As for one who is in the abode of eternity above the heaven, the angels did not imagine from him the shedding of blood and corruption on earth, nor would the showing of his excellence, nobility, and knowledge while he was above the heaven have been a refutation of their words or an answer to their question. Rather, what their answer was achieved by, and the opposite of what they imagined, is the manifestation of those virtues and sciences from him while he is in the place of his khilafah for which he was created, whereas the angels imagined that nothing but its opposite, corruption and shedding of blood, would come from him there. This is clear to whoever considers it.

As for the active participle, "fa'il," even if it has the sense of the future, it is because this is a report about what the Lord, exalted is He, will do in the future, namely making him a khalifah on earth. He has fulfilled His promise, and what He announced has occurred. This is clear that from the very beginning He made him a khalifah on earth.

As for His making him above in the heaven first and then making him a khalifah on the earth second, although it does not contradict the aforementioned khilafah, it is something the wording does not require in any way; rather, its apparent meaning requires the opposite. So one does not resort to it except by evidence that makes it necessary. And around this we revolve.

They said: Moreover, it is known, and no Muslim disagrees about it, that Allah, glory be to Him, created Adam from earth, and it is the earth of this land without doubt, as al-Tirmidhi related in his Jami' from the hadith of Awf, from Qassamah ibn Zuhayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, created Adam from a handful He took from all the earth, so the children of Adam came according to the earth's variety: among them the red, the white, and the black, and what is between those, and the easy and the hard, the evil and the good."

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith, and Imam Ahmad related it in his Musnad through many routes.

Allah, glory be to Him, has informed us that He created him from earth, and informed us that He created him from an extract of clay, and informed us that He created him from dry clay (salsal) of black, altered mud (hama masnun). It has been said that salsal is dry clay that has a ringing sound as long as it has not been fired; when it is fired, it becomes pottery.

It has also been said that salsal is that which has changed in smell, from the saying "salla" when it becomes foul. Hama is black mud that has changed.

Masnun has been said to mean poured, from "sannantu al-ma'" when one pours water. It has also been said to mean stinking, smooth, from the saying "sannantu al-hajar 'ala al-hajar" when one rubs a stone on a stone. When something flows between them, it is "sinin," and it is only foul.

All of these are stages of the earth, which is its first origin, just as He reported the creation of offspring from a drop of semen, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh. These are the conditions of the drop of semen, which is the origin of offspring. Allah, glory be to Him, did not report that He raised him from the earth above the heavens, neither before fashioning nor after it. He only reported the angels' prostration to him, his entry into the Garden, and what took place with Iblis after his creation. Thus He reported these three matters in one sequence, each linked to the others.

They said: Where is the evidence indicating the ascent of his material and his ascent after his creation above the heavens? You have no evidence for this at all, nor is it a necessary consequence of what Allah has reported.

They said: It is known that what is above the heavens is not a place for foul-smelling, altered earthly clay, which has rotted from its change. Its place is this earth, which is the place of changing and decaying things. As for what is above the angelic realms, change, stench, corruption, and transformation do not reach it.

They said: This is a matter about which sensible people have no doubt.

They said: Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿As for those who are made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills, a gift never cut off﴾ (11:108).

So He has informed us that this gift in the Garden of Eternity is uncut, and what was given to Adam was cut off. So that was not the Garden of Eternity.

They said: Moreover, there is no dispute that Allah, exalted is He, created Adam on earth as has preceded, and He did not mention in his story that He transported him to the heaven. Had He, exalted is He, transported him to the heaven, this would have been more deserving of mention, because it is among the greatest kinds of blessing upon him, and among the greatest causes of his preference and honor, and more eloquent in showing the signs of His power, lordship, and wisdom, and more eloquent in showing the purpose of the consequence of disobedience, which is the descent from the heaven to which he was transported, as was mentioned regarding Iblis. Since neither the Qur'an nor the Sunnah contains a single letter stating that He transported him to the heaven and raised him up to it after his creation on earth, it is known that the Garden in which He placed him was not the Garden of Eternity above the heavens.

They said: Moreover, Allah, glory be to Him, has informed in His Book that He did not create His servants in vain or left aimless, and He denounced those who think so. This indicates that this is contrary to His wisdom. And if the two gardens were the Garden of Eternity of Adam, they would have been created in an abode in which they are neither commanded nor forbidden.

This is refuted by His saying: ﴿Does man think that he will be left aimless?﴾ (75:36).

Al-Shafi'i and others said: idle, neither commanded nor forbidden. And He said: ﴿Did you think that We created you in vain?﴾ (23:115). So He, exalted is He, did not create them in vain, nor left them aimless, and in the Garden of Eternity there is no obligation.

They said: Moreover, He created it as a reward for those who do good, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How excellent is the reward of those who work﴾ (39:74), and as a reward for the God-fearing by His saying: ﴿And excellent is the abode of the God-fearing﴾ (16:30), and as an abode of reward by His saying: ﴿A reward from Allah﴾ (3:195). So none would dwell in it except those whom He created it for among the workers, the God-fearing, and those who followed them of their descendants, and others among the maidens of paradise and the youths.

In sum, the wisdom of Allah, exalted is He, requires that it cannot be attained except after trial, testing, patience, struggle, and various kinds of obedience. And since this is what His wisdom requires, He, glory be to Him, does nothing except what conforms to it.

They said: When what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has informed is gathered together—that He created him from the earth and made him a khalifah (vicegerent) on the earth, and that Iblis whispered to him in his place where He had settled him after Iblis had been brought down from the heaven; and that He informed His angels that He was placing a khalifah on the earth; and that the abode of Paradise has no idle talk therein nor sinning; and that whoever enters it does not leave it ever; and that whoever enters it enjoys bliss without misery; and that he neither fears nor grieves; and that Allah, Glorified is He, has forbidden it to the disbelievers, while the enemy of Allah, Iblis, is the greatest of the disbelievers—then it is impossible that he should enter it at all, neither as passing through nor as settling; and that it is an abode of bliss, not an abode of trial and testing; and other matters we have mentioned concerning the incompatibility of the attributes of the Eternal Paradise with the garden in which Adam was made to dwell—when all of this is gathered, one part to another, and examined with an eye of fairness and freedom from championing positions, the correct view in this becomes clear. And Allah is the One sought for help.

The others said: Rather, the Garden in which Adam was made to dwell, according to the early generations of the Ummah, its imams, and the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah, is the Eternal Garden (Jannat al-Khuld). Whoever said that it was a garden on the earth, in the land of India, or the land of Jeddah, or otherwise, is among the philosophers (mutafalsifah), the heretics (malahidah), and the Mu'tazilah, or among their brethren, the speculative theologians (mutakallimun) who innovated; for this is said by those who say it among the philosophers and the Mu'tazilah. The Book refutes this view, and the early generations of the Ummah and its imams are agreed on the falsity of this view. Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused and was arrogant and was among the disbelievers. (34) And We said, "O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise, and eat therefrom freely wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers." (35) But Satan caused them to slip from it and removed them from that in which they had been. And We said, "Go down, [some of] you to others as enemies, and for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time." (36)﴾

He, glorified is He, has informed that He commanded them to descend, and that some of them are enemies to others. Then He said: ﴿And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time﴾. This makes clear that they were not in the earth, but were brought down to the earth. For if they had been in the earth and had moved from it to another land, as the people of Musa moved from land to land, their settlement and provision for a time would be in the earth before the descent as it is after it.

This is false, they said. And Allah, the Exalted, has said in Surat al-A'raf when Iblis said: ﴿I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay. [Allah] said, "Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein, so get out; indeed, you are of the debased."﴾

This shows the specificity of the Garden which is in the heaven with this ruling, unlike the garden of the earth, for Iblis was not prevented from being arrogant in it. The pronoun in His saying ﴿from it﴾ refers to something known, even though it is not mentioned in the wording, because knowledge of it makes its mention unnecessary.

They said: This is unlike His saying ﴿Go down to a city, for indeed you will have what you ask﴾, for there He did not mention what they were descending from; He only mentioned what they were descending to. Unlike the descent of Iblis, for He mentioned the starting point of his descent, which is the Garden. Descent is from a height to a lowness, and the Children of Israel were in the mountains of al-Sarah overlooking Egypt, to which they descended; and whoever descends from a mountain to a valley is said to have descended.

They said: Also, the Children of Israel used to travel and journey, and whoever travels and journeys, when he comes to a town, is said to have alighted (nazala) there, because it is his custom to ride during his journey, and when he arrives he dismounts from his animals. It is said: the enemy alighted in such-and-such a land, and the caravan alighted, and the like.

The word nuzul is like the word hubut, so nazala and habata are not used except when it is from a height to a lowness. Allah, the Exalted, said after His saying ﴿Go down, [some of] you to others as enemies, and for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time﴾: ﴿He said, "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought out."﴾

This is evidence that they were not before that in a place in which they would live, die, and be brought out from it, and the Qur'an is explicit that they only came to it after the descent.

They said: Even if there were in this only the story of Adam and Musa, it would be sufficient, for Musa only blamed Adam (peace be upon him) for what befell him and his offspring of leaving the Garden, of hardship and difficulty. Had it been a garden on the earth, another of the earth's gardens would have compensated for it. And Musa is greater in rank than to blame him for having brought himself and his offspring out of a garden on the earth.

They said: Likewise the saying of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, when the people desire him to ask for the opening of the gate of Paradise for them, he says: "Has he not expelled you from it except the sin of your father?" For the apparent meaning of this, that it is the Eternal Garden, and that he excused himself to them by saying that it is not fitting for him to ask for its opening when he was expelled from it by his sin, is among the clearest evidences.

The first group said: As for your saying that whoever said it is a garden on the earth is among the philosophers, heretics, and Mu'tazilah, or their brethren, we have indeed found those who said this, and not only from these. The participation of the people of falsehood with the one of truth in a matter does not indicate its falsity, and attributing it to them does not necessitate its falsity unless it is exclusive to them. If you mean that none said this except these, that is not so; and if you mean that these are among those who hold this, it benefits you nothing.

They said: As for your saying that the early generations of the Ummah and its imams are agreed on the falsity of this view, we demand from you a sound transmission from one of the Companions or of those after them among the imams of the early generations, let alone their consensus.

They said: And no report is found from a companion, or a follower, or a follower of a follower, that is sound, connected, nor shadh, nor famous, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah, the Exalted, made Adam dwell in the Eternal Garden which is the abode of the righteous on the Day of Return."

They said: This judge, Mundhir ibn Sa'id, has related from more than one of the early generations that it was not the Eternal Garden. He said: "We shall show you that Abu Hanifah, the jurist of Iraq, and those who follow his view, have said that the Garden of Adam which Allah created is not the Eternal Garden. They are not among the isolated scholars, but among the leaders of the dissenters, and these compilations are filled with their knowledge."

We have mentioned the saying of Ibn 'Uyaynah. Ibn Muzayn mentioned in his tafsir: he said, "I asked Ibn Nafi' about the Garden: is it created?" He said, "Silence about this is better."

They said: If Ibn Nafi' held that the Garden in which Adam dwelt is the Eternal Garden, he would not have doubted that it is created, nor would he have hesitated in this.

Ibn Qutaybah said in his book Gharib al-Qur'an, regarding His saying ﴿And We said, "Go down from it"﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, in the narration of Abu Salih, said: it is like saying "so-and-so descended to such-and-such a land." He mentioned nothing else in his book. Where then is the consensus of the early generations of the Ummah and its imams?

They said: As for your argument with His saying ﴿And for you on the earth is a place of settlement﴾ following His saying ﴿Go down﴾, this does not indicate that they were in the Eternal Garden, for one of the sayings on the matter is that it was a garden in the heaven other than the Eternal Garden, as al-Mawardi related in his tafsir, and it has already been mentioned.

Also, His saying ﴿And for you on the earth is a place of settlement﴾ indicates that they have a place of settlement for a time in the earth cut off from the Garden, necessarily, for the Garden also has an earth. Allah, the Exalted, said concerning the people of the Garden: ﴿And they say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and has caused us to inherit the earth, to dwell in the Garden wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of the workers." (74)﴾

So this shows that His saying ﴿And for you on the earth is a place of settlement﴾ means the earth empty of that Garden, not everything called earth. Their first settlement was in the land of the Garden, then it became the land of trial and testing, and then the settlement of the believers on the Day of Recompense will be the land of the Garden too. So the verse does not indicate that Adam's garden is the Eternal Garden.

They said: This is exactly the same answer to your argument with His saying: ﴿He said, "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought out."﴾ For what is meant is the earth to which they were sent down and made their dwelling in place of the Garden. This is the explanation of the settlement mentioned in al-Baqarah, along with its including the mention of bringing out from it.

They said: As for His saying to Iblis, ﴿Descend from it; it is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾, and your saying that this is only in the Garden which is in the heaven, and that otherwise the garden of the earth did not prevent Iblis from being arrogant in it—this is evidence for us in the matter, for the Eternal Garden has no way for Iblis to enter it or to be arrogant in it at all. Allah, the Exalted, has informed that he whispered to Adam and his wife, denied them, deceived them, betrayed them, was arrogant over them, and envied them, and they were then in the Garden. This shows that it was not the Eternal Garden, and it is impossible that he could ascend to it after his descent and expulsion from it.

They said: The pronoun in His saying ﴿Descend from it﴾ either refers to the heaven, as is one of the two sayings. In that case He, glorified is He, brought him down from the heaven immediately after his refusal to prostrate, informed that it was not for him to be arrogant, and then he was arrogant, lied, and betrayed in the Garden, which shows that it was not in the heaven. Or it refers to the Garden according to the other saying.

It does not follow from this view that the Garden in which Adam dwelt, and his companion deceived him and swore to him falsely, is the one from which he was brought down; rather the Qur'an indicates that it was other than it, as we have mentioned.

In either case, the verse does not indicate that the Garden in which what happened between Adam and Iblis took place is the Eternal Garden.

They said: As for your saying that the Children of Israel were in the mountains of al-Sarah overlooking the land to which they descended, and that they used to travel and journey, and therefore it was said to them, "Descend," this is true and we do not dispute it, and it is itself an answer for us, for descent indicates that that Garden was higher than the land to which they descended. But as for its being the Eternal Garden, no.
