He said: "The matter is not as he said, in our view, because they had already submitted in obedience by slaughtering it, though their saying that they said to Musa was ignorance on their part and one of their blunders."

Eighth: the report of the hardness and severity of the hearts of the community, and the non-establishment of faith within them.

'Abd al-Samad Ibn Ma'qil said, from Wahb: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "After Allah, the Exalted, brought the dead man to life and he informed them of his killer, they denied the killing, and said: 'By Allah, we did not kill him,' after they had seen the signs and the truth." Allah, the Exalted, said: "Then your hearts hardened after that, so they were like stones or even harder in hardness" [al-Baqarah: 74].

Ninth: the requital of the oppressive transgressor with the opposite of his intention, both legally and by decree. The killer intended the inheritance of the slain man and the averting of killing from himself, so Allah, the Exalted, exposed and disgraced him, and deprived him of the inheritance of the slain man.

Tenth: that the Children of Israel were tested with the cow twice among all the animals: they were tested by worshipping the calf, and they were tested by the command to slaughter a cow. The cow is among the most dull-witted of animals, to the extent that it is used as a proverb.

Apparently, this story came after the story of the calf. In the command to slaughter the cow there is a reminder that this kind of animal, which does not refuse slaughter, plowing, or irrigation, is not fit to be a god worshipped besides Allah, the Exalted, and that it is only fit for slaughter, plowing, irrigation, and labor.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 74:

Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil related from Wahb: Ibn Abbas used to say, "After God Most High had brought the dead man back to life and he informed them of his killer, the people denied killing him, and said: 'By God, we did not kill him,' after they had seen the signs and the truth." God Most High said: ﴿Then your hearts hardened after that, so they became like stones or even harder in hardness.﴾

Among these lessons: the oppressive transgressor is repaid with the opposite of his aim, both by the Sacred Law and by divine decree. The killer's aim was the inheritance of the slain man and to ward off execution from himself, but God Most High exposed him and disgraced him, and deprived him of the inheritance of the slain man.

Among them also: the Children of Israel were tested with the cow twice, more than any other animal. They were tested with the worship of the calf, and they were tested with the command to slaughter a cow. The cow is among the dullest of animals, to the point that it is used as a proverbial example.

The apparent view is that this story came after the story of the calf. In the command to slaughter a cow there is an alert that this kind of animal, which does not refuse slaughter, plowing, or irrigation, is not fit to be a god worshipped besides God Most High, and that it is only fit for slaughter, plowing, irrigation, and labor.

Thus is His challenge to them to substantiate their claim, and His repeated pressing of this demand between two alternatives, one of which must hold. The invalidity of one of them has been established, so the other is necessarily affirmed. Their saying, ﴿They will not touch us the Fire except for numbered days﴾, is a report about the unseen, which is known only through revelation. Either it is speech about Allah without knowledge, and so it is a lie, or it is grounded in a revelation from Allah and a covenant He made with the one who reports it. The latter is categorically ruled out, so it is established that it is a false report, and its speaker is a liar against Allah, exalted is He.

(Fā'idah)

Someone said: "I find that when I am called by my name without my title, it is very hard on me, unlike the earlier generation (al-salaf), for they were called by their names."

It was said to him: "This is because of opposing customs, for the attachment of souls to habit is a fixed nature. Also, the name, among the earlier generation, did not indicate a lowly rank of the one being called. Today, ranks in the hearts are known by the sign of the manner of address, so if it falls short, it indicates a shortfall in his rank, and resentment arises from what lies behind the form of address. Thus, when forms of address became the measures of standing, it was hard on the one whose rank was lowered, just as it is hard on him in practice."

The commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 85:

This is a proof from God, by which He argued against the People of the Book. For He had taken from them a covenant that they would not kill one another, nor expel one another from their homes, and that they would ransom one another from captivity. These are three covenants, of which they violated two and acted upon the third: they killed one another and expelled one another from their homes, and then they ransomed their captives because God had commanded them to do so. So if you ransomed the captives because God commanded you to ransom them, then why did you kill one another and expel them from their homes, when God had forbidden you from that? Taking hold of part of the Book necessitates that you take hold of all of it. So how can you disbelieve in part of the Book and believe in part? The recompense of whoever among you does that is nothing but disgrace in the life of this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the most severe punishment. And God is not unaware of what you do.

(Section)

Among that is the saying of the Most High: ﴿Is it, whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls do not desire, that you wax arrogant, so that a group of you you call liars and a group of you you kill?﴾

This is what the theologians (nuzzar) and jurists (fuqaha') call ta-shahhi (following one's desires) and tahakkum (arbitrariness). One of them says to his companion: "You have no proof for what you claim except following your desires and mere arbitrary, baseless judgment. So if there comes to you what you do not desire, you reject it and turn it away, and if the statement agrees with what you desire and crave, whether through imitation of someone you venerate or agreement with what you already want, you accept it." This argument and the one before it silence the opponent, leaving him with no answer at all. For taking hold of part of the Book necessitates taking hold of all of it, and committing to some of its laws necessitates committing to all of them. It is not permissible for the laws to follow desires, for if the Law followed whim and appetite, then nature alone would suffice without it, and each person's desire and whim would be his law. "And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted."

Then what punishment could be greater than the punishment of one who neglects his soul and ruins it, who forgets its interests, its illness and its cure, and the means of its happiness, its success, its righteousness, and its everlasting life in the enduring bliss?

Whoever reflects on this point will find that most of creation has forgotten the reality of their own souls, has ruined them, has wasted their share from God, and has sold them cheaply, in a sale of loss (bay' al-ghabn). This becomes clear to them only at death, and it becomes fully manifest on the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain (Yawm al-Taghabun), the day when the servant realizes that he was cheated in the contract he made for himself in this abode, and in the trade he conducted for his return. Indeed, everyone trades in this world for the sake of the Hereafter.

So the losers, who believe that they are the people of profit and gain, have bought the worldly life and its share and pleasures with the Hereafter and its share. They have squandered their good things in their worldly life, enjoyed them, were content with them, found rest in them, and their striving was directed toward attaining them. So they sold, bought, and traded, and they sold the deferred for the immediate, the credit for the cash, and the absent for the present. They said: "This is prudence." One of them says:

"Take what you see, and leave what you have only heard of.
How could I sell present cash that I witness in this abode
for an absent credit in another abode, other than this one?"

Added to this is the weakness of faith, the strength of the call of desire, love of the fleeting world, and imitation of the sons of their kind. Thus most people are in this losing trade, concerning which God said of its people: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the worldly life with the Hereafter; so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.﴾ And He said of them: ﴿So their trade has not profited, nor were they guided.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 16]. So when the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain comes, the loss in this trade becomes manifest to them, and their souls are consumed with regrets.

As for the winners, they have sold the perishable for the everlasting, the base for the precious, and the trivial for the great. They said: "What is the measure of this world from its beginning to its end, that we should sell our share from God, the Most High, and the Last Abode for it? How can the servant obtain from it in this short time, which in reality is like the fleeting moment of a dream, having no comparison at all to the Abode of Permanence?" God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the day He gathers them, it will be as if they had not remained but an hour of the day, recognizing one another among themselves.﴾ [Yunus: 45].

And God, the Exalted, said: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? In what are you of mention of it? To your Lord is its finality. You are only a warner to those who fear it. It will be as if, on the day they see it, they had not remained but an evening or a morning of it.﴾ [Al-Nazi'at: 42–46].

And God, the Exalted, said: ﴿As if, on the day they see what they were promised, they had not remained but an hour of a day. A proclamation.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 35].

And God, the Exalted, said: ﴿He will say: "How many years did you remain on the earth?" They will say: "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count." He will say: "You remained only a little, if only you had known."﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 112–114].

And God, the Exalted, said: ﴿The day the Horn is blown, and We gather the criminals that day, blue-eyed, whispering among themselves: "You remained only ten [days]." We know best what they say when their most just in conduct says: "You remained only a day."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102–104].

This is the reality of the worldly life when the Day of Resurrection arrives. When they knew how brief their stay in it was, and that they had another abode other than this abode, the abode of life and the abode of permanence, they saw that the greatest loss was to sell the abode of permanence for the abode of perishing. So they traded the trade of the intelligent, and were not deceived by the trade of the foolish among people. Thus on the Day of Mutual Loss and Gain there became manifest to them the profit of their trade and the value of what they had bought. Every person in this world is a seller, a buyer, and a trader, and every person goes forth in the morning, then he is one who sells his soul, and either frees it or destroys it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 88:

There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of their saying, "Our hearts are uncovered" (ghulf).

One group said: the meaning is that our hearts are vessels (awʿiyah) for wisdom and knowledge. Then why do they not understand from you what you have brought? Do they not need you?

According to this view, "ghulf" is the plural of ghilaf (covering, sheath).

The correct view, however, is that of most of the exegetes: the meaning is that our hearts do not comprehend it, and do not understand what you say.

According to this view, it is the plural of aghlaf, like ahmar and humr (red). Abu ʿUbayda said:

"Everything that is in a sheath is aghlaf, just as one says: a sheathed sword (sayf aghlaf), a sheathed bow (qaws aghlaf), and a man who is uncircumcised (rajul aghlaf), not circumcised."

Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada said: "Upon our hearts is a veil (ghishawa), so they are in containers, and they neither grasp nor understand what you say."

This is the correct meaning of the verse, because its parallels recur in the Qur'an, such as their saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings﴾ and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their eyes were under a covering from My remembrance﴾, and similar examples.

As for the view of the one who said they are vessels for wisdom, there is nothing in the wording that indicates this at all.

There is no parallel to it in the Qur'an that would support it, and this expression is not used in praising a person himself for knowledge and wisdom. Where have you found in usage the saying of a speaker: "My heart is a sheath," or "The hearts of the believing knowers are sheaths," meaning vessels of knowledge?

A ghilaf may be a container for both good and bad things. It does not follow that if the heart is a sheath, knowledge and wisdom are inside it. This is quite evident.

If it is said: then what is the meaning of the particle "bal" (rather, nay) according to this view you have strengthened?

As for the other view, it is clear: that is, your hearts are not a place for knowledge and wisdom, rather they are sealed upon.

It is said: the purpose of the transition (idrab) with "bal" is extremely clear.

It is this: they argued that God did not open for them the path to understanding and knowing what the Messenger brought, but rather made their hearts enclosed in coverings so they do not comprehend it. So how is the proof established against them? It is as if they claimed that their hearts were created in coverings, so they are excused for not believing. God refuted them and said: ﴿Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief﴾, and in the other verse: ﴿Rather, God has sealed upon them for their disbelief﴾.

So He, glorified is He, informed that the sealing and the distancing from His guidance and grace was only because of their disbelief, which they chose for themselves and preferred over faith. So He punished them for it with sealing and curse.

The meaning is: He did not create their hearts as coverings that neither grasp nor understand, and then command them to believe while they cannot comprehend it. Rather, they acquired deeds for which We punished them by sealing their hearts and placing a seal upon them.

And among these is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what they already had, although previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾

This is another proof against the Jews in their denial of Muhammad (ﷺ).

They used to fight their neighbours among the Arabs in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam), and they would seek victory over them through the Prophet (ﷺ) before his appearance, so they would be granted victory and be helped. But when the Prophet (ﷺ) appeared, they disbelieved in him and denied his prophethood. Now, seeking victory through him (istiftah, i.e. invoking him as a means of prevailing) and denying his prophethood cannot coexist. If their seeking victory through him was because he is a prophet, then denying his prophethood is impossible. And if denying his prophethood is true, as they claim, then their seeking victory through him was false. If their seeking victory through him was true, then his prophethood is true; and if his prophethood is false, as they say, then their seeking victory through him is false. There is no answer whatsoever for his opponents to this. It can be established in many forms:

The first of them: it is said, "You acknowledged him before his appearance by seeking victory through him, so it is incumbent upon you to acknowledge him after his appearance."

The second: it is said, "You used to seek victory through him, and that was an acknowledgement from you of his prophethood before his appearance, based on what you possessed of knowledge of his coming. When you witnessed him and what was known became visible before your eyes, then affirming him at that point is more fitting. Yet you disbelieved in him at the completion of knowledge, and you believed in him when he was unseen and not yet complete. You believed in him on the assumption of his existence, and you disbelieved in him when his existence was realised. What contradiction and obstinacy could be more manifest than this?"

The third: it is said, "Your belief in him is a necessary consequence of your seeking victory through him, and the existence of the necessitating thing without its consequence is impossible."

The fourth: it is said, "Was your seeking victory through him based on evidence or not? They must say it was based on evidence. Then it is obligatory to apply that evidence consistently and to uphold its implication wherever it is found. To accept its implication in one place and deny it in another, stronger, place is the most invalid of falsehoods."

The fifth: it is said, "If seeking victory through him was a confirmation of the Prophet who announced his coming, and the proofs of the truth of that Prophet were established, then belief in him is required, as confirmation of the earlier Prophet too. And if abstaining from belief before his appearance was a denial of the earlier Prophet, then abstaining from belief in him after his appearance is an even greater denial. Thus, in your disbelief in him you are deniers of both the first and the second Prophet." This is one of the finest of these arguments.

The sixth: it is said, "If seeking victory through him was true, because of the miracles that appeared at the hands of the Prophet (ﷺ) who was foretold, then belief in him at his appearance is stronger, since the miracles that appeared at his hands, which entail his truthfulness, are added to the miracles that appeared at the hands of the Prophet (ﷺ) who was foretold. Thus the evidences of truthfulness are strengthened and his proofs reinforce one another."

The seventh: it is said, "One of two matters is necessarily the case: either your seeking victory through him was an error, or your disbelief and denial of him was. These two cannot both be true. Whichever is wrong, the other is right. But your seeking victory through him is grounded in belief in the first Prophet (ﷺ), so it is grounded in truth. Therefore it is established that your disbelief in him is the falsehood. It cannot be said that denial of him is the truth and that seeking victory through him was false, because that would entail denying one whose truthfulness you have acknowledged, without doubt."

The eighth: it is said, "Believing in him before his appearance is a consequence of believing in the first Prophet (ﷺ), and denying him at that time would be disbelief. So believing in him after his appearance is likewise. If denying him before his appearance entailed disbelief in the first Prophet (ﷺ), then after his appearance it entails it even more strongly. Thus denial of him and belief in the first Prophet (ﷺ) never coexist, neither before his appearance nor after it. Before his appearance this is by your own acknowledgement; after his appearance it is because the indication of his truthfulness is then clearer and stronger, as already explained."

The ninth: it is said, "Seeking victory through him is affirmation and acknowledgement of his prophethood, and denying him is repudiation and disbelief in it. Belief in and confirmation of the mission of one man, and denial and repudiation of it, necessarily entail disbelief. For it entails one of two things: either confirming the prophethood of one who is not a prophet, or repudiating the prophethood of one who is a prophet. Whichever it is, it is disbelief, and you have already confessed against yourselves to disbelief. So: the curse of Allah upon the disbelievers."

The tenth: the argument is established by the method of presenting premises in advance, binding them with their own admission. It is said to them: "Did you not use to seek victory through him?" They say, "Yes." It is said, "Is not seeking victory through him a form of belief in him? So you must acknowledge that." It is said, "Is it not the case that the appearance of the one you used to believe in before his existence obliges you to believe in him? So you must either acknowledge it or openly persist in obstinacy." The enemies of Allah have no objection whatsoever to these arguments, except that they say, "All of this is true, but this one who has appeared is not the one we used to seek victory through." This is among the greatest of slander and obstinacy, for the attributes and signs that are in him correspond to what they had, a correspondence like that of the known to its knowledge. Denying that he is the one is therefore a rejection of the truth and a repudiation of it, with the tongue while the heart recognises it. This is why He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾ And His saying, may He be exalted, suffices in place of all these arguments and formulations: ﴿And when there came to them a Book from Allah, confirming what they already had, although previously they had been seeking victory over those who disbelieved, yet when there came to them what they recognised, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of Allah is upon the disbelievers.﴾

The matter of truth can be displayed in many forms, and in whatever mould it is cast and whatever shape it is brought out in, it appears sound. This is the nature of the proofs of the Qur'an: in whatever form they are presented, they appear in the utmost soundness and clarity. All praise is due to Allah, who guides His believing servants.
The first wrath was because of their disbelief in the Messiah, and the second wrath was because of their disbelief in Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both.

This is an account of a debate between the Messenger and the Jews, when he said to them, ﴿Believe in what Allah has sent down,﴾ and they replied by saying, ﴿We believe in what was sent down to us,﴾ and by this restriction they meant that they should believe only in what was sent down to them and not in anything else. The proof was therefore established against them by their saying this, from two aspects, which are indicated by the Exalted's words: ﴿and they disbelieve in what is beyond it, while it is the truth,﴾ to the end of the verse.

He said: If you have believed in what was sent down to you because it is true, then it is obligatory upon you to believe in what Muhammad brought, because it is true and confirms what is with you. The ruling for the truth is belief in it wherever it is and with whomever it is. So it is incumbent upon you to believe in both truths, or else it is outright disbelief. In his words, ﴿and they disbelieve in what is beyond it, while it is the truth,﴾ there is an extremely wonderful subtle point, namely that when they disbelieved in what came after it, while it is the truth, their belief in what was sent down to them was not on account of its being true. For if they did not follow the truth in what was sent down to them, nor in what Muhammad brought, then had they believed in what was sent down to them as true, they would have believed in the second truth and given the truth its due of belief. So within this testimony against them is the proof that they had believed neither in the first truth nor in the second. The same ruling applies to everyone who separates the truth, believing in part of it and disbelieving in part of it, like one who believes in some of the Book and disbelieves in some, or believes in some of the prophets and disbelieves in some. His belief in what he disbelieves does not benefit him until he believes in all of it.

A parallel to this division is one who rejects the verses about the divine attributes and their reports, while accepting the verses of commands and prohibitions. That does not benefit him, because he has believed in part of the message and disbelieved in part. If the doubt that afflicted one who disbelieves in some of the prophets is not beneficial to him, then the doubt that afflicts one who rejects part of what the Prophet ﷺ brought is more deserving of not being beneficial. And if this is an excuse for him, then the doubt of one who denies some of the prophets is similar.

Just as one is not a believer until he believes in all the prophets, and whoever disbelieves in one of the prophets is like one who disbelieves in all of them, so too one is not a believer until he believes in all that the Messenger brought. If he believes in part of it, he is like one who disbelieves in all of it.

So reflect on this point and take it as a lesson regarding people of differing sects, and it will become clear to you that most of those who claim to have faith are free of faith. There is no power and no strength except with Allah.

The second aspect of the refutation is His saying: ﴿Why then did you kill the prophets of Allah before, if you were believers?﴾

The aspect of refutation is that if you claim that you believe in what was sent down to you and in the prophets who were sent among you, then why did you kill them before, and what was the point of the belief in them and their confirmation that was sent down to you? So you have believed neither in what was sent down to you nor in what was sent down to Muhammad. Then it is as though he anticipated from them the answer that we did not kill those whose prophethood was established, nor did we deny it. So they were answered, on the assumption of this false answer from them, that Moses had come to you with clear proofs and things about whose soundness of prophethood there is no doubt, and then after his absence from you, you worshipped the calf, associated others with Allah and disbelieved in Him. You knew the prophethood of Moses and that the proofs for his truthfulness were established. So He said: ﴿And Moses certainly came to you with clear proofs, then you took the calf after him while you were wrongdoers.﴾ Thus are the proofs and arguments, and the debates of the prophets with their opponents.

Among that is the Exalted's words: ﴿Say: If the abode of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively for you, to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾ They used to say, "We are the beloved of Allah, and the Hereafter is exclusively ours, to the exclusion of the people, and only those of us who worshipped the calf will be punished for a period, then they will come out of the Fire, and that is the length of their worship of it." So the Blessed and Exalted answered their saying that the Fire would not touch them except for a number of days, by demanding of them, and by dividing the matter between their having a covenant with Allah that He had made with them, or their having said about Allah what they do not know. There is no way for them to claim a covenant, so the second is established.

This has already been mentioned. Then He answered their claim of the exclusive possession of the Hereafter with His words: ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful,﴾ because the beloved does not dislike meeting his beloved, and the son does not dislike meeting his father, especially when he knows that his honor and reward are exclusively his. Rather, the thing most beloved to him is meeting his beloved and his father. So when he does not love that and does not wish for it, he is a liar in his saying and false in his claim.

(Benefit)

Al-Suhayli said: As for His words, ﴿and it is the truth, confirming,﴾ they have judged that it is a confirmatory circumstantial clause (hal mu'akkidah). The meaning of a confirmatory circumstantial clause is that its meaning is like the meaning of the verb, because confirmation is what is confirmed in meaning. That is like "qum qa'iman" (stand, standing) and "ana Zaydun ma'rufan" (I am Zayd, known). These are truly confirmatory circumstantial clauses. As for ﴿and it is the truth, confirming﴾, it is not a confirmatory circumstantial clause, because He said ﴿confirming what is with them,﴾ and its confirming what is with them is not in the meaning of "truth," since it is not a condition of the truth that it confirm someone or refute someone. Rather the truth in itself is truth, even if it does not confirm another. But "confirming" here is a circumstantial clause from the noun in the genitive in His words ﴿and they disbelieve in what is beyond it,﴾ and His words ﴿and it is the truth﴾ are a clause also in the sense of a circumstantial clause. The meaning is: how do you disbelieve in what is beyond it, while it is in this state, namely confirming what is with you, just as you say: "Do not insult Zayd while he is a governor, doing good to you." So the clause is a circumstantial clause, and "doing good" is a circumstantial clause after it. The wisdom in placing the clause that occupies the position of a circumstance before your saying "doing good" and "confirming" is that if you postponed it, it would be imagined that it is in the position of a circumstance from the pronoun in "doing good" and "confirming." Do you not see that if you said "insult Zayd doing good to you while he is a governor," the mind would go to the idea that you mean "doing good to you" in this state? So when you placed it first, the intended meaning became clear and the ambiguity was removed. There is another aspect that applies to this verse and to the verse in Surah Fatir: ﴿And that which We revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it,﴾ which is that "confirming" here is a circumstance governed by what is indicated by the demonstrative sense that the definite article (alif and lam) points to, because the definite article does indicate what demonstrative nouns indicate.

Sibawayh related: "li-man al-dar maftūḥan bābuhā" (To whom is this house, its door being open?).

So your saying "maftūḥan bābuhā" is a circumstance that is not governed by the "settledness" (istiqrār) connected to "li-man," because that contradicts the intended meaning. The correct meaning is "li-man hādhā al-dār maftūḥan bābuhā," and by mentioning the definite article it has dispensed with the demonstrative, and the addressee knows that it is a pointing, and the pointing alerts the addressee to consider, and that alerted meaning becomes the governing factor of the circumstance. Likewise His words ﴿and it is the truth, confirming﴾: it is as if He says, "that is the truth, confirming," because the truth is ancient and known by reason and by earlier scriptures. So when He pointed, the pointing alerted the governing factor of the circumstance, just as when you say "this is Zayd standing," the pointing alerts the addressee to look, and it is as if you said "look at Zayd standing," because the noun "Zayd" is the governing factor, but it indicates and alerts to the meaning governing the circumstance, and that meaning is "look." Among the things the definite article has dispensed with in place of demonstratives are the sayings "al-yawma qumta" (today you stood), "wa-l-sa'ata ji'ta" (and now you came), "wa-l-laylata fa'alta" (and tonight you did), and "al-āna qa'adta" (now you sat). You have dispensed with the demonstratives by the definite article.

I say: What the grammarians mean by "confirmatory circumstance" is not what they mean by confirmation in the section on the followers (tawabi'). The confirmation designated there is more specific than the confirmation intended in the confirmatory circumstance. Rather, what they mean by a confirmatory circumstance is that which establishes the content of the sentence by mentioning a description that does not separate from the governing factor and is not detached from it, even if the meaning of that description is not the very meaning of the sentence. This is like their saying "Zayd is your father, affectionate." Being affectionate is not the meaning of being his father, but mentioning fatherhood indicates the affection that necessarily accompanies it. Likewise His words ﴿it is the truth, confirming what is before it﴾: what is before it is truth, and truth necessarily entails that some of it confirms some of it. As for his saying that it is not a condition of the truth that it confirm someone, it may be said this is not parallel to our question. Rather, truth necessarily entails, with no separation from it, that some of it confirms other parts. So the confirming of what is before it of the truth is from the aspect of its being truth, and this is the meaning of their saying that it is a confirmatory circumstance, so understand it. The meaning is that it cannot be except in this attribute, and it establishes the content of the sentence, confirming and clarifying that it is truth in itself.

As for his saying that it is a circumstance from the genitive in His words ﴿and they disbelieve in what is beyond it﴾,

the meaning is: they disbelieve in it while it confirms what is with them.

This meaning, though correct, is not the meaning of the circumstance in the Qur'an wherever it occurs in this sense.

Suppose this claim could be made in this place; how then would one say of His words, ﴿And that which We revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what is before it,﴾ when the speech and the arrangement are one? Moreover, the meaning when "confirming" is a circumstance from His words ﴿and it is the truth﴾ is more eloquent and complete than when it is made a circumstance from the genitive noun. For when it is made a circumstance from the genitive, the denunciation is directed at them for their disbelief in it while it confirms what is with them and while it is truth, and these two are circumstances of the genitive.

That is: they disbelieve in it in this state.

When it is made a circumstance from the content of His words ﴿and it is the truth﴾, the meaning is: they disbelieve in it while it is truth and confirms what is with them. So they disbelieved in it in its greatest state, which necessarily entails confirming it and believing in it, namely the combination of its being truth in itself and its confirming what is with them. So disbelief in it when the two attributes are combined is more severe and more shameful. You will not find this meaning and this emphasis when it is said, "they disbelieve in it while it is truth and while it confirms what is with them." So reflect on it.

It is truly wonderful. Thus the statement of the grammarians and the exegetes about the verse is correct, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 94:

Some of them said: The truthful person is one who is ready to die and does not feel shame at his secret being exposed. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿So wish for death, if you are truthful.﴾

I say: This verse has a well-known body of discussion among people.

They said: It is a miracle (mu'jizah) of the Prophet ﷺ. With it he defeated the Jews, invited them to wish for death, and informed them that they would never wish for it. This is one of the signs of his prophethood ﷺ, since their inner states cannot be known except through reports of the unseen. Allah never allowed their tongues to utter such a wish.

Another group said: When the Jews claimed that the Last Abode with Allah belonged to them exclusively, to the exclusion of people, and that they were His sons and His beloved and the people of His honour, Allah refuted their claim. He said: If you are truthful, wish for death, so that you may reach Paradise, the abode of bliss, for the beloved longs to meet his beloved. Then He, glorified be He, informed them that they would never wish for it, because of the sins and transgressions their hands had committed, which stand between them and what they claimed. So He said: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 95].

Another group, including Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, said: This is of the same kind as the verse of mubahalah (mutual invocation of curse), and that when they were obstinate, rejected guidance despite its clarity, and concealed the truth, He called them to a matter that would decide between them and Him: that they should invoke death upon the liar and the fabricator. Wishing (tamanni) is a request and a supplication, so wish for death and invoke it upon the falsifier, the liar and the fabricator.

On this view, the meaning is not that they should wish it for themselves specifically, as those holding the first two opinions said. Rather its meaning is: invoke death and wish it upon the one in the wrong. This is more conclusive in establishing the proof and the evidence of truthfulness, and safer from their opposing the Messenger of Allah with the words: "Then you wish it too, if you are right that you are the people of Paradise," so that they might attain the reward and honour of Allah. They were most eager of all to oppose him, so had they understood from it what those people mentioned, they would have opposed him with the same.

Moreover, we observe many of them wishing for death because of their harm, their affliction, and the severity of their condition, and invoking it. This is unlike wishing for death and invoking it upon the lying sect, for this never happens, and never occurred from any of them during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ at all. That is because of their knowledge of the truth of his prophethood and his truthfulness, and their disbelief in him out of envy and rebellion. So they will never wish it, knowing that they are the liars.

This is the view we choose. And Allah knows best what He intended by His Book.

He said in (Bada'i' al-Fawa'id):

Within this debate is a striking miracle of the Prophet: in a context of disputation with opponents who are the most eager of people for his enmity and denial, he informs them with a categorical statement that they will never wish for death. Had they known in themselves that they would wish for it, they would have found a way to refute him. Rather, they were humiliated and defeated, and they knew the truth of his words. What prevented them from wishing for death was their knowledge of what awaits them with Allah of disgrace and painful punishment, because of their disbelief in the prophets, their killing of them, and their hostility to the Messenger of Allah.

If it is said: Why did they not openly express the wish, even though they were lying, saying "We wish it"?

It is said: This is also another miracle, namely that Allah withheld from their hearts and tongues the wish for it, so their hearts did not desire it and their tongues did not utter it, in confirmation of His words: ﴿but they will never wish for it﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verses 97–98:

The Jews said to the Prophet (ﷺ), "Who is your companion who comes to you from the angels? For there is no prophet to whom an angel does not come with the news?"

He said, "It is Jibril (Gabriel)." They said, "That is the one who descends with war and fighting; he is our enemy. If you had said Mikail (Michael), who descends with plants, rain and mercy..." So God Most High revealed: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Jibril, [let him know that] he has sent it down upon your heart by God's permission, confirming what was before it, and as guidance and good tidings for the believers. Whoever is an enemy to God, His angels, His messengers, Jibril and Mikail, then indeed God is an enemy to the disbelievers.﴾

The point is that God, glorified is He, has appointed angels over the upper and lower worlds, and they manage the affairs of the world by His permission, will and command. For this reason, He sometimes attributes the management (tadbir) to the angels, because they are the ones who directly carry it out, as in His saying: ﴿And by those who manage affairs.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 5].

And He attributes the management to Himself, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne, managing the affair.﴾

And His saying: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who owns hearing and sight? And who brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living? And who manages the affair?" They will say, "God."﴾ [Yunus: 31].

So He is the one who manages the affair, by His permission and will, and the angels carry out the management directly and in obedience.

﴿And when there came to them a messenger from God, confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs, as if they did not know.﴾ (2:101)

Consider His saying, exalted is He, in this verse: ﴿And when there came to them a messenger from God, confirming what was with them.﴾ How you find under it a great proof of his truthfulness: the coming of the second messenger with what agrees with what the first messenger brought and confirms it, despite the distance of their times, and the testimony of his enemies and their acknowledgment that he did not receive it from a human. For this reason they used to test him with things they knew he could not report except by a son or one who had taken from him, while they knew that he had not taken from anyone at all. Had that been the case, his enemies would have found a way to criticize him and would have opposed him with the like of what he brought, since it is possible that, if what he brought had been taken from a human, they could have taken it from an angel or its equivalent and opposed what he brought. The point is that the agreement of what he brought with what the first messenger reported, without collusion, without prior arrangement, and without receiving it from him or from anyone who had taken from him, is a decisive proof of the truthfulness of both messengers together.

A parallel to this is a man who testifies to a testimony, reporting in it something that makes one certain that he is truthful in his testimony, with a truthfulness not open to any doubt. Then another comes from another land, who had not met the first and had not colluded with him, and reports the like of that testimony exactly, while one is certain that he had not met him and had not received it from anyone who had met him. This suffices for his truthfulness when the report stands alone. How much more so when it is accompanied by proofs that make one certain of his truthfulness, greater than the proofs that accompanied the report of the first. The agreement of the second's report with the first's report suffices for knowledge of the second's truthfulness; how much more so when the first gave him good tidings of it; and how much more so when accompanied by the second's proofs indicating his truthfulness, like those that accompanied the first and stronger than them. And God knows best.

**(Benefit)**

Permission (al-idhn) is also of two kinds. The first is universal (kawni), as in Allah's words: ﴿And they could not harm anyone thereby except by the permission of Allah﴾.

The second is religious (dini), meaning a command, as in His words: ﴿Has Allah given you permission?﴾ and His words: ﴿Permission is given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged﴾.

**[Section: The Stages of the Lover]**

The lover has three stages: a stage of beginning (ibtida'), a stage of middle (tawassut), and a stage of end (intiha').

As for the stage of his beginning, they said: it is obligatory for him to resist it (his passion) with everything he is able to do, when reaching his beloved is impossible, by decree and by law. If he is unable to do that, and his heart refuses except to travel to his beloved, which is the stage of the middle and the end, then it is incumbent upon him to conceal that, not to disclose it to the creation, and not to gloat over his beloved or expose her among the people. Otherwise he combines shirk and injustice. Injustice in this domain is among the greatest kinds of injustice, and it may cause greater harm to the beloved and her family than injustice to her property. For exposing her in his passion exposes the beloved to people's gossip and to dividing into those who believe and those who deny. Most people believe in this domain on the slightest suspicion. When it is said, "So-and-so did such a thing with so-and-so, a man or a woman," one person denies it and nine hundred and ninety-nine believe it.

The report of a lover who exposes himself, in this matter, is considered by people to give certain knowledge. Indeed, when the one who was loved tells them about himself falsely and by slander against another, they are certain of his truthfulness with a certainty that admits no contradiction. Even if the two of them were brought together in one place by chance, they would be certain that this was the result of a promise and an arrangement between them. Their certainty in this domain rests on assumptions, imaginings, doubts, illusions and false reports, just as their certainty about observable sensory matters does. With this, the people of slander fell upon the pure and purified one, the beloved of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was declared innocent from above the seven heavens, on the pretext of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal bringing her alone behind the army, until those who perished perished. Had Allah, glorified is He, not undertaken her innocence, her defence, and the refutation of her accuser, it would have become another matter.

The point is that in publicizing the afflicted one's love for someone who is not lawful for him to be joined with, there is, through his injustice and harm, what constitutes aggression against her and her family, and an exposure to many people believing their suspicions about her. If he seeks help against her from someone who inclines her toward him, whether through desire or fear, the injustice spreads and grows, and that intermediary becomes an unjust pimp (dayyuth). If the Prophet (ﷺ) cursed the broker (ra'ish), who is the intermediary between the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it in delivering the bribe, then what do you think of the pimp who is the intermediary between the lover and the beloved in bringing about union? The lover and the pimp then cooperate in oppressing the beloved and oppressing others whose achievement of his aim depends on wronging them in person, property or honour. Often what is sought depends on killing a soul whose life prevents his aim, and how many slain have had their blood spilled for this reason: a husband, a master, a relative. How many women have been turned against their husbands, and slave girls and male slaves against their masters! The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed whoever does that and disowned him, and it is among the greatest of major sins.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade a man to propose upon his brother's proposal and to bid upon his brother's bid, how then about one who strives to separate a man from his wife and his slave girl until he reaches them himself?

Lovers of forms and their pimp-helpers among the cuckolds do not consider this a sin. If the lover seeks union with his beloved and sharing with her husband or master, then in that there is the sin of wronging another, which may not fall short of the sin of fornication, even if it is not greater than it. The right of the other is not dropped by repentance from fornication, for although repentance removes the right of Allah, the right of the servant remains, and he has the claim to demand it on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, among the injustices of a father is corrupting his child, the fruit of his heart, and one who is dearer to him than himself. Thus the injustice of corrupting a husband's beloved and violating his bed is greater than taking all of his property. For this reason, it hurts him more than the taking of his wealth, and nothing is worth more to him than the shedding of his blood. How great an injustice, and more sinful than committing fornication! If that right belongs to a warrior in the way of Allah, the perpetrator will be made to stand before him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him, "Take from his good deeds as much as you wish," as the Prophet (ﷺ) reported.

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "What do you think?" meaning: what do you think will remain of his good deeds? If it is added that the wronged party is a neighbour or a close relative within the prohibited degrees, the injustice multiplies and becomes an emphatic injustice, causing the severing of kinship and the harming of a neighbour. "The one who severs ties of kinship will not enter Paradise," and "one whose neighbour is not safe from his harms" (will not enter Paradise).

If the lover seeks help from the devils of the jinn in achieving union with his beloved, whether through magic, enslavement, or something similar, then to shirk and injustice is added the disbelief of magic. If he himself does not do it but is content with it, he is content with disbelief, not disliking the attainment of his aim, and this is not far from disbelief.

The point is that cooperation in this domain is cooperation in sin and transgression.

As for what accompanies the attainment of the lover's aim of widespread injustice whose harm extends, it is no hidden matter. When he obtains his objective from the beloved, the beloved has other aims that she wants the lover to help her achieve, and he finds no escape from helping her. So each of them continues to help the other in injustice and aggression. The beloved helps the lover to wrong those connected to her, her family, relatives, master, or husband, and the lover helps the beloved to wrong whoever her aim depends upon wronging. Each of them helps the other in their aims which include wronging people, so aggression and injustice occur because they share in ugliness through cooperating in injustice, as is the custom among lovers and beloveds: the lover helps his beloved in what involves injustice, aggression and oppression, to the point that he may strive for her a position unfitting for her and not suited to one like her, or for acquiring wealth unlawfully, or for lording over others. When her dispute with others arises, or they complain to each other, the only one in the wrong or the wronged is the beloved, whoever she may be. Added to that is the lover's injustice to people by plotting to take their wealth and reaching his beloved through this by theft, usurpation, betrayal, a false oath, highway robbery, or something similar. It may even lead to killing a soul that Allah has forbidden, in order to take its wealth and reach his beloved with it.

All these calamities, and multiples of them, and multiples of multiples, arise from love of forms. It may even drive a person to outright disbelief. A group who grew up in Islam have become Christians because of love. This happened to one of the callers to prayer (mu'adhdhin) when he saw a beautiful woman on a roof, became captivated by her, descended, went in to her, and solicited her. She said, "I am a Christian; if you enter my religion I will marry you." He did so, and that same day he climbed a step among them, fell from it, and died. This was mentioned by 'Abd al-Haqq in his book al-'Aqiba.

When the Christians want to convert a captive, they show him a beautiful woman and command her to make him desire her, until her love takes root in his heart, and then she offers herself to him if he enters her religion. At that point: ﴿Allah firmly establishes those who believe with the firm word in the worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah misguides the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

In love there is injustice by each of the lover and the beloved toward the other, by helping the other in fornication, and injustice to oneself in it. Each of them wrongs himself and his companion, and their injustice extends to others as mentioned before. Greater than that is their injustice through shirk. Love thus contains all kinds of injustice.

If the beloved does not fear Allah, she exposes the lover to ruin, and that is an injustice from her: she makes him desire her, adorns herself for him, and attracts him in every way until she extracts his wealth and benefit from him, yet does not let him have her, so that her aim is not lost by his attaining his desire from her. She inflicts on him the worst torment. The lover may kill his beloved to satisfy his own soul against her, especially if she grants union to someone else. How many slain there are for love on both sides! How much blessing it has removed, how much wealth it has reduced to poverty, how many ranks it has brought down, how much unity it has scattered, and how many families and children of a man it has corrupted! When a woman sees her husband in love with another, she takes a lover for herself, so the man is torn between ruining his house by divorce and being a pimp (qiyada). Some people prefer one, and some prefer the other.

So the intelligent person must not allow love of forms to govern him, lest it lead him to these corruptions, or most of them, or some of them. Whoever does that is the one who neglects his soul and exposes it to danger. If it is destroyed, he is the one who destroyed it. Had he not repeatedly gazed at his beloved's face and hoped for union, his love would not have taken root in his heart. The first cause of love is admiration, whether it arises from looking or hearing. If it is not accompanied by hope of union, and despair accompanies it instead, love does not arise in him. If hope accompanies it, but he turns away from it, does not dwell on it, and does not occupy his heart with it, that love does not arise in him. If he prolongs his thinking about the beauties of the beloved with that hope, and fear of something greater in his estimation than the pleasure of union accompanies it, whether a religious fear such as entering the Fire, the wrath of the Almighty, or bearing the burdens of sins, and this fear overcomes that hope and that thinking, then that love does not arise in him. If this religious fear is absent, and a worldly fear accompanies it, such as fear of destroying his soul or his wealth, or losing his status and the fall of his rank among people, or falling from the eyes of one dear to him, and this fear overcomes the call of love, he repels it. Likewise, if he fears losing someone he loves more and who is more beneficial to him than that beloved, and he prefers the love of that person over love of this beloved, love is repelled from him. But if all of that is absent, and the love of the beloved prevails, the heart is drawn to her entirely, and the soul inclines toward her with complete inclination.

(Section)

The Ghadabiyya community said:

The Torah prohibited matters that had previously been permitted, and it did not bring the permitting of something prohibited. The abrogation (naskh) that we deny and reject is that which necessitates the permitting of something prohibited, because the prohibition of a thing is only on account of the harm (mafsada) in it. So when a law comes with its prohibition, that is among its confirmations and affirmations. But if someone comes who permits it, we know by the permitting of the harm that he is not a prophet. This is unlike the prohibition of what was permitted, for we are then obligated to worship by its prohibition.

They said: Your law has come with the permitting of much of what the Torah prohibited, even though it was only prohibited because of the harm in it.

This point is what the Ghadabiyya community relies upon, and their later ones inherit it from their predecessors, and the theologians (al-mutakallimun) did not satisfy them in answering it. Rather, they prolonged their discussion with them about lifting the original state of non-obligation (al-bara'a al-asliyya) through the laws, and about abrogating permissibility by prohibition.

By the life of God, this indeed refutes their doubt, because lifting the original non-obligation, and lifting permissibility by prohibition, is a change of what the ruling was upon, whether the presumptive (istis-habi) or the legal ruling, into another ruling for a benefit that required its change. There is no difference, in the requirement of benefit, between changing permissibility into prohibition or changing prohibition into permissibility.

The doubt that arose for them in one of the two places is exactly the same in the other place. For the permissibility of a thing in the law follows the absence of its harm, since if there were a preponderant harm in it, the law would not have come with its permitting. So if another law prohibited it, it is certainly necessary that its prohibition in it is the benefit, just as its permitting in the earlier law was the benefit. If the permitting of the forbidden fats in the earlier law entailed the permitting of harms, far be it from God, then the prohibition of what was permitted in the earlier law entails the prohibition of benefits. Both are certainly false.

So if it is permissible for the Torah's law to prohibit what Abraham and those before him used to permit, it is permissible for another law to make lawful some of what was forbidden in the Torah.

This false and refuted doubt is the one with which the Ghadabiyya community rejected the prophethood of our master Muhammad (ﷺ). It is exactly the same doubt with which their predecessors rejected the prophethood of al-Masih, and they inherited it, disbelief from disbelief. They said to Muhammad (ﷺ), just as their predecessors said to al-Masih: "We do not acknowledge the prophethood of anyone other than the law of the Torah."

It is said to them: How then did you acknowledge Musa's prophethood, when he came with changing some of the laws of those before him? If that discredits al-Masih and Muhammad, peace be upon them, it discredits Musa too. You cannot discredit their prophethood with any discredit except that its like applies equally to the prophethood of Musa, just as you do not establish Musa's prophethood with any proof except that its multiples bear witness to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). So it is among the clearest impossibilities that Musa be a truthful messenger while Muhammad is not a messenger, or that al-Masih be a messenger while Muhammad (ﷺ) is not a messenger.

It is also said to the Ghadabiyya community: The forbidden thing is either such that its prohibition is due to its essence and self, such that its permitting is prevented at any time, or its prohibition is due to the harm it contains, in one time and not another, one place and not another, one state and not another.

If it is the first, it follows that what the Torah prohibited would be forbidden to all the prophets at every time and place, from the era of Nuh to the Seal of the Prophets, peace be upon them.

If it is the second, it is established that prohibition and permission follow benefits, and differ with the difference of time, place and state. Thus one thing would be forbidden in one religion and not another, at one time and not another, in one place and not another, in one state and not another. This is known necessarily from the laws, and the wisdom of the Wisest of the wise does not fit anything other than this.

Do you not see that if the prohibition of the Sabbath were due to its essence, it would be forbidden to Abraham, Nuh and all the prophets?

Likewise, what the Torah prohibited of foods, marriages and others, if it were forbidden in its essence and self, it would be necessary to prohibit it for every prophet and in every law.

Since the Lord, exalted is He, is not subject to any restriction, but does what He wills, rules as He desires, tests His servants as He wills, and He rules and is not ruled over, what is it that makes it impossible for Him, or prevents Him, from commanding one nation with a command from the commands of the law, then forbidding another nation from it, or prohibiting something for one nation and permitting it for another?

Rather, what prevents Him, glorified is He, from doing that within a single law at two different times, according to the benefit? He has explained this in His saying: ﴿Whatever We abrogate of a verse, or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that God is over all things competent?* Do you not know that God has the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106–107].

So He informed, glorified is He, that the generality of His power, His dominion, and His disposal in His kingdom and creation does not prevent Him from abrogating what He wills and confirming what He wills, just as He erases from His decreed, cosmic rulings what He wills, and confirms. Likewise with His religious, commanding rulings: He abrogates from them what He wills and confirms from them what He wills.

Among the greatest disbelief and the greatest injustice is that the Messenger who came with clear proofs and guidance be opposed, his prophethood be repelled, and his message be denied, on the grounds that he brought the permitting of some of what was forbidden to those before him, or the prohibition of some of what was permitted to them. And with God is success; He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills.

It is strange that this Ghadabiyya community restricts God, exalted is He, from abrogating what He wills of His laws, while they have abandoned the law of Musa, peace be upon him, in most of what they are upon, and have adhered to what their rabbis and scholars legislated for them.

Among that: they say in their prayer what its translation is as follows: "O God, sound a great trumpet for our gathering, and gather us together from the four corners of the earth to Your holy place, glory be to You, O gatherer of the scattered of the children of Israel."

And they say every day what its translation is as follows: "Restore our judges as at first, and our counsellors as at the beginning, and build Jerusalem, the city of Your holiness, in our days, and honour us by its building, glory be to You, O builder of Jerusalem."

This is their saying in their prayer, though they know that Musa and Harun, peace be upon them, said none of that. Rather, these are sections they fabricated after the collapse of their state.

Likewise their fasts: like the fast of the burning of the Holy House, the fast of Hasa, and the fast of Gedalia, which they made obligatory, which Musa did not observe, nor Yushaʿ ibn Nun. Likewise the fast of the crucifixion of Haman. None of that is in the Torah; rather they instituted them for reasons that required their institution among them.

This.

Yet the Torah says what its translation is: "Do not add to the matter that I am commanding you anything, and do not subtract from it anything."

The Torah contains very many commands which they are all agreed to suspend and nullify. Either they are abrogated by other texts of the Torah, or by a sound transmission from Musa, peace be upon him, or by the ijtihad of their scholars.

On all three possibilities, their doubt about denying abrogation is refuted.

Then, strangely, the greatest of those commands which they agree not to say or act upon, they base on the sayings of their scholars and rulers. They have agreed to suspend the stoning of the adulterer, although it is a text of the Torah, and to suspend many rulings explicitly stated in the Torah.

Among Satan's manipulation of them: they claim that if the jurists make something lawful for them, it becomes lawful, and if they prohibit it, it becomes forbidden, even if the text of the Torah is contrary.

This is their permitting themselves to abrogate what they wish from the Torah's law. They have thus restricted the Lord, exalted and sanctified is He, from abrogating what He wills of His law, and permitted that for their rabbis and scholars.

Just as Iblis was arrogant to prostrate to Adam, seeing that as a disgrace to him, then he was content to be a pimp for every rebel and sinner.

And just as the idol worshippers refused that the prophet sent to them be a human, then were content that their god and object of worship be a stone.

And just as the Christians, by their abandonment, exonerated God from having a son and a consort, yet did not shy from attributing that to God, glorified is He.

And just as the Pharaonic Jahmiyya exonerated the Lord, glorified is He, from being established upon His Throne, lest it imply confinement, then placed Him, glorified is He, in wells and taverns, and in the bellies of animals.

(Section)

The Ghadabiyya community said:

The Torah prohibited matters that had previously been permitted, and it did not bring the permitting of something prohibited. The abrogation (naskh) that we deny and reject is that which necessitates the permitting of something prohibited, because the prohibition of a thing is only on account of the harm (mafsada) in it. So when a law comes with its prohibition, that is among its confirmations and affirmations. But if someone comes who permits it, we know by the permitting of the harm that he is not a prophet. This is unlike the prohibition of what was permitted, for we are then obligated to worship by its prohibition.

They said: Your law has come with the permitting of much of what the Torah prohibited, even though it was only prohibited because of the harm in it.

This point is what the Ghadabiyya community relies upon, and their later ones inherit it from their predecessors, and the theologians (al-mutakallimun) did not satisfy them in answering it. Rather, they prolonged their discussion with them about lifting the original state of non-obligation (al-bara'a al-asliyya) through the laws, and about abrogating permissibility by prohibition.

By the life of God, this indeed refutes their doubt, because lifting the original non-obligation, and lifting permissibility by prohibition, is a change of what the ruling was upon, whether the presumptive (istis-habi) or the legal ruling, into another ruling for a benefit that required its change. There is no difference, in the requirement of benefit, between changing permissibility into prohibition or changing prohibition into permissibility.

The doubt that arose for them in one of the two places is exactly the same in the other place. For the permissibility of a thing in the law follows the absence of its harm, since if there were a preponderant harm in it, the law would not have come with its permitting. So if another law prohibited it, it is certainly necessary that its prohibition in it is the benefit, just as its permitting in the earlier law was the benefit. If the permitting of the forbidden fats in the earlier law entailed the permitting of harms, far be it from God, then the prohibition of what was permitted in the earlier law entails the prohibition of benefits. Both are certainly false.

So if it is permissible for the Torah's law to prohibit what Abraham and those before him used to permit, it is permissible for another law to make lawful some of what was forbidden in the Torah.

This false and refuted doubt is the one with which the Ghadabiyya community rejected the prophethood of our master Muhammad (ﷺ). It is exactly the same doubt with which their predecessors rejected the prophethood of al-Masih, and they inherited it, disbelief from disbelief. They said to Muhammad (ﷺ), just as their predecessors said to al-Masih: "We do not acknowledge the prophethood of anyone other than the law of the Torah."

It is said to them: How then did you acknowledge Musa's prophethood, when he came with changing some of the laws of those before him? If that discredits al-Masih and Muhammad, peace be upon them, it discredits Musa too. You cannot discredit their prophethood with any discredit except that its like applies equally to the prophethood of Musa, just as you do not establish Musa's prophethood with any proof except that its multiples bear witness to the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). So it is among the clearest impossibilities that Musa be a truthful messenger while Muhammad is not a messenger, or that al-Masih be a messenger while Muhammad (ﷺ) is not a messenger.

It is also said to the Ghadabiyya community: The forbidden thing is either such that its prohibition is due to its essence and self, such that its permitting is prevented at any time, or its prohibition is due to the harm it contains, in one time and not another, one place and not another, one state and not another.

If it is the first, it follows that what the Torah prohibited would be forbidden to all the prophets at every time and place, from the era of Nuh to the Seal of the Prophets, peace be upon them.

If it is the second, it is established that prohibition and permission follow benefits, and differ with the difference of time, place and state. Thus one thing would be forbidden in one religion and not another, at one time and not another, in one place and not another, in one state and not another. This is known necessarily from the laws, and the wisdom of the Wisest of the wise does not fit anything other than this.

Do you not see that if the prohibition of the Sabbath were due to its essence, it would be forbidden to Abraham, Nuh and all the prophets?

Likewise, what the Torah prohibited of foods, marriages and others, if it were forbidden in its essence and self, it would be necessary to prohibit it for every prophet and in every law.

Since the Lord, exalted is He, is not subject to any restriction, but does what He wills, rules as He desires, tests His servants as He wills, and He rules and is not ruled over, what is it that makes it impossible for Him, or prevents Him, from commanding one nation with a command from the commands of the law, then forbidding another nation from it, or prohibiting something for one nation and permitting it for another?

Rather, what prevents Him, glorified is He, from doing that within a single law at two different times, according to the benefit? He has explained this in His saying: ﴿Whatever We abrogate of a verse, or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or similar to it. Do you not know that God is over all things competent?* Do you not know that God has the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106–107].

So He informed, glorified is He, that the generality of His power, His dominion, and His disposal in His kingdom and creation does not prevent Him from abrogating what He wills and confirming what He wills, just as He erases from His decreed, cosmic rulings what He wills, and confirms. Likewise with His religious, commanding rulings: He abrogates from them what He wills and confirms from them what He wills.

Among the greatest disbelief and the greatest injustice is that the Messenger who came with clear proofs and guidance be opposed, his prophethood be repelled, and his message be denied, on the grounds that he brought the permitting of some of what was forbidden to those before him, or the prohibition of some of what was permitted to them. And with God is success; He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills.

It is strange that this Ghadabiyya community restricts God, exalted is He, from abrogating what He wills of His laws, while they have abandoned the law of Musa, peace be upon him, in most of what they are upon, and have adhered to what their rabbis and scholars legislated for them.

Among that: they say in their prayer what its translation is as follows: "O God, sound a great trumpet for our gathering, and gather us together from the four corners of the earth to Your holy place, glory be to You, O gatherer of the scattered of the children of Israel."

And they say every day what its translation is as follows: "Restore our judges as at first, and our counsellors as at the beginning, and build Jerusalem, the city of Your holiness, in our days, and honour us by its building, glory be to You, O builder of Jerusalem."

This is their saying in their prayer, though they know that Musa and Harun, peace be upon them, said none of that. Rather, these are sections they fabricated after the collapse of their state.

Likewise their fasts: like the fast of the burning of the Holy House, the fast of Hasa, and the fast of Gedalia, which they made obligatory, which Musa did not observe, nor Yushaʿ ibn Nun. Likewise the fast of the crucifixion of Haman. None of that is in the Torah; rather they instituted them for reasons that required their institution among them.
