Just as Iblis was arrogant to prostrate to Adam, seeing that as a disgrace to him, then he was content to be a pimp for every rebel and sinner.

And just as the idol worshippers refused that the prophet sent to them be a human, then were content that their god and object of worship be a stone.

And just as the Christians, by their abandonment, exonerated God from having a son and a consort, yet did not shy from attributing that to God, glorified is He.

And just as the Pharaonic Jahmiyya exonerated the Lord, glorified is He, from being established upon His Throne, lest it imply confinement, then placed Him, glorified is He, in wells and taverns, and in the bellies of animals.

This is a claim made by each of the two communities that no one will enter Paradise except those who belong to them. The Jews said: "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews," and the Christians said: "None will enter it except those who are Christians." The statement was abbreviated in the most eloquent and concise way, while remaining free of ambiguity and with its meaning clear. So God demanded from them proof for the validity of the claim, saying: ﴿Say: Produce your proof, if you are truthful.﴾ This is what is called the question of demanding evidence (su'āl al-muṭālaba bi'l-dalīl). Whoever makes a claim without evidence is told: "Produce your proof, if you are truthful in what you claim." Those who hold that the one who negates must also provide evidence, just as the one who affirms must, use this verse as their argument. Scholars have related three positions on this matter, the third being that it is obligatory in legal matters (al-sharʿiyyāt) but not in rational matters (al-ʿaqliyyāt). Their use of the verse as evidence is not sound, because God did not demand proof for a bare negation. Rather, they made a claim whose content is the affirmation that they will enter Paradise and that others will not enter it, so they were required to produce the evidence indicating this compound claim, made up of negation and affirmation. The one who makes such a claim is, by the consensus of people, obligated to provide evidence. The disagreement concerns only a bare negation. Had these people cited God's words: ﴿And they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾, it would have been closer to the point, even though it also contains both negation and affirmation. But the claim in that verse is directed at the negation, and the purpose of the statement is: "We will not be punished after those days." God did not reject their acknowledgment that they would be punished during those days, but rather their claim that they would not be punished after them, and that is pure negation. For this reason we said that using that verse as evidence is closer than using this one.

(Fa'ida: a useful point)

If the direction of the qibla is uncertain to someone, there are three opinions on it.

The first: he should make ijtihad (independent effort to determine it) and pray one prayer. This is the most correct of the opinions in the four legal schools, and it is the well-known one.

The second: he prays four prayers, facing four directions, so as to fulfil the obligation with certainty, just as they said regarding garments that are najis (impure), and just as they said regarding one who has missed a prayer from a day and does not know which it was: he prays five prayers.

The third opinion: the obligation to face the qibla has been dropped from him in this situation, so he prays in whichever direction he wishes.

This is the position of Abu Muhammad Ibn Hazm.

He argued that Allah only imposed facing the qibla upon one who knows the direction of the Ka'ba and is able to turn towards it. As for one who is unable to do so, Allah never imposed turning towards it upon him. It is not permissible to obligate him with what Allah and His Messenger have not obligated him with. And when turning is not obligatory for him, because its obligation is conditional upon ability, he prays towards whatever direction he wishes, like the traveller performing a voluntary prayer, and the invalid who cannot turn towards the qibla.

I say: This opinion is more preponderant and more correct than the opinion that obligates four prayers upon him, for it is an obligation that Allah and His Messenger did not impose, and it has no parallel at all among the obligations of the Lawgiver. Nowhere in the Shari'a is there a case in which Allah obligates the servant to perform a prayer and then repeat it again, except due to negligence in performing it initially, such as one who abandons tranquillity (tuma'nina) or one who prays without wudu' and the like.

As for commanding a prayer, having him perform it upon that command, and then commanding him to repeat that very same prayer, this never occurred at all, and the principles of the Shari'a reject it.

Analogizing this issue to the issue of garments and to the one who forgets a prayer from a day is analogy based on a disputed matter applied to a similar disputed matter. Perhaps the discussion concerns even those two issues as well. Had their rulings been established by a Book, a Sunna, or ijma', there would be what there would be in analogizing upon them; rather, it would not be valid, because the aspect of difference is either equal to the aspect of unification or more apparent, and in either case the analogy is void. What remains is the examination of preferring one of the two opinions of ijtihad or the opinion of choice (takhyir) in the issue of the qibla over the other.

Whoever supports the opinion of choice argues with what is in al-Tirmidhi and Sunan Ibn Majah from 'Amir ibn Rabi'a, from his father, who said: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a journey on a dark night, and we did not know where the qibla was, so each man prayed according to his own direction. When we woke up, we mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed: ﴿Wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾."

al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, except that it is from the narration of Ash'ath al-Sammân, and in it there is weakness."

al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of 'Ata' from Jabir, who said: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ on a march, and clouds came over us, and we became confused, and we disagreed about the qibla, so each one of us prayed separately, and one of us began drawing lines in front of himself so that we would know our positions. We mentioned that to the Prophet, and he did not order us to repeat, and he said: 'Your prayers are sufficient for you.'"

al-Daraqutni said: "Muhammad ibn Salim narrated it from 'Ata'." He said: "It is also narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Arzami from 'Ata', and both of them are weak."

al-'Uqayli said: "The text of this hadith is not narrated through any sound channel."

They also argued with what has been mentioned previously, that Allah only commanded facing the qibla for one who knows it and is able to face it, and as for the helpless ignorant person, the obligation of facing it is dropped from him, so he is not burdened with it.

Whoever supports ijtihad argues that Allah the Exalted obligated the servant to fear Him as much as he is able: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾. This necessitates the obligation of ijtihad upon him in fearing his Lord, the Exalted. Taqwa is doing what has been commanded and abandoning what has been forbidden. They said: Furthermore, it is known that when he stands to pray, it is not permissible for him to face whatever direction he wishes from the outset; rather, he looks at the risings and settings of the stars and the bearings of the qibla until he knows its direction and faces it. This is a type of ijtihad, and the indicators of direction vary in obscurity and clarity, so it is obligatory upon every person to do what is within his capacity of that. If he does not hit it with certainty, he hits it with probability, and that is what he is able to do. Whenever he abandons what is within his capacity, he has not feared Allah the Exalted according to his ability.

As for your saying that Allah only obligated facing the qibla upon one able to do it and knowing it, we say: Allah the Glorified and Exalted obligated upon every servant what his ability leads him to of His obedience. So when he is unable to attain this certainty, and the indicators of direction, it drops from him; but from where does the exertion of his effort and his capacity appropriate to him drop from him?

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah 2, verses 116–117:

The *qunut* (devout submission) here is the general servitude shared by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, which none of them is exclusive in and which is not limited to any time. It is the servitude of subjugation (*qahr*), so the *qunut* here is a *qunut* of compulsion and humility, not a *qunut* of obedience and love. This differs from His saying ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾, where the word is singular because they do not all share in perishing.

A parallel to this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Each of you is responsible for those under his care," for God will call every shepherd to account individually.

(Section)

His saying: ﴿They say, "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him﴾, up to His saying: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾.

God answered their claim that He has taken a son and declared Himself exalted above it. Then He mentioned four proofs for the impossibility of His taking a son.

The first: whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. This contradicts the claim that taking a son within them makes it a son of His, because a son is a part of his father and a partner to him. Therefore, he cannot be a creation of His, owned by Him, since a creation is owned, sustained, and a servant among the servants, and the son is like the father. How then could he be His servant, His creation, and His possession, while being a part of Him? This is among the most false of falsehoods. He reinforced the content of this proof with His saying: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾. This affirms their servitude to Him, and that they are owned and sustained, with no partner, equal, or son among them. Therefore, attributing a son to God is among the greatest forms of associating partners with Him, since the one who associates with God makes for Him a partner from among His creatures while acknowledging that it is owned by Him. This is as the polytheists used to say in their *talbiyah* (the pilgrim's call): "Here I am, O God, here I am. You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns." They made those they associated with Him owned, servant, created. The Christians made for Him a partner who is equal to Him and a part of His parts, just as some polytheists made the angels His daughters. God said: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion from His servants﴾. So if whatever is in the heavens and the earth is His, servants who are devoutly obedient, sustained and owned, it is impossible that He should have among them a partner. Anyone who acknowledges that God owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth is necessarily led to monotheism without fail. For this reason, God argues against the polytheists using their own acknowledgment of this, as in His saying: ﴿Say, "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?" They will say, "To God." Say, "Then will you not remember?"﴾ More explanation of this will come, God willing, in its proper place.

The second proof: His saying ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾. This is one of the most eloquent proofs against the impossibility of attributing a son to Him. For this reason, He said in Surah al-An'am: "Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son?", meaning: from where could the originator of the heavens and the earth have a son? The way this proof is established is that whoever brought into being these heavens and the earth, with their greatness, their signs, their creation and their innovation, is able to bring into being what is less than them, and has no relation to them at all. How then can they take this individual as an equal to Him, a partner and a part, while He is the originator of the upper and lower worlds, their creator and their maker? How could He be unable to bring this individual into existence without a father, so that they could claim he is His son? If He originated the upper and lower worlds, what could prevent Him, or stop Him, from originating this servant, forming him and creating him, with the same power by which He created the upper and lower worlds? Whoever attributes a son to God does not know the Lord, has not believed in Him, and has not worshipped Him. It becomes clear that this proof is among the most eloquent against the impossibility of attributing a son to Him. If you wish to establish this reasoning another way, you may say: since the relation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them to Him is only by bringing into being, creating and originating, He produced and originated that from non-existence into existence. How then could any of it be related to Him by begetting, while His power to create the world and what is in it has never ceased, and He has never needed a helper, a companion or a partner in it?

If you wish to establish it in yet another way, you may say: relation to Him by begetting necessitates His need and poverty for a place of birth, and this contradicts His self-sufficiency and His being alone in originating the heavens and the earth. God pointed to this meaning in His saying: ﴿And they say, "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him. Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ So His perfect power, His perfect self-sufficiency and His perfect lordship make attributing a son to Him impossible, and attributing it to Him undermines the perfection of His lordship, His self-sufficiency and His power. For this reason, attributing a son to Him is an insult to Him, blessed and exalted, as it is established in the two *Sahihs* (Bukhari and Muslim) from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: The son of Adam insults Me, and it is not fitting for him to do so. He denies Me, and it is not fitting for him to do so. As for his insult to Me, it is his saying: God has taken a son, while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient, who has not begotten nor been begotten, and there is none equal to Me. As for his denial of Me, it is his saying: He will not bring me back as He originated me, and the first creation is no easier for Me than its return." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said about the Christians: "Humiliate them but do not wrong them, for they have reviled God with a reviling that no human has ever uttered against Him." God said: ﴿And to warn those who say, "God has taken a son"; they have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers﴾, up to the end of the verse.

He also said: ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾.

This is only because it includes insulting the Lord, blessed and exalted, belittling Him, and attributing to Him what prevents the perfection of His lordship, His power and His self-sufficiency.

The third proof: His saying ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. The way this proof is established is that whoever's power is sufficient to bring into existence whatever He wills by a mere command and by His saying "Be," what need has He for a son? He does not multiply through one, nor is He strengthened by one, nor does He seek help from one. Only one who cannot create what he wants to create needs a son, and only one who, when he wills something, cannot simply say "Be" and it is, needs one.

This weak, needy creature who cannot bring about what he wants is the one to whom a son would be attributed. God has mentioned other proofs for the impossibility of attributing a son to Him, and we will mention them here.

The fourth proof: His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His creation over everything, and the impossibility of attributing a wife to Him. He said in Surah al-An'am: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no companion?﴾, up to the end of the verse. As for the contradiction between the comprehensiveness of His creation and attributing a son to Him, it is clear: if He had a son, that son would not be a creation but a part, and this contradicts His being the Creator of everything. From this it becomes clear that the philosophers, who claim that the intellects and souls are produced from Him, either through an intermediary or without one, are worse than the Christians. Whoever claims the world is eternal has removed it from being created by God, and his saying is more corrupt than the saying of the Christians, because the Christians excluded from His comprehensive creation one or two individuals, while whoever affirms the eternity of the world has removed the upper world, the lower world and the angels from being created by God. The Christians' disbelief has not reached this extent. As for the contradiction between the absence of a companion and having a son, it is also clear, because a son is only produced from two origins: an agent and a receptive substrate, which join in a particular way, so that a part is separated from one of them into the other, from which the son comes. How can one who has no companion have a son? For this reason, when the common Christians understood that a son requires a companion, they were not ashamed to claim that Mary is a god and the mother of the god Jesus. Their common people say, "O mother of God, forgive me," and some of them openly state that she is the wife of the Lord. There is no doubt that the claim of begetting necessitates this, or else it is an begetting that cannot be conceived or imagined. The elite of the Christians are in confusion and misguidance, and their common people are not ashamed to speak of a wife and begetting that is conceivable. Exalted is God above their saying, far beyond it. The people of this corrupt doctrine are the most misguided of God's creation. They are as God described them: ﴿They had already gone astray and led many astray, and they strayed from the right path﴾.

The fifth proof: as for the contradiction between the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and having a son, this requires a particular understanding. It may be established by saying: if He had a son, He would know him, because He has knowledge of everything. But He does not know of any son, so it is impossible that He should have a son He does not know. This is an argument from the negation of His knowledge of a thing to the negation of that thing in reality, since if it existed, He would know it. Therefore, since He does not know it, it does not exist. A similar argument is His saying: ﴿They worship besides God what neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, up to the end of the verse. This is a negation of the intercessors they claimed, by negating the Lord's knowledge of them, which necessitates the negation of what is known. The enemies of God cannot persist in obstinacy and say, "God does know that these exist," because He only knows the existence of what He has brought into existence, and its being, and He knows that He will bring into existence what He wills to bring into existence. So He knows Himself and His attributes, and He knows His creatures that have come into existence and ceased, those that have come into existence and remain, and those not yet brought into existence. As for anything else that is neither created by Him nor owned by Him, the Lord, exalted is He, does not know it, because it is impossible in itself. He knows it as impossible, not as actual, because if He knew it as actual, knowledge of it would be the same as ignorance, and that is among the greatest impossibilities.

These are the proofs of the Lord, blessed and exalted, against what His enemies and those who slander Him have attributed to Him. So weigh them against the long and broad arguments of the speculative theologians (*mutakallimun*), which are like the *dari'* (a thorny plant) that neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. When you weigh the two, the superiority becomes clear to you, if you are perceptive. Whoever is blind to these proofs is blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the path. Praise be to God, who has enough the believing servants with His Book and with what He has deposited in it of proofs, and with its clarity, from the empty chatter of the theologians and the ravings of the bewildered. The blessing of God is truly great upon a servant whom He has made self-sufficient, through understanding His Book, from need of anything else. ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe﴾.

A parallel to this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Each of you is responsible for those under his care," for God will call every shepherd to account individually.

(Section)

His saying: ﴿They say, "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him﴾, up to His saying: ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾.

God answered their claim that He has taken a son and declared Himself exalted above it. Then He mentioned four proofs for the impossibility of His taking a son.

The first: whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him. This contradicts the claim that taking a son within them makes it a son of His, because a son is a part of his father and a partner to him. Therefore, he cannot be a creation of His, owned by Him, since a creation is owned, sustained, and a servant among the servants, and the son is like the father. How then could he be His servant, His creation, and His possession, while being a part of Him? This is among the most false of falsehoods. He reinforced the content of this proof with His saying: ﴿All are devoutly obedient to Him﴾. This affirms their servitude to Him, and that they are owned and sustained, with no partner, equal, or son among them. Therefore, attributing a son to God is among the greatest forms of associating partners with Him, since the one who associates with God makes for Him a partner from among His creatures while acknowledging that it is owned by Him. This is as the polytheists used to say in their *talbiyah* (the pilgrim's call): "Here I am, O God, here I am. You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You; You own him and what he owns." They made those they associated with Him owned, servant, created. The Christians made for Him a partner who is equal to Him and a part of His parts, just as some polytheists made the angels His daughters. God said: ﴿And they have attributed to Him a portion from His servants﴾. So if whatever is in the heavens and the earth is His, servants who are devoutly obedient, sustained and owned, it is impossible that He should have among them a partner. Anyone who acknowledges that God owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth is necessarily led to monotheism without fail. For this reason, God argues against the polytheists using their own acknowledgment of this, as in His saying: ﴿Say, "To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?" They will say, "To God." Say, "Then will you not remember?"﴾ More explanation of this will come, God willing, in its proper place.

The second proof: His saying ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾. This is one of the most eloquent proofs against the impossibility of attributing a son to Him. For this reason, He said in Surah al-An'am: "Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son?", meaning: from where could the originator of the heavens and the earth have a son? The way this proof is established is that whoever brought into being these heavens and the earth, with their greatness, their signs, their creation and their innovation, is able to bring into being what is less than them, and has no relation to them at all. How then can they take this individual as an equal to Him, a partner and a part, while He is the originator of the upper and lower worlds, their creator and their maker? How could He be unable to bring this individual into existence without a father, so that they could claim he is His son? If He originated the upper and lower worlds, what could prevent Him, or stop Him, from originating this servant, forming him and creating him, with the same power by which He created the upper and lower worlds? Whoever attributes a son to God does not know the Lord, has not believed in Him, and has not worshipped Him. It becomes clear that this proof is among the most eloquent against the impossibility of attributing a son to Him. If you wish to establish this reasoning another way, you may say: since the relation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them to Him is only by bringing into being, creating and originating, He produced and originated that from non-existence into existence. How then could any of it be related to Him by begetting, while His power to create the world and what is in it has never ceased, and He has never needed a helper, a companion or a partner in it?

If you wish to establish it in yet another way, you may say: relation to Him by begetting necessitates His need and poverty for a place of birth, and this contradicts His self-sufficiency and His being alone in originating the heavens and the earth. God pointed to this meaning in His saying: ﴿And they say, "God has taken a son." Glory be to Him. Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ So His perfect power, His perfect self-sufficiency and His perfect lordship make attributing a son to Him impossible, and attributing it to Him undermines the perfection of His lordship, His self-sufficiency and His power. For this reason, attributing a son to Him is an insult to Him, blessed and exalted, as it is established in the two *Sahihs* (Bukhari and Muslim) from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: The son of Adam insults Me, and it is not fitting for him to do so. He denies Me, and it is not fitting for him to do so. As for his insult to Me, it is his saying: God has taken a son, while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient, who has not begotten nor been begotten, and there is none equal to Me. As for his denial of Me, it is his saying: He will not bring me back as He originated me, and the first creation is no easier for Me than its return." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may God be pleased with him) said about the Christians: "Humiliate them but do not wrong them, for they have reviled God with a reviling that no human has ever uttered against Him." God said: ﴿And to warn those who say, "God has taken a son"; they have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers﴾, up to the end of the verse.

He also said: ﴿The heavens are almost rent apart from it, the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin﴾.

This is only because it includes insulting the Lord, blessed and exalted, belittling Him, and attributing to Him what prevents the perfection of His lordship, His power and His self-sufficiency.

The third proof: His saying ﴿When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. The way this proof is established is that whoever's power is sufficient to bring into existence whatever He wills by a mere command and by His saying "Be," what need has He for a son? He does not multiply through one, nor is He strengthened by one, nor does He seek help from one. Only one who cannot create what he wants to create needs a son, and only one who, when he wills something, cannot simply say "Be" and it is, needs one.

This weak, needy creature who cannot bring about what he wants is the one to whom a son would be attributed. God has mentioned other proofs for the impossibility of attributing a son to Him, and we will mention them here.

The fourth proof: His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His creation over everything, and the impossibility of attributing a wife to Him. He said in Surah al-An'am: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He has no companion?﴾, up to the end of the verse. As for the contradiction between the comprehensiveness of His creation and attributing a son to Him, it is clear: if He had a son, that son would not be a creation but a part, and this contradicts His being the Creator of everything. From this it becomes clear that the philosophers, who claim that the intellects and souls are produced from Him, either through an intermediary or without one, are worse than the Christians. Whoever claims the world is eternal has removed it from being created by God, and his saying is more corrupt than the saying of the Christians, because the Christians excluded from His comprehensive creation one or two individuals, while whoever affirms the eternity of the world has removed the upper world, the lower world and the angels from being created by God. The Christians' disbelief has not reached this extent. As for the contradiction between the absence of a companion and having a son, it is also clear, because a son is only produced from two origins: an agent and a receptive substrate, which join in a particular way, so that a part is separated from one of them into the other, from which the son comes. How can one who has no companion have a son? For this reason, when the common Christians understood that a son requires a companion, they were not ashamed to claim that Mary is a god and the mother of the god Jesus. Their common people say, "O mother of God, forgive me," and some of them openly state that she is the wife of the Lord. There is no doubt that the claim of begetting necessitates this, or else it is an begetting that cannot be conceived or imagined. The elite of the Christians are in confusion and misguidance, and their common people are not ashamed to speak of a wife and begetting that is conceivable. Exalted is God above their saying, far beyond it. The people of this corrupt doctrine are the most misguided of God's creation. They are as God described them: ﴿They had already gone astray and led many astray, and they strayed from the right path﴾.

The fifth proof: as for the contradiction between the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and having a son, this requires a particular understanding. It may be established by saying: if He had a son, He would know him, because He has knowledge of everything. But He does not know of any son, so it is impossible that He should have a son He does not know. This is an argument from the negation of His knowledge of a thing to the negation of that thing in reality, since if it existed, He would know it. Therefore, since He does not know it, it does not exist. A similar argument is His saying: ﴿They worship besides God what neither harms them nor benefits them﴾, up to the end of the verse. This is a negation of the intercessors they claimed, by negating the Lord's knowledge of them, which necessitates the negation of what is known. The enemies of God cannot persist in obstinacy and say, "God does know that these exist," because He only knows the existence of what He has brought into existence, and its being, and He knows that He will bring into existence what He wills to bring into existence. So He knows Himself and His attributes, and He knows His creatures that have come into existence and ceased, those that have come into existence and remain, and those not yet brought into existence. As for anything else that is neither created by Him nor owned by Him, the Lord, exalted is He, does not know it, because it is impossible in itself. He knows it as impossible, not as actual, because if He knew it as actual, knowledge of it would be the same as ignorance, and that is among the greatest impossibilities.

These are the proofs of the Lord, blessed and exalted, against what His enemies and those who slander Him have attributed to Him. So weigh them against the long and broad arguments of the speculative theologians (*mutakallimun*), which are like the *dari'* (a thorny plant) that neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. When you weigh the two, the superiority becomes clear to you, if you are perceptive. Whoever is blind to these proofs is blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the path. Praise be to God, who has enough the believing servants with His Book and with what He has deposited in it of proofs, and with its clarity, from the empty chatter of the theologians and the ravings of the bewildered. The blessing of God is truly great upon a servant whom He has made self-sufficient, through understanding His Book, from need of anything else. ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, recited to them? Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe﴾.

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some preceding discussion:

This following (mutaba'ah) is the recitation (tilawah) for whose people Allah praised them in His saying, ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾, and in His saying, ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it should be recited; those believe in it﴾. The meaning is: they follow the Book of Allah with the following it truly deserves. And the Exalted said, ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer﴾. And He said, ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred and to whom belongs everything. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims (91). And to recite the Qur'an﴾.

So the true meaning of tilawah in these passages is the complete, absolute recitation, which is the recitation of both the wording (lafz) and the meaning (ma'na). The recitation of the wording is a part of what is called absolute recitation, while the true reality of the wording is nothing other than following.

It is said: "Ittabi' athar fulan" (follow the trail of so-and-so), "talawtu atharahu" (I followed his trace), "qafawtuhu" and "qassastuhu" meaning I went after him, and from this is His saying, ﴿By the sun and its brightness, and the moon when it follows it﴾, meaning it follows it in rising after its setting. It is also said, "ja'a al-qawm yatluw ba'duhum ba'dan," meaning they follow one another. The reciter of speech is called "tali" (reciter) because he follows some letters with others; he does not pronounce them all at once, but follows some of them with others in order, and whenever a letter or word ends, he follows it with another letter and another word. This recitation is a means and a method, while the intended recitation is the true recitation, which is the recitation of the meaning and following it: affirming its report, complying with its command, and stopping at its prohibition, and taking it as a model, wherever it leads you, you follow with it. Thus the recitation of the Qur'an encompasses the recitation of its wording and its meaning, and the recitation of the meaning is more noble than mere recitation of the wording. Its people are the People of the Qur'an, who have praise in this world and the Hereafter, for they are truly the people of recitation and following.

Ibn al-Qayyim's commentary on Surah 2, verse 135:

And among that is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "Be Jews or Christians, you will be guided."﴾ So answer this claim with His saying: ﴿Say, "Rather, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah."﴾

This answer, despite its brevity, contains both a rejection (manʿ) and a counter-argument (muʿaraḍa). As for the rejection: it is contained in the particle "bal" (rather), which indicates a turning away (iḍrāb), meaning: the matter is not as they say. As for the counter-argument: it lies in His saying ﴿the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth (ḥanīfan)﴾, meaning: we follow, or let them follow, the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth. Within this counter-argument is the establishment of proof that it is more deserving of being correct than what you invite to, namely Judaism and Christianity. This is because He described the bearer of the religion as ḥanīf, not a polytheist. Whoever's religion is ḥanīfiyyah (pure monotheism) and tawḥīd is more deserving of being followed than one whose religion is Judaism or Christianity. Indeed, ḥanīfiyyah (inclining toward truth) and tawḥīd are the religion of all the prophets, the one from which Allah accepts no other religion from anyone, and it is the fiṭrah (natural disposition) upon which He created His servants. Whoever is upon it is the one who is guided, because whoever is a Jew or a Christian, ḥanīfiyyah entails turning to Allah in worship, reverence, exaltation, love, and humility.

And tawḥīd entails singling Him out with this turning to the exclusion of others, so that He is worshipped alone, loved alone, obeyed alone, and no other god is set alongside Him. So who is more deserving of guidance: the bearer of this religion, or the religion of Judaism and Christianity? There remains for the opponents only one question, which is that they say: "We too are upon his religion, we have not departed from it, and Abraham and his sons were Jews or Christians." Answer this question by saying that they are lying in this, and that Allah, the Exalted, knows that he was neither a Jew nor a Christian. So He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes were Jews or Christians?﴾ to the end of the verse.

The Exalted established this answer in Surah Āl ʿImrān with His saying: ﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And Allah is the Protector of the believers.﴾ If they say, "Suppose Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, we are still upon his religion, even if we adopt this name?"

Answer this with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "We believe in Allah"﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and we are Muslims to Him.﴾ These are for the believers. He said: ﴿And if they believe in the like of what you have believed, then they have been guided.﴾ And if they come with faith like what you have come with, then they are upon the religion of Abraham and are guided. And if they do not come with faith like your faith, then they have nothing to do with Abraham and his religion, and they are only in opposition and enmity. For the religion of Abraham is belief in Allah, His books, and His messengers, and not to differentiate between any of them, believing in some and disbelieving in others. Whoever does not come with such faith is innocent of the religion of Abraham and is in opposition to those who are upon his religion.

(Fa'ida)

The words of the Most High: ﴿With the like of what you have believed in﴾. But does He have no like?

The answer is from several angles:

The first: that the purpose is rebuke (al-tabkit), and the meaning is: "Produce another religion like it," and that is impossible.

The second: that the word "like" (mithl) is superfluous (silah).

The third: that you believed in the Furqan without alteration (tasahhuf) or distortion (tahrif). So if they believe in the Torah without alteration or distortion, then they have been guided.

The fourth: that the purpose is: "If they believe in the like of that by which you became believers."

Ibn Jarir narrated that Ibn Abbas said: "Say: 'We believe in Allah,' and if they believe in what you believe in..."

Abd al-Jabbar said: "It is not permissible to abandon a mutawatir recitation."

This is a question from the foolish ones, which they raised against the believers, and its content is: if the first qibla was true, then you have abandoned the truth; and if it was false, then you were upon falsehood. The wording of the verse, even if it does not indicate this, was said by the foolish ones who disputed about the qibla.

Then Allah, exalted is He, answered it with a healing reply, after having first mentioned preliminaries that establish and clarify it. The question came from the disbelievers, who raised it in multiple forms that all return to one thing. They said what has preceded, and they said: "If he were a prophet, he would not have abandoned the qibla of the prophets before him," and they said: "If he were a prophet, he would not do something today and its opposite tomorrow." The polytheists said: "He has returned to your qibla, so he is about to return to your religion." And the People of the Book said: "And if he were a prophet, he would not have separated from the prophets before him."

The talk multiplied and the trial grew severe upon some people, as God, the Exalted, said: ﴿And indeed, it was difficult, except for those whom Allah guided﴾.

Reflect upon His wisdom, the Mighty, the Wise, and His gentleness and guidance in this story. When He knew that this change was a great matter, how He prepared for it, paved the way for it, and made it easy through principles that preceded it. He mentioned abrogation (naskh), and that when He abrogates something He brings something like it or better than it, and that He is capable of that and nothing can overpower Him. Then He established submission to the Messenger and that one should not object to him or ask in order to test him, as happened with Moses and his people. Then He mentioned the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), its glorification and sanctity, mentioned its builder, praised him, and made obligatory the following of his creed. Thereby He established in souls the orientation toward the House with glorification, reverence, and love, and toward its builder with following, allegiance, and agreement. He informed, exalted is He, that He made the House a place of return (mathaba) for people, to which they return and from which they never have enough. Hearts are devoted to its love, constantly longing for it, turning toward it wherever they are. Then He informed that He commanded Abraham and Ishmael to purify it for those who circumambulate, those who stand, and those who pray, and He attributed it to Himself by saying: ﴿that you purify My House﴾. This attribution is what settled in hearts such love for it and longing for it as settled there, and it is what drew the hearts of the world toward it. When these matters became established in the hearts of the people of faith, and they were reminded of them, it was as if they were calling out to them: face it in prayer. But this was contingent upon the arrival of the command from the Lord of the House. So when the decree was issued: ﴿Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾, the Messenger of Allah received it, and those firm in faith received it with glad tidings and acceptance, and it was a festival for them. This was because the Messenger of Allah often turned his face toward the sky, awaiting that Allah would change the qibla away from the qibla of the People of the Book, so Allah gave him the qibla that He was pleased with. The disbelievers met it with opposition and raised false doubts, and the weak among the believers met it with distress and hardship. So God, the Exalted, mentioned the categories of people at the command to face the Ka'bah, and began that by consoling His Messenger and the believers regarding what the foolish among the people say: ﴿So do not care about their saying, for it is the saying of a fool﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Say: To Allah belong the east and the west; He guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾. Thus God, the Exalted, informed that the east and the west belong to Him, that He is their Lord. So wherever you worship Him by His command, in whatever direction, they are obedient to Him, as He said: ﴿And to Allah belong the east and the west, so wherever you turn, there is the Face of Allah﴾. Thus no one who faces a direction by His command faces anything but Him, exalted is He. So if you were praying toward other than the Ka'bah by His command, and then He commanded you to pray toward it, you have only prayed to Him, first and last, and you were upon truth in the first and the last facing, because both were by His command and pleasure. You moved from one to another by His pleasure. Then He drew attention to the excellence of the direction to which He commanded them to face second, by saying that He guides whom He wills to a straight path, just as He guided you to the qibla He made your qibla, legislated for you, and was pleased with. But He commanded you to face other than it first for a wisdom in that: that He, glorified is He, would know who follows the Messenger, turns with him wherever he turns, and obeys his commands however they change. He is the All-Knowing of everything, but He willed to make His unseen knowledge become observed and witnessed, so that thereby is distinguished the one firm in faith who submits to the Messenger and yields to him, from one who worships Allah on an edge, who turns back on his heels at the slightest doubt.

This is among some of the wisdom in His making the first qibla other than the Ka'bah. He did not legislate it in vain or without purpose. Then He, glorified is He, informed that just as He made for them the middle of the directions as a qibla for their worship, so He made them a middle nation (ummah wasat), and so He chose the middle qibla among the directions for the middle nation among the nations. Then He mentioned that this preference and distinction is so that they may be witnesses over the nations, so that their testimony over creation is accepted on the Day of Resurrection. Then Allah, exalted is He, answered what the believers asked about, namely their prayer toward the first qibla and the prayer of their brethren who died before the change. He said: ﴿And Allah would never let your faith go to waste﴾. And regarding this there are two opinions. The first: He would not let your prayer toward Jerusalem go to waste, but would reward you for it, because it was by His command and pleasure. The second: He would not let your faith in the first qibla go to waste, nor your belief that Allah legislated it and was pleased with it. The majority of the early and later scholars hold the first view, and it necessarily implies the second. The wisdom in abrogating facing Jerusalem...

(From the proofs for following the statements of the Companions)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾.

The way of deducing proof from the verse is that He, may He be exalted, informed that He made them a nation that is choice and just. This is the true meaning of "middle" (wasat): they are the best of nations, and the most just in their statements, their deeds, their intentions and their purposes. For this reason they deserved to be witnesses for the messengers over their nations on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah accepts their testimony against them, for they are His witnesses. Therefore He honoured them, raised their mention, and praised them. Since He, may He be exalted, made them witnesses, He informed His creation, among the angels and others, of the state of these witnesses, and commanded His angels to send blessings upon them, to supplicate for them, and to seek forgiveness for them. The witness accepted by Allah is the one who testifies with knowledge and truthfulness, so he reports the truth grounded in his knowledge of it, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿except for those who bear witness to the truth while they know﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 86]. A person may report the truth by coincidence without knowing it, and he may know it yet not report it. So the witness accepted by Allah is the one who reports it on the basis of knowledge. Now, if it were the case that one of them would issue a fatwa that was an error, opposing the ruling of Allah and His Messenger, and no one else would give the fatwa of truth, which is the ruling of Allah and His Messenger, whether with the first fatwa being widely known or without it being widely known, then this nation, the just and choice, would have unanimously agreed upon what opposes the truth. Rather, they would have divided into two parts: a part that issued a fatwa with falsehood, and a part that remained silent about the truth. This is impossible, for the truth does not pass them by and leave them to those who come after them, certainly. To those who oppose their statements we say: had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it.

(A subtle point)

He, may He be exalted, informed that He made them just and choice, and mentioned them before bringing them into existence, because of what had preceded in His knowledge of taking them as witnesses who bear witness over the nations on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever does not fulfil this testimony, in knowledge and action, in recognition and affirmation, in calling and teaching, and in guidance, is not among the witnesses of Allah. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[The mufti's preliminary introduction to a strange ruling]

[It is part of the mufti's etiquette to prepare the way for a ruling that seems strange.] The seventh benefit: (If a ruling is very strange, one that souls are not accustomed to and have grown used to its opposite, then the mufti should lay down before it something that signals it and paves the way for it), such as evidence for it and an introduction preceding it. Reflect on Allah's mention of the story of Zakariyya (Zechariah) and the child being brought forth from him after the years of youth had passed and he had reached the age at which, customarily, one of his kind does not beget children. He mentioned his story as an introduction before the story of the Messiah and his birth without a father. For when souls became familiar with a child born to two elderly shaykhs to whom children are not customarily born, it became easy for them to believe in the birth of a child without a father. Likewise, before the story of the Messiah, He mentioned Maryam's (Mary's) receiving her provision out of its time and season.

This is what encouraged the soul of Zakariyya and moved it to seek a child, even though it was not the appropriate time.

Reflect also on the story of the abrogation of the qibla. Because it was very difficult for souls, see how He, glorified is He, prepared for it several preparations. Among them: the mention of abrogation (naskh) (the replacement of one ruling by another); among them: that He brings something better than what was abrogated or its like; among them: that He is over all things Powerful, and that He has knowledge of all things. The all-encompassing power and knowledge are suited to this second matter just as they were suited to the first.

Among them: His warning them against objecting to His Messenger, as those before them objected to Musa (Moses), but rather He commanded them to submit and comply.

Among them: His warning them against giving ear to the Jews, and that their doubts should not mislead them, for they wish to turn them back into disbelievers after the truth has become clear to them.

Among them: His informing that entering Paradise is not by Judaism or Christianity, but is by submitting one's face, intention, deed and purpose to Allah together with following His command.

Among them: His, glorified is He, informing about His vastness, and that wherever the one who prays turns his face, there is the Face of Allah, the Exalted; for He is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. Thus He mentioned the two kinds of encompassing, the essential and the knowledge-based, so that they would not imagine that they were not facing His Face in the first qibla, nor in the second; rather, wherever they turn, there is the Face of Allah, the Exalted.

Among them: that He, glorified and exalted is He, warned His Prophet ﷺ against following the desires of the disbelievers among the People of the Book and others, and rather commanded that he and his community follow what has been revealed to him, so that they face Him alone with their hearts.

Among them: that He mentioned the greatness of His Sacred House, the greatness of its builder and his religion, and condemned those who turn away from it, and commanded following it. So He exalted the House, its builder and his religion. All of this is a preparation before the change, along with the noble aims and lofty objectives contained within it.

Then He mentioned the virtue of this Community, and that they are the middle (wasat) community, the just, the best. This required that their Prophet ﷺ be the most middle and the best of the prophets, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them all, and that their Book be likewise, their religion likewise, and the qibla they face likewise. Thus the fitting harmony appeared, both in the legal (shar‘i) and the decreed (qadari) rulings of His commands, and His dazzling wisdom became manifest and was made clear to pure, illuminated minds by the light of their Lord, blessed and exalted is He.

The point is that the mufti is worthy of mentioning, before a strange ruling, introductory premises that make it agreeable and point to it, and serve as a preparation before it. And success is from Allah.

Then He, the Exalted, informed of the intensity of the disbelief of the People of the Book, that even if the Messenger brought them every sign, they would not follow his qibla. In this is consolation for him, and [a command to] leave them and their qibla. Then He cleared him of their qibla, saying: ﴿And you are not one who follows their qibla﴾. Then He mentioned their disagreement about the qibla, and that each group among them does not follow the other group, because the qibla is among the distinctive features of the religion, its markers and its apparent rites. The people of every religion do not part from their qibla unless they part from their religion. So in these three sentences He informed, with three statements, that includes the disavowal of each group from the qibla of the other group, and includes the information that if the People of the Book saw every sign indicating the truthfulness of the Messenger, they would not follow his qibla, out of obstinacy and blind imitation of their forefathers; and that, if they agree in opposing the true qibla, they are nevertheless in disagreement and divided in their falsehood, so one group does not follow the qibla of another. They agree in opposing the truth in choosing falsehood. In this verse there is also a firmness for the Messenger and the believers in holding to their qibla, and that he should not occupy himself with what the People of the Book say: "Turn to our qibla and we will follow you in your religion." For this is deception and cunning from them, since if they saw every sign indicating your truthfulness, they would not follow your qibla, because disbelief has taken hold of their hearts, so there is no hope for the truth in them. Nor are you one who follows their qibla, so let them cut off their hopes of your agreeing with them and returning to their qibla. Likewise they are also in disagreement among themselves, so none of them follows the qibla of another. They disagree about the qibla, and you, O believers, are not in agreement with any of them regarding their qibla. Rather, Allah has honored you with a qibla other than the qibla of these divided people, which Allah chose for you and was pleased with. The Exalted reinforced this meaning by His saying: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires after the knowledge that has come to you, then indeed you would be, at that time, among the wrongdoers﴾. All of this is a firmness and a warning against agreeing with them regarding the qibla, and a disavowal of their qibla, just as they disavow your qibla, and just as some of them disavow the qibla of others. You, O believers, are more deserving of disavowing their qibla, which Allah the Exalted has honored you by turning away from it. Then He reinforced that by His saying: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 146:

﴿They recognise it as they recognise their own sons.﴾ For they had, before they saw him, a description of his attributes, and when they saw his person it corresponded to that description. The phrase "as they recognise their own sons" comes by way of izdiwaj al-kalam (the pairing of speech, a rhetorical device in which two parallel elements are balanced), and by comparing one of two certainties with the other. So reflect on it.

(A subtle point)

We mentioned in the book al-Fawa'id al-Makkiyya the reason for the use of ﴿those to whom We gave the Book﴾ and ﴿those who were given the Book﴾, and the difference between the two passages: wherever the agent is mentioned, those to whom He gave the Book are placed in a context of praise, and wherever the agent is omitted, those who were given it are placed in a context of blame or are divided in their condition.

This is among the secrets of the Noble Qur'an.

Similar to this is ﴿Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those whom We chose from among Our servants﴾, and He said: ﴿Then there succeeded them a later generation who inherited the Book, taking the goods of this lower world﴾. In sum, everything that is ascribed to Allah, the Exalted, is good, wise, beneficial and just, and evil is not ascribed to Him.

Then He, may He be exalted, informs of the specific direction of each nation toward its own qibla, saying: ﴿And for each there is a direction toward which it turns﴾. The more sound of the two opinions is that the meaning is "he is turned toward it," that is, "he turns his face toward it," so the pronoun refers back to "each." It has also been said that the pronoun refers to God, meaning "God turns him toward it," but this is nothing, because God never turned them toward a false qibla, nor did He ever command the Christians to face the east. Rather, they themselves turned to this qibla of their own accord and turned their faces toward it.

His saying ﴿So race to the good deeds﴾ indicates the soundness of this view: that is, since the people of the (other) religions have turned toward their directions, you should race to the good deeds, hasten to what God has chosen for you and is pleased with, and has given you as your direction, and do not hesitate about it. ﴿Wherever you are, God will bring you all together﴾: He will gather you from the various directions and distant regions to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, just as you gather from all directions toward the qibla you face. Thus you will be gathered from all the corners of the earth to the place of standing toward which all creatures turn.

This is similar to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a way. Had God willed, He would have made you one community, but He tests you in what He has given you, so race to the good deeds. To God is your return﴾. He informed that their return is to Him when He mentioned the plurality of their laws, and likewise He mentioned exactly the same thing when He informed of the plurality of their direction and qibla, saying: ﴿And for each there is a direction toward which it turns, so race to the good deeds. Wherever you are, God will bring you all together﴾.

Beneath this there is a wondrous secret, which whoever understands will grasp: when there is difference in paths, creeds, laws and qiblas, the closest of them to the truth is the one that is most indicative of God and most conducive to reaching Him, because the return of all is to Him alone on the Day of Resurrection, however their states, times and places may differ. Their return is to one Lord and one God. Thus it should be that the destination and return of all of them is to Him alone in this world, so that they worship none other and submit to no religion other than His, for He is their true God in this world and the next. But when most people have refused this, except for disbelief, and have gone off on false paths and worshipped other than Him, even though they follow a religion other than His, then you, O believers, race to the good deeds, hasten to them, and do not go along with those who hasten into falsehood and disbelief. Reflect on this wondrous secret in the two surahs: the Day of Decision and the Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 150:

Abu al-Qasim al-Suhayli said:

God, exalted is He, said in the abrogating verse: ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾. That is: from whatever direction you come to the prayer and set out toward it, face the Ka'bah. Whether you were facing Bayt al-Maqdis or not, since he (ﷺ) was in Makkah, he would strive, in facing Bayt al-Maqdis, to have the Ka'bah in front of him.

He said: "Reflect on His saying: ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face﴾ and ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾. He did not say 'wherever you set out', and this is because he was the imam of the Muslims. He would go out to them at every prayer to lead them in prayer, and this was obligatory upon him, since he was the imam who was followed. So the mention of setting out, in his specific case, conveyed this meaning, and the ruling for others was not like this, since setting out does not apply to them in this way, especially women and those who have no obligation of congregation."

I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: In this there appears another meaning, namely that His saying ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ is a general address to him and to his community, requiring them to turn toward the Sacred Mosque wherever they are on the earth. His saying ﴿And from wherever you set out, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque﴾ is an address in the singular form, but what is intended is the community, like His saying ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾ and its counterparts. It conveys the command to face it from whatever direction and place one sets out from. His saying ﴿And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾ conveys the command to face it in whatever place one settles. He, exalted is He, did not restrict the setting out with an end point; rather He left its end unrestricted, just as He generalized its beginning. So from wherever one sets out, to whatever destination one goes, whether for prayer, raid, pilgrimage or otherwise, he is commanded, he and the community, to face the Sacred Mosque, and wherever they are on the earth, he is commanded, he and the community, to face it. Thus the two verses cover all the states of the community: at the beginning of their movement from where they set out, at its end when they arrive, and in their state of settling wherever they are. This conveys the generality of the command to face it in the three states that a servant never leaves. So reflect on this meaning and weigh it against what Abu al-Qasim stated, and the preponderance will become clear to you. God knows best what He intended by His words; this is only a tightening of the understanding of those of us who are deficient. So His saying "from wherever you set out" covers the beginning of the setting out and its end, for him and for the community.

This address was more fitting for him, since the beginning of the turning was upon his hands, and he was extremely eager for the change. His saying ﴿And wherever you are﴾ covers all the places of existence, for him and for the community, and they were more fitting for this address because of the multiplicity of their places of dwelling and their great number, according to their multitude, the difference of their lands and regions, and their spread around the Ka'bah to the east, west, Yemen and Iraq. So the better way to address them was to say: "And wherever you are," that is, from the regions of the earth, east and west and all its directions. There is no doubt that they are more included in this address than he is. So reflect on these subtle points, for you may not find them in any place other than this, and God knows best.

Abu al-Qasim said: "The Creator, exalted is He, repeated the command to turn toward the Sacred House in three verses, because the deniers of the change of the qibla were of three categories of people: the Jews, since they do not hold to abrogation in the basis of their doctrine; the people of doubt and hypocrisy, whose denial of it was intense because it was the first abrogation to be revealed; and the Quraysh disbelievers, who said: 'Muhammad regrets leaving our religion, so he will return to it as he returned to our qibla.' Before that, they used to argue against him, saying: 'Muhammad claims that he calls us to the religion of Ibrahim and Isma'il, yet he has departed from Ibrahim and Isma'il and preferred over them the qibla of the Jews.' So God said to him, when He commanded him to pray toward the Ka'bah: ﴿So that people will have no argument against you, except those of them who were unjust﴾, as an exception of disconnection, meaning: but those of them who were unjust do not turn back and are not guided. And He said: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾, meaning: do not be among those who doubted and wavered. The meaning of 'the truth is from your Lord' is that what I commanded you of turning toward the Sacred House is the truth upon which the prophets before you were, so do not waver in this. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord﴾, and He said: ﴿And indeed, a group of them conceal the truth while they know﴾, meaning they conceal what they know, that the Ka'bah is the qibla of the prophets." Then he related by way of Abu Dawud in the book of the Abrogating and the Abrogated:

He said: Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us: 'Anbasah narrated to us from Yunus from Ibn Shihab, who said: "Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik did not venerate Iliya as his household venerated it." He said: "I travelled with him while he was crown prince, and with him was Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah. Sulayman said while sitting in it: 'By God, in this qibla toward which the Muslims and the Christians pray there is indeed a wonder.'" So I saw it, and the correct version is "the Jews."

Khalid ibn Yazid said: "As for me, by God, I read the Book that God revealed to Muhammad, and the Jews did not find it in the Book that God revealed to them. Rather, the Ark of Tranquility was upon the rock, and when God, mighty and majestic, became angry with the Children of Israel, He lifted it, so their prayer toward the rock was by their own consultation."'

Abu Dawud also related that a Jew disputed with Abu al-'Aliyah concerning the qibla. Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Musa used to pray at the rock while facing the Sacred House, so the Ka'bah was his qibla, and the rock was in front of him." The Jew said: "Between me and you is the mosque of the Prophet Salih (ﷺ)." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "I prayed in the mosque of Salih, and its qibla was the Ka'bah." End.

I (Ibn al-Qayyim) say: This section contains a great benefit, namely that the People of the Book's facing their qibla was not by revelation or divine stipulation, but by their own consultation and ijtihad. As for the Christians, there is no doubt that God did not command them in the Gospel or elsewhere to face the east at all, and they acknowledge this, and acknowledge that the qibla of Christ was the qibla of the Children of Israel, which is the rock. Their elders and predecessors instituted this qibla for them, and they excuse them by saying that Christ delegated to them the authority to make lawful and unlawful and to legislate rulings, and that what they made lawful and unlawful, He too made lawful and unlawful in heaven. So they agree with the Jews that God did not legislate facing the east upon the tongue of His messenger at all, and the Muslims bear witness against them of this. As for the qibla of the Jews, there is absolutely no command in the Torah to face the rock; rather, they used to set up the Ark and pray toward it from wherever they set out, and when they arrived they set it upon the rock and prayed toward it, and when it was lifted they prayed toward its place, which is the rock. As for the Samaritans, they pray toward a mountain of theirs in the land of Syria, venerate it, and make pilgrimage to it. I saw it myself, in the town of Nablus, and I debated their scholars about facing it, and I said: 'It is an invalid, innovated qibla.' One of their notables said: 'This is the correct qibla, and the Jews erred in missing it, because God, exalted is He, commanded in the Torah to face it specifically.' Then he cited a text he claimed was from the Torah concerning facing it. I said to him: 'This is certainly an error against the Torah, because it was revealed only to the Children of Israel, who are its addressees, and you are a branch of them in it, and you received it only from them. And this text is not in the Torah that is in their hands, and I have seen it, and this is not in it.' He said to me: 'You are right; it is only in our Torah specifically.' I said: 'It is impossible that the people of the Torah, to whom it was addressed, who received it from the Interlocutor (al-Kalim, Musa), and who are scattered across the regions of the earth, would all have concealed this text, removed it, and changed the qibla they were commanded, while you preserved them and preserved the text about it.' He did not return an answer.

I say: All of this strengthens the view that the pronoun in His saying ﴿And for each there is a direction, he is facing it﴾ refers to (each), meaning: he turns his face toward it; the meaning is not that God makes him face it. Here is one reason:

The second: no mention of His name preceded the pronoun in the verse; even if His name is mentioned earlier, returning the pronoun to Him rather than to 'each' returns it to other than the one more fitting for it, and prevents it from the nearer thing that follows it.

The third: if the pronoun returned to Him, it would say 'He makes him face it' (huwa muwalliha iyyaha); this is the form of the wording, as He said: ﴿We will let him have what he turned to﴾. The correct wording is to say 'He made him face the qibla' (wallahu al-qibla), not 'he made the qibla face him.' So reflect on this.

As for Abu al-Qasim's statement that He repeated the command to face it three times in response to the three groups, it is not clear, and there is no indication of it in the wording. What appears is that He commanded it in each context for a meaning that the context requires. Mentioning it the first time was the initiation of the ruling and the abrogation of the first qibla, when He said: ﴿We have seen the turning of your face in the sky, so We shall surely turn you to a qibla you will be pleased with. So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it﴾. Then He mentioned that the People of the Book know that this is the truth from their Lord, as they find it in their books. Then He informed of their worship and disbelief, and that even if He brought them every sign, they would not follow their qibla, nor would he follow their qibla, nor would some of them follow the qibla of others. Then He warned him against following their desires. Then He repeated the People of the Book's recognition of him as they recognize their sons, and that they conceal the truth knowingly. Then He informed that this is the truth from his Lord, so no doubt shall reach him in it. Then He informed that for each of the nations there is a direction that it faces and turns toward, so race, you believers, to the good deeds. Then He repeated the command to face it from wherever one sets out, within this context which exceeds mere abrogation. Then He repeated the command, not as a pure repetition, but including within it the command to face it wherever they are, just as He had commanded them to face it first wherever they were at the abrogation, and at the initiation of the legislation of the ruling He commanded them to face it wherever they were at the establishment and beginning of the ruling, and after the argument and dispute, the ruling in their favor, and the explanation of their obstinacy and opposition despite their knowledge. So the command was mentioned in every situation because the context requires it. Reflect on this, and God knows best.

As for his statement that the exception in His saying ﴿except those of them who were unjust﴾ is disconnected (munqati'), most people have said this, and its basis is that the unjust have no proof, so their exception from what was mentioned before is disconnected.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah say: "The exception is not disconnected; rather it is connected, on its proper footing. What led them to judge it disconnected was that they thought the proof here means the correct, true proof. Proof in the Book of God is used in two senses:

The first: the true, correct proof, as in His saying: ﴿And that was Our proof, which We gave to Ibrahim against his people﴾, and His saying: ﴿Say: To God belongs the conclusive proof﴾.

And it is used for the mere act of arguing, whether with truth or falsehood, as in His saying: ﴿And if they argue with you, say: I have submitted my face to God﴾, and His saying: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their argument is only that they say: Bring our fathers, if you are truthful﴾, and His saying: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Ibrahim about his Lord﴾, and His saying: ﴿And those who argue about God after He has been answered, their argument is baseless with their Lord﴾. And when 'proof' is a name for whatever is argued with, whether true or false, it is correct to make the proof of the unjust an exception from His saying: ﴿So that people will have no argument against you﴾. This is in the utmost precision. The meaning is that the unjust argue against you with a false, baseless argument, so do not fear them, but fear Me."

Among this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it is said to them: Follow what God has sent down, they say: No, we follow what we found our fathers upon. Even though their fathers did not understand anything nor were they guided?﴾ This is a debate that God related between the Muslims and the disbelievers. The disbelievers resorted to imitating their fathers, thinking that it would save them because of their good opinion of them, and God judged between them with His saying: ﴿Even though their fathers did not understand anything nor were they guided?﴾. In another place: ﴿Even though Satan was calling them to the punishment of the Blaze?﴾, and in another place: ﴿He said: Even though I brought you what is better guidance than what you found your fathers upon?﴾. So He informed of the invalidity of this argument, and that it does not save them from God's punishment, because it is imitation of one who has no knowledge and no guidance from God. The meaning: even if Satan were calling them to the punishment of the Blaze, they would imitate them; and even if they had no knowledge or guidance, they would still imitate them. This is the condition of one who has no aim in guidance nor in following the truth; his only aim in imitation is to repel the truth and the proof when it binds him, for if his aim were the truth, he would follow it when it became clear to him. I have brought you what is better guidance than what you found your fathers upon. So if you were among those who follow the truth, you would follow what I brought you. You did not imitate the fathers because they were upon the truth; rather, I have brought you something better than what you found them upon, and you only made their imitation a shield with which you repel the truth I brought you.

[Part Three]

(Section note)

They said: gratitude (shukr) is desired for its own sake, while patience (sabr) is desired for the sake of something else. Patience is praised only because it leads to and brings one to gratitude, so it serves gratitude.

It is established in the two Sahihs that the Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer until his feet swelled. He was asked: "Do you do this when Allah has forgiven you your past and future sins?" He said: "Shall I not be a grateful servant?"

It is established in the Musnad and at-Tirmidhi that the Prophet ﷺ said to Mu'adh: "By Allah, I love you, so do not neglect to say after every prayer: O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well."

Ibn Abi'd-Dunya said: Ishaq ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu Mu'awiyah and Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, who said: Among the supplications of the Prophet ﷺ was: "O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well."

He also said: Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, al-Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Talq ibn Habib, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah said: "Whoever is given four things has been given the good of this world and the Hereafter: a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, a body patient under trial, and a wife who does not betray him in herself or in his wealth."

He also mentioned, from the hadith of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Aishah, that the Prophet said: "Allah does not bestow a blessing upon a servant and he knows that it is from Allah, except that Allah records his gratitude for it. And Allah does not know of a servant's regret over a sin except that Allah forgives him before he asks forgiveness. And a man buys a garment for a dinar, wears it, and praises Allah, and it does not reach his knees before he is forgiven."

It is established in Sahih Muslim that he said: "Indeed Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it."

This is the great reward, the greatest kind of reward, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the good pleasure of Allah is greater﴾, in return for his gratitude expressed in praise.

Ibn Abi'd-Dunya mentioned, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Salih, who narrated to us from Abu Zuhayr Yahya ibn 'Attarid al-Qurashi, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: "Allah does not grant a servant gratitude and then deprive him of increase."

Because Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Allah grants enjoyment of a blessing for as long as He wills; but if it is not met with gratitude, it turns into punishment for the heart."

For this reason they called gratitude "the guardian" (al-hafiz), because it preserves the blessings that exist, and "the attractor" (al-jalib), because it draws in blessings that have been lost.

Ibn Abi'd-Dunya also mentioned, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said to a man from Hamadhan: "Blessing is joined to gratitude, and gratitude is tied to increase. The two are linked together, so increase from Allah will never cease until gratitude from the servant ceases."

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: "Bind the blessings of Allah with the gratitude of Allah." He used to say: Gratitude is the fetter of blessings.

Mutarrif ibn 'Abdullah said: "That I be afflicted with health and give thanks is dearer to me than that I be tested and endure patiently."

Al-Hasan said: "Mention these blessings often, for mentioning them is gratitude."

(Section)

Whoever spends something for the sake of Allah, Allah replaces it with something better.

Among the proofs is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So remember Me, and I will remember you; and be grateful to Me and do not deny Me﴾.
