And when he heard the promise, he stretched out and was aflame with longing for it and joy at attaining it, so he was given the name of the hopeful. His two states are inseparable and never part from each other. Every hopeful one is fearful of losing what he hopes for, just as every fearful one is hopeful that he will be safe from what he fears. Therefore the two names alternate upon him. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿What is wrong with you that you do not hope for dignity from God?﴾

They said in its interpretation: "What is wrong with you that you do not fear the greatness of God."

It has already been mentioned that God, glorified is He, limited hope to those who believed, emigrated, and strove.

The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained faith as having branches, outward and inward actions; and he explained emigration as abandoning what God has forbidden, and jihad as striving against the self for the sake of God. So he said: "The emigrant is one who abandons what God has forbidden, and the mujahid is one who strives against his self for the sake of God." The point is that God, glorified is He, made the people of hope those who believed and emigrated, and excluded others from these communities.

As for wishes (al-amani), they are the capital of the bankrupt, which they have deferred in the mold of hope; these are their wishes. They proceed from a heart crowded with the whisperings of the self, and whoever enters it is darkened; he uses his heart in its ploys, and whenever he does so, the goodness of the outcome and salvation grip him, and he refers the matter to pardon, forgiveness, and grace, saying that the Generous does not exact His full due, sins do not harm Him, and forgiveness does not diminish Him. This is called hope, but it is only whispering and false wishes which the self casts into the ignorant heart, and it finds rest in them. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿It is not according to your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Book: whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper﴾.

So when the servant abandons the guardianship of the Truth and His support, God abandons His guardianship and support of him, and he finds for himself, besides Him, no protector or helper. When he abandons His guardianship and support, his own self and Satan take him as an ally, and he is left to his self; his support of it replaces the support of God and His Messenger. Thus he exchanges God's guardianship for the guardianship of his self and his Satan, and His support for the support of his self and his desire. Then no place remains for hope. So if the self says to you, "I am in the station of hope," then demand proof from it and say, "This is a wish; bring your proof if you are truthful." The intelligent person does righteous deeds out of hope and yearning, while the foolish and incapable one abandons righteous deeds and relies on the wishes he calls hope. And God is the Granter of success.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 222:

As for His the Exalted's saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are constantly repentant and loves those who purify themselves﴾, it carries a meaning other than what has been mentioned. That purity is of two kinds: purity by water from minor and major impurities (al-ahdath wa al-najasat), and purity by repentance from shirk and sins. This second purity is the foundation for purity by water, and purity by water is of no benefit without it. Rather, it completes it, prepares it, and makes it ready by its occurrence. Therefore it deserves to be mentioned first, because the servant, when he first enters Islam, has already purified himself by repentance from shirk, and then purifies himself with water from ritual impurity.

(Benefit)

His the Exalted's saying, ﴿They ask you about menstruation. Say: It is an injury, so keep away from women during menstruation﴾. He did not make the ruling of withdrawal (i'tizal) contingent upon menstruation itself as its cause, and He said, ﴿Say: It is an injury﴾, and did not say "menstruation," because the verse is in the form of ﴿Say: It is an injury﴾, which is an informative statement about a reality. The addressees know that the aspect of it being an injury is the very fact of it being menstruation. This differs from making the ruling depend on it, since that is known only through the Shari'ah. So reflect on this.

(Admonition)

Woe to you, do not belittle yourself, for the one who repents is beloved, and the one who denies is sound.

Your acknowledgment of bankruptcy is the very eye of wealth. Lowering your head in remorse is elevation. Your admission of error is the very attainment of being right. The commodity of servanthood was offered in the marketplace of sale, so the angels paid the price, ﴿while we glorify You with Your praise﴾, and Adam said, "I have nothing but the coins of bankruptcy, stamped with ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves﴾."

It was said: this is what is spent on the treasury of the elite.

The groaning of sinners is dearer to us than the chanting of those who glorify.

(Benefit)

When a menstruating woman's bleeding stops, she is like one in a state of major impurity (junub) regarding what is obligatory upon her and what is forbidden to her. Her fasting and her ritual bath are valid, prayer becomes obligatory upon her, she may perform ablution, and she may sit in the mosque. Divorcing her is permissible according to one of the two opinions, except in one matter where she differs from the junub: intercourse with her, which is contingent upon performing the ritual bath. The difference between her and the junub in this is that the impurity of menstruation necessitates the prohibition of intercourse, and its impurity is removed only by the ritual bath, unlike the impurity of major ritual impurity (janabah), which does not necessitate prohibiting intercourse, and such a thing is not possible in it at all.

Some jurists excepted another matter, which is undoing the hair for the ritual bath, as it is obligatory for the menstruating woman according to one of the two opinions but not for the junub. There is no need for this exception, so reflect on it.

Chapters: On the rulings concerning anal intercourse:

Among them, it is one of the major sins. Among them, it necessitates execution if it is with a boy.

Ahmad stated this in one of the two narrations.

The second: its punishment is the punishment for adultery, as Malik and al-Shafi'i said. If it is with his wife or his slave-girl, it necessitates discretionary punishment (ta'zir).

Regarding expiation (kaffarah), there are two views. One is that he owes the expiation of one who has intercourse with a menstruating woman, as chosen by Ibn 'Aqil. The second is that there is no expiation for it, and this is the view of most of our companions. Among them, the wife may annul the marriage because of it, as mentioned by more than one of our companions.

If it is with a non-related woman, our companions differ regarding its punishment. What Abu al-Barakat and Abu Muhammad and others said is that its punishment is the punishment for adultery.

Ibn 'Aqil said in his Fusul: "If intercourse in the anus is with a non-related woman, the punishment that we require for sodomy (liwat) is obligatory. Accordingly, its punishment is execution in every case. If it is with his slave, some of our companions held that he is freed by it, and they treated it as a manifest mutilation (muthlah)."

This is also the view of some of the early generation (salaf).

Al-Nasa'i said in his Sunan al-Kubra: "It is permissible for the judge to say to the defendant, 'Swear,' before the claimant asks him." Hannad ibn al-Sarri reported to us from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Whoever swears an oath in which he is a wrongdoer, in order to seize by it the property of a Muslim man, will meet Allah while He is angry with him."

Al-Ash'ath said: By Allah, it was concerning me. There was a dispute between me and a man from the Jews over land, and he denied it to me, so I brought him before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you have evidence?" I said: "No." He said to the Jew: "Swear." I said: "By Allah, he will swear and my right will be lost." So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price...﴾ the verse.

Al-Nasa'i said: "We do not know of anyone who followed Abu Mu'awiyah in his saying, 'He said to the Jew: Swear.'" End of quote.

It is permissible for the judge to say to him, "Swear," if he intends by it deterrence and intimidation, or if he knows that the claimant intends to make him swear, or if he knows that the defendant is innocent of the claim. For in all three cases of his intention, he has helped in righteousness and piety and the manifestation of truth. Most of the judges' procedures and customs have no basis in the Shari'ah. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

[Section: The wisdom in distinguishing between the istihadah and menstruation regarding intercourse]

As for his saying: "He prohibited intercourse with a menstruating woman because of harm, and permitted intercourse with a woman with istihadah despite the presence of harm, and they are equal," the first premise is true, while the second is ambiguous. If what is meant is that the harm of istihadah equals the harm of menstruation, the premise is false. If what is meant is that it is another kind of harm, then distinguishing between them is not distinguishing between equals, so his objection is invalid on both interpretations.

Among the wisdom of the Lawgiver is His distinguishing between them. The harm of menstruation is greater, more lasting, and more damaging than the harm of istihadah. The blood of istihadah is from a vein, and in the genital area it is like a nosebleed in the nose: its flow is harmful, and its cessation is a sign of health. Menstrual blood is the opposite of this. The two bloods are not equal in reality, in custom, in ruling, or in cause. So it is from the perfection of the Shari'ah that it distinguishes between the two bloods in ruling just as they differ in reality. And success is from Allah.

He concluded the ruling on fay' (return), which is going back and returning to the wife's pleasure and kindness toward her, with: "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," meaning He returns to His servant with His forgiveness and mercy when he returns. The recompense is of the same kind as the deed: just as the servant returned to what is better (التي هي أحسن), Allah returned to him with forgiveness and mercy.

﴿And if they are determined upon divorce, then indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. Since divorce is a word that is heard and a meaning that is intended, He followed it with the name "Hearing" for what is uttered, and "Knowing" for its content.

He concluded the ruling on fay' (return), which is going back and returning to the wife's pleasure and kindness toward her, with: "Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," meaning He returns to His servant with His forgiveness and mercy when he returns. The recompense is of the same kind as the deed: just as the servant returned to what is better (التي هي أحسن), Allah returned to him with forgiveness and mercy.

﴿And if they are determined upon divorce, then indeed Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾. Since divorce is a word that is heard and a meaning that is intended, He followed it with the name "Hearing" for what is uttered, and "Knowing" for its content.

(Section: The wisdom of the waiting period (ʿiddah) of divorce)

As for the waiting period of divorce, its rationale cannot be explained by that, for it is obligatory only after consummation (al-masīs) by agreement, and not for the sake of the womb's being free (barāʾat al-raḥm), because that is achieved by a single menstrual cycle, like istibrāʾ (the purification of the womb), although the freeing of the womb is one of its objectives.

It may not be said, "It is an act of devotion (taʿabbud)," for the reason already mentioned. Its ruling becomes clear only when the rights contained in it are known. It contains the right of God, which is compliance with His command and seeking His pleasure; a right of the divorcing husband, which is the extension of the period in which he may take her back (al-rajʿah); a right of the wife, which is her entitlement to maintenance (nafaqah) and lodging (sukna) for as long as she is in the ʿiddah; a right of the child, which is the safeguarding of the establishment of his lineage (nasab) and that it not be mixed with that of another; and a right of the second husband, which is that he not water his seed in another's field. The Lawgiver (al-Shāriʿ) has attached to each of these rights the rulings that befit it. Thus, in safeguarding her right (the husband's), it is ordained that she remain in the home, that she neither leave nor be expelled. This is what the Qur'an requires, and it is the explicit position of the Imam of the people of hadith and the Imam of the people of opinion (ra'y).

Upon the right of the divorcing husband is ordained his being enabled to take her back so long as she is in the ʿiddah; upon her right is ordained her entitlement to maintenance and lodging; upon the right of the child is ordained the establishment of his lineage and its attribution to his father alone, to the exclusion of others; and upon the right of the second husband is ordained his entering upon her with insight and with a womb that is clear, not occupied with a child belonging to another. So making it three menstrual periods (qurūʾ) serves to safeguard these rights and to complete them. The Qur'an has indicated that the ʿiddah is a right of the husband over her, by His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, there is no waiting period for you to reckon against them﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 49]. This is evidence that the ʿiddah is due to the man from the woman after consummation. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And their husbands have more right to take them back during that period, if they desire reconciliation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228]. So He made the husband more entitled to take her back during the ʿiddah. Since the ʿiddah is three qurūʾ or three months, the period of waiting is lengthened so that he may consider her matter: whether he will keep her in kindness or release her with good conduct. Likewise, God, glory be to Him, granted the one who swears off (al-mūlī) a waiting period of four months in which to consider his matter: whether he will return or divorce. And likewise He made the period for the disbelievers' travel (tasyīr) four months, so that they might consider their situation and choose for themselves.

(Benefit)

Shaykh Tāj al-Dīn said: "Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām was asked about the meaning of the jurists' statement to the one who pronounces a revocable divorce, 'Say: I have taken back my wife into my marriage.' What does it mean, since she has not left the marriage, being a wife in all rulings?

I said to him: 'Its meaning is that she has returned to the complete marriage, in which she was not heading toward irrevocable separation by the passing of time; and by the divorce she came to be heading toward irrevocable separation by the completion of the ʿiddah.'" He said: "You have done well."

[Section: The wisdom in equalizing woman with man in some rulings and not others]

As for his statement: "He equalized between man and woman in the bodily acts of worship and in the penal prescriptions (ḥudūd), and made her half of him in blood-money (diyah), testimony, inheritance, and the ʿaqīqah," this too is from the perfection of His Law, its wisdom and its gentleness. The benefit of the bodily acts of worship and the benefit of the punishments are shared between men and women, and the need of one of the two sexes for them is like the need of the other; so it is not fitting to differentiate between them. Yes, He did differentiate between them in the places most suited to differentiation, namely the Friday prayer (Jumuʿah) and congregational prayer (jamāʿah): He restricted their obligation to men, not women, because they are not of those who go out and mix with men. Likewise He differentiated between them in the act of worship of jihad, of which females are not among the people. And He equalized them in the obligation of Hajj, since both kinds need its benefit, and in the obligation of zakāt, fasting, and purification. As for testimony, the woman was made half of the man in it because of a wisdom that the Mighty and Wise indicated in His Book: the woman is weak in intellect and little in retention of what she remembers. God has preferred men over women in intellect, understanding, memory, and discernment; so the woman cannot take the place of the man in that. Refusing to accept her testimony altogether would lose many rights and nullify them, so it was among the best and most intellectually fitting arrangements that a second woman be joined to her in accepting testimony, so that she may remind her if she forgets; thus the testimony of two women stands in place of the testimony of one man, and the knowledge or prevailing assumption produced by their testimony is that produced by the testimony of one man. As for blood-money, since the woman is less than the man, and the man is more beneficial than her, filling the religious offices, governorships, guarding the frontiers, jihad, cultivating the earth, and performing the crafts without which the interests of the world are not complete, and defending the world and religion, their value was not equal with that, namely the blood-money. The blood-money of a free person functions as the value of a slave and other property; so the wisdom of the Lawgiver required that her value be half of his, given the difference between them.

If it is said: "But you have contradicted this, for you made their blood-money equal in what is below one-third."

It is said: There is no doubt that the Sunnah has come with this, as al-Nasāʾī narrated from the hadith of ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: «The blood-money of a woman is like the blood-money of a man until it reaches a third of her blood-money.»

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: "This is from the Sunnah." Although Abū Ḥanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, al-Layth, al-Thawrī, and a group disagreed with it, saying: "It is half in both little and much." But the Sunnah takes precedence. The distinction between what is below one-third and what exceeds it is that what is below it is small, so the woman's calamity in it is compensated by her equality with the man. For this reason the male and female fetus were equal in blood-money because its blood-money is small, namely the ghurrah; so what is below one-third takes the place of the fetus.

As for inheritance, the wisdom of the preference in it is evident: the male has more need of wealth than the female, because men are the maintainers (qawwāmūn) over women, and the male is more beneficial to the deceased during his life than the female. God, glory be to Him, indicated this by His saying, after He prescribed the shares and differentiated between their measures: ﴿Your fathers and your sons—you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 11]. And since the male is more beneficial than the female and more in need, he is more deserving of preference.

If it is said: "This is refuted by the children of the mother (uterine siblings)." It is said: Rather, the consistent application of this equality is among the children of the mother, male and female alike, for they inherit only by the mere womb-tie (raḥm mujarrad). The kinship through which they inherit is only the kinship of the mother, and in it they are equal; so there is no sense in preferring their males over their females, unlike paternal kinship. As for the ʿaqīqah, the matter of preference in it follows the honor of the male and what God distinguished him with over the female. Since the blessing through him to the parent is more complete, and the joy and happiness through him more perfect, thanksgiving for it is greater; for whenever a blessing increases, its thanks increases. And God knows best.

(Fawa'id)

The divisions of marriage (firaq al-nikah) are twenty:
The first: separation by divorce (firqat al-talaq).
The second: annulment due to inability to pay the dowry (al-faskh lil-'usrah bil-mahr).
The third: annulment due to inability to provide maintenance (al-faskh lil-'usr 'an al-nafaqah).
The fourth: separation by ila' (fur'qat al-ila').
The fifth: separation by khul' (fur'qat al-khul').
The sixth: separation by the two arbitrators (tafriq al-hakamayn).
The seventh: separation of the impotent man (firqat al-'anin).
The eighth: separation by li'an (firqat al-li'an).
The ninth: separation when a slave woman is freed under a slave husband (firqat al-'itq tahta al-'abd).
The tenth: separation by deception (firqat al-ghurur).
The eleventh: separation due to defects (firqat al-'uyub).
The twelfth: separation due to nursing (firqat al-radha').
The thirteenth: separation due to intercourse by mistake (wat' al-shubhah), where the wife becomes forbidden.
The fourteenth: separation when one of the spouses converts to Islam (firqat islam ahad al-zawjayn).
The fifteenth: separation when one of them apostatizes (firqat irtidad ahadihima).
The sixteenth: separation when a husband converts to Islam while having two sisters, or more than four wives, or a woman and her paternal aunt, or a woman and her maternal aunt.
The seventeenth: separation by captivity (firqat al-sabi).
The eighteenth: separation when one spouse comes to own the other (firqat milk ahad al-zawjayn sahibatahu).
The nineteenth: separation due to ignorance of which of two marriages came first (firqat al-jahl bi-sabq ahad al-nikahayn).
The twentieth: separation by death (firqat al-mawt).

Of these separations, some are for the wife alone: separation by emancipation, deception and defect. Some are for the husband alone: divorce, deception and also defect. Some involve the judge's intervention: separation of the impotent, the two arbitrators, ila', inability to pay maintenance or dowry, and the marriage of two guardians. Some do not depend on either spouse or the judge: li'an, apostasy, intercourse by mistake, one spouse's conversion, and one spouse coming to own the other, and nursing.

Also, some of these separations cannot be remedied except after a marriage and consummation, which is the exhaustion of the three (divorces). Some can never be remedied: separation by li'an, nursing and intercourse by mistake. Some can be remedied only within the waiting period ('iddah): separation by apostasy, conversion of one spouse, and revocable divorce. Some can be remedied by a new contract: separation by khul', inability to pay dowry or maintenance, separation by ila', defects and deception. All of these are annulments (faskh), except divorce, ila' separation, and separation by the two arbitrators.

[Section: Pronouncing the Three Divorces with One Utterance]

The seventh example: In the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and the time of his successor Abu Bakr, and the early part of the caliphate of 'Umar, if a man pronounced three divorces with one utterance, it was counted as one, as is established in the Sahih from Ibn 'Abbas. Muslim related in his Sahih from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Triple divorce during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and the first two years of 'Umar's caliphate was counted as one. Then 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'Indeed, people have hastened in a matter in which they had a period of deliberation. So if we enforce it upon them,' and he enforced it upon them." In his Sahih also, from Tawus: Abu al-Sahba' said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Do you not know that the triple divorce was counted as one during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr, and three during the governorship of 'Umar?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Yes." In his Sahih also: Abu al-Sahba' said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Bring your inconsistencies. Was not the triple divorce one during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr?" He said: "It was so. But when it was the time of 'Umar, people persisted in divorce, so he enforced it upon them."

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud from Tawus: a man called Abu al-Sahba', who often questioned Ibn 'Abbas, said: "Do you not know that when a man divorced his wife three times before consummating with her, they counted it as one during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abu Bakr, and the early part of the governorship of 'Umar - may Allah be pleased with him?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Yes. When a man divorced his wife three times before consummation, they counted it as one during the time of the Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr, and the early part of 'Umar's governorship. But when he saw that people were persisting in it, he said: 'Enforce them upon them.'"

In the Mustadrak of al-Hakim, from the narration of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mu'ammal, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah: Abu al-Jawza' came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "Do you know that the three (divorces) were returned to one during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" He said: "Yes." 

Al-Hakim said: "This is a sahih hadith, and this is a chain other than the route of Tawus from Abu al-Sahba'."

Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Sa'd ibn Ibrahim related to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from 'Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Rukanah ibn 'Abd Yazid, brother of Banu al-Muttalib, divorced his wife three times in one sitting, and he grieved over her greatly. The Messenger of Allah asked him: 'How did you divorce her?' He said: 'I divorced her three times.' He said: 'In one sitting?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then that is only one, so take her back if you wish.' So he took her back." Ibn 'Abbas used to hold that divorce only takes effect at each purity (tuhr).

Imam Ahmad authenticated this chain and graded it as good (hasan). He said regarding the hadith of 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb from his father from his grandfather, that "the Prophet ﷺ returned his daughter to Ibn Abi al-'As with a new dowry and a new marriage contract": this is a weak hadith, or he said: "It is feeble; al-Hajjaj did not hear it from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb; he heard it only from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-'Azrami, and al-'Azrami's narrations are worth nothing." The hadith that he related, that "the Prophet ﷺ left them both in the first marriage," and its chain according to him is the chain of the hadith of Rukanah ibn 'Abd Yazid. Al-Tirmidhi said about it: "There is no fault in its chain." So this is a sahih chain according to Ahmad, and there is no fault in it according to al-Tirmidhi. So it is a proof so long as nothing stronger contradicts it, so how much more so when it is supported by something of its kind or stronger?

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Salih related to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, Ibn Jurayj informed us, who said: "Some of the Banu Abi Rafi', mawla of the Prophet ﷺ, informed me, from 'Ikrimah, mawla of Ibn 'Abbas, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Abd Yazid, Abu Rukanah, and his brothers divorced Umm Rukanah, and he married a woman from Muzaynah. She came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'It is of no more use to me than this hair from the hair of her head,' and she took a hair from her head. The Prophet ﷺ was seized with zeal, so he summoned Rukanah and his brothers. Then he said to his companions: 'Do you see that so-and-so resembles so-and-so of 'Abd Yazid, and so-and-so resembles him in such-and-such?' They said: 'Yes.' The Prophet ﷺ said to 'Abd Yazid: 'Divorce her,' and he did. He said: 'Take back your wife, Umm Rukanah and his brothers.' He said: 'I divorced her three times, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I know. Take her back,' and he recited: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their waiting period﴾ [al-Talaq: 1]."

Abu Dawud said: The hadith of Nafi' ibn Jubayr and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ali ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah, from his father, from his grandfather, that "Rukanah divorced his wife and the Prophet ﷺ returned her to him," is more sound, because they are the man's children and family and know him better; "and that Rukanah only divorced his wife with al-batta (irrevocable divorce), so the Prophet ﷺ made it one."

Our shaykh - may Allah be pleased with him - said: Abu Dawud, since he did not narrate in his Sunan the hadith that is in the Musnad of Ahmad - meaning the one we mentioned just now - said: "The hadith of al-batta is more sound than the hadith of Ibn Jurayj that Rukanah divorced his wife three times, because they are the people of his household." But the great imams who know the defects of hadith and jurisprudence, such as Imam Ahmad, Abu 'Ubayd and al-Bukhari, declared the hadith of al-batta weak, and made clear that it is a narration of unknown people whose reliability and precision are not established. Ahmad confirmed the hadith of the three and made clear that it is correct, and said: "The hadith of Rukanah does not establish that he divorced his wife with al-batta." In another narration from him: "The hadith of Rukanah concerning al-batta is worth nothing, because Ibn Ishaq narrates it from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas - may Allah be pleased with him - that Rukanah divorced his wife three times, and the people of Madinah call three al-batta." Al-Athram said: "I said to Ahmad: 'The hadith of Rukanah concerning al-batta' and he declared it weak.

The point is that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab - may Allah be pleased with him - was not unaware that this was the Sunnah, and that it is a mercy from Allah to His servants, since He made divorce occur once after another. What occurs once after another, the one obligated cannot make all its instances occur at once, like li'an. For if he says: "I testify by Allah four times that I am among the truthful," it is one instance. If he swears in the qasamah and says: "I swear by Allah fifty oaths that this is his killer," it is one oath. If one who confesses to fornication says: "I confess four times that I committed fornication," it is one time. Whoever counts the four does not regard it as anything but a single confession. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever says in a day: 'Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi' a hundred times, his sins will be removed, even if they are like the foam of the sea." If he says: "Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi a hundred times" all at once, he does not obtain this reward until he says it time after time. Likewise his saying: "Whoever glorifies Allah after every prayer thirty-three times, praises Him thirty-three times, and magnifies Him thirty-three times," etc.; he is not acting upon it until he says that time after time, and he does not gather them all in one utterance. Likewise his saying: "Whoever says in a day: 'La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir,' a hundred times, it will be a protection for him from Satan that day until evening." This is not attained except by saying it time after time. Likewise His saying: ﴿O you who believe, let your slaves and those who have not reached puberty among you ask permission from you three times﴾ [al-Nur: 58]. And likewise His saying in the hadith: "Seeking permission is three times; if he grants you permission, well, otherwise return." If a man said "three times" like that, it would be one time until he asks permission time after time. This applies to actions as it does to statements and utterances alike, such as His saying: ﴿We will punish them twice﴾ [al-Tawbah: 101], which means once after another. Likewise Ibn 'Abbas's saying: "Muhammad saw his Lord with his heart twice," means once after another. Likewise the Prophet ﷺ's saying: "A believer is not stung from the same hole twice." This is the meaning derived from the language and custom in the hadiths mentioned. These texts mentioned and His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229] are all of one door and one niche. The hadiths mentioned explain the meaning of His saying: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾ [al-Baqarah: 229], just as the hadith of li'an explains His saying: ﴿The testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah﴾ [al-Nur: 6].

This is the Book of Allah, this is the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is the language of the Arabs, this is the custom of discourse, and this is the successor of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, with all the Companions in his time and for three years of 'Umar's time upon this view. If one were to count them by name, one by one, he would find that they regarded the triple (divorce) as one, either by fatwa or by approval of it, or by silence. Even if there were among them someone who did not hold this view, he did not deny the fatwa issued with it. Rather, they were between one who gave the fatwa, one who approved the fatwa, and one who was silent without denying it.

This was the position of every Companion from the time of al-Siddiq until the first three years of 'Umar's caliphate, and they definitely exceeded a thousand, as Yunus ibn Bukayr reported from Abu Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr narrated to me from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "There were martyred from the Muslims at the Battle of al-Yamamah twelve hundred men, of whom seventy were reciters, all of whom had recited the Qur'an. And Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr died during the caliphate of al-Siddiq." Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "When the Muslims among the Muhajirun and Ansar were struck at al-Yamamah, and most of the jurists and reciters of the Muslims were struck among them, Abu Bakr turned to the Qur'an, fearing that a group of it would perish." Every Companion from the time of the caliphate of al-Siddiq until the first three years of 'Umar's caliphate held that the triple (divorce) was one, whether by fatwa, approval, or silence. For this reason some scholars claimed that this was an ancient consensus. The Ummah, praise be to Allah, did not reach consensus against it. Rather, there were always those among them who gave this fatwa, generation after generation, until this day. The scholar of the Ummah and interpreter of the Qur'an, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, gave this fatwa, as Hammad ibn Zayd narrated from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "If he says: 'You are divorced three times' in one utterance, it is one." He also gave a fatwa for three. He gave a fatwa for this and for that.

And Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf issued a fatwa that it counts as one (divorce). Ibn Wadhdhah related this from them. From Ali, may Allah honour his face, and from Ibn Mas'ud there are two reports, as there are from Ibn Abbas.

Among the Successors (al-tabi'un), Ikrimah issued a fatwa to this effect. Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related it from Ayyub, from him. Tawus also issued a fatwa to this effect.

Among the successors of the Successors (tabi' al-tabi'in), Muhammad ibn Ishaq issued a fatwa to this effect. Imam Ahmad and others related it from him. Khilas ibn Amr and al-Harith al-Ukli also issued a fatwa to this effect.

Among the followers of the successors of the Successors, Dawud ibn Ali and most of his companions issued a fatwa to this effect. Abu al-Muflis, Ibn Hazm and others related it from them. Some of the companions of Malik also issued a fatwa to this effect; al-Tilimsani related it in his commentary on Ibn al-Jallab's Tafri', as an opinion held by some Malikis.

Some of the Hanafis issued a fatwa to this effect. Abu Bakr al-Razi related it from Muhammad ibn Muqatil. Some of the companions of Ahmad also issued a fatwa to this effect; Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah related it from him, and said: "The grandfather (Ibn Taymiyyah's grandfather) used to issue this fatwa at times."

As for Imam Ahmad himself: al-Athram said, "I asked Abu Abd Allah about the hadith of Ibn Abbas: 'Triple divorce was counted as one in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr and Umar,' by what do you repel it?" He said: "By the reports of people from Ibn Abbas in many ways that contradict it." Then he mentioned from a number of narrators from Ibn Abbas that it is three. He thus stated clearly that he only abandoned the view of this hadith because of a report from Ibn Abbas that contradicted it. The root of his school and the principle upon which he built it is that when a hadith is authentic, he does not reject it because a narrator of it contradicts it; rather, he acts upon what the narrator reported. He did this in the report of Ibn Abbas and his fatwa concerning the sale of a slave-girl: he acted upon the report that it is not a divorce, and abandoned his own opinion. On this principle, the view that triple divorce counts as one can be derived for him, for when he stated that he left the hadith only because the narrator contradicted it, and stated in several places that the narrator's contradiction does not necessitate abandoning the hadith, two opinions arise for him on the question. His followers derive from him, as opinions in his school, far fewer than that.

The point is that this view is supported by the Book, the Sunnah, analogy (qiyas), and the earlier consensus (ijma'). No consensus came after it that nullifies it. But Commander of the Believers Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, saw that people had become careless about the matter of divorce, and that many of them pronounced it all at once. So he regarded it as in the public interest to punish them by enforcing it upon them, so that they would know that if one of them pronounces it all at once, the woman becomes separated from him and forbidden to him until she marries another husband in a marriage of desire intended for permanence, not a marriage of tahlil (an intermediary marriage to make her lawful again). For they had been among the most extreme of people in this. When they knew that, they refrained from the forbidden divorce. Umar saw that this was in the public interest in his time.

He also saw that what they had been upon in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), in the time of al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), and in the early part of his own caliphate, was more fitting for them, because they did not pronounce it in succession, and they used to fear Allah regarding divorce. Allah has made a way out for everyone who fears Him. But when they abandoned the fear of Allah, played with the Book of Allah, and divorced in a manner other than what Allah prescribed, he obliged them to what they had committed themselves to, as a punishment for them. For Allah the Exalted only prescribed divorce once after another, and did not prescribe it all at once. So whoever combines the three in one utterance has transgressed the limits of Allah, wronged himself, and played with the Book of Allah. He deserves to be punished and held to what he committed himself to, and not be allowed the concession and ease of Allah. He has made it difficult for himself, has not feared Allah, and has not divorced as Allah commanded and prescribed for him. Rather, he hastened in what Allah had made a matter of patience for him, out of His mercy and kindness. He confused himself and chose the harshest and most severe. Thus this is among the matters in which the fatwa changed with the change of time. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, knew the wisdom of Umar's governance and his disciplining of his subjects in this matter, so they agreed with him on what he imposed. They stated this to those who asked them. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Whoever approaches the matter as it should be approached, it has been made clear to him. Whoever confuses himself, we shall hold him to his confusion. By Allah, you will not confuse yourselves and then we bear it for you. It is as you say."

If the triple divorce counting as three were in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, then the one who divorced would have approached the matter as it should be approached, and he would not have confused himself. And would the Prophet (ﷺ) have said to one who did that, "You play with the Book of Allah while I am among you"?

When Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr hesitated about the matter of pronouncing it, and said to the questioner: "This matter, we have no opinion on it. Go to Abd Allah ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah." When he came to them, Ibn Abbas said to Abu Hurayrah: "Give him a fatwa, for a difficult problem has come to you." Then the two of them issued a fatwa that it takes effect.

So the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and their foremost, Umar ibn al-Khattab, when they saw people had become careless about the matter of divorce, had let go of what was in their hands of it, had confused themselves, had not feared Allah regarding the divorce He prescribed for them, and had taken the strictness upon themselves, and did not stop at what was set as their limit, held them to what they had committed themselves to, and enforced upon them what they had chosen for themselves of strictness. Allah had made easy for them what He prescribed for them, in contrast to this. There is no doubt that whoever does this deserves punishment, that what he imposed upon himself be enforced upon him, since he did not accept the concession, the ease, and the leniency of Allah. For this reason Ibn Abbas said to a man who had divorced a hundred times: "You disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has been separated from you. You did not fear Allah, so He does not make a way out for you. Whoever fears Allah, He makes a way out for him." A man came to him and said: "My uncle divorced three times." He said: "Your uncle disobeyed Allah, so He has made him regret it, and he obeyed Satan, so He did not make a way out for him." The man said: "Will you not make her lawful to him (through tahlil)?" He said: "Whoever deceives Allah, Allah deceives him."

So let the scholar whose aim is to know the truth and follow it, of the Sharia and the divine decree, reflect on the acceptance by the Companions of this concession and ease in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and their fear of their Lord, Blessed and Exalted, in divorce. The concession and ease of Allah then applied to them, in Sharia and in decree. But when people embarked on foolishness, abandoned the fear of Allah, confused themselves, and divorced in a manner other than what Allah prescribed for them, Allah caused, through the tongue of the rightly guided Caliph and the Companions with him, the imposition of that upon them in Sharia and decree, the enforcement of it upon them, and the keeping of the burden which they had placed around their own necks, as they had placed it. These are among the secrets of the Sharia and the decree, which do not suit the minds of the people of this age. Then came the Imams of Islam, who followed the traces of the Companions, walking their path, seeking the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger and the enforcement of His religion.

Among them is one who abandoned the view of the hadith of Ibn Abbas, supposing it to be abrogated (mansukh). This was the method of al-Shafi'i.

He said: "If the meaning of Ibn Abbas's statement that triple divorce was counted as one in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that it was by the command of the Prophet (ﷺ), then it is likely that Ibn Abbas knew of something which was then abrogated."

If it is said: "What is the evidence for what you describe?" It is said: "It is not likely that Ibn Abbas would narrate something from the Prophet (ﷺ) and then oppose it with something, without knowing that there was a difference from the Prophet (ﷺ) on it."

If it is said: "Perhaps this was something related from Umar, and Ibn Abbas spoke about it according to Umar's statement." It is said: "We know that Ibn Abbas opposed Umar regarding temporary marriage (nikah al-mut'ah), the exchange of a dinar for two dinars, and the sale of umm al-walad (mothers of children). So how could he agree with him in something whose contrary was related from the Prophet (ﷺ)?"

[Section: The Companion's fatwa against what he himself narrated]

Those who oppose the binding of triple divorce said: "Abrogation is not established by possibility, nor is an authentic, protected hadith abandoned because its narrator contradicts it, for his contradiction is not protected." Al-Shafi'i gave precedence to the report of Ibn Abbas concerning Barirah over his fatwa which contradicts it, regarding the sale of a slave-girl being her divorce. He, Ahmad and others acted upon the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "Whoever vomits, upon him is the making up of the fast." Yet Abu Hurayrah contradicted it and issued a fatwa that there is no making up upon him. They also acted upon the report of Ibn Abbas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded his Companions to perform ramal (a brisk walk) in the first three circuits and to walk between the two corners (of the Ka'bah)." It is authentically related from him that he said: "Ramal is not a Sunnah." They acted upon the report of Aisha concerning the prohibition of a menstruating woman from circumambulating (tawaf), though it is authentically related from her that a woman menstruated while circumambulating with her, and Aisha completed the rest of her circumambulation with her. This was related by Sa'id ibn Mansur: "Abu Awanah narrated to us from Abu Bishr from Ata," and he mentioned it. They acted upon the report of Ibn Abbas on advancing or delaying the stoning, shaving and sacrifice relative to one another, and that there is no fault in this, though Ibn Abbas issued a fatwa that there is a blood-sacrifice (dam) for it. They did not turn to his statement but acted upon his report. The Hanafis acted upon the hadith of Ibn Abbas: "Every divorce is permissible except the divorce of one who is mentally incapacitated (al-m'atuh)." They said: "This is explicit regarding the divorce of one who is coerced." It is authentically related from Ibn Abbas: "There is no divorce for one who is coerced or oppressed." They and the people all acted upon the hadith of Ibn Umar that he bought a stray camel, by the most authentic chain that can be. The Hanafis and Hanbalis acted upon the hadith of Ali, may Allah honour his face, and Ibn Abbas: "The middle prayer is the Asr prayer." It is established from Ali, may Allah honour his face, and Ibn Abbas that it is the Fajr prayer. The four Imams and others acted upon the report of Aisha concerning prohibition through the milk of the stallion (the male who fathered the milk), though it is authentically related from her that she contradicted it: she used to let in those whom the daughters of her brothers had nursed, and did not let in those whom the wives of her brothers had nursed. The Hanafis acted upon the report of Aisha: "Prayer was prescribed as two units, two units," though it is authentically related from her that she completed the prayer while travelling. They did not abandon her report for their own opinion. They argued with the hadith of Jabir and Abu Musa on the command to perform ablution because of laughter during prayer, though it is authentically related from both of them that they said: "There is no ablution because of that." The people acted upon the hadith of Aisha regarding abandoning the requirement of ablution for what fire has touched, though it is authentically related from Aisha, by the most authentic chain, the requirement of ablution for prayer after eating anything fire has touched. The people acted upon the hadiths of Aisha, Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah concerning wiping over leather socks (khuffayn), though it is authentically related from all three of them the prohibition of wiping at all. So they acted upon their reports and abandoned their opinions.

And they argued for the non-application of retaliation (qisas) against a father by the hadith of Umar: "A child shall not be subjected to retaliation for his father." Yet Umar himself said: "I shall certainly apply retaliation to a father on behalf of his child." They did not take his opinion but his narration.

The Hanafis and the Malikis argued that khul' (divorce initiated by the wife in exchange for compensation) is a talaq (divorce) on the basis of two hadiths from Ibn Abbas that are not authentically transmitted from him. Yet it is authentically transmitted from Ibn Abbas, by the most sound chain, that "khul' is a faskh (annulment) and not a talaq." The Hanafis adopted a hadith that is not authentic, rather it is a fabrication of Hizam ibn Uthman and Mubashshir ibn Ubayd al-Halabi, the hadith of Jabir: "There is no mahr (bridal gift) less than ten dirhams." Yet it is authentically transmitted from Jabir that marriage is permissible with whatever is little or much.

They and others argued for the prohibition of selling ummahat al-awlad (slave women who have borne their masters' children) by the marfu' hadith of Ibn Abbas, yet it is authentically transmitted from him that their sale is permissible. Thus they preferred his narration, which was not established, over his sound fatwa (legal verdict) on the matter.

The Hanbalis and others adopted the report of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib from Umar, that he attributed the child to both parents. Yet Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib himself opposed it, and they did not take his dissent into account.

It is authentically transmitted from Umar, Uthman and Mu'awiyah that "the Messenger of God (ﷺ) performed mut'ah (combining umrah with hajj)," and it is authentically transmitted from them that they forbade mut'ah. The people took their narration and abandoned their opinion.

The people adopted the hadith of Abu Hurayrah concerning the sea: "Its water is pure and its dead animals are lawful." Yet Sa'id ibn Mansur related in his Sunan from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "Two waters do not suffice for ghusl (ritual bath) from janabah: the water of the sea and the water of the bathhouse."

The Hanbalis and the Shafi'is adopted the hadith of Abu Hurayrah on the command to wash a vessel after a dog has licked it. Yet what is authentically transmitted from Abu Hurayrah, as related by Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Sunan, is that Abu Hurayrah was asked about a pool from which a dog drinks and a donkey drinks, and he said: "Nothing makes the water unlawful."

The Hanafis adopted the hadith of Ali, may God honor his face: "There is no zakah (obligatory alms) on what exceeds two hundred dirhams until it reaches forty dirhams," despite the weakness of this hadith through al-Hasan ibn Umarah. Yet it is authentically transmitted from Ali, may God honor his face, that what exceeds two hundred has zakah due on it in proportion to its amount, related by Abd al-Razzaq from Ma'mar from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i from Asim ibn Damrah from him.

This is a subject whose tracing is long. You will see many people, when a hadith comes that agrees with the view of the one whom they follow, while that one has opposed it in his narration, say: "The proof is in what he narrated, not in his opinion." But when the narrator's opinion comes in agreement with the view of the one they follow while the hadith is contrary to it, they say: "The narrator would not have opposed what he narrated unless its abrogation (naskh) was authentically known to him; otherwise it would be a blemish on his integrity." Thus they combine in their speech between this and that, and indeed we have seen this in one and the same chapter, and this is among the ugliest of contradictions.

What we are bound to before God, and what we cannot do otherwise than, and what is the aim in this chapter, is that when a hadith is authentically transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and no other hadith abrogating it is authentically transmitted from him, it is an obligation upon us and upon the Ummah to act upon his hadith and to leave everything that opposes it. We do not abandon it for the disagreement of any person whoever he may be, neither narrator nor other. For it is possible that the narrator forgot the hadith, or was not present at the time of the fatwa, or did not perceive its indication on that issue, or interpreted it with an unpreferred interpretation, or that in his assumption there was something that opposes it while in reality it does not oppose it, or that he imitated another in his fatwa contrary to it, believing that the other was more knowledgeable than him and that he only opposed it for what is stronger. And even if all of that is assumed absent, and there is no way to know its absence or to assume it, the narrator is not infallible, and his opposing what he narrated does not require the forfeiting of his integrity until his evil deeds outweigh his good deeds. But this is not the case with one single hadith.

[Section: How the fatwa changes with the change of times and circumstances]

Once this is known, this issue is among those on which the fatwa has changed according to the times, as you have come to know, because of the public interest that the Companions saw. For they saw that the harm of people's successive pronouncement of three talaqs could not be averted except by enforcing them upon them. So they saw that the benefit of enforcement was stronger than the harm of its occurrence. Yet the door of tahlil (the temporary marriage arranged to make a divorced woman lawful to her former husband), whose doer the Messenger of God (ﷺ) cursed, was not open in any way; rather they were the most intense of God's creation in forbidding it, and Umar threatened its doer with stoning. They were knowledgeable about the permitted talaq and other matters. But in these times, in which the private parts have complained to their Lord of the harm of tahlil, and of the ugliness of what the muhallilun (those who perform tahlil) commit, which is a sore and even a blindness in the eye of the religion and a bone stuck in the throats of the believers, of ugly acts that give the enemies of the religion cause to gloat and deter many who wish to enter it because of them, to such an extent that no speech encompasses their details and no book contains them, all believers see them as among the worst ugliness and count them among the greatest disgraces, they have changed the religion's features and altered its name, and the borrowed billy-goat in them has soiled the divorced woman with the filth of tahlil, while claiming that he has made her pure for her husband. So, for God's sake, what a wonder! What purity has this cursed billy-goat lent her? And what benefit has come to her or to her divorcer through this base act? Do you think the divorcing husband or the guardian standing at the door, while the cursed billy-goat has loosened her waistcloth, uncovered her veil, and begun in that pasture, while the husband or the guardian calls out to him: "This food was not offered to you so that you would be satisfied! You know, you and the wife, and we and the witnesses and those present and the recording angels and the Lord of the worlds, that you are not counted among the husbands, and that neither the woman nor her guardians have any pleasure, joy or delight in you, but you are only like the borrowed billy-goat for mating, who, were it not for this affliction, we would not have consented to your standing at the door!" People display marriage and announce it with joy and happiness, while we urge one another to conceal this incurable disease and make it a hidden matter, without a distribution of sweets, without a drum, without a feast, without announcement, but rather urging one another in whispers, touching, concealment and secrecy. The woman is married for her religion, lineage, wealth and beauty, while the borrowed billy-goat does not ask about any of that, for he does not keep her in marriage, rather he has entered upon her ruin. God the Exalted has made each of the spouses a comfort to the other, and placed between them affection and mercy, so that through this the aim of this great contract is achieved, and the benefit for which the Mighty, the Wise, legislated it is completed. So ask the borrowed billy-goat: does he have any share of that? Or is he a stranger to the wisdom, purpose and benefit of this contract?

And ask him: has he taken this afflicted woman as a spouse and a bed to which he returns? Then ask her: has she ever been pleased with him as a husband and mate, on whom she relies in her calamities? And ask people of discernment and intellect: did so-and-so marry so-and-so? Is this considered a marriage by any law, reason or human nature? And how could the Messenger of God (ﷺ) curse a man of his Ummah who married in a lawful, sound marriage, and did not commit in his contract anything forbidden or ugly? And how could he be likened to the borrowed billy-goat, when he is among the doers of good, the righteous? And how is the woman reproached by him throughout her life among her family and neighbors, and remains with her head bowed whenever that billy-goat is mentioned among women? And ask the borrowed billy-goat: did he, at the time of this contract, which is the twin of hypocrisy, think of expenditure, clothing, or the weight of the mahr (bridal gift)? Did the afflicted woman hope from him for any of that, or did she entertain such thoughts in that moment? Did he ask her for a noble child, and did she take him as a companion and beloved? And ask the intellects and natural dispositions of all the worlds: was the best of this Ummah the one with the most tahlil, or was the muhallil whom God and His Messenger cursed the one who guided them to the path?

And ask the borrowed billy-goat and the one afflicted with him: did either of them adorn himself for the other, as men adorn themselves for women and women for men? Or did either of them have a desire for the other because of lineage, wealth or beauty? And ask the woman: would she dislike it if this borrowed billy-goat married another over her or took a concubine, or would she dislike having another wife under him? Or would she ask him about his wealth, his occupation, his good companionship and the abundance of his spending? And ask the borrowed billy-goat: has he ever asked about what those who intend the reality of marriage ask about? Or does he seek access to the house of his in-laws with gifts, camel-loads, and the cash with which a suitor of the beautiful seeks access? And ask him: is he one who takes or one who gives? And is his saying, when the reading of Ubayy (the contract's recitation) is done, "Take the expense of this wedding or reduce it," [part of his speech]?

And ask him: did he bear any of the burden of this contract, such as "take the expense of this wedding or reduce it"? And ask him about the wedding feast: did he host a feast even with a sheep? Did he invite one of his companions to it, fulfilling its right, and did they come to him? And ask him: did he bear any of the burden that married men bear, or did the companions and congratulators come to him as the custom of people has been? And was it said to him, "May God bless you both, and be upon you both, and gather you both in goodness and well-being"? Or was it said, "May God curse the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil with a complete and comprehensive curse?"

[Section]

Then ask anyone who has even minimal knowledge of people's conditions: how many a chaste free woman has had the muhallil sink the claws of his desire into her, so that after the talaq she became one of the lovers of his, though her husband had been alone in having intercourse with her; and then he and the muhallil were partners in her, by the blessing of tahlil? By God's life, how many women has tahlil brought out from their veils into prostitution, and cast among the clutches of the lewd and the sly? Were it not for tahlil, reaching the Pleiades would be easier than reaching her, wrapping oneself in shrouds would be easier than wrapping oneself in her beauty, embracing spears would be easier than embracing her, and grasping the lion's arm would be easier than grasping her shin. And ask the people of experience: how many times has the muhallil contracted a marriage with a mother and her daughter? And how many times has he deposited his semen in the wombs of more than four women, or in the womb of two sisters? That is unlawful and void in both schools of thought. And this corruption, in the books on the corruptions of tahlil, should not be singled out for mention, for it is like one wave among the waves, and who can count the waves of the sea? And how many a woman was restrained in her gaze toward her husband, but when she tasted the muhallil's little honey (ʿusaylah, the brief sexual pleasure), she went out with her face uncovered, and the union of chastity and virtue did not reunite with her afterward. If this is its path, how could the most perfect and most wise of the laws permit its tahlil? So may God's blessings and peace be upon the one who explicitly cursed it and named it "the borrowed billy-goat" among the sinners of his Ummah, as bore witness to it Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, Jabir ibn Abdullah, Uqbah ibn Amir, and Abdullah ibn Abbas. And Abdullah ibn Umar reported that they used to count it as fornication (sifah) during the time of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

As for Ibn Mas'ud, in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, the Sunan of al-Nasa'i and the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from him: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." Al-Tirmidhi said: "A hadith hasan sahih (good and sound)." Sufyan al-Thawri said: Abu Qays al-Awdi narrated to me from Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) cursed the woman who tattoos and the one who gets tattooed, the woman who joins hair and the one whose hair is joined, the muhallil and the muhallal lahu, and the one who consumes riba (usury) and the one who pays it."

And it was related by al-Nasa'i and Imam Ahmad. Al-Tirmidhi related from him (Ibn Mas'ud) "He cursed the muhallil (the one who effects a legal marriage of convenience)," and declared it sound. Then he said: "And the practice according to the people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ is upon it, among them 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan and 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, and it is the view of the jurists among the Successors (tabi'un)." Imam Ahmad related it from the hadith of Abu al-Wasil, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ: "He cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu (the one for whom it is done)." In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and in al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from al-Harith, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, its two witnesses and its scribe when they know of it, the one who makes the connecting hair (al-wasila) and the one who has a tattoo made (al-mustawshima), the one who withholds zakat and the one who transgresses in it, and the one who reverts to his heels as a bedouin after his migration (hijra), are cursed upon the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ on the Day of Resurrection."

As for the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, it is in the Musnad, the Sunan of Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of al-Sha'bi, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, from the Prophet ﷺ: "that he cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu."

As for the hadith of Abu Hurayra, it is in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and the Musnad of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, from the hadith of 'Uthman ibn al-Akhnasi, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah has cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." Yahya ibn Ma'in said: 'Uthman ibn al-Akhnasi is trustworthy (thiqa), and the one who related from him, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Makhrami, is trustworthy, one of the men of Muslim; Ahmad, Yahya, 'Ali and others declared him trustworthy. So the chain is sound (jayyid). In the Kitab al-'Ilal of al-Tirmidhi: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, Mu'alla ibn Mansur narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Makhrami, from 'Uthman ibn Muhammad al-Akhnasi, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." Al-Tirmidhi said: I asked Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari about this hadith, and he said: It is a hasan hadith; 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Makhrami is saduq (truthful), and 'Uthman ibn Muhammad al-Akhnasi is thiqa, and I used to think that 'Uthman had not heard from Sa'id al-Maqburi. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya said: This is a sound chain (isnad jayyid).

As for the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, it is in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." Mujalid, although others are stronger than him, his hadith serves as a supporting witness (shahid) and a strengthener (muqawwin).

As for the hadith of 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, it is in the Sunan of Ibn Majah from him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the borrowed ram (al-tays al-musta'ar)?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "It is the muhallil. Allah has cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." It was related by al-Hakim in his Sahih from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from Mishrah ibn Ha'an, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, and he mentioned it. This hadith has been criticized on three grounds (ilal). The first: Abu Hatim al-Busti declared Mishrah ibn Ha'an weak.

The second ground is what al-Tirmidhi reported in the Kitab al-'Ilal from al-Bukhari, who said: I asked Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari about the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Salih: al-Layth narrated to me, from Mishrah ibn Ha'an, from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the borrowed ram? It is the muhallil and the muhallal lahu, and Allah has cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." He said: 'Abdullah ibn Salih did not narrate it in our days; I do not think al-Layth heard it from Mishrah ibn Ha'an, because Hayawa narrates from Bakr ibn 'Amr from Mishrah.

The third ground is what al-Jozjani mentioned in his biography (of him), saying: They used to denounce this hadith of 'Uthman with severe denunciation. As for the first ground, Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maqdisi said: Mishrah was declared trustworthy by Yahya ibn Ma'in in the narration of 'Uthman ibn Sa'id, and Ibn Ma'in is more knowledgeable about the narrators than Ibn Hibban. I say: He is saduq (truthful) according to the memorizers (huffaz); no one ever accused him at all, nor did any of the people of hadith ever describe him as weak, and Ibn Hibban did not declare him weak. It is only said: he narrated from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir strange reports (manakir) that were not followed; so the correct position is to leave what he alone transmitted, and Ibn Hibban alone among the people of hadith held this view about him. As for the second ground, 'Abdullah ibn Salih has explicitly stated that he heard it from al-Layth, and his not having narrated it at the time when al-Bukhari met him does not harm it in any way. As for his statement, "Hayawa narrates from Bakr ibn 'Amr ibn Shurayh al-Misri from Mishrah," he means that Hayawa was a contemporary of al-Layth or older than him, and he narrated only from Bakr ibn 'Amr from Mishrah. This is a strong ground, and it is reinforced by the fact that al-Layth said "Mishrah said" and did not say "he narrated to us," though this is not necessarily binding; for al-Layth was a contemporary of Mishrah and was in his city, and al-Layth's seeking of knowledge and his collecting it did not prevent him from not hearing Mishrah's hadith from 'Uqba ibn 'Amir while he was with him in the city. As for the third ground, Shaykh al-Islam said: The denunciation of those who denounced this hadith against 'Uthman is not sound; it is only from assuming that he alone transmitted it from al-Layth, and they thought he might have erred in it since it did not reach them from other companions of al-Layth. Just as some who write hadith suppose that when a hadith is transmitted alone from a man who is not among the well-known of his companions, that is an irregularity (shudhudh) in it and a damaging defect ('illa qadiha), and this does not apply here for two reasons. The first: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, followed him in it, and we related it from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Qati'i, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, al-Abbas known as Abu Fari'q narrated to me, Abu Salih narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to me with it, and he mentioned it. Al-Daraqutni also related it in his Sunan: Abu Bakr al-Shafi'i narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Haytham informed us, Abu Salih informed us, and he mentioned it. The second: this 'Uthman ibn Salih al-Misri himself was narrated from by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, and Ibn Ma'in and Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated from him, and Abu Hatim said: He is a righteous shaykh, sound in transmission. It was said to him: Did he used to receive instruction (yulaqqin)? He said: No. Whoever is in this position, what he alone transmits is an proof; the irregular (shadhdh) is only what he contradicts the trustworthy (thiqat) in, not what he alone transmits from them. So how much more so when Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth and the one who narrated the most hadith from him, follows him in it? He is also trustworthy, although some error occurred in some of his hadith. And Mishrah ibn Ha'an, Ibn Ma'in said of him: thiqa, and Imam Ahmad said of him: he is well known. Thus it is established that this hadith is a good hadith and its chain is hasan. End of quotation."

Al-Shafi'i said: Irregularity (shudhudh) is not that a trustworthy narrator alone transmits a hadith from people; rather, irregularity is that he contradicts what the trustworthy have related.

As for the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Majah related it in his Sunan from him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu." In its chain is Zam'a ibn Salih, whom some have declared weak and others have declared trustworthy. Muslim related from him in his Sahih in conjunction with another (narrator), and there are two reports from Ibn Ma'in concerning him.

As for the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, it is in the Sahih of al-Hakim, from the hadith of Ibn Abi Maryam, who narrated to us from Abu Ghassan, from 'Amr ibn Nafi', from his father, who said: "A man came to Ibn 'Umar and asked him about a man who divorced his wife three times, and then his brother married her without prior arrangement between them, in order to make her lawful to his brother. Is she lawful to the first (husband)? He said: No, unless it is a marriage of desire (nikah raghba). We used to count this as adultery (sifah) in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said: It is sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not include it. Sa'id said in his Sunan: Muhammad ibn Nashit al-Basri narrated to us, who said: Bakr ibn 'Abdullah al-Muzani said: The muhallil and the muhallal lahu were cursed, and he (the muhallil) used to be called in the Jahiliyya "the borrowed ram." And from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: The Muslims used to say: "This is the borrowed ram."

(Section)

Ask this ram: Does he fall under the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from yourselves that you may find tranquility in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [al-Rum: 21]? And does he fall under the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous among your male and female servants; if they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾ [al-Nur: 32]? And does he fall under the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever among you is able to marry (al-ba'a), let him marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity"? And does he fall under the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Marry the loving and the fertile, for I shall boast of you among the nations on the Day of Resurrection"? And does he fall under the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Four things are from the sunan of the messengers: marriage, perfume, circumcision," and he mentioned the fourth? And does he fall under the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Marriage is my sunna; whoever turns away from my sunna is not of me"? And does he fall under the words of Ibn 'Abbas: "The best of this ummah is the one with the most wives"? And does he have a share in the words of the Prophet ﷺ: "Three are a right upon Allah to help them: the one who marries seeking chastity, and the mukatab who seeks to pay (his freedom), and he mentioned the third," or is it a right upon Allah to curse him, confirming His Messenger in what he reported about him?

And ask him: Do Allah and His Messenger curse one who does something recommended, permissible, disliked, or a minor sin, or is His curse specific to one who commits a major sin or something greater than that? As Ibn 'Abbas said: Every sin that is concluded with a curse, or wrath, or punishment, or fire, is a major sin.

And ask him: Was there among the Companions a single muhallil, or did any man among them approve of tahlil? And ask him: for what reason did 'Umar ibn al-Khattab say: "I will not be brought a muhallil or a muhallal lahu except that I will stone them both"?

And ask him: How is temporary marriage (mut'a) forbidden by explicit text, although the one who contracts it has a purpose in marrying the woman for a period of time? But since it does not fall under permanent marriage, he is one who commits what is forbidden. Then how is the marriage of the muhallil, whose only intention is that he keeps her for an hour of time or less, with no purpose whatsoever in marriage, and who has even stipulated its termination and cessation once he makes her lawful by tahlil? How can the ruling permitting this tahlil and the prohibition of mut'a come together in intellect or in the Sharia? Moreover, mut'a was permitted at the beginning of Islam, and the Companions practiced it, and some of them issued fatwas permitting it after the death of the Prophet ﷺ, whereas the marriage of the muhallil has not been permitted in any religion of any kind at all, and none of the Companions practiced it, nor did any one of them issue a fatwa permitting it. The aim is not to explain the prohibition of this contract and its invalidity, nor to mention its harms and evil, for that would require a large volume, and we shall be brief; rather, the purpose is that this is the status of tahlil before Allah, His Messenger, and the Companions of His Messenger. 'Umar therefore obliged them to (the consequences of) three divorces when they pronounced them together, so that they would refrain from it, when they knew that the woman becomes forbidden by it and that there is no way to return to her through tahlil. But when the times changed, the age of the Sunna and the traces of the earlier people became distant, and the market of tahlil was established and flourished among the people, then it is obligatory that the matter be returned to what it was in the time of the Prophet ﷺ and his successor, by issuing rulings that would stop the market of tahlil or reduce it and lessen its evil. And if the question is put to one whom Allah has granted success, enlightened with guidance and given understanding in his religion, regarding whether three (divorces) count as one and the question of tahlil, and he weighs the two together, the difference will become clear to him, and it will be known which of the two questions is more fitting for the religion and more beneficial for the Muslims.

So these are the proofs of the two questions that have been presented to you, and they have been offered to you, if you accept them. I do not think that blindness of taqlid (imitation) will do anything but increase the matter beyond what it is, nor will it leave success to guide you by choice to it. We have only indicated the two questions by a hint that informs the scholar of what lies behind them. And success is from Allah.

Section.

It has thus become clear to you the matter of one of the issues that prevent tahlil (the marriage contrived to make a divorced woman lawful to her former husband). A mufti issued a ruling on it, and some of the scholars have held it; it is better than tahlil. Even if the mufti were to rule its permissibility merely by the contract without consummation, the one doing so would be more excusable before Allah than the practitioners of tahlil, although each of them shares in opposing the text. For the texts prohibiting tahlil and explicitly cursing its perpetrator are very numerous, and the Companions and the early generations (al-salaf) are unanimous upon them, whereas the texts stipulating consummation (al-dukhul) do not reach their level, and the Successors (al-tabi'un) differed concerning them. Therefore, opposing them is easier than opposing the hadiths on tahlil. The truth is to agree with all the texts and to leave none of them aside.

Consider how the matter stood in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and in the time of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, that three (pronouncements of divorce) counted as one, while tahlil was forbidden. Then, in the remaining part of the caliphate of Umar, three became three, while tahlil remained forbidden. Umar was among the strictest of the Companions regarding it, and all of them held the same view as his concerning it. Then, in these times, tahlil has become widespread and well known, and three (pronouncements) count as three.

On this basis, it is impermissible in these times to punish people with what Umar punished them with, for two reasons. The first: most of them do not know that combining the three is forbidden, especially since many jurists do not consider it forbidden. How then is one punished who has not committed what is forbidden in his own view? The second: punishing them for this opens for them the door of tahlil, which was closed in the time of the Companions. When a punishment entails a corruption greater than the act being punished, leaving it is more beloved to Allah and His Messenger. Even if we suppose that tahlil were among what the Sharia permits, and Allah forbid, prohibiting it once it reaches this extent, whose ugliness has become flagrant, falls under blocking the means (sadd al-dhara'i'). It becomes incumbent upon the muftis and judges to prohibit it entirely, even if it is supposed that some of its instances are permissible. For no one doubts that returning to what the Companions were upon in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and the early part of Umar's caliphate is better than returning to tahlil. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 230 (part 1 of 2):

He said, regarding the woman divorced three times: ﴿So if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him after that until she marries a husband other than him. Then if he divorces her, there is no blame on the two of them for returning to each other, if they think they can keep within the limits of Allah﴾. That is, if the second husband divorces her, there is no blame on her or on the first husband for returning to each other. What is meant is renewing the contract (ʿaqd). This is not restricted to the case in which only the second husband divorces her. Rather, whenever the two separate by death, khul' (divorce initiated by the wife with compensation), faskh (annulment), or divorce, she becomes lawful to the first husband, by analogy with divorce.
