From this is the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "Do not eat from vessels of gold and silver, nor drink from their dishes, for they are theirs in this world and yours in the Hereafter."

And his saying: "The one who drinks from vessels of gold and silver is only swallowing the fire of Hell into his belly."

This prohibition is not restricted to eating and drinking. Rather, it covers all forms of use. So it is not lawful for him to bathe with them, to perform ablution with them, to anoint himself with oil from them, or to apply kohl from them. No scholar doubts this matter.

[Section: The wisdom behind the prohibition of the woman after three divorces]

As for the prohibition on the woman for the husband after three divorces, and her being permitted to him after she marries a second husband, none knows its wisdom except one who has knowledge of the secrets of the Shariah (divine law) and the general wisdoms and benefits it contains. So we say, and success is from Allah: Since permitting a man access to a woman's private part after it had been forbidden to him and withheld from him is one of the greatest blessings of Allah upon him and His favor to him, he is deserving of thanking this blessing, guarding it, fulfilling its rights, and not exposing it to loss. The Shariahs varied in this according to the benefits that Allah knew in each era and for each nation. The Shariah of the Torah came permitting him to return to her after divorce as long as she had not married. If she married, she became forbidden to him, and he had no way to her.

In this there is wisdom and benefit that is not hidden. For when the husband knows that if he divorces the woman, her affair is in her own hands, that she may marry someone else, and that if she marries someone else she becomes forbidden to him forever, his holding on to her becomes firmer and his caution against separating from her becomes greater. The Shariah of the Torah came in accordance with the Mosaic nation, and among them was the severity and burden that suited their condition. Then the Shariah of the Gospel came prohibiting divorce after marriage entirely. So if he marries a woman, he has no right to divorce her. Then came the complete, virtuous Muhammadan Shariah, which is the most perfect Shariah ever sent down from heaven in absolute terms, the most sublime, most excellent, highest, and most upright in serving the benefit of the servants in this life and the next, in the best and most complete form and the most suited to reason and benefit. For Allah, glory be to Him, perfected this religion for this nation, completed His blessing upon it, and permitted it of the good things what He did not permit to any other nation. He permitted a man to marry four of the finest women and to take concubines as he wishes, and there is no concubinage in any other Shariah besides this one. Then He perfected His law for His servant and completed His blessing upon him by granting him the right to separate from his wife and take another, since perhaps the first may not be suitable or agreeable to him. He did not make her a yoke around his neck, a fetter on his foot, or a burden on his back. He legislated for him separating from her in the most complete manner for her and for him: he divorces her once, and then she waits three menstrual periods (qurū').

Generally, this is three months. If his soul yearns for her, if he has desire for her, and the Turner of hearts (Allah) turns his heart toward loving her, he finds the way to returning to her possible and the door open. So he returns to his beloved and faces his matter, and what the hand of anger and the stirrings of Satan had removed returns to his hand. He cannot be safe from the overpowering of natures and the stirrings of Satan regarding repetition, so he is enabled to do this a second time. Perhaps she will taste the bitterness of divorce and the ruin of the home, which will prevent her from repeating what angers him, and he will taste the pain of separating from her, which will prevent him from hastening to divorce. When the third time comes, there comes the matter of Allah that cannot be averted, and it is said to him: "Your need has been met by the first and second times, and after the third you have no path to her." When he knows that the third is a final separation between him and her, and that it is the decisive one, he refrains from pronouncing it. For when he knows that after the third she is not lawful to him except after waiting three menstrual periods and marrying a husband who desires to marry and keep her, and that the first husband has no path to her until the second husband consummates with her a complete consummation in which each of them tastes the other's honey (ʿusaylah), in a way that prevents them from hastening separation, and then he separates from her by death, divorce, or khul', and then she observes a complete waiting period (ʿiddah) after that, his despair becomes clear to him at that time, through this divorce which is among the most hated of lawful things to Allah. Each of them knows that there is no path back after the third, neither by his choice nor by hers. This purpose is confirmed by cursing the second husband if he did not marry with a marriage of desire aiming at keeping her, but rather married with a marriage of tahlil (intermediary marriage), and by cursing the first husband if he takes her back through this marriage, and the second husband marries her just as the first married her, and divorces her just as the first divorced her. At that point she becomes lawful to the first husband just as she is lawful to other husbands.

If you compare this with the two abrogated Shariahs, and compare it with the altered Shariah that permits what Allah and His Messenger cursed its doer, the greatness of this Shariah, its majesty, and its supremacy over all other Shariahs will become clear to you. It came in the most perfect, complete, excellent, and beneficial forms for creation. The two abrogated Shariahs are better than the altered Shariah, for Allah, glory be to Him, legislated the two of them at a time, and He never legislated the altered one at all.

These subtleties and the like are among the matters Allah, glory be to Him, specially grants understanding of to whom He wills. Whoever reaches them should praise Allah, and whoever does not reach them should submit to the Wisest of the wise and the Most Knowing of the knowers.

Let him know that His Shariah is above the intellects of the intelligent, in accordance with the natures of the wise:

"Say to the inflamed eyes: do not advance
toward the sun, and go on embracing the darkness of nights."

"Be forgiving, do not condemn her, leave her alone,
and if she denies a truth, say: leave that for me."

Another poet said:

"Those who lack minds have criticized jurisprudence,
and it does not harm it if they criticize it."

"The shining sun is not harmed while it is rising
by the fact that one without sight does not see its light."

(Benefit)

As for legitimizing adultery under the name of marriage, it is adultery with a woman in whom he has no purpose of living with her or of her being his wife. His only aim is to satisfy his need from her, or to take a fee for committing fornication with her, and he reaches that through the name of marriage and displaying its outward form. Allah, His Messenger, the angels, the husband, and the woman all know that he is a muhallil (intermediary), not a real husband, and that he is not a spouse. He is merely a borrowed ram for mating, like the donkey of the Ushriyyin (a people of ill repute).

How strange, by Allah! What difference in reality is there between adultery and this? Yes, this is adultery witnessed by human beings, and that is adultery witnessed by the noble recording angels. As the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stated explicitly, they said: "They will remain two adulterers even if they stay for twenty years, if Allah knows that he only intends to make her lawful." The point is that when this muhallil is told, "This is adultery," he says, "It is not adultery, rather it is a marriage." Just as the usurer, when told, "This is riba (usury)," says, "Rather it is a sale." Likewise, everyone who makes a prohibited thing lawful by changing its name and form, like one who makes hashish lawful under the name "comfort delight," and makes musical instruments such as the tanbur, the ʿūd, and the barbat lawful under a name he gives them, and as some call the singer "the chanter," "the entertainer," or "the qawwal," and as some call the cuckold "the reformer," "the one granted success," or "the benefactor."

(Chapter)

Among the snares of Satan in which he attained his aim is the snare of tahlil, for which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed its doer, and he likened it to the borrowed ram. Because of it, shame and disgrace became great, and the disbelievers reproached the Muslims with it. Because of it corruption occurred that none can count except the Lord of the servants. Borrowed rams were rented out, souls were constrained, and they recoiled from it even more than they recoil from fornication, saying: "If this were a valid marriage, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not have cursed the one who brought what he legislated of marriage. Marriage is his Sunnah, and the doer of the Sunnah is brought near, not cursed. The muhallil, with the curse falling upon him, is linked with the borrowed ram." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named him the borrowed ram, and the predecessors named him the nail of fire. If you had seen the honorable free women, shamelessly displayed at the shops of the muhallilin, looking at the ram with the look of a sheep at the butcher's knife, and saying: "Would that I had been among the dead before this!" Until, when they agree on what brings the curse and hatred, he rises and makes her follow him immediately, without a wedding procession, without any announcement, but in secrecy and concealment. No trousseau is transported, no bedding is carried to the husband's house, no female companions escort her to him, no women adorn her for him, no mahr (dower) is paid or deferred, no maintenance or clothing is fixed, no feast or distribution of sweets, no drum announcing it, no signs of celebration. The husband pays the dower, while this ram mounts her for a fee. Then, when he is alone with her and the veil is drawn, while the divorcer and the guardian stand at the door, he approaches to purify her with his filthy unlawful fluid and to perfume her with the curse of Allah and His Messenger, may prayers and peace be upon him. Then, when they have completed the wedding of tahlil, and there has arisen between them no affection and mercy, which Allah mentioned in the revelation, for these are not produced by an explicit curse, and nothing brings them about except a valid, lawful marriage. If he has taken his payment for mating in advance and promptly, well; otherwise he detains her until she gives him his wages in full. Have you ever heard of a husband who does not seize the ram until he takes his wage after the condition and agreement? Then, when he has purified her and perfumed her, and freed her in his claim from the unlawful and kept her away from it, he says to her: "Confess what happened between us, so that the divorce falls upon you, and afterward reconciliation and agreement will take place between you." So the shameless woman comes into the presence of witnesses, and they ask her: "Did that happen?" She cannot deny it, so they take a payment from her or from the divorcer, and they have made their matter difficult for the two of them. Many of these hired rams for mating even make the mother and her daughter lawful within two contracts, and gather their fluid in more than four women and in the wombs of two sisters. When such is his nature and description, he deserves what Abdullah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, saying: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil."

Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (in his Sahih) and al-Tirmidhi, who said: "It is a hasan sahih hadith." He said: "And the practice is according to it among the people of knowledge, among them: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, and ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them. It is the view of the jurists among the Successors."

Imam Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, and al-Nasai in his Sunan, with a sahih chain, and their wording is: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the woman who tattoos and the one who has herself tattooed, the one who joins hair and the one for whom hair is joined, the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil, and the one who consumes riba and the one who pays it."

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad and the Sunan of al-Nasai also, from Abdullah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The one who consumes riba, the one who pays it, its witness, and its scribe, when they know it; the one who joins hair and the one who has hair joined; the one who collects charity and exceeds in it; the one who apostatizes after his migration becoming a bedouin; and the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil: they are cursed upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection."

And from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "he cursed the one for whom the muhallil is" (al-muhallal lahu). Narrated by Imam Ahmad and all the authors of the Sunan except al-Nasai.

And from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah curse the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil." Narrated by Imam Ahmad with a chain all of whose narrators are trustworthy (thiqat), whom Ibn Maʿin and others declared trustworthy.

Al-Tirmidhi said in his book al-ʿIlal: "I asked Abu ʿAbdullah Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bukhari about this hadith, and he said: 'It is a hasan hadith. ʿAbdullah ibn Jaʿfar al-Makhzumi is truthful and trustworthy, and ʿUthman ibn Muhammad al-Akhnasi is trustworthy.'"

Abu ʿAbdullah ibn Majah said in his Sunan: "Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Abu ʿAmir narrated to us, from Zamʿah ibn Salih, from Salamah ibn Wahram, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil.'"

And from Ibn ʿAbbas also, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the muhallil, and he said: 'No, except a marriage of desire. Not a marriage of deception, nor mockery of the Book of Allah, until she tastes the honey.'"

Narrated by Abu Ishaq al-Jawzjani in his book al-Mutarjam, who said: "Ibrahim ibn Ismaʿil ibn Abi Habibah narrated to me from Dawud ibn Husayn, from ʿIkrimah, from him." All of these are trustworthy except Ibrahim, for many of the hadith memorizers weaken him, while al-Shafiʿi held a good opinion of him and used his narrations as evidence.

And from ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 230 (part 2 of 2):

"Shall I not inform you of the borrowed ram?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "He is the muhallil (one who makes lawful by a temporary marriage). May Allah curse the muhallil and the muhallal lahu (the one for whom he is made lawful)."
Narrated by Ibn Majah with a chain whose narrators are all trustworthy, none of whom has been impugned.

And from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, who was among the foremost of the Successors: "He was asked about a man who divorced his wife, and then a man from the village came, without his knowledge or hers, and brought out some of his wealth and married her in order to make her lawful to him. He said: No. Then he mentioned that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about the like of this, and he said: 'No, until he marries with a desire for the marriage itself. If he does that, she is not lawful to him until he tastes her sweetness (al-ʿusaylah).'"
Narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf with a sound chain.

This mursal report was relied upon by the one who transmitted it, which indicates its authenticity in his view. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also acted upon it, as will come, and it agrees with the rest of the connected reports. Such a report is authoritative by the consensus of the Imams. This and the preceding one are explicit regarding the intended (mental) tahlil. Likewise is the report of Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "A man said to him: 'A woman I married, I intended to make her lawful to her husband, without his commanding me or his knowing?' He said: 'No. Only a marriage of desire: if you like her, keep her, and if you dislike her, leave her. We used to count this as prostitution (sifah) during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'" Mentioned by Shaykh al-Islam in Ibtal al-Tahlil.

(Section)
As for the reports from the Companions:
In al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah, the Sunan of al-Athram, and al-Awsat of Ibn al-Mundhir, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I will not be brought a muhallil or a muhallal lahu except that I will stone them both."
The wording of ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir: "I will not be brought a muhallil or a muhallal lahu except that I will stone them both." It is authentic from ʿUmar.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn al-Mughirah, who said: "Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, was asked about a woman being made lawful to her husband. He said: That is prostitution (al-sifah)." Ibn Abi Shaybah also narrated it.

ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: We were informed by al-Thawri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Shuraik al-ʿAmiri, who said: "I heard Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, being asked about a man who divorced his paternal cousin, then desired her and regretted it, and wanted a man to marry her to make her lawful to him. Ibn ʿUmar said: Both of them are fornicators, even if he remains twenty years or so, as long as Allah knows that he intends to make her lawful to him."

Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "May Allah curse the muhallil and the muhallal lahu."

al-Jawzajani narrated with a good chain from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "He was asked about a man who married a woman in order to make her lawful to her husband, and he said: May Allah curse the hall (one who makes lawful) and the muhallal lahu."

Shaykh al-Islam said: These reports from ʿUmar, ʿUthman, ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, and Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them all, although they are explicit regarding the case where the intent to make lawful is held but not declared, and there was no prior agreement on it, nevertheless they clarify that this is tahlil, and that this is the muhallil cursed upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are the most knowledgeable of his intent and purpose, especially when they transmit a hadith and interpret it in accordance with its apparent meaning. Moreover, it is not known that any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ distinguished between one tahlil and another, nor did they grant concession for any type of it, even though a woman who had been divorced thrice, like the wife of Rifaʿah al-Qurazi, used to go to him for a long period and to his successors so that she might return to her husband, and they would prevent her from that. Had tahlil been permissible, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have guided her to it, for she would not have lacked someone to make her lawful, if tahlil had been permissible.
He said: The evidences showing that these prophetic hadiths intended tahlil, even if it was not stipulated in the contract, are very many; this is not the place to mention them. End.

(Section)
Among the marvels is the opposition of these hadiths and the reports from the Companions to the verse: "And if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him thereafter until she marries another husband" (2:230).
The one to whom this verse was revealed is the one who cursed the muhallil and the muhallal lahu, and his Companions were the most knowledgeable people of the Book of Allah. They did not treat that (man) as a husband, and they annulled his marriage and cursed him.

More astonishing than this is the saying of some: "We argue that he named him 'muhallil,' so if he had not affirmed the lawfulness, he would not have been called a muhallil."
It is said: This is a grave matter, for this implies that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who did the Sunnah he brought and did what is permissible and valid in his law. Rather, he called him muhallil because he made lawful what Allah had made unlawful, and so he deserved the curse. Allah, glory be to Him, made her unlawful to the one who divorced her until she marries another husband. "Nikah" in the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger is the name for the marriage that people know among themselves, which is the one whose announcement was legislated, with the beating of tambourines, the wedding feast, and which was ordained for dwelling and tranquility, and which Allah made into affection and mercy. Its customs are the opposite of the customs of the muhallil's marriage: the muhallil does not enter upon maintenance, clothing, housing, or the giving of a dowry; no offspring or in-law relationship is established; nor does he intend to remain with the wife. Rather he enters as a borrowed one, like the borrowed ram for mating, and for this reason the Prophet ﷺ likened him to it and then cursed him. It is thus known with certainty, beyond doubt, that he is not the husband mentioned in the Qur'an, nor is his marriage the marriage mentioned in the Qur'an. Allah, glory be to Him, has created the hearts of people such that they know this is not a marriage, nor is the muhallil a husband, and that this is a repugnant, ugly thing by which the woman, the husband, the muhallil, and the guardian are shamed. How then can this enter into the marriage which Allah and His Messenger legislated, loved, and declared to be his Sunnah, and "whoever turns away from it is not of me"?

Consider His saying: "And if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them both if they return to one another" (2:230).
That is: if this second husband divorces her, there is no blame upon her and the first husband that they return to one another, i.e., she returns to him by a new contract. He used the particle "in" (if), which indicates that it is possible for him to divorce or to remain. The tahlil practiced by these people does not allow the husband either of the two; rather they stipulate upon him that whenever he has intercourse with her, she is divorced. Then, when they realized that he may not report having consummated and that her word regarding the occurrence of divorce would not be accepted, they shifted to making the condition the wife's report that he had entered upon her, so that by merely her report of that, she is divorced from him. Allah, glory be to Him, legislated marriage for lasting union and enjoyment, but these people made this marriage a cause for its termination and for the occurrence of divorce in it, for whenever he has intercourse, his intercourse becomes a cause for the ending of the marriage. This is the opposite of Allah's law.

Also: Allah, glory be to Him, made the second husband's marriage, divorce, and name like the first husband's marriage, divorce, and name. This is a husband, that is a husband; this is a marriage, that is a marriage; likewise divorce. It is known that the muhallil's marriage, divorce, and name do not resemble the first's marriage, divorce, or name. That one is a husband who desires, intends marriage, pays the dowry, and undertakes maintenance, housing, clothing, and the other characteristics of marriage, whereas the muhallil is free of all that and undertakes none of it.

If Allah and His Messenger forbade mut'ah marriage even though the husband's aim is enjoyment of the woman and remaining with her for a time while he is bound by the rights of marriage, then the muhallil, who has no purpose in remaining with the woman except as much as mounting her, like the borrowed ram for that purpose, and then parts from her, is more deserving of prohibition.

I heard Shaykh al-Islam say: Mut'ah marriage is better than tahlil marriage in ten respects:
First: mut'ah marriage was legislated at the beginning of Islam, whereas tahlil marriage was never legislated at any time.
Second: the Companions practiced mut'ah during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, and there was never a muhallil among the Companions at all.
Third: mut'ah was disputed among the Companions; Ibn ʿAbbas permitted it, though it is said he retracted, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud permitted it. In the two Sahihs, from him, he said: "We used to go on campaign with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we had no women, so we said: Shall we not castrate ourselves? He forbade us from that, then he permitted us to marry a woman with a garment for a fixed term." Then ʿAbd Allah recited: "O you who believe, do not forbid the good things Allah has made lawful for you" (5:87). And Ibn ʿAbbas's fatwa permitting it is well known.
ʿUrwah said: "ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr stood up in Mecca and said: Some people whose hearts Allah has blinded as He has blinded their eyes issue fatwas permitting mut'ah, alluding to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas. Ibn ʿAbbas called out to him, saying: You are a coarse, rude man. By my life, mut'ah was practiced during the time of the Imam of the pious, meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ibn al-Zubayr said to him: Then try it yourself; by Allah, if you do it I will stone you with your stones."
This is the statement of Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas regarding mut'ah, while that is their statement and transmission regarding tahlil marriage.
Fourth: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not transmit from him a single letter cursing the one who does mut'ah and the woman with whom it is done, whereas there is transmission from him cursing the muhallil and the muhallal lahu, and from the Companions what has already been mentioned.
Fifth: the one who does mut'ah has a valid purpose regarding the woman, and she has a purpose in remaining with him for the duration of the marriage. His purpose is the intended aim of marriage for a period, whereas the muhallil has no purpose except that he is borrowed for mating like the ram. His marriage is not intended by him, nor by the woman, nor by the guardian, and it is, as al-Hasan said, "a fire nail in the boundaries of Allah." This naming matches the meaning.
Shaykh al-Islam said: al-Hasan means that the nail is what fastens the thing nailed; likewise this one fastens that woman to her husband, though Allah has forbidden her to him.
Sixth: the one who does mut'ah did not scheme to make lawful what Allah forbade, so he is not among the deceivers who deceive Allah as if they were deceiving children; rather he is a marrier outwardly and inwardly. The muhallil is a cunning deceiver, taking the signs of Allah in mockery. For this reason, the threat and curse against him came in a way not found in the threat against the one who does mut'ah, nor anything close to it.
Seventh: the one who does mut'ah wants the woman for himself, and this is the essence and purpose of marriage. He intends by his marriage to make her lawful to himself, and he does not have intercourse with her unlawfully. The muhallil does not want her lawful for himself, but wants her lawful for another, and for this reason he is called muhallil. How far is one who desires to make lawful for himself intercourse with a woman, lest he have intercourse unlawfully, from one who does not desire that, but intends by marrying her to make her intercourse lawful for another? This is the opposite of Allah's law and religion, and the opposite of what marriage was instituted for.
Eighth: sound natures and hearts not afflicted by the disease of ignorance and blind imitation recoil from tahlil far more intensely, and reproach it most severely, to the extent that many women reproach a woman with it more than they reproach her with fornication. Mut'ah marriage is not repugnant to natures and minds, and had it been repugnant, it would not have been permitted at the beginning of Islam.
Ninth: mut'ah resembles renting a riding animal for a period, renting a house for a period of use and dwelling, renting a servant for service for a period, and similar things in which the one who pays has a valid purpose. But when it admitted a time limit, it removed it from the intended aim of marriage, which was legislated with the attribute of permanence and continuity. This differs from the marriage of the muhallil, which resembles none of that. For this reason the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, likened it to fornication, and likened it to borrowing a ram for mating.
Tenth: Allah, glory be to Him, established these causes, such as sale and rent, gift and marriage, as leading to rulings which He made their effects and consequences. He made sale a cause for ownership of the thing itself, rent a cause for ownership of the usufruct or its use, and marriage a cause for ownership of the sexual organ and the lawfulness of intercourse. The muhallil is contrary and opposed to the law and religion of Allah, for he made his marriage a cause for making the divorced woman's sexual organ owned by and made lawful to the first husband, yet he did not intend by marriage what Allah legislated for him of ownership of the sexual organ and its lawfulness for him, nor does he have any purpose in that, nor does he enter upon it. He intended instead another matter for which that cause was not legislated and was not made a path.
Eleventh: the muhallil is of the kind of the hypocrite. The hypocrite outwardly shows that he is a Muslim committed to the contract of Islam outwardly and inwardly, while inwardly he is not committed to it. Likewise the muhallil shows that he is a husband, that he desires marriage, names the dowry, and calls witnesses to the woman's consent, while inwardly it is otherwise: he does not want to be a husband, nor for the woman to be his wife, nor does he want to pay the dowry or discharge the rights of marriage; he has shown the opposite of what he conceals, and that he desires that. Allah knows, and so do those present, the woman, he, and the divorcer, that the matter is so, and that he is not a husband in reality, nor is she his wife in reality.
Twelfth: the marriage of the muhallil does not resemble the marriage of the people of Jahiliyyah, nor the marriage of the people of Islam. The people of Jahiliyyah practiced in their marriages abominable matters, but they did not accept tahlil marriage, nor did they practice it. In the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, that ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, informed him: "The marriage in Jahiliyyah was in four forms. One was the marriage of people today: a man proposes to another man for his ward or daughter, gives her dowry, and then marries her. Another: a man would say to his wife when she became clean from her menses: Send to so-and-so and seek his seed. Her husband would then withdraw from her and not touch her at all, until her pregnancy became evident from that man whose seed she sought. When her pregnancy became evident, her husband would have intercourse with her if he wished. He did this out of desire for noble offspring; this marriage was called the marriage of seeking seed. Another: a group fewer than ten would gather and enter upon a woman, all of them having intercourse with her. When she became pregnant and gave birth, and some nights passed after her delivery, she would send to them, and none of them could refuse until they gathered at her place. She would say to them: You know what your matter was, and I have given birth, so this is your son, O so-and-so, naming whomever she loved, and the child would be attributed to him, and he could not refuse. A fourth: many people would gather and enter upon a woman, and she would not refuse whoever came to her; these were prostitutes who set up banners at their doors as signs, so whoever wanted them entered. When one of them became pregnant and gave birth, they gathered for her and summoned the physiognomists, then attributed her child to whomever they thought, and he was called by his name and could not refuse it." When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ with the truth, he demolished all the marriages of Jahiliyyah except the marriage of the people of today.
It is known that the marriage of the muhallil is not of the marriage of the people which ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, indicated, which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ approved and did not demolish. Nor did the people of Jahiliyyah accept it, so it was not among their marriages, for human nature and nations reject it and reproach it.

**(Useful Point)**

Some people may think that the waiting period (*iddah*) of a widow is four months and ten nights, so that once the dawn of the tenth night has risen, the *iddah* is over.

The author of *al-Tanbih* wrote: "And if she is a slave-woman, she observes a waiting period of two months and five nights." This error is reinforced by the omission of the *ta'* (feminine ending) from *al-'ashr* (ten), since the *ta'* is only dropped with masculine nouns, as in *sab' layal wa-thamaniyat ayyam* (seven nights and eight days).

The answer to this is that when the counted noun is mentioned together with its number, the rule is as stated: the *ta'* is dropped with feminine nouns and retained with masculine nouns. When the number is mentioned without its masculine counted noun, both forms are permissible, with or without the *ta'*. This is related by al-Farra' (Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra'), Ibn al-Sikkit and others. On this basis the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six [days] of Shawwal," and he did not say *bi-sittah*. Likewise is the Qur'anic statement ﴿They will whisper among themselves, "You stayed only ten [days]."﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:103], where what is meant is days, as indicated by what follows it.

Accordingly, the *iddah* is not completed until the sun sets on the tenth day. What occurred in *al-Tanbih* is an error, and Allah knows best. He made this same mistake in the chapter on numbers and in the chapter on *istibra'* (the period to ascertain that a womb is clear).

**[Section: The wisdom behind a woman's mourning for her husband being more than her mourning for her father]**

As for his statement: "[The Law] prohibits a woman from mourning her mother and father for more than three days, yet it requires her to mourn her husband for four months and ten [days], and he is a non-relative," it is said: this is among the perfections of the beauties, wisdom and care of this Sharia for the interests of the servants in the most complete manner. Mourning the dead is a way of magnifying the calamity of death, which the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) exaggerated to the utmost extent. They added to it tearing their collars, slapping their cheeks, shaving their hair, and calling out for destruction and perdition. A woman would remain for a full year in the narrowest and most desolate room, not touching perfume, not anointing herself, not bathing, and other such things, all of which are expressions of discontent with the Lord, the Exalted, and His decrees. Allah, glorified is He, in His mercy and compassion, abolished the custom of the Jahiliyyah and replaced it with patience, praise, and *istirja'* (saying "Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we return"), which is more beneficial to the afflicted in this world and the next.

Since the calamity of death necessarily produces in the afflicted person distress, pain and grief, as human nature demands, the Wise, the All-Aware permitted a small measure of that, namely three days, in which she finds some relief and fulfils a need of her grief. This is like the permission given to the emigrant to remain in Makkah for three days after completing his rites. Whatever exceeds three days has a predominant harm, so it is prohibited. The harm of the three days, by contrast, is outweighed and overshadowed by its benefit. Weaning souls completely from what they are accustomed to is among the hardest things for them, so they are given a part of it, to make it easier for them to leave the rest. When the soul has taken a portion of what it desires, it is content with it, and when it is then asked to leave the remainder, its acceptance is closer than it would be if it were forbidden entirely.

Whoever reflects on the secrets of the Sharia and ponders its rulings will see this clearly on the surface of its commands and prohibitions, evident to whoever looks with a penetrating gaze. When it forbids them something, it compensates them with what is better and more beneficial for them. It permits them of it what their need calls for, to make it easier for them to abandon it. Thus it forbade them to sell fresh dates for dried dates, and permitted them *al-'araya* (a specific arrangement permitting the sale of fresh dates on the palm for dried dates). It forbade them to look at a non-mahram woman, and permitted them to look at a prospective spouse, a business partner, and a physician. It forbade them to consume wealth through false gambling such as backgammon and chess and the like, and permitted them to consume wealth through beneficial contests such as racing and archery. It forbade them to wear silk, and permitted them a small amount of it where need calls for it. It forbade them to earn wealth through *riba al-nasi'a* (usury through deferred exchange), and permitted them to earn it through *salam* (advance sale). It forbade them to have intercourse with their wives during fasting, and compensated them by permitting it at night, making it easier for them to abstain during the day. It forbade them fornication and compensated them by permitting them to take a second, third and fourth wife, and as many slave-women as they wished, making it extremely easy for them to abstain from it. It forbade them *al-istiqsam bi-l-azlam* (seeking decisions by arrows of divination), and compensated them with *istikhara* (the prayer seeking guidance) and its supplication, and how far apart these two are! It forbade them to marry their close relatives, and permitted them the daughters of paternal and maternal uncles and aunts. It forbade them intercourse with a menstruating woman, and allowed them to be intimate with her and to do everything with her except intercourse, making it extremely easy for them to abstain from it. It forbade them lying, and permitted them *al-ma'arid* (allusive speech) which, by its customary usage, does not require lying at all. The Prophet (ﷺ) pointed to this when he said: "Indeed in allusions there is a sufficient alternative to lying." It forbade them arrogance in word and deed, and permitted it to them in war, because of its predominant benefit that is consistent with the aim of jihad. It forbade them every animal with fangs among the beasts of prey and every bird with talons, and compensated them with all kinds of wild animals and birds of their various species and types. In summary, He did not forbid them anything foul or harmful without permitting them something good in its place that is more beneficial for them. Nor did He command them with any command without helping them to fulfil it. His mercy encompassed them, and His obligation was within their capacity.

The point is that He permitted women, because of the weakness of their intellects and their scant patience, to mourn their dead for three days. As for mourning a husband, it follows the *iddah* and is one of its requirements and complements. A woman only needs to adorn herself, beautify herself, and perfume herself so that she may be beloved to her husband, so that he desires her, and so that the companionship between them may be good. When the husband dies and she observes the *iddah* for him, while she has not yet reached another husband, what is required is the full completion of the first husband's right and the strengthening of the prohibition on a second husband before the Book reaches its term. Therefore she is prevented from what women do for their husbands. Furthermore, this blocks the means that lead to her desire for men and their desire for her through adornment, dyeing and perfuming. When the Book reaches its term, she becomes in need of what attracts a man to marry her, so she is permitted what is permitted to a woman who has a husband. There is nothing more eloquent in beauty than this combination of prohibition and permission. Even if the intellects of all the worlds were to propose something, they would not propose anything better than this.

**[Section: The wisdom behind the difference in the *iddah* between death and divorce]**

As for his distinguishing, in the *iddah*, between death and divorce, between the *iddah* of a free woman and that of a slave-woman, and between *istibra'* and *iddah*, even though the purpose in all of this is to know that the womb is clear, the reason for this only becomes clear when one knows the wisdom for which the *iddah* was prescribed and knows the kinds and types of waiting periods.

As for the first point, there are several wisdoms in prescribing the *iddah*. Among them is knowing that the womb is clear, and that the water of two or more men does not mingle in one womb, so that lineages would become mixed and corrupted. There is in that such corruption as the Sharia and wisdom forbid.

Among them is the magnifying of the weight of this contract, the raising of its status, and the showing of its nobility.

Among them is the lengthening of the period for reconciliation with a divorced woman, since he may repent and return, and thus come upon a time when he can reconcile.

Among them is the fulfilment of the husband's right and the demonstration of the effect of his loss in preventing adornment and beautification. For this reason the Law prescribed mourning for him more than mourning for a father or child.

Among them is the safeguarding of the husband's right, the woman's interest, the child's right, and the discharge of the right of Allah which He has made obligatory. In the *iddah* there are four rights. The Lawgiver has made death equivalent to consummation in securing what was contracted, since the marriage contract has as its duration a lifetime. For this reason it is treated as consummation in completing the dowry and in the prohibition of a stepdaughter (*rabiba*) according to a group of the Companions and those after them, as is the position of Zayd ibn Thabit and of one of the two narrations from Ahmad. So the purpose of the *iddah* is not merely the clearing of the womb; rather that is one of its aims and wisdoms.

The second point concerns its kinds. They are four in the Book of Allah and a fifth in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

The first kind is the mother of all waiting periods: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth to their burden﴾ [al-Talaq 65:4].

The second: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, [the wives] shall wait for four months and ten [days]﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:234].

The third: ﴿Divorced women shall wait for three menstrual periods﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:228].

The fourth: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have doubt, their waiting period is three months﴾ [al-Talaq 65:4].

The fifth is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "A pregnant woman is not to be had sexual relations with until she gives birth, and a non-pregnant woman is not to be had sexual relations with until she has undergone one menstrual cycle [to ensure her womb is clear]."

The foremost of all these kinds, the one that governs all of them, is the delivery of the child. When it occurs, the ruling is for it, and no attention is paid to anything else. There was a dispute among the early scholars regarding a widow: whether she waits for the longer of the two terms. Then agreement was reached that the waiting period ends with the delivery of the child.

As for the *iddah* of death, it is obligatory by death itself, whether or not the husband consummated the marriage with her, as the general meaning of the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah and the consensus of the people indicate. Since death is the termination and conclusion of the contract, rulings become settled by it: inheritance, the entitlement to the dowry, and so on. The purpose of the *iddah* here is not merely the clearing of the womb, as some jurists have supposed. This is shown by its being obligatory before consummation, by the clearing being achieved with a single menstrual cycle, and by the equal treatment of a young girl, a woman past menstruation, and a woman who menstruates in respect of its duration. Given that this is the case, one group said: it is purely an act of worship whose meaning cannot be understood. This is false for several reasons.

Among them: there is no ruling in the Sharia that does not have a meaning and wisdom, which whoever understands grasps, and which remains hidden from whoever it is hidden from.

Among them: waiting periods are not among purely ritual acts of worship, for they are obligatory for a young girl and an adult woman, for a sane woman and an insane woman, for a Muslim woman and a *dhimmi* woman, and they do not require an intention.

Among them: the protection of the rights of the spouses, the child, and the second husband is clearly evident in them. Therefore the correct position is that it is a protection of the sanctity of the contract after it has been completed. For this reason you find in it the observance of the husband's right and the sanctity owed to him. Do you not see that it was part of the Prophet's (ﷺ) respect and observance of his rights that his wives were forbidden to anyone after him? Since his wives in this world are definitely his wives in the Hereafter, no one was permitted to marry them after him. This is not the case with others, since this is not known in their regard. Had a woman been forbidden to others, she would have been harmed with certain harm and without any known benefit. But if she remains widowed for the sake of her children, she is praiseworthy for doing so.

In the Jahiliyyah they exaggerated greatly in respecting the husband's right and in magnifying the sanctity of this contract, to the utmost degree: a year's waiting in the worst of her clothes and in the most squalid of her homes. Allah lightened this for them through His Sharia, which He made a mercy, a wisdom, a benefit and a blessing. Indeed it is among the greatest of His blessings upon them without qualification. So to Him belongs praise, as He is worthy of it.

Four months and ten [days] accorded with wisdom and benefit, since a fixed period must exist, and the most suitable of periods for this is the period in which one knows whether a child exists or not. For the embryo is forty days a drop (*nutfah*), then forty days a clot (*'alaqah*), then forty days a lump of flesh (*mudghah*). These make four months. Then the spirit is breathed into it in the fourth stage. Therefore ten days were set so that its life might become apparent through movement, if there is a pregnancy.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 235:

When Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned allusion (ta'rid) to a woman in marriage proposals, which indicates that the one making the allusion has desire for her and love for her, and that this drives him to speech by which he may reach marriage with her, He lifted the blame (junah) from allusion, and from the heart's inclination to what it contains of leaning and love, and He negated secret promises (mu'adah sirran) to them.

It has been said: this refers to marriage (nikah). The meaning is: do not state to them outright the marriage contract, except that you allude to it with allusion. This is the well-known view.

It has also been said: it means that he marries her secretly during her waiting period ('iddah). Then when the 'iddah ends, he makes the contract public. This is supported by His words: ﴿and do not resolve upon the tie of marriage until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾, which is the end of the 'iddah. Those who prefer the first view say: the verse indicates the permissibility of allusion by negating blame, the prohibition of explicit speech by the prohibition of secret promises, and the prohibition of concluding the marriage contract before the 'iddah ends. If the meaning of "secret promise" were the secret conclusion of the contract, it would be repetition.

Then He followed that with His words: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him﴾, that you transgress what has been set as a limit for you, for He is aware of what you conceal and what you disclose.

Then He said: ﴿And know that Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾. Were it not for His forgiveness and forbearance, you would have suffered extreme hardship. He, glory be to Him, is aware of you, knows what is in your hearts, and knows what you do. If you fall into something He has forbidden, then hasten to it with repentance and seeking forgiveness, for He is the Forgiving, the Forbearing.

(Section: The Station of Muraqabah)

Among the stations (manazil) of ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ is the station of muraqabah (vigilant awareness of God).

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And know that Allah knows what is in your souls, so beware of Him﴾. He the Exalted said: ﴿And Allah is ever Watchful over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab: 52]. He the Exalted said: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]. He the Exalted said: ﴿Does he not know that Allah sees?﴾ [al-'Alaq: 14]. He the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, you are under Our eyes﴾ [al-Tur: 48]. He the Exalted said: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19]. And other verses besides these.

In the hadith of Jibril (peace be upon him), that he "asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about ihsan (excellence). He said: To worship Allah as though you see Him; and if you do not see Him, indeed He sees you."

Muraqabah is defined as the servant's continuous knowledge and certainty that the Real (al-Haqq), glory be to Him and exalted, is aware of his outward and inward states. Its persistence in this knowledge and certainty is muraqabah, and it is the fruit of his knowledge that Allah, glory be to Him, is watchful over him, observing him, hearing his speech. He is aware of his deeds at every time and every moment, every breath and every blink of an eye. One who is heedless of this is far removed from the state of the beginners (ahl al-bidayat). So how about the state of those who seek (al-muridin)? And how about the state of the knowers ('arifin)?

Al-Jurayri said: Whoever does not make taqwa and muraqabah a judge between himself and Allah the Exalted does not attain unveiling (kashf) and witnessing (mushahadah).

It was said: whoever observes Allah in his thoughts, He protects him in the movements of his limbs.

It was said to one of them: when does the shepherd drive his flock with his staff away from the pastures of destruction? He said: when he knows that there is a watcher over him.

Al-Junayd said: whoever truly realizes muraqabah fears the loss of a single moment from his Lord, and nothing else.

Dhu al-Nun said: the sign of muraqabah is preferring what Allah has sent down, magnifying what Allah has magnified, and belittling what Allah has belittled.

It was said: hope moves one to obedience, fear keeps one far from sins, and muraqabah leads you to the path of realities (haqa'iq).

It was said: muraqabah is the heart's attentiveness to observing the Real with every passing thought and every step.

Al-Jurayri said: our affair is built on two principles: that you bind yourself to muraqabah toward Allah, and that knowledge remains upright upon your outward conduct.

Ibrahim al-Khawwas said: muraqabah is the sincerity of the secret and the public for Allah, mighty and majestic.

It was said: the best thing a person can bind himself to on this path is accountability (muhasabah) and muraqabah, and directing his deeds by knowledge.

Abu Hafs said to Abu 'Uthman al-Naysaburi: when you sit with people, be a preacher to your heart and your self. Let their gathering around you not deceive you, for they observe your outward state, while Allah observes your inward state.

The masters of the path agree that muraqabah of Allah in thoughts is a cause of guarding them in the movements of outward conduct. Whoever observes Allah in his secret, Allah guards him in his movements, in his secret and his public.

Muraqabah is worshipping Allah through His names: the Watcher (al-Raqib), the Guardian (al-Hafiz), the All-Knowing (al-'Alim), the All-Hearing (al-Sami'), the All-Seeing (al-Basir). Whoever understands these names and worships according to what they require, muraqabah is attained for him. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 237:

﴿The one in whose hand is the knot of marriage﴾ is the husband. Some have said it is the guardian (wali), so that if the man pardons, he gives her the full dowry, ﴿unless they pardon﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: "The woman leaves to the husband what is owed to her, and so she has pardoned."

I say: In another narration from Ahmad, his text states that it is the father, and this is the position of Malik, and it was chosen by Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah.

I have mentioned some fifteen proofs for its preference in another place.

People stand in their prayer at five levels.

The first: the one who wrongs himself by neglecting it. He is the one who falls short in its ablution (wudu'), its times, its limits, and its pillars (arkan).

The second: the one who observes its times, its limits, its outward pillars, and its ablution, but has neglected the struggle against his self in the matter of whisperings (waswasa), so he goes off with the whisperings and thoughts.

The third: the one who observes its limits and pillars and strives against his self to repel the whisperings and thoughts. He is occupied with struggling against his enemy lest he steal his prayer, so he is in prayer and in struggle (jihad).

The fourth: the one who, when he stands to pray, perfects its rights, pillars, and limits, and his heart is absorbed in observing its limits and rights lest he lose any part of them. Rather, his whole concern is directed to establishing it as it should be, perfecting it and completing it. His heart is absorbed in the matter of the prayer and in the servitude to his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, within it.

The fifth: the one who, when he stands to pray, stands to it in the same way, but in addition to this, his heart has been seized and placed before his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, looking with his inner sight toward Him, watching Him, filled with His love and His greatness, as if he sees Him and witnesses Him. Those whisperings and steps have vanished, and their veils have been lifted between him and his Lord. This person's state, between himself and others in prayer, is better and greater than what lies between the heavens and the earth. He is, in his prayer, occupied with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, content in Him.

So the first category is punished, the second is held to account, the third has his sins expiated, the fourth is rewarded, and the fifth is brought near to his Lord, because he has a share of the one whose coolness of eye was made in prayer. Whoever has his eye cooled by his prayer in this world has his eye cooled by nearness to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in the Hereafter, and his eye is also cooled by it in this world. Whoever has his eye cooled by Allah has every eye cooled by Him. Whoever does not have his eye cooled by Allah, Exalted, has his soul torn apart by regrets over the world.

It has been narrated that when the servant stands to pray, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "Lift the veils." When he turns (iltifat), He says: "Lower them." This turning has been explained as the heart's turning away from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, toward something else. When he turns to something else, He lowers the veil between Him and the servant, and the devil enters, presents to him the affairs of this world, and shows them to him in the form of a mirror. But when he turns his heart toward Allah and does not turn away, the devil cannot intervene between Allah, Exalted, and that heart. The devil enters only when the veil has fallen. If he flees to Allah, Exalted, and brings his heart into presence, the devil flees. If he turns away, the devil returns. This is his condition and the condition of his enemy in prayer.

If it is said: What is the benefit in singling out the Asr prayer as the one whose good deeds are nullified, rather than the other prayers?

It is said: The hadith does not negate nullification (hubut) for prayers other than Asr except by the implication of a title (mafhum laqab), and that is a very weak form of implication. The singling out of Asr in mention is due to its excellence among the prayers. For this reason it is the Middle Prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta), by the clear and authentic explicit text of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

For this reason he singled it out in mention in the other hadith, which is his saying: "The one who misses the Asr prayer is as if he has been robbed of his family and his wealth" (fa-ka-annama watara ahlahu wa malahu).

That is, it is as if he has been stripped of his family and his wealth, so that he is left without family or wealth. This is an illustration of the nullification of his deeds by abandoning it. It is as if he likened his righteous deeds, and his benefit and enjoyment from them, to the position of his family and wealth. So when he abandons the Asr prayer, he is like someone who has family and wealth, goes out of his house for a need while his family and wealth are in it, and then returns to find his family and wealth taken, so he remains bereft of them, deprived and stripped of them. The illustration does not fit exactly for his righteous deeds.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 245:

His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so He may multiply it for him many times over? And for him there is a generous reward.﴾

He, glorified is He, opened the verse with the most gentle form of address, which is the interrogative that carries the meaning of a request, and it is more eloquent in requesting than the imperative form.

The meaning is: Is there anyone who will offer this goodly loan, so that he is repaid with multiplied increases?

That spending was called a goodly loan in order to rouse souls and urge them to give. For the giver, once he knows that the very substance of his wealth will return to him without fail, his soul becomes compliant and it becomes easy for him to part with it. And if he knows that the borrower is wealthy, faithful and benevolent, it is all the more conducive to the goodness of his act and the generosity of his soul.

If he knows that the borrower will trade with what he has borrowed, grow it for him and make it fruitful until it becomes many times what he gave, then with the loan he is even more generous and more openhanded.

If he knows that, along with all of that, He will add to it from His bounty and giving another reward of a different kind from the loan itself, then that reward is a great portion and a noble gift, for it differs from his loan only because of a blight in himself, namely stinginess and avarice, or a lack of trust in the guarantee.

And that comes from weakness of faith. For this reason, charity is a proof (burhan) for its giver.

All these matters are contained under these words that the verse includes. He called it a loan and informed that He is the one who borrows, not a loan out of need, but a loan of benevolence toward the lender and a solicitation of dealing with him, and so that the amount of profit may be known. He is the one who gave him his wealth and solicited from him a transaction with it.

Then He informed of what returns to him from the loan, namely the multiplied manifold increases.

Then He informed of what He gives him beyond that of additional increase, namely the generous reward.

Wherever this loan appears in the Qur'an, He qualified it as goodly. That combines three matters.

The first: that it be from the good of his wealth, not from its bad or corrupt part.

The second: that he give it with a soul content and steadfast at the time of giving, seeking the pleasure of Allah.

The third: that he not bestow favour upon it nor cause harm to the recipient.

The first relates to the wealth. The second relates to the spender, between him and Allah. The third relates to him and the receiver.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 250:

Patience (al-sabr) and the firmness of the feet (thubat al-aqdam) are both voluntary acts. However, the granting of patience and the making firm are the act of the Lord, exalted is He, and it is He who is asked. Patience and firmness, by contrast, are the acts of the servants, subsisting in them in reality.

(Benefit)

﴿When they confronted Jalut and his hosts, they said: "Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make our feet firm, and give us victory over the disbelieving people." So they routed them by the permission of Allah.﴾ In this verse there are four proofs:

First: their saying, ﴿pour upon us patience﴾. Patience is their voluntary act, yet they asked Him for it, from the One in whose hand it lies, by His will and permission: if He wills, He gives it to them, and if He wills, He withholds it from them.

Second: their saying, ﴿and make our feet firm﴾. The firmness of the feet is a voluntary act, but the making firm is His act, and the firmness is their act, and there is no way to their act except after His act.

Third: their saying, ﴿and give us victory over the disbelieving people﴾. They asked Him for victory, and that is by His strengthening their resolve, encouraging them, granting them patience and firmness, and casting into the hearts of their enemies weakness, fear and terror, so that victory is achieved. Also, a person's being victorious over another is either through bodily actions, which occur by the servant's power and choice, or through proof, clear argument and knowledge, which are also the servant's acts. He, glorified is He, has informed that victory in its entirety is from Him, and He praised the one who asks Him for it. According to the Qadariyyah, it does not fall under the Lord's power.

Fourth: His saying, ﴿so they routed them by the permission of Allah﴾. His permission here is the cosmic, decreed permission, that is, by His will, decree and measure, and not the legislative permission that means command, for that does not necessarily entail defeat of the enemy, unlike His cosmic permission and His cosmic command, for the one commanded in the cosmic sense never fails to occur.

(Section on the highest and the lowest in rank among the people of Paradise)

The highest of them in rank is the master of the sons of Adam, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others. Among them are those to whom Allah spoke, and some He raised in degrees. And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs﴾

Mujahid and others said: "Among them are those to whom Allah spoke" refers to Musa, and "some He raised in degrees" refers to Muhammad.

In the hadith of the Night Journey (isra'), whose authenticity is agreed upon, it is reported that when he passed beyond Musa, Musa said: "My Lord, I did not think You would raise anyone above me." Then he ascended beyond that to a station known only to Allah, until he passed the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha).

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-'As, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "When you hear the muezzin, say what he says, then send blessings upon me, for whoever sends one blessing upon me, Allah sends ten blessings upon him. Then ask Allah for al-Wasilah, for it is a station in Paradise that is fitting only for one of the servants of Allah, and I hope that I will be that one. Whoever asks Allah for al-Wasilah for me, intercession will be made lawful for him."

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "Musa asked his Lord, 'What is the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank?' He said: 'A man who comes after the people of Paradise have entered Paradise, and it will be said to him: Enter Paradise. He will say: My Lord, how (can I enter) when the people have taken their places and taken their shares? It will be said to him: Would you be content that you have something like the kingdom of one of the kings of the world? He will say: I am content, my Lord. It will be said: For you is that, and its like, and its like, and its like. In the fifth he said: I am content, my Lord.' He (Musa) said: 'My Lord, then who is the highest in rank?' He said: 'Those whose honour I planted with My own hand and sealed over, so no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of any human.'"

Al-Tirmidhi said: Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Shababah informed us, from Isra'il, from Thuwayr, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah said: "Indeed, the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon his gardens, his spouses, his bounties, his servants, and his couches spread over a distance of a thousand years, and the most honoured of them before Allah is the one who looks upon His Face morning and evening." Then the Messenger of Allah recited: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾

He said: This hadith has been narrated through other routes from Isra'il, from Thuwayr, from Ibn 'Umar, not raised (to the Prophet). He said: Abd al-Malik ibn Abjar narrated it from Thuwayr, from Ibn 'Umar, as a statement of Ibn 'Umar (mawquf). 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari ibn Sufyan narrated it from Thuwayr, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, similarly, without raising it.

I say: al-Tabarani narrated it in his Mu'jam from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Abjar, from Thuwayr, from Ibn 'Umar, raised: "Indeed, the lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is a man who looks over his kingdom for two thousand years, seeing its farthest end as he sees its nearest, looking at his spouses, his couches, and his servants," and the hadith continues.

Abu Nu'aym narrated it from Isra'il, from Thuwayr, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: Isra'il said: I do not know of Thuwayr except that he raised it to the Prophet ﷺ.

In the verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi) He mentions life, which is the root of all attributes, and with it His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah), which requires His essence and permanence and the negation of all defects from Him, such as drowsiness, sleep, incapacity and others. Then He mentions the perfection of His dominion, and follows it with His oneness in His dominion and that no one intercedes with Him except by His permission. Then He mentions the breadth of His knowledge and its comprehensiveness, and follows it with the statement that creatures have no path to knowing anything except after His will that they should know it. Then He mentions the vastness of His Kursi, drawing attention thereby to His vastness, glory and exaltedness, and this is a preparation before the mention of His exaltedness and greatness. Then He informs of the perfection of His power and of His preservation of the upper and lower worlds without burden, hardship or fatigue. Then He concludes the verse with these two majestic names, which indicate the exaltedness of His essence and His greatness in Himself.

He said in Surah Taha: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they do not encompass it in knowledge﴾ [Taha: 110]. There has been disagreement about the referent of the pronoun in "bihi" (it). It has been said that it refers to Allah, glory be to Him, meaning they do not encompass Allah in knowledge. It has also been said that it refers to what is before them and what is behind them. According to the first, it refers to the Knower; according to the second, it refers to the known. This second view entails the first, but not vice versa, because if they do not encompass some of His known things that concern them, then not encompassing Him in knowledge is even more certain. Likewise, the pronoun in His saying ﴿and they do not encompass anything of His knowledge﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255] may refer to Allah, and may refer to ﴿what is before them and what is behind them﴾, meaning they do not encompass anything of the knowledge of that except what He wills. According to the first, the verbal noun is an annexation to the subject; according to the second, it is an annexation to the object. The point is that if ﴿the Most High, the Most Great﴾ were only meant to signify His attribute of knowledge, power, dominion and what follows from these, it would be repetition, or even less than repetition, for mentioning these things in detail is more eloquent than indicating them by something that is understood only with difficulty. Likewise, if it is said that His highness and greatness are merely that He is greater than His creatures and superior to them, this is a great diminishing of these two magnificent attributes, and this is not fitting, nor is it good to mention and report it about Him except in the context of refuting those who equate Him with others in worship and divinity, as in His saying: ﴿Say: Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen. Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [al-Naml: 59].

And the saying of Yusuf the Truthful: ﴿Are scattered lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39], and His saying, exalted is He, about the sorcerers, that they said to Pharaoh: ﴿Indeed we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us to of magic. And Allah is better and more enduring﴾ [Taha: 73].

In a context like this it is said that Allah is better than whatever else is worshipped as a false deity. But after stating that He is the Owner of all existence, and saying with that that He is superior to His creatures and greater than His works, this is what the speech of Allah is free from. Rather, this befits those who ascribe to Him the evil similitude in His speech, making its apparent meaning disbelief at one time, misguidance at another, anthropomorphism and corporealisation at another, and contrary to clear reason at another. They distort it with false distortions and say about it what none of them would accept being said about his own speech. Thus they ascribe to His speech the evil similitude, just as they ascribed to Him, glory be to Him, the evil similitude by denying His attributes of perfection and the realities of His Most Beautiful Names. Had anyone interpreted their speech, or the speech of those they venerate, according to the way they interpret the speech of Allah and His Messenger, one of them would rise up in anger. And when the matter is examined against them, it becomes clear that the corrupt interpretations by which they interpret the speech of Allah and His Messenger are not fitting to be applied even to the words of the most excellent individual human beings.

The sanctity of faith, the Qur'an and the Messenger has fallen from their hearts. For this reason they openly declare that the Qur'an and the Sunnah do not convey knowledge or certainty in this matter, and they say that the demonstrative method (al-tariqah al-burhaniyyah) is not in the Qur'an, but is in the logic of the Greeks.

He clarifies this in:

The one hundred and eighty-ninth aspect: that the word "great" (al-'azim) is applied to entities, to speech, to attributes and to meanings. As for entities, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the Lord of the Mighty Throne﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 116], and His saying ﴿and she has a great throne﴾ [al-Naml: 23]. As for meanings, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed you are of a great character﴾ [al-Qalam: 4], and His saying ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander﴾ [al-Nur: 16]. So He is described by His essence, His attributes and His actions, and every described thing has its attribute according to its nature: the greatness of the essence is one thing, the greatness of its attributes is another, the greatness of speech is another, and the greatness of action is another. The Lord, exalted is He, possesses greatness in every respect and every aspect, by His essence. The Mu'attilah (negators of attributes) deny the greatness of His essence and affirm only a greatness of meaning; they do not affirm greatness of essence, just as they say the same about highness, that it is merely elevation of status.

(Chapter)

On the effect of his saying, "O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting, by Your mercy I seek relief," in dispelling this affliction, there is a remarkable connection. The attribute of life comprises all attributes of perfection and necessitates them, and the attribute of self-subsistence comprises all attributes of action. For this reason the Greatest Name of Allah, which when called upon He answers, and when asked by it He gives, is the name "the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting". Complete life opposes all illnesses and pains, and for this reason, when the life of the people of Paradise is perfected, no grief or sorrow or anxiety or any affliction reaches them. Deficiency of life harms actions and contradicts self-subsistence, so the perfection of self-subsistence is due to the perfection of life. The absolutely Living, whose life is complete, does not lack any attribute of perfection whatsoever, and the Self-Subsisting is never unable to perform any possible action. Therefore, seeking by means of His attribute of living self-subsistence has an effect in removing whatever opposes life and harms actions.

Similar to this is the Prophet's ﷺ seeking to his Lord, by His lordship, for Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, that He guide him to the truth regarding which people differed, by His permission. For the life of the heart is by guidance, and Allah, glory be to Him, has entrusted these three angels with life.

So Jibril is entrusted with revelation, which is the life of hearts.
Mika'il is entrusted with rain, which is the life of bodies and animals.
Israfil is entrusted with the blowing of the Trumpet, which is the cause of the life of the world and the return of souls to their bodies.

Thus seeking to Him, glory be to Him, by the lordship of these great spirits entrusted with life, has an effect in attaining the sought-after objective.

The point is that the name "the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting" has a particular effect in answering supplications and removing distresses. In the Sunan and in Sahih Ibn Hibban, it is reported marfu'an: "The Greatest Name of Allah is in these two verses: ﴿And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163], and the opening of Al 'Imran: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾."

al-Tirmidhi said: this is a sound hadith.

And in the Sunan and Sahih Ibn Hibban also, from the hadith of Anas: "A man supplicated, saying: O Allah, I ask You, because to You belongs all praise, there is no deity except You, the Bestower, Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of majesty and honour, O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'He has supplicated Allah by His Greatest Name, which when He is called upon by it He answers, and when He is asked by it He gives.'"

For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ exerted himself in supplication, he would say: "O Ever-Living, O Self-Subsisting."

(Benefit)

As for pure negative attributes, they do not enter into His descriptions, exalted is He, unless they include an affirmation, like "the One" (al-Ahad), which includes His being singular in lordship and divinity, and "al-Salam" (the Peace), which includes His freedom from every deficiency that opposes His perfection. Likewise, reporting Him by negations is because they include an affirmation, as in His saying: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾, for it includes the perfection of His life and self-subsistence. Likewise His saying: ﴿And no fatigue touched Us﴾ includes the perfection of His power. Likewise His saying: ﴿Not an atom's weight escapes your Lord﴾ includes the perfection of His knowledge. Likewise His saying: ﴿He neither begets nor is born﴾ includes the perfection of His self-sufficiency (samadiyyah) and independence. Likewise His saying: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ includes His uniqueness in His perfection and that He has no equal. Likewise His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him﴾ includes His greatness and that He is too exalted to be perceived in a way that encompasses Him. This pattern holds for every negative attribute by which He described Himself.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 257:

Since darkness stands for the paths of falsehood and light stands for the path of truth, light is mentioned in the singular while darknesses is in the plural. This is why He said: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of the darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut (false deities / every transgressor against Allah); they bring them out of the light into the darknesses﴾

So He made the protector of those who believe singular, and that is Allah, the One, the Unique; and He made those who disbelieve plural, because of their multiplicity and abundance. He made darknesses plural, which are the paths of misguidance and error, because of their multitude and diversity; and He made light singular, which is His true religion and His straight path, to which there is no way other than it. And since the right (al-yamin) is the direction of goodness and success and its people are the ones who are saved, it was mentioned in the singular; and since the left (al-shimal) is the direction of the people of falsehood, and they are the companions of the left, it was mentioned in the plural in His saying: ﴿from the right and the lefts﴾.

﴿And those who disbelieve, their protectors are the Taghut; they bring them out of the light into the darknesses...﴾

Their protectors return them to that in which they were created: the darkness of their natures, their ignorance and their desires. Whenever the light of prophethood and revelation shines upon them and they are about to enter it, their protectors prevent them from it and turn them away. That is their bringing them out of the light into the darknesses.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 2, verse 258:

Whoever reflects on the position of the disputant and the cutting off of the arguer in what this verse contains will arrive at the greatest proof in the most concise expression. When Abraham answered his interlocutor about God by saying that God is the One who gives life and causes death, the enemy of God countered him with a kind of sophistry, namely that he (himself) kills whomever he wishes and spares whomever he wishes, so he has given life to this one and caused that one to die.
